papers.title: When Microenterprises Grow, Are Consumers Better Off? Evidence from Large Loans to Microenterprises in Chile
papers.q: When microenterprises grow through large loans, are their customers better off?
papers.summary: Large loans raised treated firms' profits by USD 292 per month, 13.4%. Customers gained USD 494 per month in consumer surplus, and there is little evidence of business stealing.
papers.conclusion: The welfare gains from credit expansion extend well beyond borrowers.
papers.ident: RCT randomizing large loans to Chilean microenterprises, with customer surveys and spillover analysis on 125,000 non-treated firms.
papers.contribution: Measures customer-side benefits of microenterprise credit in an RCT in Chile, with survey data on consumer surplus and tests for business stealing among 125,000 non-treated firms.
papers.dataDetail: Chilean microenterprise RCT, customer surveys and data on 125,000 non-treated firms.

papers.title: Do Social Norms Substitute for Enforcement? Evidence from Public Officials’ Home Purchases in Singapore
papers.q: Can pro-integrity social norms substitute for formal enforcement in deterring misconduct by Singapore's public officials?
papers.summary: Civil servants disproportionately buy homes near planned but unannounced stations, concentrated one to two years before announcement, among mid-level officials and relatives. Stronger enforcement substantially reduces direct and indirect misconduct.
papers.ident: Matched comparison of civil servant versus control home purchases near planned MRT stations before announcement, plus a dynamic norms model.
papers.contribution: Identifies informed home purchases by civil servants around MRT expansions in universe-level housing data and develops a dynamic model of fragile norms and enforcement.
papers.dataDetail: Universe of Singapore housing transactions and survey measures of perceived corruption and norms.

papers.title: Flowers of Invention: The Economic Impacts of Patent Rights
papers.q: How did the 1985 introduction of plant biotechnology patent rights affect innovation, crop yields and downstream agricultural production in the United States?
papers.summary: Patent rights increased the development of novel plant varieties, driven by private research investment, with spillovers to some non-biological agricultural technologies and higher crop yields. Despite higher seed spending, counties more exposed through crop composition saw higher agricultural land values and profits.
papers.contribution: Exploits differences in crop reproductive structures across crops and a new crop-specific technology development dataset to identify effects of patent rights.
papers.ident: DiD exploiting the 1985 plant patent introduction and differences in crop reproductive structure, with county exposure by crop composition.
papers.dataDetail: Crop-specific technology development data and U.S. county agricultural outcomes.

papers.title: Buying a Station or Relaxing a Constraint? Spectrum Repacking and Dirac's Conjecture
papers.summary: Stations are vertices and interference restrictions edges. For every k at least 4 there is a network in which removing any station saves a channel but relaxing any single restriction does not, resolving Dirac's conjecture.
papers.q: Can buying out one station reduce the channels needed in spectrum repacking when relaxing any single interference restriction cannot?
papers.contribution: Constructs the missing counterexample at k=4, resolving Dirac's conjecture that every vertex-critical graph has a critical edge.
papers.ident: Theory: graph-theoretic construction of vertex-critical graphs with no critical edge.

papers.title: Automation and Optimal Taxation: A Task-Based Theory
papers.summary: Optimal tax formulas take canonical partial-equilibrium forms, yet automation changes optimal rates through endogenous wages and capital returns. Calibrated to the U.S., machine intensity peaks around the 40th wage percentile, and the optimal labor tax becomes more progressive while the optimal capital tax is sizable but unaffected.
papers.ident: Quantitative: task-based GE optimal tax model calibrated to the U.S. wage distribution and automation exposure.
papers.q: How should labor and capital income be taxed optimally in an economy with task-based automation?
papers.contribution: Characterizes optimal labor and capital taxation in a general-equilibrium task-based automation model with extensive-margin labor supply and finite capital supply elasticity.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. wage distribution and occupational automation exposure.

papers.title: Beyond the Conventional Narrative: Economic Heterogeneity and Human Capital Among American Indians
papers.summary: Outcomes vary with location, resource endowments and historical experiences, and policies such as forced relocation and boarding schools had long-lasting negative effects on human capital and mobility. Recent improvements occurred where tribes exercised greater self-governance.
papers.conclusion: Analyzing and remediating disparities requires accounting for heterogeneity across Native populations.
papers.q: How heterogeneous are economic, educational and health outcomes among American Indians, and what role did historical policies play?
papers.contribution: Argues that a one-size-fits-all approach is inadequate and discusses measurement challenges of racial and tribal identification.
papers.ident: Descriptive: review of evidence on American Indian outcomes and measurement.

papers.title: How Disability Benefits in Early Life Affect Adult Outcomes
papers.q: How does receiving SSI in childhood affect adult outcomes?
papers.summary: SSI has positive effects on children when parents do not reduce labor supply, but zero or negative effects when parents offset the transfer by working less. Income is crucial to human capital production of low-income children with disabilities relative to parent nonwork time.
papers.contribution: Uses variation across and within two quasi-experiments and a structural model of maternal labor supply and child human capital formation.
papers.ident: Two quasi-experiments in SSI eligibility, plus a structural model of maternal labor supply and child human capital.

papers.title: Correlation Neglect in Asset Prices

authors.inst: United States Securities and Exchange Commission

papers.q: Do investors neglect correlation in earnings news, producing negative serial correlation in stock returns across months of a quarter?
papers.summary: Investors fail to recognize the predictable repetition of aggregate earnings news from late announcements, so overreaction in the second month is corrected when new quarter earnings arrive. The pattern is stronger when announced earnings are more similar, with support from survey and industry-level data.
papers.conclusion: Correlation neglect occurs even among sophisticated, financially incentivized decision-makers.
papers.contribution: Documents a negative serial correlation between returns in the second month of a quarter and the first month of the next, and explains it by correlation neglect.
papers.ident: Time-series return predictability regressions around earnings announcement months.
papers.dataDetail: Stock market and industry returns, earnings announcements and survey data.

papers.title: Asset Privatization as Intergenerational Redistribution
papers.q: How does subsidized access to appreciating public assets redistribute resources across generations in fast-growing economies?
papers.summary: Capital gains on privatized housing let homeowners trade up, amplifying housing demand, prices and redistribution. Asset-based redistribution delivers higher welfare for future cohorts than pension-based redistribution while substantially reducing long-run fiscal burdens.
papers.ident: Quantitative: equilibrium model calibrated to China's housing privatization.
papers.contribution: Shows early access to assets before growth is capitalized gives incumbent generations an early claim on growth, and evaluates it in a model calibrated to China's housing privatization.

papers.title: The elusive link between FDI and economic growth: Sectoral heterogeneity and global value chains
papers.summary: Reassesses the relationship between FDI and economic growth in emerging and developing economies, with attention to sectoral heterogeneity and global value chains.
papers.q: Does FDI promote economic growth in emerging and developing economies, and does it vary by sector and global value chain position?

papers.title: Global financial spillovers of Chinese macroeconomic surprises
papers.q: How do Chinese macroeconomic surprises spill over to global financial markets?
papers.summary: Studies global financial spillovers of Chinese macroeconomic surprises, according to the title.

papers.title: Can time-varying currency risk hedging explain exchange rates?
papers.q: Can time-varying currency risk hedging explain exchange rates?
papers.summary: Asks whether time-varying currency risk hedging can explain exchange rates, according to the title.

papers.title: The health effects of genetically modified crops
papers.q: What are the health effects of genetically modified crops?
papers.summary: Studies the health effects of genetically modified crops, according to the title.

papers.title: Behavioral Attenuation
papers.q: What is behavioral attenuation?
papers.summary: Studies behavioral attenuation, according to the title.

papers.title: Timing is Everything: Parental Professional Connections and Labor Market Entry
papers.q: How do parental professional connections affect children's labor market entry timing?
papers.summary: Studies parental professional connections and labor market entry, according to the title.

papers.title: Sabotage as Industrial Policy
papers.summary: For some goods, completely destroying foreigners' productivity raises domestic real income by shifting production and improving terms of trade. For semiconductors, partial sabotage would lower U.S. real income, while comprehensive sabotage would raise it.
papers.ident: Theory: trade model with sufficient statistics for the gross benefit of sabotage, applied to semiconductors.
papers.q: Can sabotaging foreign productivity serve as trade and industrial policy, as in U.S. semiconductor policy toward China?
papers.contribution: Characterizes sabotage as trade policy with gross benefits summarized by sufficient statistics and costs set by relative unit labour costs.

papers.title: Rethinking Reference Dependence: Wage Dynamics and Optimal Taxi Labor Supply
papers.q: Can a dynamic optimal stopping model with standard preferences explain NYC taxi drivers' labor supply and the apparent behavioral biases?
papers.summary: Several apparent behavioral biases in the literature are reproduced with entirely standard preferences, and taxi drivers' earnings elasticities are similar to those of workers in experimental markets. Using a 2012 fare change, market elasticities are approximately a tenth of the size of individual elasticities.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic optimal stopping model of drivers' work times estimated on shift data, plus a 2012 fare change for market elasticities.
papers.contribution: Estimates a dynamic optimal stopping model using sufficient statistics for supply-demand equilibrium interactions, so driver opportunity costs follow from a single-agent problem.
papers.dataDetail: Large sample of New York City taxicab driver shifts, including a 2012 fare change.

papers.title: The (hidden) Samaritan contest

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.q: How does a hidden Samaritan contest work?
papers.summary: Studies a (hidden) Samaritan contest, according to the title.

papers.title: Panel threshold regression with unobserved individual-specific threshold effects
papers.q: How can panel threshold regression be estimated and tested with unobserved individual-specific threshold effects?
papers.summary: The unified estimation and inference framework is valid for static and dynamic models, whether or not individual-specific threshold effects exist. Simulations and an empirical application illustrate the method.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: correlated random effects estimation and adaptive Bonferroni inference for panel threshold regression.
papers.contribution: Shows within-regime differencing fails to give consistent threshold estimators and proposes correlated random effects with a unified framework and alternative inference methods.

papers.title: Political career incentives and the environmental costs: Evidence from China’s promotion tournaments
papers.q: How do political career incentives in China's promotion tournaments affect environmental costs?
papers.summary: Studies political career incentives and environmental costs in China's promotion tournaments, according to the title.

papers.title: ‘Returning brains’: Tax incentives, migration, and scientific productivity
papers.q: How do tax incentives for returning scientists affect migration and scientific productivity?
papers.summary: Studies tax incentives, migration and scientific productivity of returning researchers, according to the title.

papers.title: Standardized test scores and academic performance at a public university system
papers.q: How do standardized test scores relate to academic performance in a public university system?
papers.summary: Studies standardized test scores and academic performance in a public university system, according to the title.

papers.title: High dimensional alpha test for linear factor pricing model with Lq-norm
papers.q: How can zero pricing errors be tested in high-dimensional linear factor pricing models across dense and sparse alternatives?
papers.summary: Larger q leads to greater sensitivity to sparse alternatives, and the L-infinity and Lq statistics are asymptotically independent for any finite q. Simulations and real-data analysis show the tests are more robust to unknown sparsity and can outperform existing procedures.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: Lq-norm alpha tests and a Cauchy combination test for high-dimensional factor pricing models.
papers.contribution: Develops Lq-based tests for finite q bridging L2 and L-infinity statistics, with a Cauchy combination test adapting to unknown sparsity.
papers.dataDetail: Real-data analysis of asset returns.

papers.title: Gender Discrimination in Access to Capital: A Field Experiment in Ethiopia
papers.q: Do loan officers discriminate against female business owners in capital decisions in Ethiopia?
papers.summary: Gender has no effect on prize scores or consideration for a loan. Beliefs about future performance do not differ by gender and are accurate, and gender does not improve ML predictions of business performance.
papers.contribution: Randomizes owner gender across 3,696 evaluations by 84 loan officers of 916 real businesses, with incentivized beliefs and machine learning predictions of performance.
papers.conclusion: There is no trade-off between gender equity and effective capital allocation.
papers.ident: Field experiment randomizing owner gender in 3,696 business plan evaluations by loan officers.
papers.dataDetail: Evaluations of 916 businesses by 84 loan officers in an Ethiopian business plan competition.

papers.title: Job Loss, Unemployment Insurance, and Health: Evidence from Brazil
papers.q: How do job loss and unemployment insurance affect health and mortality among Brazilian workers?
papers.summary: Job loss raises hospitalization by 33% and mortality by 23% for men, with no significant effects for women, and children of male workers are also affected. External causes related to risky behavior and violence explain half the effects, and UI partially mitigates them.
papers.ident: Mass layoff event study for job loss and RDD for unemployment insurance eligibility.
papers.contribution: Links administrative employment, hospitalization, health insurance and mortality records over 17 years and uses mass layoffs and an RDD for UI.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian administrative data linking employment, hospitalizations, health insurance and mortality over 17 years.

papers.title: Return to Office and the Tenure Distribution
papers.q: How do return-to-office mandates affect employee tenure and seniority at large tech firms?
papers.summary: Firms that return to the office see reduced tenure and seniority at Microsoft, SpaceX and Apple. Mandates appear to drive senior employees away.
papers.conclusion: Return-to-office mandates pose a risk to firm productivity and innovation.
papers.ident: Distributional synthetic controls on firm-level tenure distributions around return-to-office mandates.
papers.contribution: Uses large-scale resume data with a distributional synthetic controls framework, extended with a functional bootstrap that has valid uniform confidence bands.
papers.dataDetail: Resume data for employees at Microsoft, SpaceX and Apple.

papers.title: Insurance Choice with Non-Monetary Plan Attributes: Limited Consideration in Medicare Part D
papers.summary: More than 90% of individuals consider 5 or fewer plans, approximately 10% of the menu, and unobserved heterogeneity in consideration plays a crucial role. Estimated risk preferences are comparable to existing studies of similar stakes.
papers.q: How do non-monetary plan attributes shape which insurance plans individuals consider in Medicare Part D?
papers.contribution: Proposes an insurance demand model in which non-monetary attributes determine consideration sets and monetary attributes determine expected utility.
papers.ident: Structural: limited consideration insurance demand model estimated on Medicare Part D data with unobserved heterogeneity.
papers.dataDetail: Medicare Part D plan choice data.

papers.title: More on onetary Economics
papers.q: Does the cashless limit of a monetary equilibrium converge to the non-monetary equilibrium?
papers.summary: The fraction of households meeting no firms determines money demand, while those meeting one or several firms determine competition and the sensitivity of real rates to inflation. Convergence depends on whether the financial market becomes perfectly competitive, which depends on the exact specification of frictions.
papers.contribution: Revisits the Menzio and Spinella (2025) model with financial market frictions to settle convergence of the cashless limit.
papers.ident: Theory: search-theoretic monetary model with frictions in the financial market.

papers.title: The economics of abduction marriage: Evidence from Ethiopia
papers.q: What are the economics of abduction marriage in Ethiopia?
papers.summary: Studies the economics of abduction marriage in Ethiopia, according to the title.

papers.title: Identification of non-additive fixed effects models: Is the return to teacher quality homogeneous?
papers.q: Can non-additive fixed effects models be identified, and is the return to teacher quality homogeneous?
papers.summary: Studies identification of non-additive fixed effects models and asks whether the return to teacher quality is homogeneous, according to the title.

papers.title: Matrix-valued spatial autoregressions with dynamic heterogeneous spillovers
papers.q: How can matrix-valued spatial autoregressions with dynamic heterogeneous spillovers be modelled?
papers.summary: Studies matrix-valued spatial autoregressions with dynamic heterogeneous spillovers, according to the title.

papers.title: Spatio-temporal autoregressions for high dimensional matrix-valued time series

authors.inst: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics
London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How can spatio-temporal autoregressive models be consistently estimated for high-dimensional matrix-valued time series such as intraday trading volume curves?
papers.summary: Ordinary least squares is inconsistent because of endogeneity in the spatio-temporal models. The proposed GMM-based Yule-Walker approach estimates two distinct banded weight matrices with a dual-bandwidth specification.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: iterated generalized Yule-Walker estimation of spatio-temporal matrix autoregressions.
papers.contribution: Develops an iterated generalized Yule-Walker estimator for two spatio-temporal matrix autoregressions with banded weight matrices and a two-step ratio-based procedure for dual bandwidths.
papers.dataDetail: Intraday trading volume curves across assets.

papers.title: Behavioral Signatures of Cognitive Noise
papers.summary: Limited cognitive resources force imprecise representation of information, producing coarser decisions, stochastic behavior and subjective uncertainty. Bayesian treatment of imprecision and adaptive resource allocation account for biases and context and experience effects.
papers.q: Can cognitive noise explain a wide range of behavioral anomalies with simple Bayesian models of imprecise representation?
papers.contribution: Reviews cognitive noise models, their behavioral consequences and supporting empirical evidence as a unified explanation for behavioral anomalies.
papers.ident: Theory: review of cognitive noise models drawn from neuroscience.

papers.title: Rust in Motion: The Political Environmental Trap of Vehicle Tax Exemptions
papers.q: How do vehicle tax exemptions for older cars affect fleet age, pollution and health in Brazil, and how do they relate to electoral incentives?
papers.summary: Lower exemption age thresholds raise average fleet age by up to one year, raise on-road CO2 per capita by up to 23% and PM2.5 by 4%, and worsen infant health. Incumbents face greater electoral penalties where more of the fleet re-enters the tax base after reforms raising thresholds.
papers.ident: Border-pair design on state differences in vehicle tax exemption age thresholds, plus state reforms raising thresholds.
papers.contribution: Uses a border-pair design on state variation in age thresholds for vehicle ownership tax exemptions, linking registrations, satellite pollution estimates and health data.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian municipality vehicle registrations 2013-2020, satellite pollution and health data.

papers.title: Rain Follows the Forest: Land Use Policy, Climate Change, and Adaptation
papers.q: How did the 1930s Great Plains Shelterbelt alter climate and agriculture in downwind counties?
papers.summary: The program increased precipitation and decreased temperatures for decades. Farmers expanded corn acreage and adopted water-intensive practices, contributing to the survival of small farms but less machine use.
papers.conclusion: Climate is endogenous to land use change, with long-term impacts of tree planting on agricultural development.
papers.contribution: Measures climate effects in downwind counties where no trees were planted, isolating climate from afforestation effects and enabling the study of adaptation.
papers.ident: Comparison of downwind counties by exposure to the Great Plains Shelterbelt program, isolating climate effects from afforestation.
papers.dataDetail: Great Plains counties, climate data and agricultural census records, 1930s onward.

papers.title: The Limits of Verifiability: Credibility and Flexibility in Communication
papers.q: When does verifiable communication help or hinder information transmission compared to unverifiable communication?
papers.summary: Tying claims to evidence raises credibility but limits flexibility. When preferences are sufficiently aligned, full evidence disclosure is neither sustainable nor efficient; verifiability helps when preferences are sufficiently misaligned and hinders when aligned.
papers.conclusion: Institutions imposing verification need not always improve information transmission.
papers.contribution: Identifies a credibility-flexibility tradeoff in sender-receiver settings where the sender knows more than her evidence can prove.
papers.ident: Theory: sender-receiver game comparing verifiable and unverifiable communication with partially aligned preferences.

papers.title: Signals, Steps, and Setbacks: Age Discrimination in a Laddered Labor Market
papers.q: How does age discrimination operate in a labor market with a job ladder?
papers.summary: Applications and callbacks decline sharply at posted age cutoffs, with older applicants disadvantaged in entry-level jobs and younger applicants less likely to be hired into managerial roles. Older entry-level applicants are negatively selected, consistent with the model.
papers.contribution: Uses a Chinese recruitment platform linking postings, applications and employer responses to document discrimination at posted age cutoffs, with a statistical discrimination model.
papers.ident: RD-style comparison at posted age cutoffs in job postings, with a statistical discrimination model.
papers.dataDetail: Large Chinese recruitment platform linking postings, applications and employer responses.

papers.title: “Non-Marginal” Investor Beliefs

authors.inst: United States Department of the Treasury

papers.q: How do the beliefs of non-marginal investors who step out of the market affect asset prices?
papers.summary: Non-marginal investors are more pessimistic in return forecasts and perceive greater crash risk. Subjective crash beliefs determine participation, and stocks more sensitive to non-marginal beliefs earn lower returns, especially where disagreement is high.
papers.ident: Descriptive: wedge measures between survey beliefs and option-implied benchmarks, linked to participation and returns.
papers.contribution: Constructs wedge measures between subjective investor beliefs and option-implied benchmarks from more than two decades of respondent-level surveys.
papers.dataDetail: More than two decades of respondent-level investor surveys and option-implied data.

papers.title: Loan Rates as Incentive Instruments
papers.summary: When failure pay is restricted, the bank reprices loans toward rates making repayment probabilities similar across borrowers and may take more risk. A capital requirement caps failure pay in this way, and a countercyclical requirement can generate a permanent two-point cycle.
papers.q: How do loan rates act as incentive instruments for bank employees, alongside their pricing role?
papers.contribution: Models a bank jointly designing wage contracts and loan rate menus, showing the optimal wage contract is non-monotone, including pay after default.
papers.ident: Theory: principal-agent model of bank wage contracts and loan rate menus.

papers.title: Do Online Job Postings Capture Job Vacancies?
papers.q: Do online job postings from Burning Glass capture U.S. job vacancies as measured by JOLTS?
papers.summary: Burning Glass converged toward JOLTS over 2007-2022, with representativeness varying by establishment characteristics. The level and cyclicality of skill demand survive the adjustment, but BG overstates labor market concentration (HHI) nearly threefold.
papers.contribution: Matches near-universal Burning Glass postings to JOLTS and reweights them along observables to assess prior findings.
papers.ident: Descriptive: reweighting of Burning Glass postings to JOLTS openings along establishment observables.
papers.dataDetail: Burning Glass job postings and JOLTS, 2007-2022.

papers.title: Does AI Assistance Enhance or Erode Expertise? Evidence from a Three-Month Field Experiment in Patent Drafting
papers.summary: AI access raised quality of benchmark drafting at 10 days (0.34 SD) and 90 days (0.38 SD), with larger gains among juniors. In a later AI-free redlining task treated lawyers outperformed controls by 0.32 SD, concentrated among seniors (0.45 SD), while junior scores bifurcated.
papers.ident: Pre-registered RCT giving patent lawyers access to an AI drafting assistant for three months.
papers.q: Does AI assistance enhance or erode professional expertise in patent drafting?
papers.contribution: Runs a pre-registered three-month RCT with 133 practicing patent lawyers, measuring performance with AI and judgment afterward without it, scored by blinded experts.
papers.dataDetail: 133 patent lawyers at eleven U.S. IP law firms, blinded expert scoring.

papers.title: An Empirically-Grounded Theory of Voting Based on Prosocial Motives
papers.q: Can prosocial voting motives reconcile empirical features of electoral turnout in a costly voting model?
papers.summary: The paper establishes existence of Nash equilibria matching a finite many-voter setting and derives how ideology, voting costs, polarization and expected closeness affect turnout and winning margins. With all three motives, the model reconciles empirical regularities qualitatively and quantitatively where existing models fail.
papers.ident: Theory: costly voting model with prosocial motives, related to existing studies and original data work.
papers.contribution: Proposes a spatial costly voting model in which citizens gain higher payoffs from voting when expecting more fellow supporters, more decisive votes and higher stakes.
papers.dataDetail: Existing studies and original data work on turnout.

papers.title: Expectations-based Capital Inflow Shocks
papers.q: What are the output effects of capital inflows once expectations about future conditions are purged?
papers.summary: For 27 emerging markets, capital inflows have sizable expansionary effects on output via consumption, investment and easier financing. Equity inflows have greater and more persistent effects than debt inflows, and large reversals have more pronounced effects than comparable increases.
papers.ident: Local-projection style estimates using inflow shocks purged of professional forecasters' expectations, 27 emerging markets.
papers.contribution: Develops an expectations-based measure of capital inflow shocks that removes movements predicted by professional forecasters' expectations.
papers.dataDetail: Capital flows and forecasts for 27 emerging market economies.

papers.title: The Utility of AI Tools in Auditing Adherence to Pre-Analysis Plans
papers.summary: The LLM substantially reduces the human labor required for audits, but variability in output across LLMs underscores the continued importance of human judgment.
papers.q: Can large language models audit adherence to pre-analysis plans?
papers.contribution: Applies an LLM to the authors' own research to identify precommitted choices, evaluate deviations and diagnose gaps in pre-specification.
papers.conclusion: The paper discusses best practices for AI-assisted audits of pre-analysis plans.
papers.ident: Descriptive: LLM-based audit of the authors' pre-analysis plan adherence.
papers.dataDetail: Authors' own pre-analysis plan and research documents.

papers.title: Health Insurance Underwriting and the Heterogeneous Effects of the Affordable Care Act
papers.q: How many people did the ACA ban on health insurance underwriting make better off, and how did effects vary by health risk?
papers.summary: Benefits of the reform were concentrated among low-income, high-risk or over-50 individuals.
papers.contribution: Uses a proprietary dataset of pre-ACA insurance applications and underwriting decisions to document, model and estimate heterogeneous effects of the reform.
papers.ident: Structural: model of insurance demand and underwriting estimated on pre-ACA applications, with heterogeneity by age, income and risk.
papers.dataDetail: Proprietary dataset of pre-ACA insurance applications and underwriting decisions.

papers.title: Risk Perceptions of E-Cigarettes and the Evaluation of EVALI Messaging
papers.summary: Public health messages range widely across Australia, China, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Sweden, the U.K. and U.S. Smokers' perceptions of e-cigarette risks are associated with their perceptions of smoking risk and country messaging, and many in all eight countries incorrectly believe e-cigarettes are more harmful than smoking.
papers.q: How do smokers form perceptions of e-cigarette risks, and how do public health messages such as EVALI messaging shape them?
papers.contribution: Uses Bayesian learning as framework for a cross-country descriptive analysis of messaging and perceptions in eight countries, plus online randomized experiments.
papers.ident: Cross-country descriptive survey analysis plus online randomized experiments on messaging.
papers.dataDetail: Online surveys of adult smokers in eight countries.

papers.title: How Big is Small? The Economic Effects of Access to Small Business Government Support
papers.q: How did expanding U.S. small business program eligibility affect the smallest firms?
papers.summary: Revenues decline for the smallest firms, especially younger, more productive and financially constrained ones, and procurement contracts are reallocated to larger firms. Exits increase, wages decline and patenting falls.
papers.conclusion: Expanding eligibility crowds out the smallest firms and shifts resources away from high-potential firms, reducing dynamism and innovation.
papers.contribution: Exploits quasi-random timing of eligibility standard expansions with administrative Census data.
papers.ident: Staggered DiD exploiting quasi-random timing of expansions in small business size standards.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. administrative Census firm data and procurement contracts.

papers.title: Comparisons
papers.q: When do decisions increase or decrease with comparison points such as reference points, goals, expectations and peers?
papers.summary: Decisions decrease in input comparators and increase in output comparators, confirmed in experiments on labor supply, investment and belief updating. Effects weaken when uncertainty is reduced or comparators are less informative, and the taxonomy organizes over 100 prior experimental and field observations.
papers.contribution: Develops an input-versus-output taxonomy predicting the sign of comparison effects, based on comparisons serving as information when absolute evaluation is difficult.
papers.ident: Online experiments on labor supply, investment and belief updating varying input and output comparators.
papers.dataDetail: Experiments with social and expectations-based comparison points.

papers.title: Cross-Section Estimation of Long-Run Relations Using Time-Compressed Data
papers.q: Can cross-section regressions in time-compressed (averaged or long-differenced) data estimate long-run relations consistently?
papers.summary: Estimates can be super-consistent and asymptotically normal whatever the regressor persistence, with fastest rate sqrt(NT) when compression dilutes noise; omitted fixed effects preclude noise dilution. Applications find consumption-income and growth-demographic relations well determined, but the growth-warming relation fragile.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: asymptotics of cross-section regressions in time-compressed nonstationary panel data.
papers.contribution: Analyzes time-compressed I(1) data, showing cross-section variance fans out with time, giving super-consistent estimates.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country consumption, income, growth, inflation, demographic and temperature data.

papers.title: Rational Inattention to Discrete Choices with Stable Priors
papers.q: How can the rational inattention logit model be solved when the decision maker's prior varies across choices?
papers.contribution: Solves the RI-logit model analytically for Positive Stable and Tempered Stable priors, an open problem in the literature.
papers.summary: Prior information enters choice probabilities through a choice-specific parameter, which can shift ex-ante expected utility of a risk-neutral decision maker or perceived riskiness of a risk-averse one.

papers.title: Fairness Across the World

papers.summary: Inequality acceptance depends more on its source than on the efficiency cost: implemented inequality rises 85% when caused by merit rather than luck, versus 14% when redistribution costs 50% of efficiency. papers.summary: Existing variance estimators are either conservative or invalid. The paper interprets common clustering environments from a design-based perspective and gives insights on their estimands and inference procedures.

papers.title: Helping in the Workplace: The Role of Leadership Relative to Employee Personality and Preferences

papers.summary: There is significant between-firm variation in helping, positively correlated with better organizational outcomes for employees and firms. Leadership quality and employees' general trust play a key role in explaining firm-level differences.

papers.title: Do marriage tax penalties cause delayed marriage reporting?

papers.summary: Studies whether marriage tax penalties cause delayed marriage reporting, according to the title.

papers.title: The accuracy of jobseekers’ wage expectations

papers.summary: Jobseekers on average overestimate reemployment wages, especially those with low earnings potential, and beliefs are anchored to past wages. papers.contribution: Compares subjective beliefs with benchmark and realized wages using linked survey-administrative data.
papers.ident: Descriptive: subjective wage beliefs compared with benchmark and realized wages in linked survey-administrative data.

papers.title: Immigration enforcement and safety net participation in mixed-status households

papers.summary: Studies immigration enforcement and safety net participation in mixed-status households, according to the title.

papers.title: Robust inference for time varying predictability: A Sieve-IVX approach
papers.summary: The approach gives pointwise and uniform inference for testing predictability and model specification irrespective of persistence, with asymptotic theory and good finite-sample performance in simulations. An empirical exercise examines excess returns.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: Sieve-IVX estimation and inference in predictive regressions with time-varying coefficients.

papers.dataDetail: Bond and equity return predictability data.

papers.summary: Studies multivariate inference for dynamic systemic risk measures, according to the title.

papers.title: Iterative distributed multinomial regression

papers.summary: When initialized with a consistent estimator, the estimator is asymptotically equivalent to maximum likelihood and efficient under a weak dominance condition. Simulations validate it and highlight its computational efficiency.

papers.summary: Convergence rates are derived under conditions on the mixing rate, the sparsity of cross-sectional dependence and kernel moments. The results are applied to a nonparametric specification test for cross-sectionally dependent data.

papers.title: Economic consequences of climate change: Evidence from the Philippines

papers.summary: Harmonizing equity frictions across countries would produce nearly four times larger output effects than debt frictions, and removing them would raise aggregate output by 73% more. Equity frictions also account for the negative relationship between equity financing and wealth inequality through risk sharing.
papers.ident: Quantitative: GE model of entrepreneurs' debt and equity financing calibrated on Eurozone firm ownership data.

papers.summary: Weak protection constrains suppliers to serve only a few OEMs, sometimes exclusively, especially for parts with intermediate relationship-specificity. The association strengthens with OEM bargaining power.

papers.ident: Propensity-score-weighted comparison of coverage before and after dementia onset using the Langa-Weir classification.
papers.q: How does supplemental Medicare coverage change for people with probable dementia before and after onset?
papers.contribution: Compares 3,001 people with probable dementia to 14,055 matched controls in the 2000-2016 HRS using propensity score weights.
papers.dataDetail: Health and Retirement Study 2000-2016, 3,001 people with probable dementia and 14,055 controls.

papers.title: The Global Transition – The Impact of Demographics and AI on Economic Power
papers.summary: The model includes three labor skill groups, internationally mobile capital, region-specific fiscal policy and TFP growth, and age-specific fertility, mortality and net immigration, with agents living 100 years and unintended bequests.
papers.ident: Quantitative: multi-region OLG general equilibrium model with automation adoption and demographic projections.
papers.q: How will demographics and AI automation shift global economic power this century?
papers.contribution: Builds a 17-region dynamic life-cycle general equilibrium model covering 99% of world population with country-level automation adoption decisions.
papers.dataDetail: Demographic and macro data for 17 regions covering more than 150 countries.

papers.title: Social Clubs and Political Office
papers.q: Do elite social clubs help elites keep political office in formally inclusive systems?
papers.summary: Jockey Club membership raised the probability of holding legislative office by about four percentage points, more than twice the control mean, and increased families' centrality in elite marriage networks. The advantage declines substantially after the 1912 Saenz Pena democratizing reforms.
papers.ident: DiD exploiting staggered entry of families into the Jockey Club of Buenos Aires.
papers.contribution: Exploits staggered family entry into the Buenos Aires Jockey Club in a difference-in-differences design.
papers.dataDetail: Buenos Aires Jockey Club membership, legislative office and elite marriage records, around 1912.

papers.title: Recall Fluency, Beliefs and Behavior

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.summary: Controlling for demographics and IQ, higher recall fluency people are more optimistic about stock returns, home prices and life expectancy, and their beliefs are more sensitive to domain-relevant and irrelevant similar experiences. These effects carry to investment and retirement choices.
papers.conclusion: Recall fluency emerges as an economically relevant personal trait.
papers.q: Does recall fluency shape beliefs and economic behavior?
papers.contribution: Uses Health and Retirement Study recall fluency scores and derives predictions of a standard memory model about cue sensitivity.
papers.ident: Cross-sectional regressions of beliefs and choices on recall fluency with demographic and IQ controls, guided by a memory model.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. Health and Retirement Study.

papers.title: Sticky Wage Norms and the Real Wage Cost of Unexpected Inflation
papers.summary: Most firms apply a single modal annual nominal raise to most workers, and these norms changed little during the inflation. Forty-three percent of continuously employed workers over 2021-2024 experienced a real wage decline, averaging about nine percent among those who fell behind; job-changers' wages rose nearly one-for-one with inflation.
papers.q: How did sticky wage norms affect real wages during the recent unexpected inflation?
papers.contribution: Uses administrative payroll data covering a large, nationally representative share of U.S. workers to document firm-level modal wage increase norms.
papers.ident: Descriptive: firm-level wage change norms and worker real wage trajectories in payroll data, 2021-2024.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative payroll data covering a nationally representative share of U.S. workers, 2021-2024.

papers.title: Dynamic Effects of Trade
papers.summary: Key insights are that short-run and long-run responses to liberalization differ, capital accumulation amplifies trade shocks, trade facilitates technology adoption and idea diffusion, and effects on lifetime welfare differ substantially from static measures.
papers.q: How large and how different from static gains are the dynamic effects of trade through factor accumulation and innovation?
papers.contribution: Reviews research on dynamic effects of trade, including capital accumulation and technology adoption, and what is unsettled about their magnitudes.
papers.ident: Descriptive: review of quantitative research on dynamic gains from trade.

papers.title: Credit Card Banking

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.q: Why are credit card interest rates so high and what do credit card banks earn?
papers.summary: Rates average 22%, an 18% spread over the short rate, and charge-off rates averaging around 6% explain only a fraction. Rewards and non-interest expenses are offset by interchange and non-interest income, operating expenses especially marketing are very large, and card lending still earns a 6.8% return on assets.
papers.contribution: Analyzes lifetime cash flows of 550 million monthly accounts, 90% of the U.S. credit card market, in regulatory account-level data.
papers.ident: Descriptive: decomposition of credit card account profitability using regulatory account-level data.
papers.dataDetail: Regulatory account-level data on 550 million monthly credit card accounts covering 90% of the U.S. market.

papers.title: Fetal Pollution Exposure, Cognitive Ability, and Gender-specific Parental Investment
papers.q: How does prenatal air pollution exposure interact with gender-biased parental investment to shape long-run cognitive ability in China?
papers.summary: Fetal PM2.5 exposure significantly reduces cognitive ability for women, particularly those with brothers. Conditional on the same exposure, females receive less homework assistance and attain less education, so gender-biased educational resource allocation compounds the effects.
papers.contribution: Uses nationally representative Chinese survey data to show fetal PM2.5 exposure harms women's cognition especially with brothers, and traces the family investment channel to education.
papers.ident: Regression of cognitive ability on fetal PM2.5 exposure interacted with gender and sibling composition.
papers.dataDetail: Nationally representative survey data from China and PM2.5 exposure data.

papers.title: The long shadow of typhoons: Prenatal exposure and adult mental health
papers.q: How does prenatal exposure to typhoons affect adult mental health?
papers.summary: Studies the long shadow of typhoons on adult mental health through prenatal exposure, according to the title.

papers.title: Remote work and effort provision in teams

authors.inst: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
University of North Carolina at Charlotte

papers.summary: Remote workers do not complete fewer tasks than office-based counterparts, yet teams suffer lower effort because workers respond to beliefs that remote teammates contribute less. A follow-up shows these beliefs remain salient under revenue-sharing payment.
papers.contribution: Isolates location-based beliefs about teammate effort using experiments with a real effort task and individual versus team accounts.
papers.q: Do beliefs about remote teammates' effort reduce team effort in experiments?
papers.ident: Online experiment varying teammates' remote or office location with a real effort task and minimum-effort team payment.
papers.dataDetail: Experiments with real effort tasks.

papers.title: A Comment on “The Heterogeneous Tax Pass-Through Under Different Vertical Relationships” by Bajo-Buenestado and Borrella-Mas
papers.summary: Including the term reveals a significant structural price trend for vertically integrated firms post-reform, present even in never-treated provinces by a spatial placebo test. With it, the differential pass-through becomes null for diesel while a smaller significant effect persists for gasoline.
papers.ident: Replication comment: respecified DiD with the omitted interaction and a spatial placebo test.
papers.q: Is the specification in Bajo-Buenestado and Borrella-Mas's tax pass-through analysis misspecified?
papers.contribution: Shows the original equation omits the lower-order interaction between vertical integration and the post-treatment period.
papers.dataDetail: Fuel price data from the original study across Spanish provinces.

papers.title: Demographic transition and the rise of wealth inequality
papers.q: How much has rising longevity contributed to the increase in U.S. wealth inequality over the past seventy years?
papers.summary: Improvements in old-age longevity substantially raise wealth inequality, accounting for approximately half the effect of income inequality, while tax changes matter relatively little. The contribution is expected to keep pushing wealth inequality upward.
papers.ident: Quantitative: calibrated OLG model with heterogeneous income, longevity and taxes, U.S. 70 years.
papers.contribution: Constructs an OLG model with multiple sources of inequality, calibrated to the data, to isolate the role of longevity.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. wealth, income and longevity data over the past seventy years.

papers.title: Friends with drugs: The role of social networks in the opioid epidemic
papers.q: Do friendship networks help spread the opioid epidemic across U.S. counties?
papers.summary: Having many friendship links to high-exposure counties correlates with overdose death rates, and more friends in counties hit by the shocks leads to more overdose deaths. Spillovers are attenuated in counties with more cohesive friendship networks.
papers.conclusion: Social connections contribute to the spread of the opioid epidemic.
papers.ident: Network exposure to counties affected by two quasi-natural experiments in opioid substitution.
papers.contribution: Exploits two quasi-natural experiments that pushed users from prescription to illicit opioids, with social connectedness data.
papers.dataDetail: County-level friendship link data and overdose mortality in the U.S.

papers.title: Non-monetary incentives and bureaucratic performance: Evidence from U.S. courts
papers.q: Do non-monetary incentives improve bureaucratic performance in U.S. courts?
papers.summary: Studies non-monetary incentives and bureaucratic performance using evidence from U.S. courts, according to the title.

papers.title: An Optimal Test for Strategic Interaction in Network Formation Games
papers.q: How can strategic interaction in network formation be tested optimally?
papers.summary: Agents' preferences include a dyadic component with out- and in-degree heterogeneity and homophily across K types, and a network benefit function allowing preferences over links to depend on links elsewhere.
papers.contribution: Develops an optimal test of the null in which links form independently across dyads, against alternatives with a network benefit function.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: optimal test against strategic interaction in directed network formation.

papers.title: Capital Unemployment
papers.q: How large is the unemployment of physical capital and what are its macroeconomic implications?
papers.summary: Capital unemployment is large, volatile and rises in downturns. Downturns with large increases in unemployed capital are followed by investment slumps because recovery absorbs existing unemployed capital rather than new investment.
papers.contribution: Documents idle capital searching to be traded and builds a capital accumulation model with trading frictions and financial shocks.
papers.ident: Quantitative: capital accumulation model with trading frictions and financial shocks, with evidence on idle capital.
papers.dataDetail: Data on idle capital units searching to be traded.

papers.title: Embracing the Enemy
papers.summary: The optimal contract initially seeks to exclude the Enemy but embraces him once he gains power in exchange for moderation, which also disciplines the Friend. Principals close to the Friend fully embrace the Enemy, while commitment benefits only principals close to the Friend and parties that value power little.
papers.q: How should a centrist principal allocate support between a friendly party and an enemy party over time?
papers.contribution: Models a principal who can partially influence the allocation of power between two parties with different distances from her preferred policy.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic principal contract over allocation of power between two parties.

papers.title: Reciprocity and state capacity: Evidence from a national pollution control reform in China

authors.inst: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do reciprocity and state capacity relate in a national pollution control reform in China?
papers.summary: Studies reciprocity and state capacity using a national pollution control reform in China, according to the title.

papers.title: Self-medication under uncertainty: Insights on drug quality and consumer behavior in Burkina Faso

authors.inst: RWI – Leibniz Institute for Economic Research
Institut de Recherche en Sciences de la Santé
RWI – Leibniz Institute for Economic Research
Institut de Recherche en Sciences de la Santé
Institut de Recherche en Sciences de la Santé

papers.q: How does drug quality affect self-medication with antibiotics in Burkina Faso?
papers.summary: One in three antibiotics on the market is substandard or falsified, and consumers struggle to judge quality by price or packaging. Self-medication increases as drug quality becomes more certain.
papers.contribution: Combines chemical quality tests with a lab-in-the-field experiment varying the probability of purchasing effective medicine.
papers.conclusion: Market-level quality improvements may unintentionally increase inappropriate antibiotic use, with implications for antimicrobial resistance.
papers.ident: Lab-in-the-field experiment varying the probability of purchasing effective medicine, plus chemical quality testing.
papers.dataDetail: Antibiotics tested on markets and experiment participants in Burkina Faso.

papers.title: Observability and Social Interactions in Consumption
papers.q: How do observability and commonality of income shocks shape consumption responses to a bonus?
papers.summary: Making an idiosyncratic bonus observable to coworkers lowers the MPC by 3 points, and extending it to all coworkers raises it by 6 points, implying a social-interaction parameter of 0.16 and multiplier of 1.2.
papers.conclusion: Consumption responses depend on whether income shocks are private, public or shared in a salient peer group.
papers.ident: Randomized survey experiment varying observability and commonality of a hypothetical bonus.
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized survey experiment in the Italian Survey of Consumer Expectations on responses to a EUR 1,000 employer bonus.
papers.dataDetail: Italian Survey of Consumer Expectations.

papers.title: Cycles of Infertility: Intergenerational Transmission and the Role of Assisted Reproduction
papers.q: How persistent are fertility problems across generations, and what role does assisted reproduction play?
papers.summary: Daughters whose parents reported fertility problems are 2.6 percentage points (19.4 percent) more likely to experience them, and sons 1.7 points (13.5 percent). The associations persist across measures and samples, with biological versus adopted children compared within households.
papers.ident: Descriptive: intergenerational association of fertility problems, comparing biological and adopted children in the same households.
papers.contribution: Uses comprehensive Swedish registry data to document intergenerational transmission of fertility difficulties for daughters and sons, independent of parental socioeconomic status.
papers.dataDetail: Comprehensive Swedish registry data.

papers.title: The Value Gap: Europe Cannot Scale

authors.inst: Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance

papers.summary: In 2008 U.S.-listed firms were worth about one-third more than European-listed firms; by 2023 more than 300% more, a $34 trillion difference. European firm size correlates with home-country GDP while U.S. firm size does not, and smaller European firms face a large cost-of-capital gap without substituting debt for limited equity access.
papers.q: Why has the market value gap between U.S.- and European-listed firms widened since 2008?
papers.contribution: Documents that the valuation gap is broad-based, driven by firm values rather than the number of listed firms, and larger in R&D-intensive and high-returns-to-scale industries.
papers.ident: Descriptive: comparison of aggregate firm market values and cost of capital across U.S. and European listed firms, 2008-2023.
papers.dataDetail: U.S.- and European-listed firm market values, 2008-2023.

papers.title: How Steep is the Phillips Curve in Developing Economies? A Sufficient Statistics Approach and Estimates for India
papers.q: How steep is the Phillips curve in India and why does it differ from the United States?
papers.summary: The slope of India's Phillips curve is one order of magnitude steeper than in the United States, explained by weaker macro real rigidities and less rigid prices.
papers.ident: Sufficient statistics from portable causal designs estimating firm-level pass-through of cost shocks.
papers.contribution: Develops a sufficient statistics method estimating the slope from firm-level cost pass-through and marginal cost curve slopes, with a decomposition into price rigidity, micro and macro real rigidities.
papers.dataDetail: Indian firm-level data on prices and cost shocks.

papers.title: Winning is Contagious: Social Learning and the Dynamics of Union Support

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.summary: Close election wins cause future wins within state-industries. Information about recent union wins increases union support and beliefs about coworker support, especially among workers with weak information environments, while labor market tightness information has little effect.
papers.conclusion: Social learning is a mechanism for union growth.
papers.ident: RDD on close union elections and a randomized information experiment among 9,000 low-wage workers.
papers.contribution: Combines union election data from 1961-2025 with an information experiment on 9,000 low-wage workers.
papers.q: Does social learning explain bursts in union growth?
papers.dataDetail: Union election data 1961-2025 and a survey experiment with 9,000 low-wage workers.

papers.title: Robust Signal Maximization in Spillover Experiments
papers.q: How should experiments estimating spillover effects be designed and analyzed to maximize robust signal?
papers.summary: The design trades off spillover signal strength against diffusion of spillover variation. The framework gives solutions for benchmark cases such as clustered exposure and computationally tractable approximations for general and bipartite networks.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: optimal design and recentered IV estimation for spillover experiments.
papers.contribution: Characterizes the assignment distribution and regression estimator minimizing worst-case asymptotic variance under a known exposure mapping, yielding a recentered IV estimator.

papers.title: Immigrant Earnings Assimilation, 1981–2021
papers.q: How have immigrant earnings assimilation trends changed from 1981 to 2021, including return migrants?
papers.summary: Roughly one-fifth to one-third of immigrants who arrived 1981-2010 return migrate within 10 years of arrival. The paper separately estimates assimilation for return migrants versus stayers.
papers.ident: Descriptive: cohort earnings assimilation profiles for stayers versus return migrants.
papers.contribution: Uses administrative longitudinal data tracking earnings from first U.S. year of residence, identifying return migrants, for the first 41-year trend analysis.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. administrative longitudinal earnings data on immigrants, 1981-2021.

papers.title: The Perils of Bilateral Sovereign Debt
papers.q: How does senior bilateral official lending interact with market debt in sovereign default?
papers.summary: More net market financing strengthens the government's bargaining position and improves bilateral terms, eroding the discipline of spreads and amplifying dilution, producing welfare losses. An optimal rule instead raises bilateral rates with net market financing.
papers.conclusion: The direction of the cross-elasticity can guide assessment of official lending arrangements.
papers.ident: Quantitative: sovereign default model with bilateral negotiated senior debt.
papers.contribution: Develops a quantitative sovereign default model with a large senior lender with whom borrowing terms are negotiated.

papers.title: A Currency Premium Puzzle
papers.summary: Because interest rates are immobilized, differences in expected currency returns must arise almost entirely from predictable exchange rate changes, at odds with the data.
papers.ident: Theory: general result on stochastic discount factors in open-economy asset pricing models.
papers.q: Why do quantitative asset pricing models fail to generate large interest rate differentials between risky and safe currencies?
papers.contribution: Proves that models matching the equity premium and risk-free rate puzzles immobilize interest rates because the SDF mean offsets its variance, a result holding across incomplete markets and exchange rate disconnect.

papers.title: Property Taxes and Housing Allocation Under Financial Constraints
papers.contribution: Builds an OLG model with two channels, capitalization lowering downpayments and higher holding costs, to study California property taxes and step-up basis.
papers.summary: Raising California's property taxes to Texas levels raises young homeownership and lowers elderly homeownership. Removing step-up basis also lowers elderly homeownership, suggesting bequest tax advantages sustain their tenure.
papers.conclusion: The tax treatment of housing shapes housing allocation across generations.
papers.ident: Quantitative: OLG model with financially constrained buyers, property taxes and step-up basis.
papers.q: How do property taxes shape housing allocation across generations under financial constraints?

papers.title: Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks, Bonds (and Options), Redux

authors.inst: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Do stocks, corporate bonds and options share common risk factors?
papers.summary: The common factors link to observable factors and key economic indicators and explain much of individual return variation, though pricing errors persist. A joint mean-variance efficient portfolio achieves a high Sharpe ratio, partly from cross-market hedging, and market segmentation is significant.
papers.contribution: Identifies a common factor structure across corporate securities and develops a market segmentation measure based on differences in factor risk premia.
papers.ident: Factor analysis of returns across stocks, corporate bonds and options.
papers.dataDetail: Returns on stocks, corporate bonds and options.

papers.title: Testing coefficient stability in spatial regression
papers.q: How can coefficient stability be tested in spatial regressions?
papers.summary: The test is designed for good power against persistent patterns of coefficient variation and applicable across a wide range of spatial designs.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: spatial Nyblom-type test of coefficient stability.
papers.contribution: Develops a test approximating the locally best invariant test, a spatial generalization of the Nyblom (1989) test, robust to spatial correlation in regressors and errors.

papers.title: Dual-track in the family: How spousal state employment fuels entrepreneurship
papers.q: How does spousal state employment fuel entrepreneurship in dual-track families?
papers.summary: Studies how spousal state employment fuels entrepreneurship, according to the title.

papers.title: Migration incentives and elderly health: Evidence from the Hukou reforms in China
papers.q: How do migration incentives from Hukou reforms affect elderly health in China?
papers.summary: Studies migration incentives and elderly health using the Hukou reforms in China, according to the title.

papers.title: Career guidance and investments in education: Experimental evidence from Cambodia

authors.inst: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research

papers.q: Does a career guidance workshop change educational investments of rural students in Cambodia?
papers.summary: A half-day career guidance workshop on average increased educational investments. It raised schooling efforts of high-performing students, while treated low-performing students reduced their investments.
papers.ident: RCT of a half-day career guidance workshop with 1,715 students in rural Cambodia.
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized field experiment with 1,715 students and develops a simple model explaining heterogeneity by baseline performance.
papers.dataDetail: 1,715 students in rural Cambodia.

papers.title: The effect of disaster relief on climate adaptation: Evidence from floods in Pakistan
papers.q: How does disaster relief affect climate adaptation after floods in Pakistan?
papers.summary: Studies the effect of disaster relief on climate adaptation using floods in Pakistan, according to the title.

papers.title: College, Cognitive Ability, and Socioeconomic Disadvantage: Policy Lessons from the U.K. in 1960–2004
papers.q: How did expanding U.K. university access since the 1960s change who goes to college, and what policies could have done better?
papers.summary: The expansion led to selection into college of progressively less talented students from advantaged backgrounds. Counterfactual policies existed that would have achieved the expansion with different selection.
papers.ident: Structural: general equilibrium Roy model of college choice estimated on U.K. cohorts, 1960-2004.
papers.contribution: Studies expansion consequences in a stochastic general equilibrium Roy model where tertiary attainment depends on cognitive ability and socioeconomic disadvantage.
papers.dataDetail: U.K. data on cognitive ability, family background and education, 1960-2004.

papers.title: Benefit-based taxation can include substantial redistribution
papers.q: Can benefit-based taxation include substantial redistribution?
papers.summary: Argues that benefit-based taxation can include substantial redistribution, according to the title.

papers.title: Model averaging for time–varying vector autoregressions
papers.q: How can forecasts for multivariate time series with structural change be improved by time-varying model averaging?
papers.summary: The weights adapt over time in response to structural shifts. The paper establishes asymptotic optimality for the lowest possible quadratic forecast error and derives the convergence rate of the selected weights.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: time-varying model averaging of TV-VAR forecasts.
papers.contribution: Proposes time-varying model averaging of time-varying VARs with weights selected by a penalized local criterion.

papers.title: The effects of the secondary market for corporate loans on the real economy

authors.inst: Athens University of Economics and Business

papers.q: How does the secondary market for corporate loans affect the real economy?
papers.summary: Studies the effects of the secondary market for corporate loans on the real economy, according to the title.

papers.title: Building infrastructure and cohesion through locally embedded institutions: Evidence from a field experiment in War-torn Eastern Congo
papers.q: Can locally embedded institutions build infrastructure and cohesion in war-torn Eastern Congo?
papers.summary: Studies building infrastructure and cohesion through locally embedded institutions in a field experiment in Eastern Congo, according to the title.

papers.title: A design-based approach to spatial correlation

authors.inst: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.q: What standard errors should be reported with spatial data?
papers.summary: The paper compares Eicker-Huber-White, cluster-robust and spatial-correlation-robust standard errors under combinations of sampling scheme, assignment design and model specification, and derives the distribution of M-estimators.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: design-based finite population inference with spatial correlation.
papers.contribution: Within a finite population framework, identifies three channels of spatial correlation and proves a finite population CLT for weakly dependent random fields.

papers.title: When wages rise, quality falls: Minimum wages and the hidden trade-off in competitive e-commerce markets

authors.inst: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do minimum wage increases trade off against product quality in competitive e-commerce markets?
papers.summary: Studies minimum wages and a hidden trade-off with quality in competitive e-commerce markets, according to the title.

papers.title: Cognitive Limitations and Long-Term Care Use in the Netherlands: Evidence from the Lifelines Cohort Study
papers.q: How are cognitive limitations in older adults associated with long-term care use in the Netherlands?
papers.summary: Among those with cognitive impairments, 42% use no long-term care, while users have high expenditures especially in nursing homes. Cognitive impairment is associated with care use beyond functional limitations.
papers.contribution: Links the Lifelines Cohort Study to administrative records from Statistics Netherlands.
papers.ident: Descriptive: association of cognitive impairment with long-term care use in linked cohort and administrative data.
papers.dataDetail: Lifelines Cohort Study linked to Statistics Netherlands administrative records, ages 65+.

papers.title: Replaceable but Employed: Automation and the Meaning of Work
papers.q: Can automation harm workers who are kept employed by weakening the meaning they derive from their work?
papers.summary: The meaning loss raises compensation when wages adjust fully; with partial adjustment workers bear some of the loss, and it can make automation more likely. A developer may profit from publicly demonstrating a machine before licensing, creating a meaning externality that can make development socially harmful.
papers.contribution: Models workers who value both producing useful output and knowing it depends on their own contribution, and a credible machine alternative that weakens the second source.
papers.ident: Theory: model of work meaning, wages and automation development.

papers.title: Sharing the Burden: The Impacts of Pharmacy Sector Reforms on the Labor Market for Pharmacists in Portugal
papers.q: How did Portugal's pharmacy sector reforms affect wages and employment of pharmacists?
papers.summary: Value added per pharmacist fell by a third after the 2010 reimbursement reforms, and average pharmacist wages fell by a third between 2009 and 2022. Most of the reduction came from lower wages for newly entering cohorts under a two-tier pay system, with little change in employment growth.
papers.contribution: Uses linked matched employer-employee, collective bargaining and firm financial records to trace the incidence of a large shock to pharmacy margins.
papers.ident: Longitudinal analysis of pharmacist wages after reimbursement reforms, using linked firm and bargaining data.
papers.dataDetail: Quadros de Pessoal matched to collective bargaining settlements and firm financial records, 2009-2022.

papers.title: Two Selection Problems, One Bias Term: Experimental Sign-Up Is Treatment Choice in Disguise
papers.summary: Both biases share a Roy micro-foundation and inverse-Mills characterization. A calibration shows the bias can be large for a typical experiment, and natural field experiments or three alternative reporting practices are proposed as remedies.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: selection decomposition with a Roy model and calibration.
papers.q: Is selection into an experimental sample the same bias as selection into treatment?
papers.contribution: Shows that bias from non-random sample entry equals the sorting-on-gains term in the classic selection decomposition, with a Roy micro-foundation.

papers.title: The China Backlash: Quantifying the Narrative Discourse on China
papers.q: How has U.S. discourse on China changed over time and across public sources?
papers.summary: Net sentiment towards China in presidential sources has declined since the early 2000s, predating Trump's first term. Congressional, media, social media and think tank sources show persistently negative sentiment even in earlier decades.
papers.contribution: Builds two text-based measures, the frequency of China coverage and its net sentiment, from presidential, congressional, news, social media and think tank sources.
papers.ident: Descriptive: text-as-data measures of coverage and sentiment across sources.
papers.dataDetail: Corpus of presidential and congressional records, newspapers, social media and think tank reports.

papers.title: Chinese Sputnik Moments?
papers.summary: Chinese patenting is strongly associated with other measures of innovative progress and is not concentrated in giants such as Huawei. Universities play a larger role than state-owned enterprises, few critical patents involve inventors with U.S. experience, and text-based measures show rising patent quality.
papers.q: What does Chinese patenting in critical technologies reveal about the Chinese innovation ecosystem?
papers.contribution: Compiles a dataset of almost 14 million domestic Chinese patent publications and focuses on technologies the U.S. Department of Defense deems critical.
papers.ident: Descriptive: patent counts and text-based quality measures.
papers.dataDetail: Almost 14 million Chinese patent publications, with critical technology subset.

papers.title: Demand for Safety in the Crypto Ecosystem
papers.q: Do investors treat stablecoin deposits as safe and liquid assets comparable to Treasuries?
papers.summary: The stablecoin deposit premium co-moves with the Treasury premium, falls when Treasury supply rises, and drops when perceived safety deteriorates after depegs or hacks. Investors treat stablecoin deposits as money-like, borderless and permissionless instruments.
papers.ident: Theory and panel regressions of stablecoin deposit premia on Treasury premia and safety shocks.
papers.contribution: Models a representative investor allocating liquidity across stablecoin deposits and safe assets, and tests it with granular DeFi pool data.
papers.dataDetail: Hundreds of DeFi pools across multiple protocols, tokens and blockchains.

papers.title: Selecting Innovation Funding Mechanisms: A Framework for Policymakers
papers.q: How should policymakers choose among mechanisms for funding research and development?
papers.summary: Policymakers ask whether they can articulate the work, specify success and identify the most capable performers. The answers narrow the options among grants, contracts, prizes, advance market commitments and tax credits, allowing a more tractable choice based on innovation economics.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework built on three questions about the contracting environment that narrows the set of viable funding mechanisms.
papers.ident: Theory: conceptual framework for choosing among R&D funding mechanisms.

papers.title: Reserves and the Buyer of Last Resort

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How should central bank reserves and buyer-of-last-resort interventions be designed when secondary markets may freeze?
papers.summary: Reserves help intermediaries buy assets during stress but crowd out investment, and under laissez-faire intermediaries hold too few reserves because they overlook how aggregate liquidity reduces freeze risk. The welfare benefits of restoring market functioning exceed the fiscal costs.
papers.ident: Theory: model of reserves and market freezes with optimal intervention.
papers.contribution: Proposes a market-backstop principle combining state-contingent buyer-of-last-resort interventions with modest liquidity requirements.

papers.title: A Theory of Firm Wage Dynamics
papers.q: How do firm wages evolve with firm growth and the life cycle when workers search on the job?
papers.summary: Equilibrium wages and firm growth depend only on the distribution of marginal surplus. Wages are linked to growth but not size, decline over the life cycle, and show higher short-run than long-run pass-through of productivity shocks, with optimal policy subsidizing hiring at top-ladder firms.
papers.ident: Theory: wage-posting model with firm dynamics and equal-treatment constraint.
papers.contribution: Integrates the Burdett-Mortensen wage-posting model with firm dynamics and dynamic wage contracts under an equal-treatment constraint.

papers.title: Improving Financial Literacy: From Corporate Finance to Personal Finance
papers.summary: Financial literacy is low and has not improved over time in the United States or worldwide. It is linked to savvy financial behavior, and personal finance courses in school and college are useful for improving knowledge and downstream behavior.
papers.contribution: Reviews the measurement of financial literacy from the Big Three questions to a 28-question measure and the evidence on financial education.
papers.q: What does the literature say about financial literacy levels and the effectiveness of financial education?

papers.title: The United States and Its Creditors: Assessing Foreign Demand for U.S. Assets

authors.inst: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.q: How has foreign demand for U.S. assets, especially Treasuries, evolved?
papers.summary: Rising U.S. equity prices explain much of the deterioration in the net external position, while foreign purchases of Treasuries financed most of the current account deficit. The foreign official share of Treasuries has declined sharply while the private share, especially through financial centers, has risen.
papers.contribution: Documents compositional shifts in U.S. bilateral external positions and estimates creditor positions closer to a nationality-based concept.
papers.ident: Descriptive: decomposition of U.S. external positions by region, asset class and holder.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. bilateral external position and Treasury holdings data.

papers.title: Detecting Critical Junctures as They Unfold: Foundations, Measurement, and Applications from 120 Years of Reporting

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science
London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: Can critical junctures in institutional history be detected as they unfold?
papers.summary: Critical junctures are treated as moments of uncertainty about institutions, giving the classifier a theoretically motivated object. The approach is applied to historical junctures using 120 years of newspaper reporting.
papers.contribution: Develops a text classifier that detects moments of uncertainty about institutions in contemporaneous discourse and applies it to newspaper text.
papers.ident: Text classification of newspaper discourse to measure institutional uncertainty.
papers.dataDetail: 120 years of newspaper reporting.

papers.title: How do Households Respond to Expected Inflation? An Investigation of Transmission Mechanisms

authors.inst: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Through which channels do inflation expectations affect household spending?
papers.summary: Most households did not adjust spending plans, often because they saw inflation expectations as irrelevant or kept a fixed budget. Among adjusters, most cut spending because of wealth effects, and few increased spending via intertemporal substitution.
papers.contribution: Conducts surveys with hypothetical scenarios of an increase in inflation expectations to elicit spending responses and mechanisms.
papers.ident: Survey experiments with hypothetical scenarios of higher inflation expectations.
