papers.dataDetail: Household surveys with hypothetical inflation scenarios.

papers.title: Time Travel on Professional Profiles
papers.q: Do workers retroactively edit past jobs on professional profiles, and what does this imply for research using such data?
papers.summary: 19.7 percent of established U.S. LinkedIn users retroactively edit a job they have left, and such edits are closely tied to employer changes. Edits show sharp post-2022 increases in AI-related language and reductions in work-from-home and DEI language.
papers.contribution: Uses monthly vintages of Revelio Labs data from 2020-2026 to document retroactive edits to job titles and descriptions.
papers.ident: Descriptive: comparison of monthly vintages of professional profiles.
papers.dataDetail: Monthly vintages of Revelio Labs data, 2020-2026.

papers.title: Common Ownership and Collusion
papers.q: Does common ownership facilitate explicit collusion?
papers.summary: Higher firm-pair profit weights are associated with greater cartel participation, predict future involvement and are linked to longer duration, and firms reduce them after a cartel dissolves. The relationship is concentrated in pairs in which the internalizing firm colludes while the rival does not.
papers.contribution: Combines hand-collected ownership data with the universe of legal registered cartels in Sweden, avoiding selection of detected cartels.
papers.ident: Panel analysis of firm-pair profit weights and cartel formation, duration and dissolution.
papers.dataDetail: Hand-collected ownership data and the universe of registered cartels in Sweden.

papers.title: Wage spillovers across sectors: Evidence from a localized public-sector wage cut
papers.q: How do public-sector wage cuts spill over to private-sector wages?
papers.summary: A 1% public-sector wage cut reduces private-sector wages of young workers by 0.3%, with larger spillovers where public jobs matter more as outside options. Private-sector employment and profits expand in response.
papers.contribution: Leverages a Japanese reform that cut public-sector wages in certain municipalities and restricted public jobs to young workers.
papers.ident: Variation across municipalities in a Japanese public-sector wage cut, focusing on young workers eligible for public jobs.
papers.dataDetail: Japanese municipality-level wage, employment and firm data.

papers.title: Expert inflation preferences and the evaluation of monetary policy
papers.q: How do experts' inflation preferences shape their evaluation of monetary policy?
papers.summary: Studies expert inflation preferences and their role in evaluating monetary policy, according to the title.

papers.title: The impact of election fraud on government performance
papers.q: How does election fraud affect government performance?
papers.summary: Studies the impact of election fraud on government performance, according to the title.

papers.title: Labor Mobility and the Level of Unemployment in a Currency Union
papers.q: How does labor mobility affect the level of unemployment in a currency union?
papers.summary: Studies labor mobility and the level of unemployment in a currency union, according to the title.

papers.title: What drives the volatility of professional stock return forecasts? Causal evidence from macro shocks

authors.inst: NOVA School of Business and Economics
Vienna University of Economics and Business

papers.q: What drives the volatility of professional stock return forecasts, according to causal evidence from macro shocks?
papers.summary: Studies the drivers of the volatility of professional stock return forecasts using macro shocks, according to the title.

papers.title: Influencer Cartels
papers.q: Do influencer cartels inflate engagement and distort the advertising market?
papers.summary: Influencer cartels, in which groups collude to inflate engagement and advertising revenue, can improve consumer welfare if they expand engagement among the target audience. They reduce welfare if they divert engagement to less relevant audiences.
papers.contribution: Develops a model of influencer collusion over engagement and examines it empirically with novel datasets and machine learning tools.
papers.ident: Theory and empirical detection of collusive engagement using novel datasets and machine learning.
papers.dataDetail: Novel social media datasets on influencers.

papers.title: Organizational Capacity and Project Dynamics

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How do organizational capacity and opposing interests interact to shape project delivery?
papers.summary: Designers can avoid revisions by equalizing distributive benefits or inflating project scale to make delays prohibitively costly. Welfare is lowest when both capacity and the ability to revise are moderate.
papers.contribution: Develops a dynamic theory of project development in which higher capacity speeds progress but opponents may incur costly delays to revise payoffs.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic model of project development with revision and delay.

papers.title: Safe Spaces: Shelters or Tribes?
papers.q: Do safe spaces act as shelters or as tribes?
papers.summary: Asks whether safe spaces function as shelters or as tribes, according to the title.

papers.title: A Theory of Redistribution and Public Good Provision under Nondemocracy
papers.summary: In equilibrium citizens support the politician expected to win, not the one who promises the most, so redistribution and public good incentives differ from voting models. Citizens better able to coordinate receive more resources and transition to democracy is not voluntary.
papers.q: How do redistribution and public good provision work when politicians compete for power in a nondemocracy?
papers.contribution: Models two office-motivated politicians competing by promises where citizens' political activity is observable and can be retaliated against.
papers.ident: Theory: political contest with observable activity and retaliation.

papers.title: Exploitation vs. Exploration: How knowledge spillovers shape healthcare practices and innovation
papers.q: How do knowledge spillovers shape healthcare practices and innovation through exploitation and exploration?
papers.summary: Studies how knowledge spillovers shape healthcare practices and innovation, according to the title.

papers.title: How to Get Away with Merger: Stealth Consolidation and Its Effects on US Dialysis
papers.q: How does stealth consolidation affect the U.S. dialysis industry?
papers.summary: Studies the effects of stealth consolidation in U.S. dialysis, according to the title.

papers.title: The Economic Dynamics of City Structure: Evidence from Hiroshima's Recovery
papers.q: How resilient is internal city structure after a large shock, as shown by Hiroshima's recovery?
papers.summary: The city structure recovered within five years after the atomic bombing. Strong agglomeration forces in the estimated model explain the recovery, and an alternative equilibrium exists in which the city center did not recover.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic quantitative spatial model estimated on digitized post-bombing city data.
papers.contribution: Builds a dynamic quantitative model of internal city structure with commuting, forward-looking location choices, migration frictions and agglomeration, using newly digitized data on Hiroshima.
papers.dataDetail: Newly digitized data on Hiroshima before and after the bombing.

papers.title: From Heterogeneous Firms to Heterogeneous Trade Elasticities: The Aggregate Implications of Firm Export Decisions
papers.q: How do firm export decisions generate heterogeneous aggregate trade elasticities?
papers.summary: Studies how heterogeneous firms' export decisions determine heterogeneous aggregate trade elasticities, according to the title.

papers.title: Additionality and Asymmetric Information in Environmental Markets: Evidence from Conservation Auctions
papers.q: How does additionality interact with asymmetric information in conservation auctions?
papers.summary: Three-quarters of marginal auction winners are not additional, and heterogeneity in counterfactual land use creates adverse selection. Scoring rules that incorporate expected land use impacts increase efficiency.
papers.ident: Structural: model of bidding and additionality estimated with satellite-derived counterfactual land use.
papers.contribution: Links Conservation Reserve Program bids to satellite-derived land use and develops a model of bidding and additionality.
papers.dataDetail: Conservation Reserve Program auction bids linked to satellite-derived land use.

papers.title: Remote Work and City Structure
papers.summary: Temporary reductions in commuters, as in the pandemic, can leave persistently large fractions of remote workers. Commuting in the largest cities has stabilized at 60 percent of pre-pandemic levels, while smaller cities are fully back, and cities with permanently low commuting lose 2.3 percent in welfare.
papers.q: How can remote work create multiple equilibria in city commuting and welfare?
papers.contribution: Models a coordination mechanism between valuable in-office interactions and commuting costs, and tests implications with cell phone mobility data.
papers.ident: Theory: coordination model with multiple equilibria, with cell phone mobility data.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. cell phone-based mobility data on commuting trips.

papers.title: Training and Job-to-Job Mobility with Transfer Fees
papers.q: Would transfer fees like those in professional soccer improve training and job-to-job mobility in the labor market?
papers.summary: Unlike non-compete clauses, transfer fees encourage training while preserving efficient mobility toward more productive firms, bringing the economy closer to the optimum. Simulations suggest a time-limited compensation mechanism would significantly increase employment.
papers.contribution: Develops a toy model and a life-cycle model with job creation and destruction, on-the-job search and training, estimated with the French Labor Force Survey.
papers.ident: Structural: life-cycle search model with training, estimated with the French Labor Force Survey.
papers.dataDetail: French Labor Force Survey.

papers.title: Tax and Occupancy of Business Properties: Evidence from UK Business Rate Reliefs
papers.q: How do UK business rate reliefs affect commercial vacancies and rents?
papers.summary: Both reliefs reduce vacancies. A given relief reduces vacancies more for eligible properties when given via retail relief, since small business relief targets only small businesses, and effects differ by urban clustering and local deprivation.
papers.contribution: Uses new data and exogenous variation in small business relief and retail relief.
papers.ident: Exogenous variation in eligibility for small business relief and retail relief.
papers.dataDetail: UK commercial property vacancy, rent and relief data.

papers.title: Perils of the Paperwork: The Impact of Information and Application Assistance on Social Benefit Take-Up in India
papers.q: Do information and application assistance raise take-up of a cash transfer for poor women in Delhi?
papers.summary: Information alone raised applications only among the literate, while basic and intensive assistance raised average application rates by 41 and 70 percent and expanded access among more vulnerable women.
papers.ident: Randomized experiment with eligible women varying information and application assistance.
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized experiment with eligible women comparing information alone with basic and intensive application assistance.
papers.conclusion: Application ordeals can limit take-up by those with high need.
papers.dataDetail: Eligible women in Delhi for an unconditional cash transfer program.

papers.title: Female Leaders and Intrahousehold Dynamics: Evidence from State Elections in India
papers.q: Does women's political representation improve reproductive health but raise intimate partner violence in India?
papers.summary: Greater representation raises public provision of reproductive health services in rural areas, increasing modern contraception and birth spacing. Intimate partner violence also increases, especially among women whose husbands prefer additional sons.
papers.contribution: Studies the effect of women's representation in state elections on health care provision, contraception and spousal abuse.
papers.ident: Close-election comparison of states with and without female leaders.
papers.dataDetail: Indian state election results linked to household health surveys.

papers.title: The Value of School Social Climate Information: Evidence from Chicago Housing Transactions
papers.summary: Disclosure raises prices of homes assigned to schools with better climate ratings, with suggestive sorting of higher-income families. A second, less publicized disclosure produced weaker capitalization but significant responses among higher-income households.
papers.ident: Border discontinuities, event studies and DiD around disclosure of Chicago school climate ratings.
papers.q: How is school social climate information capitalized into housing prices and sorting in Chicago?
papers.contribution: Exploits a shock of public disclosure of school climate ratings using border discontinuities, event studies and difference-in-differences.
papers.dataDetail: Chicago housing transactions and school climate ratings.

papers.title: Alcohol, Labor, and Agriculture
papers.summary: At 16 months the program cut positive breathalyzer tests among men by 14 percentage points and heavy drinking by 19 points, and raised household real annual harvest values by 32 percent. Mechanisms include expenditure reallocation, self-control and peer information sharing.
papers.contribution: Evaluates a randomized trial in which households received cognitive behavioral therapy and medication.
papers.q: Does reducing alcohol abuse raise labor and agricultural outcomes in rural Kenya?
papers.ident: Randomized controlled trial of cognitive behavioral therapy and medication against alcohol abuse.
papers.dataDetail: Rural Kenyan households, followed up 16 months after the intervention.

papers.title: Public debt in calibrated OLG models: Fiscal arithmetic versus welfare analysis
papers.q: How large should public debt be in calibrated OLG models when borrowing costs are below growth?
papers.summary: Welfare-maximizing debt is considerably lower than deficit-maximizing debt in the baseline calibrated to the U.S. economy. A decomposition shows the strongest forces are the positive risk-sharing effect and negative crowding-out effect, with pension policy and risk premia as key drivers.
papers.ident: Structural: calibrated stochastic OLG model with welfare decomposition.
papers.contribution: Analyzes fiscal and welfare implications of debt in stochastic OLG models with distortionary taxation and a debt-sensitive borrowing rate.

papers.title: The Option Value of Municipal Liquidity

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.summary: The facility eased liquidity pressures and reduced perceived credit risk for municipal borrowers, with low-rated issuers seeing yield reductions of at least 26 basis points. There is suggestive evidence that these effects translated into employment gains.
papers.contribution: Uses a regression discontinuity design on MLF lending eligibility population cutoffs.
papers.q: Did the Municipal Liquidity Facility ease liquidity pressures and credit risk for municipal borrowers?
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity at the population cutoffs for Municipal Liquidity Facility eligibility.
papers.dataDetail: Municipal bond yields and employment around the April 2020 MLF eligibility cutoffs.

papers.title: Instrumental variable regression with varying-intensity repeated treatments
papers.q: How can instrumental variable regression handle repeated treatments of varying intensity?
papers.summary: Studies instrumental variable regression with varying-intensity repeated treatments, according to the title.

papers.title: Green spills: Peer effects in pro-environmental behaviors

authors.inst: Vienna University of Economics and Business

papers.q: Do households' pro-environmental behaviors spill over to their neighbors?
papers.summary: Each additional solar PV installation within 100 meters reduces a household's annual electricity consumption by 0.2%. Peer installations also raise uptake of solar PV and electric vehicles, with effects that vary by household constraints.
papers.ident: Instrumental variables on geocoded panel data of peer solar PV installations.
papers.contribution: Estimates causal peer effects using geocoded panel data on 260,000 Swiss households and instrumental variables.
papers.dataDetail: Geocoded panel data on 260,000 Swiss households, 2008-2019.

papers.title: Information manipulation and repression: Theory and evidence from the COVID-19 response in Russia

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.q: How does information manipulation support repression in Russia's COVID-19 response?
papers.summary: Develops theory and evidence on information manipulation and repression in Russia's COVID-19 response, according to the title.

papers.title: Hurricanes, Climate Change Policies, and Electoral Accountability
papers.q: Do hurricanes lead legislators to support climate change legislation, and does electoral safety matter?
papers.summary: Representatives from hurricane-hit districts are more inclined to support climate legislation, but only those in safe seats change their agenda toward policies with short-term costs and long-term gains.
papers.contribution: Uses data on all federal disaster declarations from 1989 to 2020 to link hurricane exposure of districts to legislators' environmental voting.
papers.ident: Panel comparison of legislators from hurricane-affected and unaffected districts, by seat safety.
papers.dataDetail: Federal disaster declarations 1989-2020 and congressional votes on environmental bills.

papers.title: The Welfare Effects of Eligibility Expansions: Theory and Evidence from SNAP
papers.q: Would expanding SNAP eligibility raise welfare given that it also raises take-up among those already eligible?
papers.summary: Expanding eligibility raises take-up among previously eligible households, and information frictions rather than stigma drive this effect. Under the model's assumptions, expanding SNAP eligibility would raise social welfare.
papers.ident: Event study of SNAP eligibility expansions, with an online experiment and a welfare model.
papers.contribution: Documents a woodwork effect with an event study, tests mechanisms with an online experiment and survey, and builds a model of welfare programs with incomplete take-up.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative SNAP take-up data, an online experiment and an administrative survey.

papers.title: Collective Bargaining Rights, Policing, and Civilian Deaths
papers.q: Did collective bargaining rights for police unions increase civilian deaths?
papers.summary: Bargaining rights significantly increase civilians killed by police, particularly non-White civilians, with limited effects on officer safety. They explain 14 percent of non-White civilian deaths by legal intervention between 1959 and 1988.
papers.ident: Event study around staggered state adoption of police duty-to-bargain laws.
papers.contribution: Applies an event-study design to states' introduction of duty-to-bargain requirements for police unions.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. state-level deaths by legal intervention, 1959-1988.

papers.title: Rainfall Inequality, Political Power, and Ethnic Conflict in Africa
papers.q: Does rainfall-based inequality between ethnic groups predict ethnic violence in Africa?
papers.summary: Rainfall-based inequality is a strong predictor of ethnic violence, and the link depends heavily on power relations across groups. Resource inequality appears to lead to conflict by exacerbating grievances.
papers.contribution: Constructs a measure of resource inequality between ethnic groups using growing-season rainfall in ethnic homelands.
papers.ident: Panel analysis of rainfall-based inequality between ethnic homelands and ethnic violence.
papers.dataDetail: 250 ethnicities in 43 African countries, 1950-2020.

papers.title: Dissecting the Phillips curve: Evidence from cross-sectional heterogeneity and regime-dependent nonlinearity
papers.q: Is the Phillips curve heterogeneous across U.S. states and nonlinear across regimes?
papers.summary: Two groups of U.S. states emerge, one with a steep and significant Phillips curve and another with a flat and insignificant one. Heterogeneity persists across regimes, nonlinearity emerges in recessions, and much of the flattening is region-specific.
papers.ident: Group-based panel estimation of regional Phillips curves with regime-dependent nonlinearity.
papers.contribution: Develops a group-based approach that accounts for unobserved heterogeneity in the regional Phillips curve.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. state-level inflation and unemployment panel.

papers.title: Collusion by Exclusion in Public Procurement
papers.q: How can bidder preselection in procurement auctions help cartels exclude rivals?
papers.summary: Preselection allows cartels to exclude competitive rivals and thereby raise procurement costs above what is possible without it. The marker identifies bidders suspected of collusion.
papers.ident: Theory and a collusion marker derived from the optimal cartel strategy.
papers.contribution: Models partial bid-rigging cartels in two-stage auctions and builds a collusion marker applied to Slovak procurement data.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative data on Slovak public procurement auctions.

papers.title: The Economics of Discriminatory Job Reservations
papers.summary: Optimal discrimination endogenously creates good and bad jobs and assigns workers of different groups to them. Relative labor scarcity determines whether discrimination or free markets are optimal, and the model is applied to apartheid South Africa.
papers.q: Why would a dominant group reserve certain jobs and what does this imply for wages and discrimination?
papers.contribution: Models a dominant group choosing which jobs to reserve, and with them the size of the reserved set and the elasticity of substitution between reserved and unreserved jobs.
papers.ident: Theory: model of optimal job reservation by a dominant group.

papers.title: Rational Misspecification: Framework and Applications
papers.q: Would misspecified decision-makers pay for information that could make them less misspecified?
papers.summary: The bound depends on the information currently available to the decision-maker. It is applied to coarse expectations, causal misperceptions and sampling equilibria.
papers.contribution: Proposes a prior-free approach based on constrained maximal regret to bound subjective gains from acquiring a more accurate model.
papers.ident: Theory: constrained maximal regret framework applied to three models of misspecified beliefs.

papers.title: Sequential Protest Formation

authors.inst: Escola de Economia de São Paulo

papers.summary: A unique equilibrium exists and its dynamics are characterized. When it involves participation, the time between decisions shortens as the protest progresses, and a player becomes sequentially pivotal if the protest will likely end before another opportunity arrives.
papers.q: How do protests form when opportunities to participate arrive sequentially?
papers.contribution: Proposes a sequential model of protest formation in which participation opportunities arrive stochastically and the protest succeeds above a threshold.
papers.ident: Theory: sequential threshold participation game.

papers.title: Higher-Order Beliefs and (Mis)learning from Prices
papers.q: How do misperceptions of signal correlation distort behavior in a Cournot duopoly with learning from prices?
papers.summary: Exaggerating signal correlation is beneficial when agents hold flexible beliefs about price elasticity and harmful when beliefs are dogmatically correct. Because the direct and indirect effects through elasticity misinference are opposite, inference can reverse an error's viability.
papers.contribution: Studies misperceived correlation of private demand signals in an incomplete-information Cournot game.
papers.ident: Theory: incomplete-information Cournot game with misperceived signal correlation.

papers.title: Data Linkages and Privacy Regulation
papers.q: Does privacy regulation help consumers who care about privacy when firms link data?
papers.summary: A data linkage benefits the consumer when the recipient firm is sufficiently similar to the collecting firm. Voluntary consent requirements benefit consumers in equilibrium, while blanket bans on discriminatory price and quality offers harm them.
papers.ident: Theory: model of data linkages under alternative privacy regulations.
papers.contribution: Models sequential interaction with a data-collecting firm and a firm that uses the data to set quality and price, and endogenizes linkage under several regulations.

papers.title: Regression adjustment in completely randomized experiments with many covariates

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How should average treatment effects be estimated and tested in randomized experiments with many covariates?
papers.summary: In Neyman's design-based framework with covariates growing more slowly than the sample size, the paper derives first- and second-order terms of the stochastic expansions and analyzes the higher-order behavior of existing inference procedures. The methods extend to stratified experiments.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: design-based regression adjustment with many covariates.
papers.contribution: Shows that a cross-fitted regression adjustment estimator has more favorable asymptotics than Lin's and the bias-corrected estimator, and introduces a modified HC3 standard error.

papers.title: Failures of Contingent Reasoning in Annuitization Decisions

authors.inst: NOVA School of Business and Economics

papers.q: Why do people under-annuitize, and does failure of contingent reasoning explain it?
papers.summary: Annuitization was payoff-maximizing at all prices, yet take-up was incomplete and price elastic, and reframing as insurance against a bad outcome did not help. Participants underappreciated how annuitizing reduces the need for less efficient saving, and making that interaction salient or removing the need to consider it raised take-up.
papers.ident: Incentivized online experiment varying framing, salience and price of annuities.
papers.contribution: Runs an incentivized experiment on a probability-based sample of 3,038 participants testing framings of annuity choice.
papers.dataDetail: Probability-based sample of 3,038 participants.

papers.title: The costs of environmental land use regulation
papers.q: What are the costs of environmental land use regulation?
papers.summary: Studies the costs of environmental land use regulation, according to the title.

papers.title: Product Liability Litigation and Innovation: Evidence from Medical Devices
papers.q: Does product liability litigation reduce innovation in medical devices?
papers.summary: Defendant firms, and other firms to a lesser extent, reduce new product introductions in litigated categories during litigation years. The decline is temporary, does not spill beyond litigated categories, and litigation induces safer devices.
papers.conclusion: The potential welfare loss from litigation appears relatively contained.
papers.contribution: Studies new product introductions by leading medical device firms around litigation and links safety regulation to the likelihood of litigation.
papers.ident: Panel analysis of product introductions by category and year around litigation.
papers.dataDetail: Medical device firms' product introductions and product liability litigation.

papers.title: Exploiting Rivals' Strengths
papers.q: Can a dominant firm gain more by exploiting rivals through share contracts than by foreclosing them?
papers.summary: A dominant firm can require buyers to source at least a given share, below 100 percent, of their needs from it. By designing such contracts optimally it can earn as much as if it acquired its rivals' capabilities at no cost.
papers.contribution: Analyzes oligopoly where firms use contracts contingent on buyers' purchases from rivals and presents a new exploitation mechanism.
papers.ident: Theory: oligopoly with contracts contingent on purchases from rivals.

papers.title: Different no more: Country spreads in advanced and emerging economies
papers.q: Have country spreads in advanced economies become like those in emerging economies?
papers.summary: Since 2008 advanced economies have shown persistently higher and more volatile spreads, more macro volatility and stronger co-movement with emerging markets. Higher spreads reflect greater indebtedness and lower debt tolerance, while volatility and co-movement come from stronger global shocks.
papers.contribution: Documents six facts about spreads and macro volatility in advanced and emerging economies and interprets them with a small open economy model.
papers.ident: Descriptive facts interpreted through a calibrated small open economy model.
papers.dataDetail: Sovereign spreads and macro aggregates for advanced and emerging economies since 2008.

papers.title: Agency incentives and disparate revenue collection: Evidence from Chicago parking tickets

authors.inst: United States Securities and Exchange Commission

papers.q: Do agency incentives produce disparate revenue collection in Chicago parking tickets?
papers.summary: Studies agency incentives and disparate revenue collection using Chicago parking tickets, according to the title.

papers.title: Capital Services in Global Value Chains
papers.summary: Two network properties deliver larger long-run consumption gains from globalization than existing estimates, and larger gains in more capital-intensive countries. Trade-exposed sectors supply capital to consumption-influential producers, and reallocation toward producers with larger drops in capital rental prices raises capital incomes and lowers consumption price indices.
papers.q: How do capital services in global value chains change the gains from globalization?
papers.contribution: Constructs the first global dataset on intersectoral capital service expenditures and builds a dynamic multisector trade model with a capital-augmented input-output matrix.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic multisector trade model calibrated to a global capital-augmented input-output matrix.
papers.dataDetail: New global dataset of intersectoral capital service expenditures.

papers.title: The political benefits of the monoculture: Estimating the electoral effect of the market facilitation program
papers.q: Did the Market Facilitation Program deliver electoral benefits through monoculture farming?
papers.summary: Estimates the electoral effect of the Market Facilitation Program, according to the title.

papers.title: Retail Betting Markets
papers.q: What drives the rapid expansion and convergence of retail betting markets?
papers.summary: Technological innovation, behavioral biases and regulatory arbitrage have shaped the recent evolution of these markets. The review highlights considerations for policymakers and outlines directions for research.
papers.contribution: Reviews market design, economic utility and shared behavioral drivers of sports betting, prediction markets and retail options trading.

papers.title: Macro Shocks and Firm Dynamics with Oligopolistic Financial Intermediaries
papers.summary: Banks exert greater market power over productive and more financially constrained firms, which dampens capital accumulation and amplifies macro shocks. In crises banks extract higher markups, and when a large bank fails the others restrict credit, worsening and prolonging the downturn.
papers.q: How does bank market power shape macro shocks and firm dynamics?
papers.contribution: Develops a macro model with oligopolistic financial intermediaries and heterogeneous firms in which banks charge firm-specific markups.
papers.ident: Structural: macro model with oligopolistic banks and heterogeneous firms.

papers.title: Profits and Social Impacts: Complements vs. Tradeoffs for Lenders in Three Countries
papers.q: Do profits and social impact trade off for lenders using machine learning targeting?
papers.summary: Two of the three lenders could have raised average loan profit margins by 7-9 percentage points through machine learning-based targeting. Such targeting runs against credit access goals for disadvantaged groups.
papers.contribution: Estimates tradeoffs using randomized microcredit approvals from lenders in South Africa, the Philippines and Bosnia.
papers.ident: Randomized microcredit approvals with machine learning targeting counterfactuals.
papers.dataDetail: Randomized microcredit approvals from lenders in South Africa, the Philippines and Bosnia.

papers.title: Spillover Effects in Complementary Markets: A Study of the Indian Cell Phone and Wireless Service Markets
papers.q: How do spillovers between cell phone and wireless service markets shape product variety and entry?
papers.summary: Banning budget Chinese phones slows 4G deployment by about five quarters and lowers consumer welfare without raising domestic firms' profits. An unrestricted subsidy outperforms a domestic-only subsidy in coverage, welfare and domestic profits.
papers.ident: Structural: demand, pricing and network expansion model with counterfactual simulations.
papers.contribution: Estimates a structural model of demand, pricing, network expansion and phone product choice during India's 4G rollout.
papers.dataDetail: Indian cell phone and wireless service market data during the 4G rollout.

papers.title: Information and Macroeconomic Expectations: Global Evidence

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.summary: Most consumers rely on local sources such as utility bills, shopping and acquaintances, which produce biased macroeconomic expectations. Distrust in governments and central banks helps explain reliance on local sources, and demographic gaps in bias mostly reflect sorting into information sources rather than different processing.
papers.contribution: Uses global survey data on 47,000 consumers in 47 countries representing 90% of world GDP.
papers.q: How do consumers around the world form macroeconomic expectations from information sources?
papers.ident: Cross-country survey analysis of information sources and expectation biases.
papers.dataDetail: 47,000 consumers across 47 countries.

papers.title: The Welfare Effects of Conditioning the Potential Duration of UI Benefits on Prior Work History
papers.q: Is it welfare-improving to condition unemployment insurance duration on prior work history?
papers.summary: An additional week of benefits lengthens unemployment by 0.30 weeks and costs the government $96 on average. Mechanical costs fall steeply with prior hours while behavioral costs rise modestly, so the fiscal externality of extending UI rises with labor market attachment.
papers.ident: 25 regression discontinuities at work-history thresholds for potential benefit duration.
papers.contribution: Uses 25 regression discontinuities in Canada's UI system and administrative records on the universe of claims from 1997 to 2018.
papers.dataDetail: Universe of Canadian UI claims, 1997-2018.

papers.title: Early Life Healthcare Access and Later-life Mortality: Evidence Using Openings of County Health Departments
papers.q: Did early-life exposure to county health departments raise later-life longevity?
papers.summary: Exposure to a county health department opening during fetal development and early years is associated with a 1-4 month increase in longevity. Effects are more concentrated among non-white individuals and those with lower-educated parents.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences by age of exposure relative to county health department opening.
papers.contribution: Links Social Security Administration death records to the 1940 census and compares exposure by age to the county's year of health department opening.
papers.dataDetail: SSA death records linked to the 1940 census.

papers.title: Elite Capture, Meritocracy and Social Stability: Evidence from the Chinese Imperial Examinations
papers.q: Did anonymizing Imperial Examinations in Song China strengthen meritocracy and stability?
papers.summary: The reforms anonymized submissions and ended local officials' discretion to recommend candidates. They increased the share of successful commoners, narrowed performance gaps with elites and reduced social unrest in treated prefectures.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing prefectures with and without prominent elite families around Northern Song exam reforms.
papers.contribution: Applies a difference-in-differences to Northern Song exam reforms across prefectures with and without prominent elite families, using data from 960-1127.
papers.dataDetail: Prefecture-level data on exam candidates and unrest, 960-1127.

papers.title: Beliefs That Predict Returns and Beliefs That Attract Flows: Policy Insights and Sentiment Catering in Mutual Funds
papers.summary: Policy beliefs, not macro beliefs, predict subsequent market returns and help explain fund alphas. Residual sentiment shapes equity allocations and attracts flows without predicting returns, and funds strategically position stated beliefs to cater to investors.
papers.ident: Text-based belief decomposition with an instrument from maturing wealth management products for fund flows.
papers.contribution: Decomposes beliefs in Chinese mutual funds' Outlook reports into macro fundamentals, government policy and residual sentiment, and instruments flows with maturing wealth management products.
papers.q: Do mutual fund managers' policy beliefs predict returns while their sentiment attracts flows?
papers.dataDetail: Mandatory Outlook reports of Chinese mutual funds.

papers.title: Equity as Tribute: The Market for Passive State Equity
papers.summary: Owners' consent reveals nothing about whether they benefit because sellers capitalize the policy improvement into the price, so purchases occur at a discount. A government with bargaining power can pay zero for an exposed firm, and one that can raise exposure drives the price to its legal floor, so equity becomes tribute.
papers.conclusion: Prohibition is nonetheless dominated because a passive stake corrects political underweighting of shareholders.
papers.q: Does a government's passive equity stake in a regulated firm signal that the stake benefits owners?
papers.contribution: Models the price of a passive state stake and the firm's policy exposure as jointly determined in equilibrium.
papers.ident: Theory: equilibrium pricing of passive state equity with endogenous policy exposure.

papers.title: Temperature Fluctuations and Economic Conditions: Evidence from Weekly U.S. Data
papers.q: How do temperature fluctuations affect weekly U.S. state economic conditions?
papers.summary: A temperature shock modestly raises economic conditions in the short run and then lowers them persistently in the medium run, more so at higher base temperatures. The labor market is the primary channel.
papers.ident: Panel local projections of weekly state economic conditions on temperature shocks, with a search and matching model.
papers.contribution: Estimates a panel local projection with high-frequency weekly data from 1987 to 2024 and builds a weekly search and matching model with a heat damage stock and slow adaptation.
papers.dataDetail: Weekly U.S. state-level economic conditions and temperature, 1987-2024.

papers.title: Global Pension Asset Allocations and Debt Markets
papers.q: How have pension fund asset allocations around the world shifted away from fixed income?
papers.summary: Pension investors have moved away from fixed income in both defined contribution and defined benefit programs, and into riskier mutual fund holdings and alternative investments. Declining government bond yields are associated with lower bond portfolio shares.
papers.contribution: Documents the evolution of global pension asset allocations and links shifts to declining local currency government bond yields.
papers.ident: Descriptive and panel evidence relating pension portfolio shares to government bond yields.
papers.dataDetail: Global sample of pension fund asset allocations.

papers.title: Investing in Mothers? The Long-Run Impact of a Universal Child Care Program on Maternal Work and Income
papers.q: What are the long-run effects of Quebec's universal child care on mothers' work and income?
papers.summary: There is an enduring positive impact on mothers' employment long after children age out of preschool. The earnings effect grows to twice the participation effect through rising intensity of work and higher hourly wages, with occupational upgrading and within-occupation growth.
papers.contribution: Documents the life-cycle impact of the program on maternal employment, earnings, benefit receipt and tax remittances.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing mothers in Quebec with other provinces after the child care program rollout.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian tax and administrative data on mothers.

papers.title: Industry Distress Anomaly

authors.inst: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Do more distressed industries earn lower expected equity returns?
papers.summary: The anomaly remains significant after controlling for firm-level distress and disappears in placebo industries formed by reshuffling firms. Industries with greater idiosyncratic left-tail risk are more distressed but have weaker feedback and lower exposure to discount-rate shocks.
papers.contribution: Documents an industry-level distress anomaly and shows with theory and evidence that competition-distress feedback amplifies exposure to discount-rate shocks.
papers.ident: Portfolio sorts and regressions with placebo industries, and a theoretical model of competition-distress feedback.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. firm and industry equity return data.

papers.title: Managerial Coordination in Decentralized Markets
papers.q: Why do some buyers contract directly with producers while others use an intermediary that coordinates assignments?
papers.summary: The trade-off determines which buyers use an intermediary. Producers working through intermediaries earn lower, less variable pay but have greater job security, and intermediaries expand trade while shifting its gains from producers to buyers.
papers.contribution: Develops a repeated-game model in which intermediaries aggregate fluctuating demand and lengthen productive relationships at the cost of double marginalization.
papers.ident: Theory: repeated-game model of intermediated contracting.

papers.title: Do ultra-poor graduation programs build women’s resilience to weather shocks? Evidence from rural Ethiopia
papers.q: Do ultra-poor graduation programs protect women from weather shocks in rural Ethiopia?
papers.summary: Women exposed to dryness shocks face worse nutrition, lower household food security and assets, and higher risk of intimate partner violence. The graduation program fully buffers the violence increase and partially buffers other effects, likely through improved savings.
papers.ident: Cluster-randomized trial data interacted with community-level dryness shocks.
papers.contribution: Matches panel data from a large cluster-randomized trial with detailed weather records to identify community-level exposure to dryness shocks.
papers.dataDetail: Panel from a cluster-randomized trial of a graduation program on Ethiopia's PSNP, matched with weather records.

papers.title: Difference-in-differences with interference

authors.inst: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.summary: The approach allows spatially correlated assignments and relaxes restrictions such as immediate-neighborhood interference and correctly specified spillover functions. It adopts a finite-population conditional perspective.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: doubly robust DiD estimators with neighborhood interference.
papers.contribution: Shows canonical DiD fails to identify interesting effects under neighborhood interference and proposes doubly robust estimators for the direct effect on the treated under a modified parallel trends assumption.
papers.q: How should difference-in-differences handle interference among neighboring units?

papers.title: Unconventional policy and idiosyncratic risk

authors.inst: Libera Università Internazionale degli Studi Sociali Guido Carli

papers.summary: Optimal policy features a division of labor in which balance-sheet policy targets cross-sectional objectives such as private debt, while interest-rate policy stabilizes aggregates. The optimal response to a deleveraging crisis then involves a shorter, not longer, duration of zero interest rates.
papers.ident: Theory: heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian model with credit frictions and optimal policy.
papers.q: How should conventional and balance-sheet monetary policy be divided when households face idiosyncratic risk?
papers.contribution: Shows in a New Keynesian model with heterogeneous households and credit frictions that idiosyncratic uncertainty adds a consumption-risk channel amplifying balance-sheet policy.

papers.title: Effective tax rates, firm size and the global minimum tax
papers.q: What is the revenue potential of corporate minimum taxes given effective tax rates across firm sizes?
papers.summary: Documents facts on effective corporate tax rates and the revenue potential of minimum taxes, leveraging firm-level tax returns from 16 countries.
papers.contribution: Documents new facts on corporate taxation using firm-level tax returns from 16 countries.
papers.ident: Descriptive analysis of firm-level tax returns across 16 countries.
papers.dataDetail: Firm-level tax returns from 16 countries.

papers.title: Mental Models of the Stock Market
papers.q: What mental models do investors and experts use to forecast and explain stock returns?
papers.summary: Investors strongly disagree in forecasts and reasoning. Most academics view markets as efficient while most households equate higher expected earnings with higher expected returns, and professionals split among efficiency, mispricing and expected earnings reasoning.
papers.ident: Survey experiments with scenarios of stale earnings news.
papers.contribution: Surveys the general population, retail investors, financial professionals and academic experts using scenarios with stale news about future earnings.
papers.dataDetail: Surveys of households, retail investors, financial professionals and academic experts.

papers.title: Women’s labor subsidy: Evidence from Chile
papers.q: How does a women's labor subsidy affect employment in Chile?
papers.summary: Studies a women's labor subsidy in Chile, according to the title.

papers.title: Estimation and inference on average treatment effect in percentage points under heterogeneity
papers.q: How should average treatment effects in percentage points be estimated from log outcomes under heterogeneity?
papers.summary: The problem is particularly relevant for difference-in-differences with log outcomes and staggered adoption. The estimand is a lower bound on the percentage-point ATE for the target population and coincides with it absent within-group heterogeneity.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: estimation and inference for a percentage-point ATE lower bound.
papers.contribution: Highlights the Jensen's inequality bias of the semi-log approximation under heterogeneity and proposes new estimation and inference methods for an estimand that bounds the percentage-point ATE.

papers.title: Do social movements influence decision makers? Evidence from U.S. immigration courts
papers.q: Do protests influence decisions in U.S. immigration courts?
papers.summary: There is some evidence of a small, temporary influence, with removal probability falling by about 2 percentage points for up to three weeks after the protests began. There is little evidence of medium or long-term effects, and effects vary by case, location and judge characteristics.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing removal outcomes around the onset of the 2006 protests across locations.
papers.contribution: Applies a difference-in-differences design to administrative court data around the 2006 immigration reform protests.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative immigration court removal proceedings data.

papers.title: Is inflation relief passed-through? Evidence from excise taxes
papers.q: Are inflation relief measures passed through to consumers through excise taxes?
papers.summary: Studies the pass-through of inflation relief using excise taxes, according to the title.

papers.title: The Bronx Is Burning: Urban Disinvestment Effects of Fair Access to Insurance Requirements Plans
papers.q: Did FAIR plans meant to end insurance redlining cause urban disinvestment?
papers.summary: FAIR plans in 26 states prohibited considering environmental hazards, forced insurer pooling and paid out above market values in declining areas. They inadvertently led to significant housing disinvestment and faster neighborhood population decline, with rising Black population shares.
papers.ident: Triple-difference across time, neighborhoods with likely FAIR access and participating states.
papers.contribution: Uses a triple-difference design comparing pre and post FAIR periods, neighborhoods with and without likely access, and participating and non-participating states.
papers.dataDetail: Neighborhood-level housing and population data around the 1960s FAIR plans.

papers.title: Fiscal Policy in Small Open Economies: The International Intertemporal Keynesian Cross
papers.summary: The initial debt-fueled rise in consumption is offset by a later drop to repay foreign debt. The paper also provides conditions that overturn the result.
papers.contribution: Derives conditions under which the cumulative fiscal multiplier is exactly one and deficits are not self-financing in a small open economy.
papers.q: Is fiscal policy as effective in small open economies as in closed economies with realistic MPCs?
papers.ident: Theory: intertemporal Keynesian cross in a small open economy.

papers.title: Excessive Pharmaceutical Marketing Expenditure: Policy Remedies from China

authors.inst: Dongbei University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: Can centralized drug procurement curb excessive pharmaceutical marketing spending in China?
papers.summary: Winning firms gain large market shares without high marketing costs. The auctions significantly reduce sales costs and prices, with winning firms showing notable decreases in marketing-related labor demand.
papers.contribution: Uses a policy experiment in which certain generics are procured through centralized auctions in pilot cities.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing pilot cities with centralized procurement auctions to others.
papers.dataDetail: Chinese pharmaceutical firm sales, prices and labor demand data.

papers.title: Property rights and market frictions: Evidence from the universe of land dispute files in China
papers.q: How do property rights and market frictions interact in China's land disputes?
papers.summary: Studies property rights and market frictions using the universe of land dispute files in China, according to the title.
papers.dataDetail: Universe of land dispute files in China.

papers.title: Do Health Insurers Matter for Health Outcomes? Evidence from a Large Natural Experiment in Colombia
papers.summary: The termination decreased the breadth of incumbent insurers' provider networks by 10% and raised mortality by 20%. Congestion from the surge of enrollees and narrower networks that excluded higher-quality providers serving sicker patients drove the change.
papers.q: Do health insurers matter for health outcomes?
papers.contribution: Leverages the abrupt termination of Colombia's largest insurer to study spillovers on patients enrolled with other insurers.
papers.ident: Natural experiment from the abrupt termination of Colombia's largest health insurer.
papers.dataDetail: Colombian insurer provider network, enrollment and mortality data.

papers.title: Was Javert Right to Be Suspicious? Marginal Treatment Effects with Duration Outcomes

authors.inst: Escola de Economia de São Paulo

papers.q: How can marginal treatment effects be identified when outcomes are right-censored durations?
papers.summary: In an application to sentences in Brazil, people whom most judges would punish take longer to recidivate. People punished only by strict judges recidivate sooner than if not punished.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: marginal treatment effects with censored durations and judge instruments; applied to sentencing in Brazil.
papers.contribution: Identifies distributional and quantile marginal treatment effect functions with a conditionally exogenous instrument and random censoring, and proposes semi-parametric estimators.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian criminal sentencing and recidivism data.

papers.title: From catastrophe to culture: The role of historical disasters in shaping long-term orientation

authors.inst: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do historical disasters shape long-term orientation in culture?
papers.summary: Studies the role of historical disasters in shaping long-term orientation, according to the title.

papers.title: Disclosure in Insurance Markets with Limited Screening
papers.q: Can statistical information disclosure be safely implemented in competitive insurance markets with limited screening?
papers.summary: No statistical instrument is safe, since there always exists a nonnegligible set of prior beliefs about consumers' risk types, compatible with the observed market, under which additional disclosure strictly worsens welfare.
papers.contribution: Analyzes consumer welfare effects of disclosure via a statistical instrument under natural constraints.
papers.ident: Theory: competitive insurance market with limited screening and information disclosure.

papers.title: An Evaluation of Protected Area Policies in the European Union
papers.summary: There are no meaningful impacts on either outcome across four decades, countries, cohorts or land characteristics. Strict protection is applied where development pressure is low, while in high-pressure regions protection is typically weak.
papers.ident: Staggered difference-in-differences of protected area introduction on vegetation and nightlights.
papers.q: Do EU protected areas reduce vegetation loss and development?
papers.contribution: Uses staggered introduction of protected areas between 1985 and 2019 to study selection of protected land and causal effects on vegetation cover and nightlights.
papers.dataDetail: EU protected areas 1985-2019 with vegetation cover and nightlights data.

papers.title: Flexible covariate adjustments in regression discontinuity designs
papers.q: How can covariates be used more efficiently in regression discontinuity designs?
papers.summary: The conventional RD framework gives a robustness property under which the optimal adjustment function can be estimated flexibly with machine learning without affecting first-order properties of the RD estimator. The estimators accommodate many covariates and are simple to implement.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: covariate-adjusted regression discontinuity estimators.
papers.contribution: Proposes estimators that run a standard RD analysis after subtracting a function of covariates from the outcome and characterizes the variance-minimizing function.

papers.title: Exorbitant Privilege of the Periodic Table? Geoeconomics, Endogenous Centrality and Strategic Minerals for the Green Transition
papers.summary: Trade in these materials has reorganized into a hub-and-spoke system centered on China, unlike the more diffuse structure for fossil fuels, even though China holds few reserves. Centrality was built through processing investment, industrial policy and development finance, and can translate into pricing power.
papers.ident: Descriptive trade network analysis with a stylized model of endogenous centrality.
papers.q: How did China become the hub of the trade network in electrification metals, and does centrality confer pricing power?
papers.contribution: Uses bilateral trade data for thirteen electrification metals over 1995-2023 and a stylized model in which a country chooses how central to become.
papers.dataDetail: Bilateral trade data for thirteen electrification metals, 1995-2023.

papers.title: Structural Estimation with Unstructured Data
papers.q: Can unstructured text data sharpen the structural estimation of monetary policy in a DSGE model?
papers.summary: Incorporating text improves predictive performance and materially alters structural inference in a medium-scale New Keynesian model. The model estimates a lower policy response to inflation, higher price stickiness and lower indexation, implying a flatter and less backward-looking Phillips curve.
papers.ident: Structural: Bayesian DSGE estimation with a text-based measurement block.
papers.contribution: Augments a state-space DSGE model with a measurement block linking structural shocks to series from FOMC transcripts, using a spike-and-slab prior.
papers.dataDetail: FOMC transcripts and U.S. macroeconomic time series.

papers.title: Determining Gender Differences in Education and Labor Market Outcomes
papers.q: Why do women attain more college education yet earn less than men across OECD countries?
papers.summary: Gaps are driven mainly by gender differences in average compensation at non-college jobs, where lower estimated compensation for non-college women raises their college premium and incentives to attend. Gender wage gaps among college workers are largely driven by differences in other model components.
papers.contribution: Estimates a dynamic choice model of education and labor market outcomes and decomposes gender gaps through counterfactuals for 21 OECD countries.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic education and labor market choice model with counterfactual decompositions.
papers.dataDetail: Data for 21 OECD countries on education and labor market outcomes.

papers.title: Life After Divorce: Effects of Joint Custody on Parents and Children
papers.q: How does joint versus sole custody after divorce affect parents and children?
papers.summary: For fathers joint custody substantially raises earnings and improves mental health, while mothers show no measurable effects. For children it raises test scores and school quality without affecting mental health.
papers.contribution: Links Swedish administrative data to over 25 years of newly collected custody rulings and exploits random assignment of disputes to judges with different propensities to grant joint custody.
papers.ident: Random assignment of custody disputes to judges differing in propensity to grant joint custody.
papers.dataDetail: Swedish administrative data linked to over 25 years of court custody rulings.

papers.title: Severe Cognitive Impairments and Long-term Care in Germany
papers.q: What are the care patterns and costs of severe cognitive impairment among older people in Germany?
papers.summary: About 4% of elderly people living at home have severe cognitive impairment. They are 30% more likely to receive any care and get about 6 more hours of formal care and 6 more of informal care per week.
papers.contribution: Measures the economic costs of cognitive impairment, including medical, nursing and at-home care, using SHARE Wave 9.
papers.ident: Descriptive: associations of severe cognitive impairment with care receipt in survey data.
papers.dataDetail: SHARE Wave 9, elderly people in Germany.

papers.title: Offshore dollar funding shocks and the dollar exchange rate
papers.q: How do offshore dollar funding shocks affect the dollar exchange rate?
papers.summary: Studies offshore dollar funding shocks and the dollar exchange rate, according to the title.

papers.title: Better Together? The Impact of Cash Transfers and Couples' Financial Planning on Household Dynamics and Economic Outcomes

authors.inst: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.q: Does adding a couples' financial planning exercise to a cash transfer improve household outcomes?
papers.summary: Relative to cash only, planning raises the share of the transfer spent on productive investment and improves economic outcomes by 0.16 standard deviations. For households with the highest ex-ante conflict risk, the gains come at the cost of additional intimate partner violence.
papers.ident: Randomized trial comparing cash plus joint planning, cash only and pure control.
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized trial in rural Liberia that layers facilitated joint financial planning on top of an unconditional cash transfer.
papers.dataDetail: Rural Liberian couples in a cash transfer program.

papers.title: Who Wants to Break Up Big Firms? Harm, Fairness, and the Demand for Antitrust
papers.summary: Treatments on perceived market share, consumer harm, unfair competition and negative image each moved their targeted beliefs, but their effects on demand for antitrust differed sharply.
papers.ident: Pre-registered randomized information treatments in an online survey.
papers.q: What drives public support for breaking up big firms?
papers.contribution: Runs a pre-registered information experiment with 4,000 American households informed about one of five real antitrust cases.
papers.dataDetail: 4,000 American households and five real antitrust cases.

papers.title: Diagnostic Thresholds, Written Consent Requirements, and the Utilization of Scarce Organs
papers.q: How do diagnostic thresholds and written consent requirements affect the use of deceased donor kidneys?
papers.summary: Age-based ECD thresholds led to 4.0 and 5.4 percentage point differences in discard rates of otherwise indistinguishable kidneys, and a KDPI discontinuity led to a 2.6 point difference. Thresholds shape decision making and information acquisition, with procurement biopsy rates rising at the age cutoff.
papers.contribution: Exploits age-based discontinuities in the Expanded Criteria Donor system and a discontinuity in the Kidney Donor Profile Index using data on the universe of U.S. donors and recipients.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuities at donor age and KDPI thresholds.
papers.dataDetail: Universe of U.S. organ donors and transplant recipients, ECD system 2002-2014.

papers.title: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Merger Simulations
papers.q: How accurate are prospective merger simulations?
papers.summary: Predicted price changes are typically larger than realized ones. Despite overprediction, full merger simulations identify mergers with large price changes better than structural presumptions and approximations of the merger effect.
papers.contribution: Compares realized price changes with simulation predictions for 101 consumer packaged goods mergers.
papers.ident: Comparison of ex ante simulation predictions with ex post realized price changes for consummated mergers.
papers.dataDetail: 101 consumer packaged goods mergers with retail scanner data.

papers.title: Optimal Currency Strategies Under Deviations From Interest Parity

authors.inst: Network for Studies on Pensions, Aging and Retirement

papers.q: What currency exposures are optimal for global equity and bond investors given deviations from interest parity?
papers.summary: The main conclusions of the risk-minimizing framework hold in a larger, longer panel and are robust to CIP deviations. Equity investors minimizing risk should hold exposures to the U.S. dollar.
papers.contribution: Extends the Campbell et al. (2010) framework with measured CIP hedging costs and expected-return-driven demands from UIP deviations over 1975-2023.
papers.ident: Portfolio optimization using measured CIP and UIP deviations across a panel of countries.
papers.dataDetail: Developed and emerging market equity, bond and currency data, 1975-2023.

papers.title: Learning and the Efficiency of Expert Referrals
papers.q: How well do primary care physicians learn about specialist quality when making referrals?
papers.summary: Specialist quality and costs vary substantially within geographic markets, and PCPs adjust referrals based on outcomes of their own patients. The model quantifies losses from informational frictions and simulates reallocations under improved information.
papers.ident: Structural learning model of referrals, with design-based evidence on physician responses to patient outcomes.
papers.contribution: Estimates a structural learning model of PCP referral choices using data on 4.5 million Medicare joint replacement surgeries, with design-based evidence on referral adjustment.
papers.dataDetail: 4.5 million joint replacement surgeries for Medicare beneficiaries.

papers.title: Supply Chain Risk, Trade and Economic Fragility

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.q: How does aggregate risk shape production, trade and sourcing in complex supply chains?
papers.summary: Risk has a positional effect on sourcing and welfare through cross-stage complementarity and within-stage substitutability. A country's own risk always lowers its welfare while risk elsewhere has ambiguous effects, and risk attenuates comparative advantage by shifting sourcing away from productive suppliers.
papers.ident: Structural: multi-country supply chain model with risk, quantified for 50 countries.
papers.contribution: Develops a quantitative multi-country model with multisourcing across production stages in which sourcing shares equal an input's expected output elasticity.
papers.dataDetail: Quantification for 50 countries and 3 production stages.

papers.title: Walking with Feet Tied to the Past: Childhood Exposure to the 1918 Influenza Pandemic and Later-Life Male Mortality
papers.q: How did childhood exposure to the 1918 influenza pandemic affect later-life male mortality?
papers.summary: The paper evaluates early-life and childhood exposure effects on old-age longevity and candidate mechanisms, extending work focused on in utero exposure that found mixed results.
papers.ident: Event-study and DiD comparing cohorts by age at exposure in cities with high versus low 1918 influenza mortality.
papers.contribution: Links Social Security death records to the full-count 1940 census and applies event-study and DiD regressions to cohorts with different age at exposure, by city exposure to 1918 influenza mortality.
papers.dataDetail: SSA death records linked to the full-count 1940 census.

papers.title: Physician Learning and Forgetting: Evidence from the US Military

authors.inst: The University of Texas at San Antonio
The University of Texas at San Antonio

papers.summary: Readmission rates rise by 48% in the first two months after a surgeon returns, returning to baseline within six months. Obstetricians keep elevated cesarean rates for up to nine months, and doubling recent volume reduces readmission and C-section rates.
papers.ident: Quasi-random assignment of military physicians to deployments and event study around return to practice.
papers.contribution: Exploits quasi-random assignment of U.S. military physicians to combat deployments that produce gaps in practice.
papers.q: How does physician skill depreciate and recover after gaps in clinical practice?
papers.dataDetail: U.S. military health care system records on physicians and patients.

papers.title: Critical Peak Rewards: Evidence from a Nationwide Demand Response Program
papers.q: How effective was the world's first nationwide demand flexibility program in cutting peak demand?
papers.summary: The program paid consumers to cut demand below a baseline at 16 peak events in winter 2023-24. Customers who opted into events reduced demand by 23.1% among compliers, at an average cost of 2,325 pounds per MWh, and solar, batteries, heat pumps and EVs increased response.
papers.ident: Randomized encouragement design to sign up for the demand flexibility program, with complier estimates.
papers.contribution: Runs a natural field experiment with 2.7 million customers, randomly encouraging sign-up while 119,999 are held as controls.
papers.dataDetail: 2.7 million customers, with 119,999 controls, winter 2023-24.

papers.title: A two-pronged approach to currency internationalization

authors.inst: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How can a two-pronged approach promote currency internationalization?
papers.summary: Studies a two-pronged approach to currency internationalization, according to the title.

papers.title: Estimating Trends In Mental Distress Using Survey Data
papers.q: Do household surveys give consistent trends in mental distress among U.S. adults?
papers.summary: The study asks whether different measures, or the same indicator from different surveys, show consistent changes over time. It also compares single-item measures with validated multi-question screeners and the consequences of different functional forms.
papers.contribution: Compares measures and functional forms of mental distress across five major household surveys for 18-64 year olds over 1999-2019.
papers.ident: Descriptive: comparison of mental distress measures across surveys and over time.
papers.dataDetail: Five major U.S. household surveys, ages 18-64, 1999-2019.

papers.title: Spreading Out Across Expanding Idea Space
papers.q: Are U.S. inventions spreading out across an expanding idea space?
papers.summary: Inventions have become increasingly dissimilar over nearly two centuries, corroborated by a 98% decline in patent interference rates. Different text representations can yield opposite conclusions, so a validation framework selects among them.
papers.contribution: Applies validated neural language models to the claims of over 11 million U.S. patents, 1836-2023, and develops a spatial competition model of inventors' location choice.
papers.ident: Text embedding similarity of patent claims validated against interference rates, with a spatial competition model.
papers.dataDetail: Full text of claims of over 11 million U.S. patents, 1836-2023.

papers.title: Human Capital in Venture Capital: Evidence From 100,000 Venture Capitalists
papers.q: How concentrated is investment success among venture capitalists and what explains it?
papers.summary: Fewer than 40% of VCs with any investments are credited with a successful one, and 90% of profits come from 5% of VCs. Education, experience and demographics predict careers and outcomes, and superstar status increases access to highly valued startups.
papers.ident: Marginal inclusion on the Forbes Midas List as a quasi-experiment for superstar status.
papers.contribution: Builds a dataset of over 100,000 professionals at U.S. VC firms and uses marginal inclusions on the Forbes Midas List as quasi-experimental variation.
papers.dataDetail: Over 100,000 professionals affiliated with U.S. VC firms.

papers.title: Training AI for When Humans Will Use It
papers.summary: Optimal training can be discontinuous in economic variables, and the paper studies heterogeneous users and monopoly model trainers. Maximizing unconditional accuracy is generally suboptimal.
papers.q: How should AI be trained when humans will use its predictions in decisions?
papers.contribution: Models AI as part of a composite experiment where it makes a coarse prediction and shows optimal training through a geometric argument.
papers.ident: Theory: value of AI predictions in a composite decision environment.

papers.title: Ambiguity vs. Risk in Investment Decisions: A Continuous Decomposition
papers.q: How can the effect of ambiguity on asset values be decomposed from risk?
papers.summary: Ambiguity adjusts beliefs into distorted probabilities characterized by first-order stochastic dominance. Increased ambiguity aversion depresses optimal asset demand.
papers.contribution: Provides a continuous-space framework within the KMM smooth ambiguity model and a decomposition of valuation into risky valuation and cost of uncertainty.
papers.ident: Theory: smooth ambiguity asset valuation in continuous prior space.

papers.title: Melitz meets Lewis: The impacts of roads on structural transformation and businesses
papers.q: How do roads affect structural transformation and business composition?
papers.summary: Highways led to fewer businesses where structural transformation is weak and more where it is strong. Lower non-agricultural trade costs reduce firm numbers while cheaper agricultural imports release labor and raise them, and faster agricultural productivity growth in China differentiates the two countries.
papers.contribution: Combines evidence from highway programs in India and China with a two-sector regional trade model with endogenous firm entry.
papers.ident: Highway program exposure with a two-sector trade model replicating the results.
papers.dataDetail: Highway programs and business counts in India and China.

papers.title: Asymptotics of CoVaR inference in two-quantile-regression
papers.q: What are the asymptotics of CoVaR inference in a two-quantile-regression framework?
papers.summary: Studies the asymptotics of CoVaR inference in two-quantile-regression, according to the title.

papers.title: The impact of pension reforms and rapid aging on savings and labor supply: The case of China

authors.inst: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do pension reforms and rapid aging affect savings and labor supply in China?
papers.summary: Studies the impact of pension reforms and rapid aging on savings and labor supply in China, according to the title.

papers.title: Money and gender: Proxy respondents and the mismeasurement of income in surveys

authors.inst: CAF – Development Bank of Latin America
CAF – Development Bank of Latin America

papers.q: How do proxy respondents lead to mismeasurement of income by gender in surveys?
papers.summary: Studies proxy respondents and the mismeasurement of income in surveys by gender, according to the title.

papers.title: Exporter survival with uncertainty and experimentation

authors.inst: Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros
Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.q: Why do new exporters survive so poorly, and less than re-entrants?
papers.summary: The model has four relevant parameters yet matches the survival profile of entrants and re-entrants and delivers predictions about other exporter dynamics facts.
papers.contribution: Extends a standard exporter dynamics model with firms experimenting to resolve uncertainty about foreign-market profitability, estimated on Peruvian customs data.
papers.ident: Structural: exporter dynamics model with experimentation, estimated on customs data.
papers.dataDetail: Peruvian customs data.

papers.title: The Long Shadow of Housing Discrimination: Evidence from Racial Covenants
papers.q: Did racial covenants shape neighborhood segregation even after they became unenforceable?
papers.summary: Covenants could have served as focal points for coordination on an initial equilibrium of neighborhood formation, with investment durability and path dependency. Covenant enforceability affected early-stage neighborhood composition.
papers.contribution: Assembles novel parcel-level data on racial covenants and exploits delays between covenant execution and construction to isolate exposure to enforceable covenants.
papers.ident: Quasi-experimental design using delays between covenant execution and housing construction before the 1948 Shelley v. Kraemer ruling.
papers.dataDetail: Novel parcel-level data on racial covenants.

papers.title: Identification-robust inference for the LATE with high-dimensional covariates
papers.q: How can the LATE be tested robustly with high-dimensional covariates and weak identification?
papers.summary: Simulations show size and power robust to weak identification and high dimensionality, outperforming conventional tests. An application studies the effect of railroad access on urban population growth.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: identification-robust inference for the LATE with debiased machine learning.
papers.contribution: Proposes a test statistic with uniformly correct asymptotic size and algorithms using double/debiased machine learning.
papers.dataDetail: Railroad and population data in the application.

papers.title: Industrial Clusters in the Long Run: Evidence from Million-Rouble Plants in China
papers.q: How do large successful plants affect local industrial clusters over the long run?
papers.summary: Counties hosting these plants were 80% more productive than controls in 1982 but 20% less productive by 2010. The decline reflects local establishments with low productivity, limited innovation and high markups, as specialization hindered spillovers and new clusters.
papers.ident: Plant siting driven by the geopolitics of the Sino-Soviet alliance and airbase locations.
papers.contribution: Uses the siting of Million-Rouble Plants built in the 1950s during the Sino-Soviet alliance, with airbase locations providing exogenous variation.
papers.dataDetail: Chinese county-level and establishment data from the 1950s to 2010.

papers.title: Departmentalized instruction and elementary school effectiveness
papers.q: How does departmentalized instruction affect elementary school effectiveness?
papers.summary: Studies departmentalized instruction and elementary school effectiveness, according to the title.

papers.title: The incidence of rent subsidies: Evidence on rents, housing choices and supply
papers.q: Do rent subsidies to low-income households raise rents?
papers.summary: Large increases in allowances had little or no effect on rents, with a one-euro increase raising rent by roughly 0.036 euros (standard error 0.028). Recipients' housing choices and rental supply changed little, suggesting subsidies can help recipients even in supply-constrained markets.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around a reform of Finland's housing allowance generating quasi-random variation.
papers.contribution: Studies a Finnish housing allowance reform that caused large quasi-random variation in allowances, using register data spanning five years before and after.
papers.dataDetail: Finnish register data, five years before and after the reform.

papers.title: Behavioral responses to inheritance taxes: Evidence from Brazil
papers.q: How do taxpayers respond to an announced increase in inheritance and gift taxes in Brazil?
papers.summary: Gifts surge by about 300% just before the reform, and estate filings fall by 30% largely because small estates become exempt. Taxable households reduce declared bequests with an elasticity of 2.3-3.2, and liquid assets move from bequests to gifts.
papers.contribution: Uses administrative microdata from a reform whose rate increase was known three months in advance.
papers.ident: Event study around an announced increase in inheritance and gift tax rates.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian administrative microdata on gifts and estates.

papers.title: Monitoring and delivering: Evidence from dropout rates in Brazil
papers.q: How does monitoring affect service delivery and dropout rates in Brazil?
papers.summary: Studies monitoring and delivery through dropout rates in Brazil, according to the title.
