papers.title: Optimal monetary policy with confounding information
papers.q: What is optimal monetary policy when firms cannot tell aggregate from idiosyncratic shocks?
papers.summary: Misattribution of aggregate nominal disturbances to firm-specific factors makes strict price stability suboptimal, and the optimal policy fully stabilizes the output gap while accommodating price level fluctuations. The price level is procyclical when firms learn from demand signals and countercyclical when they learn from productivity signals.
papers.ident: Theory: New Keynesian model with signal extraction and optimal policy.
papers.contribution: Develops a model of optimal monetary policy with a signal-extraction problem in price setting.

papers.title: Agricultural trade and adaptation to climate change in sub-Saharan Africa
papers.summary: Using median yield changes across five climate models, the continent-wide welfare loss is 2.4% of GDP, with country losses up to 60% of GDP in the worst model. The loss is 19% smaller with lower trade costs and over seven times larger if trade flows are capped at current levels.
papers.q: How does trade mediate the welfare effects of climate change on agriculture in sub-Saharan Africa?
papers.contribution: Builds a model of production, consumption and trade of 24 crops across 271 regions to simulate climate change effects.
papers.ident: Structural: multi-region trade model of agriculture with climate yield shocks.
papers.dataDetail: 24 crops across 271 regions of sub-Saharan Africa, five climate models.

papers.title: The Labor Market Effects of Expanding Overtime Coverage
papers.q: How does expanding overtime coverage affect employment and pay?
papers.contribution: Uses an event-study design with administrative payroll data and state-level salary threshold changes from 2014-2021.
papers.summary: Firms do not increase employment by substituting workers for hours, nor lower base pay to offset overtime costs. Instead employers raised salaries above the threshold to keep workers exempt, indicating costly monitoring and adjustment of hours.
papers.ident: Event study around state-level changes in the salary threshold for overtime coverage.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative payroll data, 2014-2021.

papers.title: Let’s Chat: Leveraging Chatbot Outreach for Improved Course Performance
papers.contribution: Runs a pre-registered experiment with chatbot messaging in large-enrollment undergraduate courses.
papers.summary: Chatbot messaging increased final grades and engagement with academic supports such as tutoring. Effects were consistent across demographics except for treated women in a Microeconomics course, whose final grades were seven percentage points higher.
papers.conclusion: AI-enabled outreach can enhance student engagement, learning and course performance.
papers.ident: Pre-registered randomized experiment of chatbot outreach in large undergraduate courses.
papers.q: Can non-generative AI chatbot outreach improve course performance in large undergraduate classes?
papers.dataDetail: Undergraduate students in large-enrollment courses.

papers.title: Unruly by Design: Fee Volatility and Strategic Attacks in Bitcoin Mining
papers.q: How does fee volatility create incentives for strategic attacks in Bitcoin mining?
papers.summary: When adjacent blocks have large reward disparities, miners have incentives to attempt alternative versions of prior blocks to claim others' rewards. Fee differentials are associated with such attacks and longer waiting times between blocks, implying possible destabilization as block subsidies are withdrawn.
papers.ident: Theory and regressions of attack frequency on fee differentials between adjacent blocks.
papers.contribution: Develops a model of aberrant miner behavior and tests it with a new 2017-2025 dataset.
papers.dataDetail: Bitcoin block data, 2017-2025.

papers.title: Job Ads as Signals: Evidence from a Priced Amenity and Worker Beliefs
papers.q: Do job ads signal unlisted job attributes and bias willingness-to-pay estimates from discrete choice experiments?
papers.contribution: Embeds a priced amenity, a monthly public transport pass, in a large discrete choice experiment with German workers and adds a belief-elicitation experiment.
papers.summary: Many workers overvalue the ticket by more than 100%, including public transport users. Advertising an amenity shifts beliefs about unlisted job attributes, and posted wages similarly signal unlisted attributes, contaminating the money metric used for WTP.
papers.ident: Discrete choice experiment with an amenity of known price and a belief-elicitation experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Large-scale discrete choice experiment with German workers.

papers.title: The match between ‘She’ and ‘Her’: Performance gains from gender match in higher education
papers.q: Does matching students and instructors by gender improve performance in higher education?
papers.summary: Studies performance gains from gender match in higher education, according to the title.

papers.title: Banking on a Corporate Rebrand
papers.q: Can a corporate rebrand mitigate a negative shock, as seen for German-named U.S. banks in World War I?
papers.summary: Banks that kept German names saw significant declines in assets, deposits and market share. Banks that rebranded mitigated much of the shock, especially those adopting a new nonethnic name.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences of German-named banks that kept or changed names after U.S. entry into World War I.
papers.contribution: Uses the 1917 anti-German backlash as a natural experiment on banks with very similar German names.
papers.dataDetail: Historical bank data around 1917 for U.S. banks with German names.

papers.title: Long Term Care and Cognitive Impairment in Spain
papers.q: How does cognitive impairment affect health and long-term care use and costs among older Spaniards?
papers.summary: Socioeconomic status is the strongest predictor of impairment. Physical limitations predict overall care use more strongly than cognitive impairment alone (73% versus 55%) and nursing home residence (2.0% versus 0.9%), and informal caregiving is the overwhelming share of care.
papers.contribution: Uses pooled pre-COVID longitudinal data on individuals aged 65+ to estimate care utilization, costs and financial burden.
papers.ident: Descriptive: associations of impairment with care use in longitudinal survey data.
papers.dataDetail: Pooled pre-COVID longitudinal sample of Spaniards aged 65+.

papers.title: Choice Between Public and Private Healthcare Systems: Evidence from Veterans
papers.q: What explains elderly veterans' choice between VA care and private Medicare-financed care?
papers.summary: 50-60% of geographic variation in VA use is due to individual demand-side factors and the rest to place-based factors. Place-based factors matter more for inpatient and emergency care than for outpatient and primary care.
papers.contribution: Analyzes veterans who move across areas with different VA utilization to separate individual-specific from place-specific factors.
papers.ident: Mover design comparing veterans' VA use before and after moving across areas.
papers.dataDetail: Medicare and VA data on elderly veterans.

papers.title: Assessing the Benefits of Optimized Agentic AI Systems for Asset Pricing
papers.summary: Agentic AI systems extract structured signals from earnings call transcripts and optimize over them. The best-optimized systems more than double the explanatory power of a baseline.
papers.q: How can the benefits of optimized agentic AI systems for asset pricing be evaluated without look-ahead bias?
papers.contribution: Introduces a real-time, out-of-sample benchmark measuring how well AI systems explain contemporaneous stock returns around earnings announcements using only announcement-time information.
papers.ident: Real-time out-of-sample benchmark explaining earnings-announcement returns.
papers.dataDetail: Earnings call transcripts and stock returns around earnings announcements.

papers.title: Forecasting the Covid Surge in Inflation
papers.q: Could time series models have forecast the post-2021 surge in U.S. inflation?
papers.summary: Univariate models using only current and past inflation did not forecast the surge better, while multivariate models incorporating sectoral inflation measures did.
papers.ident: Real-time forecast comparison of inflation models.
papers.contribution: Compares univariate and multivariate time series models with stochastic volatility and time-varying persistence using real-time data.
papers.dataDetail: Real-time U.S. aggregate and sectoral inflation data.

papers.title: How Do State “Auto-IRA” Policies Affect Household Balance Sheets?
papers.q: How do state auto-IRA policies affect household balance sheets?
papers.summary: The policy is associated with increases in IRA and employer-sponsored plan ownership and assets, and in checking or savings account ownership and balances. Credit card debt also rises, suggesting spillovers to liquidity management and borrowing.
papers.contribution: Compares private-sector workers likely exposed to Oregon's Auto-IRA policy with similar workers in not-yet-adopting states using the SIPP.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing exposed workers in Oregon with similar workers in not-yet-adopting states.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of Income and Program Participation.

papers.title: How Might Fiscal Policy Respond to the Rise of Artificial Intelligence?
papers.q: How might U.S. fiscal policy respond to the rise of artificial intelligence?
papers.summary: For each scenario the paper considers policy responses related to growth, income distribution, support for displaced workers and taxation and ownership of capital. Given uncertainty about AI's effects, policies robust to different scenarios are especially valuable.
papers.contribution: Analyzes long-term scenarios combining faster productivity growth, greater inequality, job displacement and a higher capital share, and assesses implications for federal debt and policy responses.
papers.ident: Scenario analysis of AI's fiscal implications.

papers.title: The Effect of School Disruptions on Parental Labor Supply: Evidence from Canadian Panel Data
papers.q: How did COVID-19 school closures affect the labor supply of Canadian parents?
papers.summary: Restrictions on in-person schooling reduced employment among partnered mothers of school-aged children by about 2 percentage points. For fathers adjustments are much weaker and concentrated among single fathers, and school closures increased public benefit receipt among single parents.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences using variation in grade-level school closures across 141 cities.
papers.contribution: Collects grade-level school closure data for 141 Canadian cities and links it to individual panel data from the Labour Force Survey.
papers.dataDetail: Labour Force Survey panel data and administrative tax records for Canada.

papers.title: Ports, Technology and Inter-City Trade: The Economics and Geopolitics of Evolving Maritime Transport Networks
papers.summary: Global shipping is highly concentrated among a changing lineup of top ports while lower-ranked ports disperse, and state-owned Chinese terminal operators account for growing volumes, with efficiency gains mostly for Chinese vessels. Containerization reshaped which port cities could expand and reinforced hubs.
papers.contribution: Draws on digitized historical shipping records, georeferenced ship movements and shipment-level routing data to present five stylized facts and synthesize the literature.
papers.q: How have ports and technology reshaped the global maritime transport network and inter-city trade?
papers.ident: Descriptive stylized facts on the maritime network, with a literature synthesis.
papers.dataDetail: Digitized historical shipping records, georeferenced ship movements and shipment-level routing data.

papers.title: Psychosocial Health and Well-Being After A Mortality Shock
papers.q: How does an unexpected mortality shock affect psychosocial health in the short and long run?
papers.summary: Two years after the tsunami both community and individual mortality exposures predict elevated depression and post-traumatic stress symptoms. After ten years, individual exposures are slightly attenuated but still significant, while community-level mortality predicts only post-traumatic stress.
papers.contribution: Contrasts community-level tsunami mortality with individual loss of close kin using longitudinal survey data from the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
papers.ident: Panel analysis exploiting variation in tsunami mortality at the community and individual level.
papers.dataDetail: Study of the Tsunami Aftermath and Recovery, population-representative longitudinal survey.

papers.title: Measuring the Value of Disability Insurance from Take-Up Decisions
papers.q: How much do people value disability insurance, as revealed by take-up decisions?
papers.summary: In Canada, raising DI benefits by $1 creates a disincentive cost of $0.60 and an insurance value of $2.20. DI benefits are therefore not overly generous in the Canadian context.
papers.contribution: Develops a revealed-preference approach comparing the DI take-up response to a change in benefits with the response to a change in wages.
papers.ident: Revealed preference: comparing take-up responses to benefit changes versus wage changes.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian disability insurance take-up data.

papers.title: Retrieval Failures and Consumption Smoothing: A Field Experiment on Seasonal Poverty
papers.q: Do retrieval failures cause farmers to under-save and fail to smooth consumption?
papers.summary: Farmers underestimate upcoming spending by 50%. Treated individuals increase remembered expenses by 36-60%, concentrated among small, irregular and stochastic items, spend less immediately, and hold 15% higher savings six weeks later.
papers.contribution: Runs a field experiment among Zambian farmers randomizing a prompt to think through future expenses in categories.
papers.ident: Randomized intervention prompting associative recall of future expenses.
papers.dataDetail: Zambian farmers with one annual harvest.

papers.title: Economic Well-Being of Latino Households in the U.S.: a Scoping Review of Research on Poverty, the Safety Net, and Family Supports
papers.summary: The search yielded more than 5,000 studies, a greater than five-fold increase since the early 2000s, mostly on Medicaid and health insurance and about half on government benefit programs. Few studies examine Latino employment outcomes in the context of benefit availability, and studies find higher poverty and material hardship.
papers.contribution: Conducts a preregistered PRISMA scoping review of research from 1990 to 2025 on poverty, the safety net and family supports.
papers.q: What does research say about the economic well-being of Latino households in the U.S.?
papers.dataDetail: More than 5,000 studies from peer-reviewed journals, 1990-2025.

papers.title: Securing power, compromising climate: Evidence from drought shocks in China

authors.inst: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do drought shocks lead to political security motives that compromise climate outcomes in China?
papers.summary: Studies how securing power can compromise climate, using drought shocks in China, according to the title.

papers.title: The International RBC Model Finally Works!
papers.summary: The model accounts for the Backus-Smith, Backus-Kehoe-Kydland and weak trade-balance-exchange-rate correlation puzzles, and also the Fama puzzle and the stronger currencies of high interest rate countries.
papers.contribution: Incorporates uninsurable countercyclical income risk into a standard international RBC model relying solely on productivity shocks.
papers.q: Can uninsurable countercyclical income risk solve the quantity puzzles of international RBC models?
papers.ident: Structural: international RBC model with incomplete markets and countercyclical idiosyncratic risk.

papers.title: Pulp Friction: The Value of Quantity Contracts in Decentralized Markets
papers.q: How valuable are quantity contracts in decentralized markets where trading frictions prevent matching?
papers.summary: Quantity contracts provide quantity assurance but prevent sellers from allocating production across buyers after conditions realize. The average value of a contract is 10% of profits, and would be 55% larger if sellers could allocate production optimally ex post.
papers.contribution: Estimates a model of quantity contracts in the pulp and paper industry using proprietary invoice data.
papers.ident: Structural: model of quantity contracts and spot trading frictions estimated on invoice data.
papers.dataDetail: Proprietary invoice data from the pulp and paper industry.

papers.title: Going Viral: Protests and Polarization in 1932 Hamburg
papers.q: Do mass protest marches polarize societies, as Nazi marches in 1932 Hamburg suggest?
papers.summary: Propaganda can persuade by raising the share of areas with high Nazi support, but marches can also backfire by repelling voters, so marches lead to polarization. Effects diffused through social networks, with spillovers of similar importance as direct exposure and growing over time.
papers.contribution: Estimates the impact of Nazi marches using granular data from 622 voting precincts over six elections and tracks diffusion through social networks proxied by 1918 Spanish flu contagion.
papers.ident: Precinct-level variation in exposure to marches across six elections, with social spillovers proxied by 1918 flu contagion patterns.
papers.dataDetail: 622 voting precincts in Hamburg across six elections, 1932.

papers.title: Consumption stimulus with digital coupons: Heterogeneity and policy design

authors.inst: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.q: How should digital coupons be designed to stimulate consumption efficiently and equitably?
papers.summary: The program generates large and heterogeneous short-term effects that vary across consumers and locations. High-response consumers patronize larger businesses, so benefits are regressively allocated, and targeting the most responsive consumers can more than double aggregate stimulus while a hybrid design with support for small businesses improves efficiency and equity.
papers.contribution: Analyzes a large-scale Chinese digital coupon program and runs counterfactuals on targeting rules.
papers.ident: Program evaluation with heterogeneous responses and counterfactual targeting analysis.
papers.dataDetail: Large-scale digital coupon program transaction data from China.

papers.title: The effectiveness of entry deregulation: Quasi-experimental evidence from China's export compulsory inspection deregulation

authors.inst: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Is entry deregulation effective, as shown by China's export compulsory inspection deregulation?
papers.summary: Studies the effectiveness of entry deregulation using China's export compulsory inspection deregulation as a quasi-experiment, according to the title.

papers.title: Consumption responses to a major minimum wage increase: Evidence from Spain

authors.inst: Università degli Studi del Piemonte Orientale “Amedeo Avogadro”

papers.q: How do household consumption patterns respond to a major minimum wage increase?
papers.summary: The increase led to a significant 4.5% rise in household consumption, with the largest gains in nonessential categories such as electronics, leisure, restaurants and hotels. Findings are corroborated by the Spanish Household Budget Survey.
papers.contribution: Uses confidential point-of-sale and credit card transaction data at the municipal level and geographic variation in exposure to Spain's 2019 minimum wage increase of 22.3%.
papers.ident: Geographic variation in exposure to Spain's 2019 minimum wage increase.
papers.dataDetail: Municipal-level point-of-sale and credit card data and the Spanish Household Budget Survey.

papers.title: Adult children's human capital accumulation and parents' risky behaviors: Evidence from the higher education expansion in China

authors.inst: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics
Shanghai University of Finance and Economics
Anhui University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do adult children's human capital gains from higher education expansion affect parents' risky behaviors in China?
papers.summary: Studies the effect of adult children's human capital accumulation on parents' risky behaviors using China's higher education expansion, according to the title.

papers.title: The Selective Disclosure of Evidence: An Experiment

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.summary: Findings confirm the key qualitative predictions and suggest selection, rather than concealment, is often the dominant distortion. Some senders are deception averse and overcommunicate, receivers respond too optimistically to both concealed and selected evidence, and selection still generates greater overall distortion.
papers.q: Is selection or concealment the dominant distortion when senders disclose verifiable evidence?
papers.contribution: Runs an experiment based on a model in which an informed sender discloses evidence selected from a larger pool, leveraging its comparative statics.
papers.ident: Laboratory experiment testing comparative statics of a selective disclosure model.

papers.title: Noncausal AR processes driven by causal GARCH volatility

authors.inst: Centre de Recherche en Économie et Statistique

papers.q: How can noncausal autoregressive processes driven by causal GARCH volatility be modeled?
papers.summary: Studies noncausal autoregressive processes driven by causal GARCH volatility, according to the title.

papers.title: The impact of international conflict on cross-border commercial dispute resolution
papers.q: How does international conflict affect enforcement of foreign commercial court decisions?
papers.summary: The enforcement rate of Ukrainian decisions in Russia fell by 26% and of Russian decisions in Ukraine by 33%. Courts increasingly justified refusals on discretionary legal grounds and undue-notification claims.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around the 2014 annexation of Crimea.
papers.contribution: Assembles novel data on the universe of Russian and Ukrainian court decisions on enforcing foreign decisions and applies difference-in-differences around the 2014 annexation of Crimea.
papers.dataDetail: Universe of Russian and Ukrainian court decisions on enforcement of foreign cross-border commercial decisions.

papers.title: Southern roots abroad: The long-run impact of the Confederate migration to Brazil
papers.q: What are the long-run effects of the Confederate migration to Brazil?
papers.summary: Studies the long-run impact of the Confederate migration to Brazil, according to the title.

papers.title: The dynamics of costly norms
papers.q: Why do costly social norms exhibit different dynamics, collapsing, eroding or escalating?
papers.summary: The examples include duelling, footbinding, female genital cutting and wasteful consumption. The analysis can guide policy design and shows that some interventions can be counterproductive.
papers.contribution: Develops a theoretical framework explaining norm dynamics through different forces of social influence that lends itself to empirical estimation.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic model of social pressure and conformity.

papers.title: Structural Change in Production Networks and Economic Growth

authors.inst: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

papers.q: How does structural change in intermediate input and investment networks shape growth?
papers.summary: The share of output produced by services is rising in both networks, while the relative price of services producing intermediates and consumption is rising and that for investment is falling. Structural change reallocates resources to the slowest growing intermediate producers and the fastest growing investment producers.
papers.contribution: Documents trends in input-output and investment networks and develops a multi-sector growth model with complements in intermediates and substitutes in investment production.
papers.ident: Structural: multi-sector growth model with input-output and investment networks matched to relative price trends.
papers.dataDetail: Input-output and investment network data on goods and services.

papers.title: Depression stigma
papers.q: Does perceived depression stigma affect help-seeking among people with depression?
papers.summary: A large majority overestimate the stigma associated with depression. An information intervention reducing perceived stigma decreases demand for psychotherapy, and merely prompting people to think about stigma has a similar effect, because it raises optimism about mental health and willingness to rely on friends and family.
papers.contribution: Introduces a new measure of perceived stigma and runs experiments with 1,844 Americans suffering from depression.
papers.ident: Randomized information interventions with a mechanism experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Sample of 1,844 Americans with depression.

papers.title: The Value of Names: Civil Society, Information, and Governing Multinationals
papers.q: Do markets penalize multinationals tied to the assassination of mining activists?
papers.summary: Firms featured in coverage experience significant negative abnormal returns, with a median 10-day loss exceeding USD 100 million. The response is persistent and consistent with reputational costs, magnified by media attention and information-sensitive institutional investors.
papers.contribution: Conducts an event study of stock returns for firms featured in media coverage of mining activist assassinations.
papers.ident: Event study of abnormal stock returns around media coverage of assassinations.
papers.dataDetail: Assassinations of mining activists linked to media coverage and firm stock returns.

papers.title: Losses from a Disability: Temporal Variety and Earnings in the Long Run
papers.summary: Temporal variety is income superior. People reporting a disability in two consecutive surveys do almost 4 percent fewer activities per day and earn about 50 percent less, and the monetary equivalent of lost variety exceeds that of lost earnings.
papers.conclusion: Single one-time self-reports of disability may understate shortfalls.
papers.q: How much do people with a mobility disability lose through reduced temporal variety and earnings?
papers.contribution: Uses diaries from the American Time Use Survey 2009-24 linked to Current Population Surveys in propensity-score models.
papers.ident: Propensity-score matching comparing people with disability in two consecutive surveys to demographically identical others.
papers.dataDetail: American Time Use Survey 2009-24 linked to Current Population Surveys, ages 25-61.

papers.title: Tax Incentives and Venture Capital Risk-Taking: Evidence from the QSBS Program
papers.q: Do tax subsidies for startup investing prompt investors to take more risk?
papers.summary: Subsidies prompt bunching at tax-eligible holding-period thresholds. Where subsidies apply, VCs shift their project selection toward riskier ventures, investing more in pre-commercial startups.
papers.ident: Bunching, triple-differences and matching exploiting industry eligibility, vintage and holding-period requirements.
papers.contribution: Analyzes 158 thousand investor-firm pairings with bunching, triple-differences and matching designs around the QSBS program changes.
papers.dataDetail: 158 thousand investor-firm pairings over two decades.

papers.title: Importing Aggregate Demand

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How are open economies exposed to global demand shocks, through quantities or prices?
papers.summary: Elevated marginal propensities to consume push toward quantities, while financial frictions increase price adjustment. In quantitative explorations the spending effect tends to win, necessitating aggressive domestic policy action.
papers.contribution: Shows that failures of Ricardian equivalence and global financial market imperfections have opposite effects on whether foreign booms are absorbed by consumption or real exchange rate appreciation.
papers.ident: Theory: open economy model with high MPCs and financial frictions.

papers.title: Estimating individual responses when tomorrow matters
papers.q: How can individuals' responses to counterfactual changes be estimated when expectations matter?
papers.summary: Illustrated in a consumption and saving model with an income tax that changes current income and beliefs about future income. Applied to Italian survey data, beliefs matter for evaluating the impact of tax policies on consumption.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: three-step estimation using panel subjective expectations.
papers.contribution: Proposes an approach based on average partial effects and a three-step estimator using panel data on subjective expectations.
papers.dataDetail: Italian survey data with subjective expectations.

papers.title: Forecasting with Uncertain Persistence
papers.summary: Correctly specified and Bayesian forecasts may underreact at short horizons and overreact at long horizons. This explains puzzles including excess responsiveness of long rates to short rates, apparent term premia, predictability of bond yields and excess volatility of long-horizon forward prices.
papers.ident: Theory: Bayesian forecasting with uncertain persistence.
papers.q: How does uncertainty about persistence affect forecasts and explain asset pricing puzzles?
papers.contribution: Shows that with uncertainty about persistence, forecasts necessarily become more persistent and overreact at long horizons.

papers.title: Benefit-Based Taxation can Include Substantial Redistribution
papers.summary: The results counter a long-standing concern about the benefit principle in the tradition of Smith. Since redistribution is widespread in practice, they remove an obstacle to the benefit principle as a normative foundation of tax policy.
papers.q: Can benefit-based labor income taxation coexist with substantial redistribution?
papers.contribution: Shows theoretically and in plausibly specified simulations that benefit-based taxation is consistent with redistribution through transfers and negative average tax rates at levels reflecting U.S. policy.
papers.ident: Theory and simulations of benefit-based income taxation with transfers.

papers.title: Educational mobility across multiple generations in Indonesia
papers.q: Does educational persistence across three generations in Indonesia understate or overstate mobility?
papers.summary: Contrary to findings in developed countries, there is greater multigenerational mobility than parent-child correlations suggest. Regional exposure to the 1997-98 Asian financial crisis and variation in marital customs confirm the relevance of financial constraints and cultural norms.
papers.ident: Multigenerational regressions, with regional variation in crisis exposure and marital customs as tests of mechanisms.
papers.contribution: Studies multigenerational education correlations with the IFLS and Census data and develops a theory with credit constraints and marital sorting norms.
papers.dataDetail: Indonesian Family Life Survey and Census data, three generations.

papers.title: Congestion Pricing and Emergency Medical Service Response: Evidence from New York City
papers.q: Did New York City's congestion pricing speed up emergency medical service response?
papers.summary: Vehicular traffic declines by roughly 18 to 21 percent near the boundary, with increases in pedestrian and bicycle activity. The program identifies a novel external benefit in faster EMS response times.
papers.ident: Difference-in-discontinuities at the 60th Street boundary of the congestion pricing zone.
papers.contribution: Exploits the sharp geographic boundary of the congestion relief zone at 60th Street in a difference-in-discontinuities design after the January 2025 program start.
papers.dataDetail: New York City traffic, mobility and EMS response time data around January 2025.

papers.title: Quality, Selection, and Congestion: Equilibrium Hospital Outcomes During Covid-19
papers.q: How do hospital quality, patient selection and congestion shape Covid-19 mortality?
papers.summary: Intensive care strain increased hospital mortality, and without congestion deaths would fall 9.6%. Patients value high-quality hospitals but their choices did not reflect capacity strain information, and informing them without accounting for congestion could raise deaths by 3.8%.
papers.contribution: Estimates an equilibrium model of hospital outcomes using Covid-19 data and distance instruments to control for selection.
papers.ident: Distance instruments for patient selection and an equilibrium model of hospital choice and congestion.
papers.dataDetail: Covid-19 hospital patient and outcome data.

papers.title: Is Growth Additive?
papers.summary: There is strong evidence that U.S. TFP growth is conditionally additive. Bayesian estimation selects the additive over the exponential model even from low priors, and professional forecasts and international TFP series agree.
papers.ident: Bayesian model comparison of additive versus exponential TFP growth.
papers.q: Is TFP growth additive rather than exponential?
papers.contribution: Tests whether the conditional expectation of the next TFP increment is proportional to current TFP using Bayesian estimation on U.S. data.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. and international TFP series and professional forecasts.

papers.title: The Pass-through of Tariffs and Exchange Rates

authors.inst: École Nationale de la Statistique et de l'Analyse de l'Information

papers.summary: Under PCP a tariff is contractionary and worsens the trade balance, while under LCP it is expansionary and improves it, owing to differential exchange rate pass-through. In welfare terms the situation reverses, with a tariff under LCP lowering short-run welfare and possibly raising it under PCP.
papers.q: How does the invoicing currency change the short-run effect of tariffs?
papers.contribution: Compares the impact of a unilateral tariff under producer currency pricing, local currency pricing and dollar currency pricing.
papers.ident: Theory: open economy model with alternative invoicing regimes.

papers.title: Human capital consequences of expanding the supply of higher education institutions in a developing country

authors.inst: Universidad de la República de Uruguay
Universidad de la República de Uruguay
CAF – Development Bank of Latin America

papers.q: What are the human capital consequences of expanding the supply of higher education institutions in a developing country?
papers.summary: Studies the human capital consequences of expanding the supply of higher education institutions in a developing country, according to the title.

papers.title: Growth, Firm Scale, and the Energy Intensity of Production
papers.q: Why does energy intensity of production decline as economies grow?
papers.summary: The scale dependence arises from physical scaling laws and technology investment. As average firm size rises with growth, production becomes endogenously less energy-intensive, implying significant reductions in aggregate energy intensity as India grows.
papers.ident: Causal research design on Indian firm microdata with a general equilibrium model.
papers.contribution: Uses microdata from India and a causal research design to show energy expenditure shares fall steeply with firm scale, and builds a general equilibrium model.
papers.dataDetail: Indian firm-level microdata on energy expenditure.

papers.title: From Minor Ailments to Major Illnesses: A Practical Framework for Valuing Morbidity in Environmental Policy Analysis
papers.summary: The resulting WTP estimates significantly exceed commonly used cost-of-illness measures, suggesting undervaluation of health states in policy evaluations. Sensitivity analyses show variation consistent with that for the value of statistical life.
papers.contribution: Introduces a framework deriving willingness-to-pay estimates for health conditions using preference weights and a baseline condition with known WTP.
papers.q: How can morbidity be valued in environmental policy analysis when cost-of-illness and QALY approaches miss willingness to pay?
papers.ident: Calibration of willingness to pay for health states from preference weights and a baseline known WTP.
papers.dataDetail: Preference weights for health states and a baseline value of known WTP.

papers.title: Literature Review and Evidence Aggregation: a Toolkit for Applied Micro
papers.q: How can analysts summarize prior studies, predict effects in new contexts, and correct for selective publication?
papers.summary: Illustrated with examples from labor, public, behavioral, environmental and development economics, and some tools work even with only three prior studies. After correcting for selectivity, the mean effect is 12% to 21% of the simple mean, and a cookbook for meta-analysis is offered.
papers.ident: Econometric methodology for meta-analysis with selectivity correction.
papers.contribution: Provides a toolkit for summarizing literature, predicting effects in new contexts by reweighting prior estimates with covariates, and correcting selectivity bias.

papers.title: In Their Shoes: Empathy Through Information
papers.q: Can information about an outgroup amplify empathy and prosocial behavior when paired with a simulated experience?
papers.summary: Information enhances empathetic response and prosocial behavior when it increases perceived similarity to the protagonist. Eye-tracking shows information concentrates witnesses' gaze on the protagonist's struggles, tracing the effect to attention.
papers.ident: Randomized virtual reality and lab experiments with eye-tracking.
papers.contribution: Runs an immersive virtual reality experiment simulating the struggle of unauthorized migrants, replicated in controlled lab experiments with eye-tracking.
papers.dataDetail: Participants in a virtual reality experiment and lab experiments.

papers.title: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
papers.summary: Several market failures likely lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income. Customized housing mobility services with subsidized vouchers can help low-income families move to higher-opportunity areas, and place-based policies creating mixed-income neighborhoods appear to improve long-term outcomes.
papers.q: Why are mixed-income neighborhoods under-supplied given the causal effects of childhood neighborhoods?
papers.contribution: Reviews evidence on neighborhood effects and identifies missing markets for opportunity from capital market imperfections, spillovers, behavioral biases and search frictions.

papers.title: Racial Disparities in Education During and Following the Pandemic: Evidence in Connecticut through 2025
papers.q: How have racial disparities in education evolved during and after the pandemic in Connecticut?
papers.summary: The pandemic had persistent negative effects on test scores with substantial racial disparities, and middle school shows persistent increases in severe disciplinary incidents and disparities. Racial disparities in attendance and chronic absenteeism substantially recovered by 2024-25.
papers.contribution: Examines racial and ethnic disparities in test scores, absenteeism and discipline for K-12 students through the 2024-25 school year.
papers.ident: Descriptive: trends in disparities before and after the pandemic.
papers.dataDetail: Connecticut K-12 test scores, absenteeism and discipline data through 2024-25.

papers.title: The Labor Market Value of Community College Bachelor’s Degrees: Initial Evidence from a Resume Audit Study in Early Childhood Education
papers.q: How do employers value community college bachelor's degrees in early childhood education?
papers.summary: Fictitious applications were submitted to real job vacancies to test how employers value credentials from community college baccalaureate programs. The pilot study examines callbacks across credential types.
papers.contribution: Conducts the first resume audit study of community college baccalaureate degrees, varying credentials, institutions and demographic signals.
papers.ident: Resume audit study with randomized credentials on fictitious applications to real vacancies.
papers.dataDetail: Fictitious applications to early childhood education job vacancies.

papers.title: Seemingly Anchored Inflation Expectations
papers.summary: Prolonged low short-run inflation persistence in pre-COVID decades makes long-run expectations insensitive to surprises, matching anchoring tests. The model has unique predictions that distinguish it from true anchoring.
papers.ident: Theory: experience-based learning model compared with anchoring tests.
papers.q: Can experience-based learning explain seemingly anchored inflation expectations without anchoring to a target?
papers.contribution: Shows evidence usually cited for anchored expectations is consistent with a model where individuals learn only from their lifetime history of realized inflation.
papers.dataDetail: Inflation expectations survey and realized inflation data.

papers.title: Competition and Misconduct in Certification Markets with Externalities
papers.summary: Misreporting emerges as soon as competition is introduced. Delegating each market to a single agent reduces approval rates without compromising service quality or ex-ante competition for the market, and delivers substantial and permanent reductions in vehicle emissions.
papers.q: How does competition among private inspectors lead to misreporting in vehicle certification markets?
papers.contribution: Combines theory with evidence from Chile's concentrated vehicle-inspection markets.
papers.ident: Theory and comparison of competitive versus single-agent inspection market regimes in Chile.
papers.dataDetail: Chilean vehicle inspection data on approval rates and emissions.

papers.title: Causal Inference for Asset Pricing
papers.summary: Cross-sectional IV and difference-in-differences identify relative elasticity, own-minus-cross price elasticity for assets sharing observables. A missing-coefficient problem leaves substitution unidentified, which requires time-series regressions on portfolios sorted on observables, applied to corporate bonds and Fed asset-purchase programs.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: identification of demand elasticity and substitution under homogeneous substitution; applied to Fed corporate bond purchases.
papers.contribution: Characterizes natural experiments identifying demand elasticity and price impact under homogeneous substitution conditional on observables.
papers.q: How can natural experiments identify asset demand elasticities and substitution when portfolio choice spans many assets?
papers.dataDetail: Corporate bond data and Fed asset-purchase programs.

papers.title: Multinational network restructuring, geopolitical exposure, and home country effects – Evidence for European MNEs
papers.q: How do European multinationals restructure their networks given geopolitical exposure and home country effects?
papers.summary: Studies multinational network restructuring, geopolitical exposure and home country effects for European multinationals, according to the title.

papers.title: How Do People React to Income-Based Fines? Evidence from Speeding Tickets Discontinuities
papers.q: How do people react to income-based fines, as seen in speeding tickets in Finland?
papers.summary: Speeding distributions are smooth at the cutoff, with no bunching below the fine hike. Fines about 200 euros larger decrease reoffending by 15% in the following six months, driven by high-income individuals facing the highest fine.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity at the income-dependent fine threshold of 20 km/h over the limit.
papers.contribution: Uses a regression discontinuity at the 20 km/h threshold where Finnish speeding tickets become income dependent.
papers.dataDetail: Finnish speeding ticket data.

papers.title: The expenditure elasticity for food and calories: Evidence from unconditional cash transfers in Kenya
papers.q: What is the expenditure elasticity of food and calories among extremely poor households?
papers.summary: The elasticity of food expenditure is 0.86 and of calories 0.66, higher than in many previous studies, plausibly because households are extremely poor, but significantly lower than non-experimental estimates in the same context.
papers.ident: Randomized cash transfers as exogenous variation in household budgets.
papers.contribution: Uses exogenous budget variation from two unconditional cash transfer programs in rural Kenya with detailed food expenditure, nutrition and price data.
papers.dataDetail: Two unconditional cash transfer programs in rural Kenya with food expenditure and nutrition data.

papers.title: What is core inflation?
papers.summary: Ex food and energy and other core measures are superior predictors than headline itself. Simple averaging across measures and horizons works best, and the averaging estimator also fares well on closeness to a common trend and measuring demand-driven inflation.
papers.q: What is core inflation, and which measures best predict future headline inflation?
papers.contribution: Assesses competing measures of core inflation, including new ones, taking the view that core inflation is a simple predictor of headline inflation.
papers.ident: Forecast comparison of core inflation measures.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. headline and core inflation measures.

papers.title: Managing Monetary Policy Normalization
papers.q: How should central banks manage normalization of rates and balance sheets after a liquidity trap?
papers.summary: Optimal balance sheet size depends on private reserve demand, fiscal interactions and liquidity management. After a liquidity trap shock, optimal policy expands reserves at the lower bound, starts quantitative tightening before rate liftoff, and normalizes rates and reserves together.
papers.ident: Theory: monetary model with a liquidity channel and optimal balance sheet policy.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework where liquidity conditions shape aggregate demand through a liquidity channel so reserves act as an independent instrument alongside interest rates.

papers.title: Subjective Earnings Risk

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.q: How large is subjective earnings risk when quitting or being fired is allowed?
papers.summary: Job transitions are the key drivers of subjective risk. Subjective earnings risk varies systematically across the population, is many times smaller than traditional estimates, and can help explain why many hold limited liquid assets.
papers.contribution: Introduces a survey instrument measuring earnings risk with job transitions and links it with administrative data for credibility checks.
papers.ident: New survey instrument linked to administrative earnings data.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of subjective earnings risk linked to administrative data.

papers.title: Trust, business group verticality, and firm productivity
papers.q: How does trust among owners and affiliates shape business group verticality and firm productivity?
papers.summary: Higher verticality is associated with higher firm productivity, and groups with higher average trust are more vertically structured. More trustworthy affiliates sit closer to the ultimate owner and are more productive, robust to using somatic distance as an instrument for trust.
papers.ident: Instrumental variable using somatic distance as an instrument for bilateral trust, with a theoretical model.
papers.contribution: Builds a model of trust and group structure and a novel dataset extending Amadeus ownership links into ownership chains for a large European sample.
papers.dataDetail: Amadeus ownership links extended into ownership chains for a European sample.

papers.title: Exorbitant Privilege of the Periodic Table? Geoeconomics, Endogenous Centrality and Strategic Minerals for the Green Transition
papers.summary: Trade in these materials reorganized into a hub-and-spoke system centered on China, unlike the more diffuse structure for fossil fuels, even though China holds few reserves. Centrality was built through processing investment, industrial policy and development finance, and can translate into pricing power.
papers.ident: Descriptive trade network analysis with a stylized model of endogenous centrality.
papers.q: How did China become the hub of the trade network in electrification metals, and does centrality confer pricing power?
papers.contribution: Uses bilateral trade data for 13 electrification metals over 1995-2023 and a stylized model in which a country chooses how central to become.
papers.dataDetail: Bilateral trade data for 13 electrification metals, 1995-2023.

papers.title: Introduction by the Editor
papers.summary: The issue includes a methodological paper developing efficient climate emulators embedded in economic models. Papers span dimensions of heterogeneity in the effects of climate change and mitigation, notably carbon taxes, and show that distributional consequences depend on policy design.
papers.contribution: Introduces a special issue of papers on dynamic, spatial and heterogeneous-agent structural modelling of climate change and climate policy.
papers.q: What does a special issue on climate change and inequality in structural models contribute?

papers.title: A Word of WARN-ing: Advance Notice of Layoffs and Labor Market Outcomes
papers.q: Do state WARN Acts improve labor market outcomes after layoffs?
papers.summary: State WARN adoption raises the likelihood of 30+ days of notice by about 4 percentage points, and lengthy notice reduces immediate joblessness by 4 to 7 percentage points, most for low-skill workers. Longer-term outcomes are less robust.
papers.ident: IV using state WARN Act adoption, supplemented with local average response functions.
papers.contribution: Studies state-level Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Acts with instrumental variables and local average response functions to address weak instruments.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. displaced worker data, 1993-2019.

papers.title: College Majors and Earnings Growth
papers.q: How do college majors affect earnings growth?
papers.summary: Studies college majors and earnings growth, according to the title.

papers.title: Social learning in agriculture: A scalable farmer-to-farmer extension approach for dairy farmers

authors.inst: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement
Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement
Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.q: Can a farmer-to-farmer extension approach scale social learning among dairy farmers?
papers.summary: Studies a scalable farmer-to-farmer extension approach for social learning among dairy farmers, according to the title.

papers.title: Geography versus income: The heterogeneous effects of carbon taxation

authors.inst: Institut National de la Statistique et des Etudes Economiques

papers.q: How do the effects of carbon taxation differ by geography and income?
papers.summary: Studies the heterogeneous effects of carbon taxation across geography and income, according to the title.

papers.title: Shaping forecast models for arbitrary choice of bandwidth
papers.q: How can forecast models be shaped for an arbitrary choice of bandwidth?
papers.summary: Studies shaping forecast models for arbitrary choice of bandwidth, according to the title.

papers.title: The Effect of Financial Resources on Fertility: Evidence from Administrative Data on Lottery Winners
papers.q: Do financial windfalls from lottery wins raise fertility?
papers.summary: A substantial win significantly increases fertility with an implied wealth elasticity of around 0.06, mainly through first births among the previously childless. About 25% of the effect stems from increased marriage rates.
papers.ident: Triple-differences around lottery prize winnings.
papers.contribution: Uses wealth shocks from lottery prizes among over 0.4 million winners in Taiwan with a triple-differences design.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative panels covering over 0.4 million lottery winners in Taiwan.

papers.title: Nobel Lecture: The Economics of Creative Destruction
papers.q: How does creative destruction drive economic growth?
papers.summary: Nobel Lecture on the economics of creative destruction, according to the title.

papers.title: Nobel Lecture: Creative Destruction and Economic Growth
papers.q: How does creative destruction drive economic growth?
papers.summary: Nobel Lecture on creative destruction and economic growth, according to the title.

papers.title: The Effect of High-Tech Clusters on the Productivity of Top Inventors: Comment
papers.summary: The original event study does not use variation from inventors moving across cities, and the instrument was constructed incorrectly. The corrected analysis finds null effects, so the reported elasticity may not be causal.
papers.ident: Corrected event study and instrument for the effect of cluster size on inventor patenting.
papers.q: Is the reported causal elasticity between technology cluster size and inventor patenting robust to correcting a coding error?
papers.contribution: Runs a corrected event study using inventors moving across cities and fixes a coding error in the instrument of Moretti (2021).
papers.dataDetail: Patent data on top inventors across cities.

papers.title: The Aggregate Costs of Uninsurable Business Risk
papers.q: How large are the aggregate costs of uninsurable business risk?
papers.summary: Because firms can limit risk by operating at a smaller scale, the model predicts large macroeconomic losses from uninsurable risk, much larger than those from credit constraints. Self-financing lets entrepreneurs overcome credit constraints quickly, yet even wealthy entrepreneurs remain exposed to risk.
papers.contribution: Documents large fat-tailed transitory fluctuations in private firms' profit shares using firm-level data and interprets them with a model of entrepreneurial dynamics.
papers.ident: Structural: model of entrepreneurial dynamics calibrated to firm-level profit share fluctuations.
papers.dataDetail: Firm-level data on private businesses.

papers.title: Market Opacity and Fragility: Why Liquidity Evaporates When It Is Most Needed
papers.summary: This produces strategic complementarities and multiple equilibria, so an initial dearth of liquidity can turn into a liquidity rout as in a flash crash. Greater order flow transparency or more dealers present at all times raises total welfare.
papers.q: Why does market liquidity evaporate when it is most needed?
papers.contribution: Models how lack of market transparency impairs liquidity provision by nonstandard suppliers and makes liquidity demand increase in illiquidity.
papers.ident: Theory: market microstructure model with opacity and multiple equilibria.

papers.title: Nobel Lecture: The Past and Future of Innovation: Can Progress Be Sustained?
papers.q: Can innovation-driven progress be sustained?
papers.summary: Nobel Lecture on the past and future of innovation and whether progress can be sustained, according to the title.

papers.title: Understanding High-Wage Firms: Monopoly, Monopsony, and Bargaining Power
papers.summary: The model reveals challenges in estimating monopsony and bargaining power and proposes an alternative approach. It shows that passthrough of firm shocks to wages depends on the shock type, how markups shape wage premia, and how stronger worker bargaining power affects wages and welfare.
papers.q: How do firm market power and worker bargaining power shape wages and welfare?
papers.contribution: Documents wage and market power patterns in French micro-data and builds a model with vertically differentiated goods and profit sharing with workers.
papers.ident: Structural: model of vertically differentiated goods and rent sharing estimated on French micro-data.
papers.dataDetail: French firm-level micro-data.

papers.title: U.S. liquid government liabilities and emerging market capital flows
papers.q: How does the liquidity of U.S. government liabilities affect capital flows to emerging markets?
papers.summary: QE increases liquidity, giving investors assurance that part of their portfolio can be sold readily, so they are more willing to invest in illiquid emerging market loans.
papers.contribution: Provides new evidence that U.S. and other rich-country investment in emerging markets rises under QE and reverses under tightening, and proposes a liquidity-based theory.
papers.ident: Theory and panel evidence linking Fed QE and tightening to emerging market capital flows.
papers.dataDetail: Capital flows from the U.S. and high-income countries to emerging markets.

papers.title: Ideological Alignment and Evidence-Based Policy Adoption
papers.q: Does the ideological alignment of the messenger affect whether policymakers adopt evidence-based policies?
papers.summary: Policy adoption rises 65 percent when informing institutions align ideologically with policymakers. Think tanks and media outlets are equally effective when aligned, and the paper explores information exposure, belief updating and implementation as channels.
papers.ident: Nationwide randomized trial varying the ideology of the sender of policy information.
papers.contribution: Runs a nationwide RCT with ideologically opposite think tanks, newspapers and a research institution to communicate a cost-effective policy to local policymakers.
papers.dataDetail: Local policymakers contacted by think tanks, major newspapers and a research institution.

papers.title: The Return to College, Marriage, and Intergenerational Mobility
papers.q: Does a rising return to college reduce intergenerational mobility by changing marriage and parental investment?
papers.summary: Educated mothers in states with larger return increases are more likely to be married, less likely to divorce, have more educated spouses and own more valuable houses. Their children also have relatively higher 8th grade test scores and college completion rates.
papers.contribution: Studies how increases in the return to education by state affect educated mothers' marriage and investments relative to less-educated mothers.
papers.ident: Comparison of educated and less-educated mothers across states with different increases in the return to education.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. state-level data on mothers, marital status and children's test scores.

papers.title: The Effect of Omitted Variables on the Sign of Regression Coefficients
papers.q: Is it easier for omitted variables to flip a coefficient's sign than to drive it to zero?
papers.summary: Whenever the delta is large, suggesting omitted variables are unimportant, a much smaller value reverses the sign of the parameter. The methods are illustrated in four empirical applications and two meta-analyses.
papers.contribution: Shows the behavior of Oster's delta and proposes a modified robustness measure, with a companion Stata module regsensitivity.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: sensitivity analysis of regression coefficients to omitted variables.

papers.title: University Research and the Market for Higher Education
papers.q: How does competition for students and tuition drive university research?
papers.summary: When students are highly stratified across colleges or tuition rises sharply with rank, universities spend on R&D even if its contribution to teaching is small, explaining internally funded research despite negligible patent returns. Calibrated simulations suggest tuition policies boost university research while research subsidies crowd it out.
papers.ident: Structural: model of university competition for students, calibrated to microdata.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework where university research depends endogenously on competition in the market for higher education.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. university-level data on research, tuition and students.

papers.title: MCA: High-dimensional modal component analysis towards the mode
papers.q: How can modal component analysis be performed in high dimensions?
papers.summary: Studies high-dimensional modal component analysis toward the mode, according to the title.

papers.title: Dynamic Individuals, Static Neighborhoods: Migration and Earnings Changes in Poor Neighborhoods
papers.q: Why do poor neighborhoods stay poor despite their residents' earnings growth?
papers.summary: Many residents of poor neighborhoods have persistently low earnings, while a large number experience sizable growth and move to richer areas. Earnings increases cause upward moves, so selective migration depresses growth of poor neighborhoods' average earnings by roughly 60 percent.
papers.ident: Idiosyncratic firm-specific pay changes as variation for earnings-induced moves.
papers.contribution: Uses administrative data linking residential histories to longitudinal earnings and estimates causal sorting from firm-specific pay changes.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative data linking residential histories to longitudinal earnings.

papers.title: Labor Market Responses to Tariffs: Frictions, Dynamics, and Policy Responses
papers.summary: Effects of trade shocks differ across industries, regions and occupations and evolve slowly, implying important adjustment frictions and the need for dynamic frameworks. The review discusses policies mitigating costs to workers and sharing the gains from trade more equitably.
papers.contribution: Reviews the evidence and modeling frameworks on trade and labor markets, emphasizing labor-market frictions and adjustment dynamics.
papers.q: How do labor markets adjust to tariffs and trade shocks, and what policies help workers?

papers.title: Selection, Structural Transformation, and the Cost Disease of Services

authors.inst: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.summary: Reallocated workers earn more than incumbents in professional services but less than incumbents in education, health and public services. The selection effect on professional services productivity growth is 10 percentage points higher than in a conventional model, but contributes little overall to the cost disease.
papers.contribution: Documents earnings of workers reallocated from manufacturing relative to incumbents and builds a generalized quantitative Roy model.
papers.q: Does selection into sectors explain the cost disease of services?
papers.ident: Structural: generalized Roy model of sector selection estimated with U.S. data.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. worker-level data on sector transitions and earnings.

papers.title: Strategic Simplicity in Multidimensional Screening
papers.q: What strategically simple mechanisms exist for multidimensional screening with status-quo rights?
papers.summary: Static OSP mechanisms take the form of polarized-ray mechanisms in which agents choose from menus of narrowly defined veto rights along differentiated directions of trade. For general extensive-form games the characterization retains much of the polarized-ray structure, before turning to a more demanding notion of simplicity.
papers.ident: Theory: obvious strategy-proofness in multidimensional screening.
papers.contribution: Characterizes obviously strategy-proof mechanisms for allocating heterogeneous items when each agent can demand a status-quo assignment.

papers.title: Openness, Integration, and the International Monetary Order
papers.q: How do trade and financial policy configurations reshape the hierarchy of global currencies?
papers.summary: Tariffs reduce effective size on the goods side and capital controls on the financial side. The economy with the deepest integration in the global trading network keeps the largest safety premium and gains anchor status, and the model evaluates policy levers for the euro.
papers.ident: Structural: calibrated general equilibrium model of currency hierarchy.
papers.contribution: Develops a calibrated general-equilibrium model where currency safety and anchor status arise from an economy's effective size in setting world prices.

papers.title: Government Funding Costs Under Financial Repression
papers.q: How does financial repression affect government funding costs?
papers.summary: When fiscal policy is profligate and monetary policy accommodates, repression raises bond values, reduces the inflationary cost of unfunded expansions and lowers risk premia, but bondholders pay a lower inflation tax and earn lower future real returns. When monetary policy does not accommodate, repression can provide stopgap deficit funding.
papers.ident: Theory: endowment economy with limited participation and a repression policy rule.
papers.contribution: Studies repression policies in an endowment economy with limited asset market participation through a wedge in the Euler equation and fiscal redistribution.

papers.title: The Economic Consequences of Effective Carbon Taxes
papers.q: What are the macroeconomic and sectoral consequences of effective carbon taxes in the Nordic countries?
papers.summary: Carbon taxes reduce emissions as expected but also impair macroeconomic activity, with some heterogeneity across sectors and countries.
papers.ident: Local projections of emissions and activity on a new effective carbon tax measure.
papers.contribution: Constructs a novel monthly measure of effective carbon tax rates accounting for time-varying emission coverage of explicit and implicit taxes, and uses it in local projections.
papers.dataDetail: Monthly effective carbon tax rates for four Nordic countries.

papers.title: An Analytical Model of Behavior and Policy in an Epidemic
papers.q: How do individually optimal and socially optimal behavior differ during an epidemic?
papers.summary: Individually optimal behavior is excessively cautious, flattening the curve and prolonging the epidemic. Socially optimal behavior results in a higher infection rate focused on minimizing cumulative deaths at minimum cost.
papers.contribution: Analytically characterizes optimal mitigation by susceptible individuals and the resulting equilibrium trajectory, using a phase diagram.
papers.ident: Theory: tractable equilibrium epidemic model with optimal mitigation.

papers.title: Pricing and Production Without the Invisible Hand
papers.q: How do pricing and production work when firms choose both prices and quantities without market clearing?
papers.summary: Markups are governed by the probability of rationing rather than demand elasticity, and higher uncertainty reduces production and increases markups. The model marries Old and New Keynesian traditions with rational expectations.
papers.ident: Theory: macro model with rationing and Walrasian disequilibrium.
papers.contribution: Develops a macroeconomic model where firms choose prices and quantities optimally and markets are generically in Walrasian disequilibrium, slack or rationed.

papers.title: Immigration, Innovation, and the Geography of Growth
papers.q: How did the 1880-1920 mass immigration shape U.S. innovation and regional growth?
papers.summary: Immigrants disproportionately settled in urban innovation hubs. Arrivals after 1880 raised U.S. income per capita by 8.2% by 1940, and removing the 1920s restrictions would have raised it a further 1.7% by 2000.
papers.contribution: Builds a dataset linking census records to immigration records and the universe of U.S. patents, and a spatial growth model with skill sorting.
papers.ident: Structural: spatial growth model with skilled sorting, calibrated to linked census and patent data.
papers.dataDetail: Linked census, immigration records and the universe of U.S. patents, 1880-1940.

papers.title: Wealth Inequality and Safe Asset Demand
papers.q: How does wealth inequality shape safe-asset demand and the emergence of bubbles?
papers.summary: This generates bubbles even under stationary wealth distributions with no aggregate uncertainty or growth, unlike classic rational bubbles. Prior pricing analyses of aggregate assets may be incomplete because they overlook possible violations of the transversality condition.
papers.ident: Theory: heterogeneous-agent economy with extreme poverty risk and safe assets.
papers.contribution: Shows that assets insulated from idiosyncratic risk become infinitely valuable when agents face sufficiently high probabilities of extreme poverty.

papers.title: The Fragility of Semi-Liquid Private Credit Funds
papers.q: How fragile are semi-liquid private credit funds to investor redemptions?
papers.summary: Cash buffers and loan repayments cannot fund repeated 5% redemptions, inflows decline when outflows rise, and outflows are met with loan sales, borrowing and delayed repurchase payments. Strategic complementarity arises because redemptions impose liquidation and leverage costs on remaining investors.
papers.contribution: Studies funds with over $300 billion in assets that hold illiquid loans but allow quarterly redemptions at NAV, typically capped at 5% of shares.
papers.ident: Panel analysis of fund flows, liquidity buffers and redemptions.
papers.dataDetail: Fund-level data on semi-liquid private credit funds.

papers.title: Prices Versus Quantities Revisited: What Do Policymakers Need to Know to Set Pigouvian Taxes and Subsidies?
papers.q: What information do policymakers need to set Pigouvian taxes and subsidies?
papers.summary: Standard logic says the size of the externality suffices, but this fails with fixed costs, deadweight losses or distributional concerns.
papers.contribution: Presents a model showing that learning about equilibrium quantities can be valuable if interventions have fixed costs, deadweight losses or distributional concerns, applied to congestion pricing and a Boston housing subsidy.
papers.ident: Theory: prices versus quantities model with fixed costs and distribution, applied to two policies.

papers.title: Compensation vs. Reinforcement: Experimental Identification of Parental Aversion to Inequality in Offspring
papers.q: Do parents compensate disadvantaged children or reinforce those with higher expected returns?
papers.summary: Transfers raised short-run attendance of treated students but untreated siblings were 3.7 percentage points less likely to graduate from college, about 30 percent below the control mean. The estimated model implies limited parental aversion to inequality in children's outcomes.
papers.ident: Student-level randomized cash transfers with sibling spillovers and a dynamic structural model.
papers.contribution: Uses a conditional cash transfer experiment randomized at the student level to create sibling variation in transfers, with a dynamic household schooling model.
papers.dataDetail: Households with siblings in a conditional cash transfer experiment.

papers.title: International Risk-Sharing in a Fragmented World
papers.q: How does geopolitical risk shape financial fragmentation and international risk sharing?
papers.summary: When geopolitical risk is high, bilateral lending increasingly follows geopolitical alignment. Aligned countries face more synchronized shocks, so fragmentation limits the effectiveness of international risk sharing.
papers.contribution: Uses bilateral official lending data from 1910 to 2024 and a limited-commitment model of sovereign borrowing with geopolitical considerations.
papers.ident: Panel analysis of lending and geopolitical alignment, with a limited-commitment model.
papers.dataDetail: Bilateral official lending data, 1910-2024.

papers.title: Fragmentation of Shareholder Power
papers.q: Does fund proliferation and decentralized stewardship fragment shareholder power and weaken governance?
papers.summary: Fund proliferation does not necessarily weaken governance, since stronger manager incentives and concentrated portfolios of specialized funds can offset the effects, especially when preferences are intense. Strong preferences can also lead managers to compete by granting investors control through pass-through voting.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework to evaluate trade-offs of tailored portfolios, fund proliferation and decentralized stewardship driven by heterogeneous investor preferences.
papers.ident: Theory: model of asset manager stewardship and investor preference heterogeneity.

papers.title: The effects of immigration on agricultural development
papers.q: Did immigration contribute to agricultural development in Brazil during the Age of Mass Migration?
papers.summary: A greater share of European immigrants led to higher farm values in 1920, mainly through more intense cultivation of land. It is unlikely that immigration slowed Brazil's structural transformation.
papers.contribution: Instruments a municipality's immigrant share with the interaction of aggregate inflows and railway network expansion.
papers.ident: Instrument combining aggregate immigrant inflows with railway network expansion.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian municipality-level data, 1855-1920.

papers.title: Chronic depression, child development and human capital among the forcibly displaced: Evidence from Syrian refugees
papers.q: How do chronic maternal depression, child development and human capital interact among Syrian refugees?
papers.summary: Studies chronic depression, child development and human capital among forcibly displaced Syrian refugees, according to the title.

papers.title: Fostering Cooperation: The Conflict-Reducing Effects of Intervillage Competition for Government Transfers

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: Does competition between villages for government transfers reduce conflict within villages?
papers.summary: Higher competition for transfers reduces within-village conflict regardless of the competition's outcome, with stronger effects in ethnically fractionalized and segregated villages, along with higher attendance at village meetings.
papers.ident: Triple-differences on village competition for national government transfers.
papers.contribution: Uses a triple-differences design on intergroup competition for national transfers in Indonesia.
papers.dataDetail: Indonesian village-level data on conflict and transfers.

papers.title: Equity and efficiency when needs differ
papers.summary: A dilemma between holding households responsible for their needs and compensating them is of first-order importance for social welfare but plays a minor role in inequality measurement. The criteria are ready to use for analyzing redistributive policies.
papers.contribution: Introduces partial compensation and axiomatically characterizes new families of welfare criteria, with extension to multidimensional commodity spaces.
papers.q: How should social welfare and inequality be measured when households have different needs?
papers.ident: Theory: axiomatic characterization of welfare criteria with heterogeneous needs.

papers.title: onetary Economics at 30: A Reexamination of the Relevance of Money in Cashless Limiting Monetary Economies
papers.summary: The result breaks down when the microstructure allows an endogenous interest rate and market power in credit intermediation, which should give pause to basing monetary policy advice on models without money.
papers.q: Is money irrelevant for monetary transmission in cashless limiting economies?
papers.contribution: Reexamines Woodford's (1998) cashless-limiting result and shows it relies on a peculiar credit-market structure with perfectly competitive, zero-interest deferred payment arrangements.
papers.ident: Theory: monetary model with credit intermediation and market power.

papers.title: Skill-Replacing Technology and Bottom-Half Inequality
papers.summary: The model explains why middle wages declined despite routine workers being dispersed across the bottom half, why the decline stopped while technology kept advancing, and why average routine wages did not fall. It predicts a falling return to skill and falling skill in routine occupations, confirmed with an interactive fixed-effects model.
papers.ident: Theory with interactive fixed-effects tests of predictions on skill returns and skill levels.
papers.q: Why did middle wages decline and then stop declining under routine-biased technological change?
papers.contribution: Proposes a model of skill-replacing routine-biased technical change where technology substitutes for skill in routine tasks rather than for workers.
papers.dataDetail: U.S. worker wage and occupation data.

papers.title: Censored partial linear quantile regression with endogeneity
papers.q: How can censored partial linear quantile regression handle endogeneity?
papers.summary: Studies censored partial linear quantile regression with endogeneity, according to the title.

papers.title: Nonlinear Pricing in Oligopoly: How Brand Preferences Shape Market Outcomes

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Escola Brasileira de Economia e Finanças

papers.q: How do brand preferences shape nonlinear pricing in oligopoly?
papers.summary: Depending on whether low types are more or less brand-switching than high types, quality is inefficiently low at the bottom or high at the top, and information rents change sign by type. More competing firms may decrease welfare, so much that monopoly may be welfare superior, and pure-strategy equilibria fail to exist.
papers.contribution: Studies oligopolistic second-degree price discrimination with consumers' propensity to switch brands varying with taste for quality.
papers.ident: Theory: oligopoly screening with type-dependent brand switching.

papers.title: What Causes Geographic Variation in Drug Prescribing? Evidence from Physician Migration

authors.inst: The University of Texas at San Antonio

papers.q: How much of geographic variation in prescription drug spending is due to individual physicians?
papers.summary: Movers' prescribing converges toward the average of their new location but far from completely. Physician-specific factors explain about 60 to 70 percent of cross-sectional variation in spending.
papers.contribution: Tracks prescribing before and after physician relocations in Medicare Part D.
papers.ident: Mover design comparing prescribing of physicians before and after relocation.
papers.dataDetail: Medicare Part D prescribing data.

papers.title: Cash transfer at birth reduces criminal activity of fathers and children
papers.q: Does a cash transfer at birth reduce criminal activity of fathers and children?
papers.summary: Studies the effect of a cash transfer at birth on criminal activity of fathers and children, according to the title.

papers.title: Cleaner but Volatile Energy? The Effect of Coal Plant Retirement on Market Competition in the Wholesale Electricity Market
papers.summary: The variable marginal cost of gas generation creates an environment where market power could increase after the transition. The adverse impact is mitigated under a well-planned transition leading to a more competitive industry structure.
papers.q: Does coal plant retirement and the switch to gas increase market power in wholesale electricity?
