papers.contribution: Uses counterfactual analysis of several transition paths that differ in which firms retire coal and invest in gas.
papers.ident: Structural: counterfactual simulation of wholesale electricity competition under transition paths.
papers.dataDetail: Wholesale electricity market data.

papers.title: Threshold spatial panel regression with fixed effects
papers.q: How can threshold regression be applied to spatial panel models with fixed effects?
papers.summary: Studies threshold spatial panel regression with fixed effects, according to the title.

papers.title: Do Wage Floors Increase Employment Risk for Workers with Disabilities? Evidence from Minimum Wage Increases and Subminimum Wage Repeal
papers.q: Do minimum wage increases and subminimum wage repeal reduce employment for workers with disabilities?
papers.summary: There is little evidence that minimum wage increases reduce employment or participation of people with disabilities, including severe disabilities, and confidence intervals generally rule out economically meaningful negative effects. Terminating subminimum wages does not reduce employment opportunities.
papers.contribution: Examines state minimum wage increases and subminimum wage terminations with American Community Survey data from 2010-2023.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences using state minimum wage increases and subminimum wage terminations.
papers.dataDetail: American Community Survey, 2010-2023.

papers.title: How Climate Shocks Produce Armed Rebellion: The 1970 Bhola Cyclone and the Birth of Bangladesh
papers.q: How do climate shocks produce armed rebellion, as in the 1970 Bhola cyclone?
papers.summary: Cyclone exposure amplified separatist voting and increased participation in guerrilla warfare, inducing an additional 48,613 insurgents. Effects are larger where grievances are pre-existing and relief provision weaker.
papers.contribution: Combines satellite imagery, archival records, electoral returns and insurgent biographies to study the cyclone that killed about 350,000 in East Pakistan.
papers.ident: Variation in cyclone exposure from satellite imagery, with electoral returns and insurgent biographies.
papers.dataDetail: Satellite imagery, archival records, electoral returns and insurgent biographies for East Pakistan, 1970-1971.

papers.title: An Informational Rationale for Viewpoint Neutrality in Education
papers.summary: When students' actions reflect teacher-side information correlated across peers, observing many such actions can give it excessive social weight. A planner may optimally reduce instruction precision, and the case for a cap is stronger when peer interaction is homophilous.
papers.q: Can limiting the precision of instruction improve students' decisions when they learn socially from peers?
papers.contribution: Models students who learn from teachers, outside information and peers, showing privately Bayesian actions need not be optimal inputs into social learning.
papers.ident: Theory: social learning model with correlated teacher information.

papers.title: Elderly Health and Longevity in the US: Evidence and Implications
papers.q: How have declining elderly mortality and morbidity affected Social Security and Medicare finances?
papers.summary: Demographic changes raised expected lifetime Social Security spending by 14%, over twice the 6% for Medicare. The added 2.4 years of life expectancy were entirely healthy, and time with severe limitations fell by about 30%, reducing nursing-home and home-health use.
papers.contribution: Uses nearly three decades of Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey data (1992-2019) to estimate changes in expected lifetime spending.
papers.ident: Descriptive: lifetime spending decomposition by health status, with a stylized model.
papers.dataDetail: Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey, 1992-2019.

papers.title: The Short- and Long-Run Effects of Railroads on Mexico-US Migration
papers.summary: Locations with railroad access had migration rates four times higher in the early twentieth century, through sequential migration first to rail hubs and then to the US. Railroad access also raised urbanization and development, and today such locations have weakly lower migration rates.
papers.ident: IV based on least-cost paths between historical cities for railroad access.
papers.contribution: Uses an IV strategy based on least-cost paths between historical cities to estimate the effect of railroad access.
papers.q: How did railroads in early 1900s Mexico affect migration to the United States, in the short and long run?
papers.dataDetail: Mexican railroad network and migration data, early 1900s to early 21st century.

papers.title: Planning Capital and Discovery-Based Learning-by-Doing: Investment as Staged Discovery in the Hyperscale Era
papers.summary: The answers change what the firm knows and the cost of future inquiry, and successful histories carry over to related problems. The accumulated diagnostic understanding is called planning capital.
papers.q: How can frontier investment be understood as staged discovery that builds planning capital?
papers.contribution: Treats investment as a sequence of costly inquiry stages in which firms sharpen diagnostic understanding, choose questions, take costly actions and interpret answers.
papers.ident: Theory: staged discovery model of firm investment.

papers.title: The Search Costs of Inflation in the Labor Market
papers.q: What are the search costs of unanticipated inflation in the labor market?
papers.summary: Inflation reduces real wages under nominal contracts, so workers intensify on-the-job search, which is costly but moves workers to more productive matches. A COVID-sized inflation shock produces an average welfare loss of 0.44% of consumption, with top-wage workers losing over six times as much as bottom-wage workers.
papers.ident: Structural: calibrated job ladder model with nominal wage contracts and search effort.
papers.contribution: Extends the Postel-Vinay and Robin job ladder to a nominal environment with privately chosen search effort and calibrates it to pre-pandemic U.S. moments.
papers.dataDetail: Pre-pandemic U.S. labor market moments.

papers.title: Measuring Neural Engagement in High-Stakes Trading

authors.inst: East China University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Can wearable EEG measure neural engagement of professional day traders during high-stakes trading?
papers.summary: The index shows spike-and-decay patterns around execution, and more successful trades are preceded by larger spikes in the 30 seconds before execution, while baseline levels have no predictive power. Higher engagement is associated with attenuated behavioral biases.
papers.contribution: Reports a field study using wearable EEG to construct a psychophysiological Engagement Index around trade execution.
papers.ident: Field study linking EEG engagement dynamics to trade performance.
papers.dataDetail: Wearable EEG recordings from professional day traders during live trading.

papers.title: The Informed Insider: A Leading Measure of Quality
papers.q: Can employee reviews provide a forward-looking measure of firm product and service quality?
papers.summary: The indices vary meaningfully across firms and within firms over time and are validated against third-party customer satisfaction data used to train the models.
papers.ident: Machine learning on employee review text, validated against customer satisfaction measures.
papers.contribution: Trains machine learning models on over 4.3 million Glassdoor reviews to build quality indices for S&P 1500 firms for 2008-2023.
papers.dataDetail: Over 4.3 million Glassdoor reviews for S&P 1500 firms, 2008-2023.

papers.title: Shaping Major Choice: The Role of High School Counselors
papers.q: Can informing high school counselors about the economics major change students' major choices?
papers.summary: The study evaluates effects on students' major preferences and outcomes using application, admissions, enrollment and course-taking records. Economics is often misunderstood and underrepresents women and minorities.
papers.contribution: Randomly invites counselors from Texas high schools to a one-day workshop on the economics major and tracks students at a large public university.
papers.ident: Randomized invitation of school counselors to an information workshop.
papers.dataDetail: Application, admissions, enrollment and course-taking records at a large public university in Texas.

papers.title: AI Diffusion Gaps: Unequal Integration of AI Across K-12 Schools
papers.q: How unequal is the integration of generative AI across K-12 schools?
papers.summary: AI use has spread rapidly as a productivity aid, with students mainly using it for homework and writing and educators for lesson planning and administration. Teacher training, guidance and policies lag adoption, and the paper documents two diffusion gaps across schools.
papers.contribution: Reports an original national survey of K-12 school principals measuring institutional AI integration through policies, training, guidance, leadership and tools.
papers.ident: Descriptive: national survey of principals on AI integration.
papers.dataDetail: National survey of K-12 school principals.

papers.title: Air Pollution and Early Childhood Outcomes: Evidence from Georgia Childcare Providers
papers.q: Does air pollution reduce preschool attendance?
papers.summary: A one-unit increase in county-week average particulate pollution decreases attendance by around 2 percentage points. Effects seem larger for racial minorities and children with working parents.
papers.ident: Thermal inversions as an instrument for particulate pollution.
papers.contribution: Uses restricted Georgia administrative data and thermal inversions as an instrument for particulate matter.
papers.dataDetail: Restricted administrative childcare attendance data from Georgia.

papers.title: How Serious Are Experimenter Demand Effects? Evidence and Mitigation Strategies
papers.summary: Good design is normally sufficient to address demand concerns, and bounding works well when concerns remain. Existing evidence suggests that the potential impact of experimenter demand is limited.
papers.q: How serious are experimenter demand effects and how can they be mitigated?
papers.contribution: Provides an overview of design best practices and bounding techniques and summarizes recent empirical assessments of demand effects.

papers.title: US Monetary Spillovers, Foreign Exchange, and Gold Reserves at Times of Geopolitical Fragmentation
papers.q: Do larger foreign exchange and gold reserves dampen exchange rate responses to U.S. monetary policy?
papers.summary: Countries with larger dollar reserves show smaller depreciations after U.S. tightening, while non-dollar reserves do not, and gold reserves are also associated with smaller depreciations. Buffer effects concentrate in countries without swap and repo lines.
papers.contribution: Tests a reserve balance-sheet channel with high-frequency FOMC surprises, minute-level exchange rates and predetermined reserves for 18 countries.
papers.ident: High-frequency event study of exchange rates around FOMC surprises, interacted with predetermined reserve holdings.
papers.dataDetail: FOMC monetary surprises, minute-level exchange rates and reserve holdings for 18 countries.

papers.title: Paying for Quality vs. Paying for Rank: When Purifying a Metric Backfires
papers.q: When does making a performance metric less gameable backfire?
papers.summary: Where evaluations assign prices, partially purifying the metric raises gaming when gameable variation dominates, since market trust rises faster than exposure to gaming falls. Where they assign rank positions, purification never backfires and mean gaming falls monotonically.
papers.contribution: Solves two matching markets in closed form, one where evaluations assign prices and one where they assign positions by rank.
papers.ident: Theory: gaming of metrics in price-based and rank-based markets.

papers.title: What Happens to Contractors After States Ban Affirmative Action?
papers.summary: Bans led MWBE contractors to downsize gradually, most for Black-owned and larger firms, without higher shutdown rates. New MWBEs became relatively less common, and a calibrated model suggests bans act like large reductions in MWBE productivity and scrap values.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around state bans on affirmative action in contracting, with a calibrated model.
papers.q: What happens to minority- and women-owned contractors when states ban affirmative action in contracting?
papers.contribution: Uses restricted Census business records to study bans on affirmative action in state contracting.
papers.dataDetail: Restricted Census business records.

papers.title: Climate and Prehistoric Migration
papers.q: How did climate drive human migration in prehistoric Western Eurasia?
papers.summary: Migration declines with differences in growing degree days, precipitation and soil between origins and destinations. Farmers match on thermal and soil conditions and pastoralists on precipitation, and warming increases farmer expansion while cooling increases pastoral expansion.
papers.contribution: Develops a sorting framework where subsistence knowledge depreciates with ecological distance and uses ancient DNA identity-by-descent segments to build bilateral migration flows over 10,000 years.
papers.ident: Gravity-style analysis of ancient DNA migration flows with ecological distance.
papers.dataDetail: Ancient DNA identity-by-descent segments across Western Eurasia over 10,000 years.

papers.title: Trading Frictions in Dynamic Cap-and-Trade Markets

authors.inst: Libera Università Internazionale degli Studi Sociali Guido Carli

papers.q: How do multiple trading frictions interact in dynamic cap-and-trade markets?
papers.summary: Access choices are characterized in closed form and the equilibrium premium is unique. Endogenous access dampens the response to each friction in isolation, but multiple frictions interact non-additively and can amplify the price response.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic model of market access and intermediation, calibrated to EU ETS transactions.
papers.contribution: Develops a dynamic stochastic model of markets with an externality and frictions in participation, intermediation and information, quantified with 2.7 million EU ETS registry transactions.
papers.dataDetail: 2.7 million EU ETS registry transactions.

papers.title: Panel Attrition, Data Imputation and Age Patterns in Subjective Ill-being
papers.q: How does panel attrition affect the age profile of subjective ill-being?
papers.summary: Attrition is high, highest among the young and among wave 1 web interviewees. After adjusting, subjective ill-being declines with age in both waves, which would not be apparent from wave 2 regressions alone.
papers.ident: Attrition-adjusted estimates of age profiles using IPW, multiple imputation and LOCF.
papers.contribution: Applies inverse probability weighting, multiple imputation and last observation carried forward to the Global Flourishing Study.
papers.dataDetail: Global Flourishing Study, waves 1 and 2.

papers.title: Task-Specific Technical Change and Comparative Advantage

authors.inst: Centre de Recerca en Economia Internacional

papers.q: How does AI reshape workers' comparative advantage through task-specific technical change?
papers.summary: AI narrows wage inequality and raises average wages across scenarios from slow to rapid progress. The key equalizing force is simplification, as AI lowers tasks' skill requirements and lets lower-skilled workers perform them.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic task-based occupational choice model estimated on panel data.
papers.contribution: Develops a dynamic task-based model with multidimensional skills, occupational choice and on-the-job skill accumulation, and estimates it using panel data and a database of task-level skill requirements.
papers.dataDetail: Panel worker data and a new database of task-level skill requirements.

papers.title: Transportation Infrastructure and Urban and Regional Development
papers.contribution: Reviews the theoretical and empirical literature on transportation infrastructure and the distribution of people and activity across a system of cities.
papers.summary: Theory makes robust predictions for the internal structure of cities but permits much for systems of cities. City-level evidence shows improved urban transportation causes suburban migration with small impact on city population, while cross-country evidence on systems of cities remains underdeveloped.
papers.q: What does the literature say about how transportation infrastructure shapes urban and regional development?

papers.title: Price Discrimination With Manipulable Observables
papers.q: How does a seller's price discrimination change when buyers can manipulate the observables it uses?
papers.summary: With covert pricing, equilibrium market segmentation is always coarse, which limits price discrimination. With transparently posted prices, every buyer pays a personalized price, though this does not always reduce buyer or social welfare.
papers.contribution: Compares covert and transparently posted discriminatory pricing when buyers can manipulate observables at a cost.
papers.conclusion: Calls for transparency in how sellers use consumer data need care, and welfare assessments based only on observed prices, conduct and coverage can mislead.
papers.ident: Theory: price discrimination model with costly manipulation of observables.

papers.title: Recovering Within-Country Inequality from Trade Data
papers.q: Can a country's within-country inequality be recovered from what it imports?
papers.summary: If preferences are non-homothetic, rich and poor consumers buy different goods, so imports carry information on inequality. Global trade data allow a single comparable estimation for many countries over time, with good coverage of developing countries and robustness and cross-validation checks.
papers.contribution: Develops a method that infers the income distribution from import data using non-homothetic preferences.
papers.ident: Structural: non-homothetic demand model inverting import patterns into inequality measures.
papers.dataDetail: Global bilateral trade data for a large sample of countries over time.

papers.title: Peer Learning, Enforcement, and Reputation
papers.q: How does transparency among firms shape a regulator's enforcement reputation and firms' misconduct?
papers.summary: In the transparent setting, reputation concerns create positive or negative enforcement externalities between firms. When reputation concern is strong, negative externalities dominate and encourage misconduct, and otherwise both externalities are positive and deter it.
papers.contribution: Studies a two-period learning model in which firms test a regulator's enforcement propensity through misconduct, in transparent and opaque settings.
papers.conclusion: A strong reputation always benefits the regulator in the opaque setting but often backfires under transparency.
papers.ident: Theory: two-period reputation and learning model of regulation.

papers.title: More power outages, more CO2 emissions: Evidence from self-generation in China's manufacturing firms

authors.inst: Nanjing University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: Do power outages raise CO2 emissions through firms' self-generation in China?
papers.summary: The title indicates that more power outages increase CO2 emissions through self-generation of electricity by Chinese manufacturing firms.

papers.title: Bounding the Effect of Persuasion with Monotonicity Assumptions: Reassessing the Impact of TV Debates
papers.summary: Monotonicity assumptions are used to bound the persuasion rate and related parameters, and the method revisits earlier evidence on TV debates by Le Pennec and Pons. The sharp upper bounds on persuasive effects remain modest.
papers.contribution: Introduces a framework that partially identifies the persuasion rate without exogenous treatment, parallel trends or credible instruments.
papers.q: How large can the persuasive effect of televised debates be under plausible monotonicity assumptions?
papers.ident: Econometric theory: partial identification of the persuasion rate from monotonicity assumptions.
papers.dataDetail: Data from a prior study of presidential TV debates.

papers.title: Innovation, Patenting and Appropriability: Survey Evidence from a Nationally Representative Sample of U.S. Firms
papers.q: How do U.S. firms protect the rents from innovation, and how common is patenting?
papers.summary: Just 1.4 percent of firms obtain patents, but they account for 87 percent of R&D investment. Firms rate utility patents as less important than trade secrets, trademarks and copyrights, and industry and size, but not age, are strongly correlated with IP use.
papers.contribution: Documents stylized facts on intellectual property use from a nationally representative survey of U.S. businesses for 2008-2015.
papers.ident: Descriptive: stylized facts from a nationally representative firm survey.
papers.dataDetail: Nationally representative survey of U.S. businesses, 2008-2015.

papers.title: Can electric vehicles aid the renewable transition? Evidence from a field experiment incentivizing midday charging
papers.summary: Incentives to charge during solar hours raise charging by 34%, mostly outside the home, while incentives to reduce peak charging lower it by 17-27%, mostly at home. Participants respond by shifting time and location, driving less and lowering battery state-of-charge, with stronger midday responses for commuters and those with fast home chargers.
papers.ident: Randomized field experiment with time-based charging incentives.
papers.contribution: Runs a field experiment tracking 390 electric vehicles minute-by-minute with time-based charging incentives.
papers.q: Can time-based incentives shift electric vehicle charging toward midday solar generation?
papers.dataDetail: Minute-by-minute charging data for 390 electric vehicles.

papers.title: Building opportunity: the intergenerational effects of Chilean school construction
papers.q: Did Chilean school construction have intergenerational effects on opportunity?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the intergenerational effects of school construction in Chile.

papers.title: Central bank communication by ??? The economics of monetary policy leaks
papers.summary: Eurosystem leaks are frequent relative to other major central banks, and many appear strategically placed by insiders. High-frequency market reactions to leaks are large relative to standard monetary surprises, often exceeding attributed statements by policy-makers.
papers.contribution: Builds a novel database of media-reported anonymous leaks about euro area monetary policy and studies their market effects.
papers.q: How do anonymous leaks of monetary policy information affect euro area financial markets?
papers.conclusion: Leaks mainly reflect minority opinions and do not usually lock in decisions, and post-meeting leaks about dissent change market perceptions.
papers.ident: High-frequency event study of financial market reactions around leaks.
papers.dataDetail: Database of media-reported anonymous Eurosystem leaks with high-frequency market data.

papers.title: Identification and estimation in a time-varying endogenous random coefficient panel data model
papers.q: How can average partial effects be identified in a panel model with time-varying endogenous random coefficients?
papers.summary: Regressors may be correlated with random coefficients through a fixed effect and a time-varying shock. Conditional on the two controls, variation from instruments identifies the parameters, leading to three-step series estimators with established convergence rates and asymptotic normality.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: sufficient statistic for the fixed effect and control function for the random shock.
papers.contribution: Develops a panel method that identifies the average partial effect and the local average response function using a sufficient statistic and a control variable.

papers.title: Impulse Response Analysis of Structural Nonlinear Time Series Models
papers.q: How can impulse responses be estimated in structural nonlinear time series models?
papers.summary: A two-step procedure flexibly captures nonlinearities without fixed parametric forms, with uniform estimation guarantees. Simulations show robustness to misspecification with modest efficiency losses, and a US monetary policy application finds larger GDP responses to rate hikes than linear models.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: sieve estimation of nonlinear structural autoregressions.
papers.contribution: Develops a semiparametric sieve approach and an iterative algorithm to compute impulse responses of nonlinear structural autoregressions.
papers.dataDetail: US monetary policy and oil supply news shock applications.

papers.title: Patterns and Implications of Ability Tracking: Evidence from Texas Public Schools
papers.q: What are the patterns and implications of ability tracking in Texas public schools?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of ability tracking and its implications using evidence from Texas public schools.

papers.title: The power of electricity: Small hydropower and girls’ education
papers.q: Does small hydropower electrification improve girls' education?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effect of small hydropower electricity on girls' education.

papers.title: Payment data, information disclosure, and privacy
papers.q: How does information derived from payment data affect welfare and privacy?
papers.summary: Disclosure tends to improve welfare when interest rates are low but may reduce it when rates are high. A central bank can craft noisy messages that encourage investment through Bayesian persuasion, whereas private banks trading information in a competitive market may produce too much of it.
papers.ident: Theory: general equilibrium model of information disclosure and Bayesian persuasion.
papers.contribution: Develops a general equilibrium framework to assess the welfare effects of aggregate-demand information from payment data.
papers.conclusion: Privacy concerns may dissuade some consumers from digital payments and lower information precision, but need not reduce welfare.

papers.title: Estimating the consumption-smoothing value of Medicaid expansion: Evidence and limits
papers.q: How much consumption-smoothing value does Medicaid expansion provide, and what are the limits of its estimation?
papers.summary: The title indicates an estimate of the consumption-smoothing value of Medicaid expansion, with attention to the limits of the evidence.

papers.title: Time-of-day effects on disclosure of intimate partner violence
papers.q: Does the time of day affect disclosure of intimate partner violence?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of time-of-day effects on the disclosure of intimate partner violence.

papers.title: Evaluating the environmental and economic implications of curbing transboundary pollution: Evidence from China
papers.q: What are the environmental and economic effects of curbing transboundary pollution in China?
papers.summary: The title indicates an evaluation of the environmental and economic implications of curbing transboundary pollution in China.

papers.title: Competition in a Spatially Differentiated Product Market with Negotiated Prices

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How do negotiated prices and spatial differentiation shape market power and merger effects?
papers.summary: The model is estimated on transaction-level data from the UK brick industry to measure market power and analyse mergers. Counterfactuals show that switching from individually negotiated to uniform pricing raises markups and merger price effects on average.
papers.contribution: Develops an estimable model of discrete choice with negotiated prices, consistent with non-cooperative bargaining and with a tractable likelihood under GEV disturbances.
papers.ident: Structural: bargaining model with GEV discrete choice, estimated by maximum likelihood on transaction data.
papers.dataDetail: Transaction-level data on product choice and price in the UK brick industry.

papers.title: Is the information channel of monetary policy alive in emerging markets?
papers.q: Do emerging-market central banks' rate decisions convey information that shifts inflation and output forecasts?
papers.summary: After an unexpected rate increase, inflation and output forecasts rise in the short run, supporting an information shock behind the policy decision. A baseline New Keynesian model explains this only when the interest rate carries information about shocks other than the monetary policy shock.
papers.ident: Forecast responses to unexpected policy rate decisions in high-frequency event windows.
papers.contribution: Studies how forecasts respond to unexpected policy rate decisions using high-frequency, short-horizon datasets for Brazil and Chile with the same source for outcome and regressors.
papers.dataDetail: Forecast datasets for Brazil and Chile.

papers.title: Reconciling Micro Elasticities with the Macro Decline in Labor Supply
papers.summary: Micro estimates condition on non-labor income, while macro variation lets capital income adjust alongside labor income, strengthening the income effect. A model with heterogeneous households gives closed-form expressions in which the distribution of the labor share determines the gap, and a cross-sectional regression conditioning on the labor share recovers the macro elasticity.
papers.ident: Quantitative: heterogeneous-household model with closed-form micro and macro elasticities.
papers.q: How can small micro labor supply elasticities be reconciled with the strongly negative macro relationship between wages and hours?
papers.contribution: Reconciles micro and macro elasticities with one utility specification and heterogeneity in non-labor income.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country and time-series data on hours and wages.

papers.title: Quota Mechanisms: Finite-Sample Optimality and Robustness
papers.q: How well do quota mechanisms perform in finite samples and under robustness concerns?
papers.summary: The title indicates an analysis of the finite-sample optimality and robustness of quota mechanisms.

papers.title: Data-Driven Automation
papers.q: How does data accumulated as a byproduct of activity drive automation dynamics?
papers.summary: Data both augments the productivity of automated tasks and expands the automation frontier. The paper derives conditions for partial versus full long-run automation, and in the full case the labor share of tasks decays as a power law in time. The economy is generically inefficient and a planner tilts the direction of data accumulation.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic model of data accumulation and task automation.
papers.contribution: Builds a dynamic model of data-driven automation with task-specific data that accumulates endogenously and spills over across tasks.

papers.title: Demand shocks during the post-pandemic inflation surge: An international perspective
papers.q: What role did demand shocks play in the post-pandemic inflation surge across countries?
papers.summary: The title indicates an international analysis of demand shocks during the post-pandemic inflation surge.

papers.title: The Targets of Geoeconomic Coercion
papers.summary: Private entities internalize less than their own government the equilibrium consequences of acquiescing, which lets the hegemon exploit the gap between private cost and social value to itself. Coercing the government gives up part of this advantage but offers other benefits.
papers.ident: Theory: hegemon coercion of private versus government targets.
papers.q: Should a hegemon coerce private firms or governments in a targeted country?
papers.contribution: Characterizes conditions under which a hegemonic country optimally targets private entities or the foreign government when exerting geoeconomic power.

papers.title: From means-tested programs to Universal Basic Income - The role of endogenous participation in transfer programs
papers.q: How does endogenous participation shape the design of transfers from means-tested programs to a universal basic income?
papers.summary: The title indicates an analysis of the role of endogenous participation in transfer programs when moving from means-tested programs to a universal basic income.

papers.title: Can Online Activity Be Regulated? Evidence from Adult Websites
papers.q: Can online activity be regulated, given circumvention and substitution toward noncompliant sites?
papers.summary: Access restrictions reduced overall time on adult sites by roughly 10%. For every 100 hours on top sites before restrictions, about 50 remained at noncompliant sites, 30 persisted through VPN circumvention, 10 were substituted to noncompliant sites and 10 were no longer spent.
papers.ident: Staggered adoption of state age verification laws across 25 US states since 2023.
papers.contribution: Studies the effects of state age verification laws that led prominent adult websites to restrict access, using individual-level browsing panel data.
papers.dataDetail: Individual-level panel data on browsing activity.

papers.title: The Value of One Office Day a Month
papers.summary: Monthly office days gradually raised productivity, with treated employees handling 7.8% more calls per hour. They also spent 36 more minutes communicating with colleagues after an office visit, and randomly assigned desk neighbors were 11 percentage points more likely to communicate afterward.
papers.conclusion: Monthly office days reduced attrition by a third.
papers.ident: Randomized assignment of employees to remote work or one monthly office day.
papers.q: Does one office day a month raise productivity and retention among remote workers?
papers.contribution: Reports a randomized controlled trial in a large multinational assigning 248 customer-service employees to fully remote work or one office day a month.
papers.dataDetail: Call-level productivity and communication data for 248 customer-service employees.

papers.title: Measuring Financial Literacy with the Big Three: Why It Works
papers.q: Why does the Big Three index reliably measure financial literacy?
papers.summary: Results confirm the scale's validity and reliability, with item characteristics stable across populations and settings. There is no evidence of measurement differences across demographic subgroups or countries.
papers.conclusion: The Big Three index performs similarly to the longer Big Five scale in measuring literacy and predicting financial behaviors.
papers.contribution: Estimates item difficulty and discrimination parameters with Item Response Theory and runs a meta analysis of their stability across datasets and countries.
papers.ident: Item Response Theory estimates of item parameters with meta analysis across datasets.
papers.dataDetail: Financial literacy survey datasets from multiple countries.

papers.title: Beliefs and Actions under Government Policy Uncertainty: Evidence from Student Loan Forgiveness

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How does uncertainty about student loan forgiveness affect households' beliefs, spending and debt payments?
papers.summary: Borrowers more optimistic about forgiveness cut student loan payments by $40 per month and raise non-durable spending by $80 per month. Optimistic borrowers may also postpone durable spending while waiting for uncertainty to resolve.
papers.ident: Randomized information provision experiment on beliefs about forgiveness, linked to administrative outcomes.
papers.contribution: Runs an information provision experiment embedded in a survey eliciting beliefs about forgiveness, linked to credit bureau, employment verification and nondurables consumption data.
papers.dataDetail: Survey linked to credit bureau data, employment verification and nondurable consumption data.

papers.title: Automation and Repression
papers.summary: Decentralized automation raises capital's income share and the likelihood of a successful revolt. The capitalist state can regulate automation, redistribute via taxes or repress political action, which creates more room for automation.
papers.conclusion: The main result is a complementarity between automation and repression.
papers.ident: Theory: global game of revolt embedded in an automation model.
papers.q: How do automation, redistribution and repression interact when workers can revolt?
papers.contribution: Builds a model of automation in which workers' revolt is a global game and a capitalist state chooses regulation, redistribution and repression.

papers.title: Regulatory Competition in the US Life Insurance Industry
papers.summary: States vie to attract insurers with lower capital requirements, while the costs fall on consumers in other states. Competition leads regulators to set lower capital requirements, which raises default risk but also consumer surplus by lowering prices.
papers.ident: Structural: quantitative model of the insurance market with state regulators' revealed-preference objectives.
papers.q: What are the effects of regulatory competition between states in the US life insurance industry?
papers.contribution: Documents competition between state regulators and develops a quantitative model of the insurance market to evaluate its effects.
papers.conclusion: On net, competition decreases regulators' utility based on their revealed-preference objective functions.
papers.dataDetail: State regulation and insurer data for US life insurance.

papers.title: Dollar Erosion: Understanding the Loss of Reserve Currency Status
papers.q: What would losing reserve currency status cost the United States in goods and asset markets?
papers.summary: Loss of seigniorage of 1% of GDP a year makes American households spend less, mostly on US goods, so a real depreciation of the dollar clears the excess supply. Standard parameters imply an 8.8% real depreciation, and reabsorbing about 50% of GDP in dollar bonds raises the real interest rate by 90 basis points.
papers.conclusion: The aggregate wealth loss is roughly one year of US GDP.
papers.contribution: Quantifies the effects of losing reserve currency status through seigniorage losses in goods markets and reabsorption of dollar bonds in asset markets.
papers.ident: Quantitative: calibrated open-economy model with home bias and dollar bond reabsorption.

papers.title: Peer Effects in Consideration and Preferences
papers.q: Can peer effects in preferences be separated from peer effects in consideration sets using choice data?
papers.summary: Peer effects on preferences, consideration, or both have different behavioural implications in the data, which allows the set and type of network connections to be recovered. Each agent's preferences and consideration mechanisms can then be recovered, without relying on exogenous covariates or menu variation, and the results are applied to tea chains' expansion decisions.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: nonparametric identification of peer effects in preferences and consideration.
papers.contribution: Develops a discrete choice model with peer effects in preferences and consideration sets and shows nonparametric identification from a sequence of choices.
papers.dataDetail: Expansion decisions of tea chains.

papers.title: Equity financing and exports: Evidence from IPO approvals in China

authors.inst: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Does equity financing from IPO approvals raise firms' exports in China?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the relationship between equity financing and exports using IPO approvals in China.

papers.title: Liability dollarization and exchange rate pass-through to domestic prices
papers.q: How does liability dollarization affect exchange rate pass-through to domestic prices?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the link between liability dollarization and exchange rate pass-through to domestic prices.

papers.title: AIC for many-regressor heteroskedastic regressions

authors.inst: Center for Economic Research and Graduate Education – Economics Institute

papers.q: How does the Akaike information criterion behave in regressions with many regressors and heteroskedasticity?
papers.summary: The title indicates an analysis of the AIC in heteroskedastic regressions with many regressors.

papers.title: Large-scale land acquisitions in Ethiopia: Impacts on agricultural productivity and deforestation
papers.q: How did large-scale land acquisitions in Ethiopia affect agricultural productivity and deforestation?
papers.summary: The title indicates an assessment of the impacts of large-scale land acquisitions in Ethiopia on agricultural productivity and deforestation.

papers.title: Do pensions enhance effort and selective retention?: Evidence from public schools

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.q: Do pensions enhance effort and selective retention among public school teachers?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of whether pensions enhance effort and selective retention, using evidence from public schools.

papers.title: The effect of dating markets on maternal and neonatal health
papers.q: How do dating markets affect maternal and neonatal health?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effect of dating markets on maternal and neonatal health.

papers.title: How do Monetary Policy and Inflation Announcements Affect Firm Expectations in High Inflation?
papers.q: How do monetary policy and inflation announcements shape firms' inflation expectations and FX management in high inflation?
papers.summary: Firms' aggregate inflation expectations respond to monetary policy shocks in a state-dependent way. In stable inflation environments, firms react in line with standard theory, anticipating lower prices and a worse outlook, while in volatile settings they adopt a supply-side view.
papers.ident: Survey-based surprises in a narrow window around policy and inflation announcements.
papers.contribution: Defines monetary policy and inflation surprises from survey forecasts in a narrow window around announcements, for Turkish firms in 2015-2024.
papers.dataDetail: Survey data on Turkish firms' inflation expectations and FX management, 2015-2024.

papers.title: Spatial Implications of Telecommuting
papers.q: How does the rise of telework reallocate residents and jobs within and across cities?
papers.summary: Simulated increases in the attractiveness and productivity of telework produce a non-monotonic pattern of reallocation of residents and jobs, validated by correlation with local changes since 2019. Workers who can telecommute gain and those who cannot lose, and broader access to jobs reduces wage inequality across residential locations.
papers.contribution: Builds a quantitative spatial model with telecommuting that varies by education and industry, quantified over 4,502 US locations.
papers.ident: Structural: quantitative spatial model matched to the distribution of jobs and residents across 4,502 US locations.
papers.dataDetail: Jobs and residents across 4,502 US locations.

papers.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Field Experiments to Explore Novel Features of Parental Speech and Foster Child Development
papers.q: Which features of parental speech foster child development?
papers.summary: The model identifies acoustic features of parental speech that map into children's skills, and the intervention helping parents provide nurturing interactions improves parental speech. The data are used to explore two causal channels and one potential moderator.
papers.ident: Experimental and natural variation from two home-visiting randomized experiments.
papers.contribution: Combines field experiments with a signal processing model on more than 600 hours of recorded parent-child interactions from two Chicagoland home-visiting experiments.
papers.dataDetail: More than 600 hours of recorded parent-child interactions with child assessment data.

papers.title: GLP-1 Therapy and the Reshaping of Socioeconomic Gradients in Health
papers.q: How do the benefits of GLP-1 therapy for obesity vary across socioeconomic and demographic groups?
papers.summary: The largest differences emerge across education: individuals without a high school degree gain roughly 14% more lifetime net social value, 16-17% larger GRASA-QALYs and 20% greater life expectancy gains relative to the cohort mean. Those with college degrees experience gains 15-27% below the mean.
papers.contribution: Estimates lifetime health and economic benefits of GLP-1 treatment using a nationally representative microsimulation of US adults and Shapley-value decomposition.
papers.ident: Quantitative: microsimulation of lifetime outcomes with Shapley-value decomposition of gains.
papers.dataDetail: Nationally representative microsimulation model of US adults.

papers.title: Innovation without Borders? The Geography of Technological Diffusion
papers.q: How well does technological innovation diffuse across borders, as seen in firms' AI investment beliefs?
papers.summary: Firms substantially underestimate competitors' current AI investment, domestically and abroad, and update expectations about competitors' future AI investment after the information treatment. The treatment also significantly raises firms' own expected AI investment rate.
papers.ident: Randomized provision of information on AI investment shares in a firm survey experiment.
papers.contribution: Runs a large field experiment with 3,300 firms in twelve EU countries, giving half of them accurate information about domestic and foreign AI investment shares.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of 3,300 firms across twelve EU countries.

papers.title: The Effect of Height on Adolescents' Body Image Perceptions and Behaviors
papers.q: Does height causally affect adolescents' body image perceptions and behaviors?
papers.summary: Taller adolescents are more likely to perceive themselves as overweight even at a given BMI, and less likely to underestimate their weight category. Taller boys are more likely to assess their category correctly while taller girls are more likely to overestimate it, and the shifts translate into behavioral responses for girls but not boys.
papers.ident: Within-individual variation in height during adolescence, conditioning on BMI.
papers.contribution: Uses NLSY97 within-individual variation in height during adolescence, conditioning on BMI, to estimate effects on body image.
papers.dataDetail: National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 (NLSY97).

papers.title: Intergenerational Mobility in Late Qing Dynasty: Evidence from Northeast China
papers.q: How did intergenerational class mobility evolve in late Qing China?
papers.summary: Before 1850, mobility patterns were stable and converged toward a steady state. From about 1850, class dynamics became unstable until the dynasty's collapse, with the transition coinciding with the Opium Wars and Taiping Rebellion.
papers.ident: Descriptive: Markov-chain mobility measures with two mobility concepts.
papers.contribution: Uses a data set from Liaoning province and Markov-chain measures to document mobility across social classes in two distinct epochs.
papers.dataDetail: Historical population records from Liaoning province in Northeast China.

papers.title: Predicting Labor Force Types
papers.q: Can early-life information predict who will be weakly attached to the labor market in prime age?
papers.summary: A small group of people accounts for most flows between labor market states and spells outside employment. The less attached group is disproportionately female, less educated and in poor health.
papers.contribution: Uses k-means clustering on NLSY79 employment, unemployment and non-employment spells between ages 30 and 50 to identify weakly attached individuals, then predicts membership from pre-30 information.
papers.ident: Machine learning: k-means clustering of labor force histories, then prediction from early-life variables.
papers.dataDetail: National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1979 (NLSY79), ages 30 to 50.

papers.title: How Small is Small? Non-linearities in Heterogeneous Agent Models
papers.summary: MPCs are highly non-linear in wealth and fall sharply away from borrowing constraints, so larger transfers shift households out of high-MPC regions. Linear methods substantially overstate stimulus effects at empirically relevant sizes, in partial and general equilibrium.
papers.conclusion: Local methods are unreliable for shocks and policies where a failure of Ricardian equivalence matters.
papers.ident: Quantitative: calibrated heterogeneous-agent models comparing linear and non-linear solutions.
papers.q: How much do non-linear MPCs in heterogeneous-agent models limit the size of fiscal transfer effects?
papers.contribution: Shows that in calibrated heterogeneous-agent models the consumption response to a transfer is strongly concave in its size.

papers.title: Falling Dominoes? The Impact of the US Exit from Free Trade on the Sustainability of Trade Cooperation
papers.q: How does the US exit from free trade affect other countries' optimal tariffs and trade cooperation?
papers.summary: A country's optimal import tariffs depend on partners' expenditure shares on its goods and on trade and labor supply elasticities. The impact of US withdrawal on other countries' optimal tariffs and on the sustainability of cooperation is minimal.
papers.contribution: Evaluates optimal tariffs and the sustainability of cooperation in a multi-country, multi-sector global network trade model after a US withdrawal.
papers.ident: Structural: analytical optimal tariff formula and quantitative multi-country, multi-sector model.

papers.title: Government demand and firm growth
papers.q: Does selling to government raise firm growth in a developing country?
papers.summary: Firms increase total sales after entering government contracts but see no productivity gains in value added per worker. Sales to non-government customers drop sharply, persistently, and this is not seen when firms start to sell to large private buyers.
papers.ident: Event study with correction for self-selection and staggered treatment timing.
papers.contribution: Uses Ugandan administrative data and an event study that corrects for firm self-selection and heterogeneity in treatment timing.
papers.dataDetail: Ugandan administrative firm data and an original survey of firms in public procurement.

papers.title: Is high-speed internet detrimental for early childhood development? Evidence from a countrywide program
papers.q: Does high-speed internet harm early childhood development?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effect of high-speed internet on early childhood development, using a countrywide program.

papers.title: Tatonnement and Price Setting in General Equilibrium
papers.q: When is a general equilibrium stable under tatonnement and price setting?
papers.summary: The abstract states that the question of when an equilibrium is stable has remained largely unresolved for over 150 years and that the paper proposes a resolution.
papers.contribution: Proposes a resolution to the question of equilibrium stability in general equilibrium theory.
papers.ident: Theory: stability of general equilibrium under tatonnement.

papers.title: Are carbon tariffs climate policy?
papers.summary: A US carbon tariff raises US emissions, lowers foreign emissions, and achieves half the global reductions of the combined policy. Both approaches raise US GDP and welfare, the combined policy more so through terms of trade, and multilateral tariff-only agreements give modest reductions that do not rise monotonically with membership.
papers.q: Are carbon tariffs effective climate policy without a domestic carbon tax?
papers.contribution: Builds a quantitative trade model comparing US carbon tariffs with and without a domestic carbon tax on carbon-intensive, trade-exposed sectors.
papers.ident: Quantitative trade model with counterfactual carbon tariff and carbon tax policies.

papers.title: Incentives, Evidence, and Reminders for Bureaucrats: Overcoming Barriers to Policy Scale Up
papers.q: What interventions get frontline bureaucrats to implement a proven policy at scale?
papers.summary: Only 37% of control schools verifiably implemented the program when ordered by the Ministry, compared with 83% in the original trial. Sharing research evidence, modest incentives and assistance had precise null effects, and past implementation did not raise take-up, ruling out fixed adoption costs as the explanation.
papers.ident: Randomized nationwide experiment varying interventions to school principals.
papers.contribution: Runs a nationwide experiment in the Dominican Republic testing evidence, financial incentives, implementation assistance and reminders for school principals.
papers.dataDetail: Schools in the Dominican Republic, with Ministry of Education implementation records.

papers.title: Macroeconomic and Fiscal Consequences of Quantitative Easing
papers.q: What are the macroeconomic and fiscal consequences of quantitative easing?
papers.summary: In a deep liquidity trap, QE can give a sizeable boost to output and inflation and reduce public debt substantially, unlike fiscal expansion, which raises debt. More caution is warranted in a shallow liquidity trap where the notional interest rate is only slightly negative.
papers.ident: Quantitative: DSGE model with segmented asset markets.
papers.contribution: Evaluates QE with a DSGE model with segmented asset markets, focusing on macro objectives and the consolidated government and central bank fiscal position.

papers.title: Measuring Housing Quality Using Revealed Preference: A Geographic PageRank Approach
papers.q: Can migration flows reveal the quality of places?
papers.summary: Using public data, the paper constructs GPR rankings for US counties and metropolitan areas, extended over time and to population subgroups. As an application, GPR works as an anti-instrument for unobserved housing quality and recovers a correctly signed implicit price of air pollution in line with quasi-experimental benchmarks.
papers.contribution: Introduces Geographic PageRank, a recursive measure of place quality built from the full network of migration flows.
papers.ident: PageRank algorithm on migration flows, used as an anti-instrument for unobserved quality.
papers.dataDetail: Public data on US county and metropolitan area migration flows.

papers.title: Does Regional Variation in Wage Levels Identify the Effects of a National Minimum Wage?
papers.q: Does regional variation in wage levels identify the effects of a national minimum wage?
papers.summary: The designs can be unreliable in many plausible settings. In the Brazilian case study, employment and wage inequality estimates vary sharply across specifications, which offers a plausible explanation for conflicting findings in the literature.
papers.conclusion: The paper concludes with practical recommendations for applied researchers.
papers.contribution: Studies effective-minimum-wage and fraction-affected or gap designs with theory and extensive simulations, plus a Brazilian case study.
papers.ident: Econometric theory and simulations of regional exposure designs for a national minimum wage.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian labour market data in a case study.

papers.title: From rents to results: China’s anti-corruption reforms and the effectiveness of aid to Africa
papers.q: How do China's anti-corruption reforms affect the effectiveness of aid to Africa?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how China's anti-corruption reforms relate to the effectiveness of aid to Africa.

papers.title: Familiar strangers: The role of diaspora networks in foreign investment and long-run development
papers.q: What role do diaspora networks play in foreign investment and long-run development?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the role of diaspora networks in foreign investment and long-run development.

papers.title: Reducing trade with Russia: Sanctions vs. firms’ voluntary suspension of activities
papers.q: How much did sanctions and firms' voluntary suspensions each reduce trade with Russia?
papers.summary: Voluntary suspensions contributed to reductions in exports and imports of 20% and 24%, while sanctions contributed 10% and 34%. The combination caused a much larger reduction in trade with Russia than sanctions alone.
papers.contribution: Uses Spanish firm-level data to separate the effects of trade sanctions and voluntary suspension of activities on exports and imports with Russia.
papers.ident: Firm-level comparison of trade changes by sanctions exposure and voluntary suspension.
papers.dataDetail: Spanish firm-level trade data after Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

papers.title: How to grow an invoicing currency: Micro evidence from Argentina
papers.q: How does an invoicing currency grow, as in Argentina's RMB invoicing after a swap line expansion?
papers.summary: The share of imports from China invoiced in RMB surged, displacing the dollar, then declined after the late-2023 election as the dollar shortage eased. Banks played a key role: firms tied to banks with limited US dollar loans, or borrowing from a Chinese state-owned bank, were more likely to switch to RMB.
papers.contribution: Exploits Argentina's 2023 expansion of a currency swap line with China using firm-level import data, bank-firm loan relationships and bank balance sheets.
papers.ident: Policy experiment from the 2023 swap line expansion, with firm-bank exposure differences.
papers.dataDetail: Argentine firm-level import data, bank-firm loan relationships and bank balance sheets.

papers.title: The benefits of public transit to households: Evidence from India
papers.q: What are the benefits of public transit to households in India?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the household benefits of public transit using evidence from India.

papers.title: Experimental Auctions with Securities
papers.summary: Contrary to theory, debt auctions generate more revenue than equity auctions, explained by overbidding in debt auctions. Second-price equity auctions generate slightly more surplus, and in informal auctions buyers use equity more than theory predicts while sellers successfully choose dominant bids.
papers.contribution: Implements security-bid auctions experimentally, where buyers bid with debt and equity linked to the project's ex-post revenue.
papers.q: How do debt and equity security-bid auctions compare in revenue and surplus in the laboratory?
papers.ident: Laboratory experiment comparing debt and equity security-bid auction formats.

papers.title: Housing wealth, family relationship and mental health: Evidence from China
papers.q: How do housing wealth and family relationships shape mental health in China?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of housing wealth, family relationships and mental health using evidence from China.

papers.title: The forsaken road: Reassessing living standards following the Cuban Revolution and the American embargo
papers.q: How did living standards change after the Cuban Revolution and the American embargo?
papers.summary: The title indicates a reassessment of living standards following the Cuban Revolution and the American embargo.

papers.title: A quantitative urban model for transport appraisal
papers.summary: Partial equilibrium models restrict the ability to quantify impacts outside the transport market. The specification yields travel time valuations from an explicit leisure-labour trade-off, unique to each residence-workplace pair, and decomposes the aggregate welfare change.
papers.q: How can transport appraisal capture general equilibrium effects beyond the transport market?
papers.contribution: Designs an appraisal method integrating causal estimates of key parameters into an invertible spatial general equilibrium model.
papers.ident: Structural: invertible spatial general equilibrium model with causally estimated parameters.

papers.title: Wasserstein worst-case scenarios and asset pricing
papers.q: How do Wasserstein worst-case scenarios affect asset pricing?
papers.summary: The title indicates an analysis of worst-case scenarios defined with Wasserstein distance and their implications for asset pricing.

papers.title: Choosing (not) to choose: Uncovering intrinsic preferences for choice autonomy

authors.inst: Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts

papers.q: Do people have an intrinsic preference for choice autonomy, apart from its instrumental value?
papers.summary: A majority of subjects display a preference for choice autonomy, while a significant minority is averse to their own choice.
papers.contribution: Proposes an elicitation method for intrinsic preference for choice autonomy that controls for instrumental value of choice.
papers.ident: Experimental elicitation controlling for the instrumental value of choice.

papers.title: Formalizing microentrepreneurs through targeted tax systems: Evidence from Brazil

authors.inst: NOVA School of Business and Economics

papers.q: Can targeted tax systems formalize microentrepreneurs in Brazil?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of formalizing microentrepreneurs through targeted tax systems in Brazil.

papers.title: Estimation of characteristics-based quantile factor models

authors.inst: Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros

papers.q: How can characteristics-based quantile factor models be estimated?
papers.summary: The paper derives convergence rates, limiting distributions of estimated factors and loading functions, and a consistent criterion for the number of factors at each quantile. The estimators work with heavy-tailed errors, short time dimensions and factor numbers differing from the number of characteristics.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: three-stage estimation of quantile factor models with characteristic-dependent loadings.
papers.contribution: Proposes a three-stage estimator for quantile factor models whose loadings are unknown functions of observed characteristics.

papers.title: The Effect of Education Policy on Crime: An Intergenerational Perspective
papers.q: How does education policy affect crime across generations?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effect of education policy on crime from an intergenerational perspective.

papers.title: Financial frictions, FX reserves, and exchange rate management with local-currency debt
papers.q: How do financial frictions shape FX reserves and exchange rate management with local-currency debt?
papers.summary: The title indicates an analysis of financial frictions, FX reserves and exchange rate management when debt is denominated in local currency.

papers.title: Estimation and inference in boundary discontinuity designs: Distance-based methods
papers.q: How can treatment effect heterogeneity along a boundary be estimated and tested in boundary discontinuity designs?
papers.summary: The geometric regularity of the boundary, a one-dimensional manifold, determines feasible convergence rates and valid inference. The paper derives bounds on misspecification bias, uniform distributional approximations for boundary-robust inference, and minimax lower bounds.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: distance-based local polynomial estimation in boundary discontinuity designs.
papers.contribution: Studies nonparametric distance-based local polynomial estimation of the boundary average treatment effect curve with identification, estimation and inference results.

papers.title: Debiasing and t -Tests for Synthetic Control Inference on Average Causal Effects
papers.q: How can valid inference on synthetic control average treatment effects be done?
papers.summary: The t-test is easy to implement, provably robust to misspecification and valid with stationary and nonstationary data, avoiding long-run variance estimation. It performs well in application-based simulations and is illustrated by revisiting the effect of carbon taxes on emissions.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: cross-fitted debiasing and self-normalized t-statistic for synthetic control.
papers.contribution: Proposes a K-fold cross-fitting bias correction and a self-normalized t-test for average effects estimated by synthetic controls.
papers.dataDetail: Carbon tax and emissions application.

papers.title: Local and spillover effects of trade on structural transformation: Evidence from Brazil

authors.inst: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.q: How does trade affect structural transformation locally and through spillovers in Brazil?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the local and spillover effects of trade on structural transformation in Brazil.

papers.title: U.S. monetary spillovers to emerging markets: Both policy drivers and vulnerabilities matter
papers.q: How do policy drivers and vulnerabilities shape US monetary spillovers to emerging markets?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of US monetary spillovers to emerging markets, emphasizing both policy drivers and vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Rent Guarantee Insurance
papers.summary: It increases welfare by improving risk sharing, reducing the need for large security deposits and reducing homelessness. Unrestricted access is not financially viable because of moral hazard and adverse selection, but restricting access can restore viability.
papers.conclusion: Private insurers target better-off renters, public insurers focus on households most at risk, and stronger tenant protections increase effectiveness.
papers.q: Can rent guarantee insurance reduce housing insecurity and homelessness?
papers.contribution: Introduces rent guarantee insurance in a quantitative equilibrium model of housing insecurity.
papers.ident: Quantitative: equilibrium model of housing insecurity with rent guarantee insurance.

papers.title: Do Voters Punish Inflation or Pay Cuts? Inflation and Real Wages in U.S. Elections
papers.q: Do voters punish inflation or real wage declines in US elections?
papers.summary: Real wage decline, rather than higher inflation, predicts Republican electoral gains, in line with economic voting. Inflation retains an association with presidential vote shares beyond pure economic voting.
papers.contribution: Uses county-level data on family budget costs, nominal income and electoral results for 2021-2024, exploiting within-state variation in price changes.
papers.ident: Within-state, cross-county variation in changes in local prices and real wages.
papers.dataDetail: US county-level family budget costs, nominal income and election results for President and Congress.

papers.title: On the right track? Railroads, industrial development, and distributional effects in historical China

authors.inst: Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

papers.q: How did railroads affect industrial development and distribution in historical China?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of railroads, industrial development and distributional effects in historical China.

papers.title: The Missing Value of Data
papers.q: How much is data worth as an asset missing from national accounts?
papers.summary: Data investments are missed in national accounts, depreciation losses are missed in firms' balance sheets, and consumption bartered for data is omitted. The paper capitalizes data value and asks what measured GDP would be if data were treated like a physical asset.
papers.ident: Output-based measurement of data value from firms' revenue forecast quality.
papers.contribution: Proposes an output-based approach that treats data as an asset, measures its volume from the quality of firms' revenue forecasts and determines its depreciation endogenously.

papers.title: AI for Structural Estimation
papers.q: Can AI methods cut the time needed to solve and estimate dynamic equilibrium models from days to minutes?
papers.summary: The state space is extended to include equilibrium prices and model parameters so that one model solution clears markets and estimates parameters. Neural networks trained on simulated data approximate the mapping from parameters to moments and are used to minimize the model-data moment distance and to find equilibrium prices.
papers.ident: Structural estimation using neural network surrogates for moment conditions and market clearing.
papers.contribution: Develops a global method treating prices as pseudo parameters and market clearing as moment conditions, built on neural network approximations.

papers.title: How Efficient was the Affordable Care Act at Reducing Uninsured Rates?
papers.q: How efficient was the Affordable Care Act at reducing uninsured rates?
papers.summary: The paper estimates the total effect of the ACA, including Medicaid expansion and Marketplace coverage. For adults in households below 150% of the poverty line, increases in public coverage were associated with one-for-one decreases in uninsurance and no change in employer coverage.
papers.contribution: Examines 2008-2024 American Community Survey trends in uninsured, public and employer-sponsored coverage by income relative to the poverty line, exploiting state-by-year variation in ACA implementation.
papers.ident: State-by-year variation in ACA implementation, by income group.
papers.dataDetail: American Community Survey, 2008-2024.

papers.title: An Unfunded Mandate? Medicaid Continuous Coverage Requirements and State Fiscal Burdens During COVID-19
papers.q: Did Medicaid continuous coverage requirements during COVID-19 cost states more than the higher federal match gave them?
papers.summary: The provisions were ex-ante expected to produce revenues and expenditures of similar magnitudes, but the ex-post realizations remained unquantified. The paper estimates states' share of the cost of the continuous coverage provision nationwide.
papers.contribution: Quantifies the ex-post state fiscal effect of the March 2020 provisions pairing a 6.2 point FMAP increase with a continuous coverage requirement.
papers.ident: Descriptive: accounting of state Medicaid costs against the FMAP increase.
papers.dataDetail: State Medicaid enrollment and expenditure data during COVID-19.

papers.title: Texting parents about early child development: Behavioral changes and unintended social effects

authors.inst: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.q: Can texting parents about early child development change behavior, and with what unintended social effects?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of behavioral changes and unintended social effects from texting parents about early child development.

papers.title: From trade protectionism to legal protectionism: How the Trump trade war harms US firms in China
papers.q: How does the Trump trade war affect US firms in China through legal protectionism?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how the Trump trade war harms US firms in China through a shift from trade protectionism to legal protectionism.

papers.title: Optimal Long-Term Care Provision and Insurance with Heterogeneous Preferences and Risks
papers.q: How should long-term care provision and insurance be designed with heterogeneous risks and preferences?
papers.summary: The optimal scheme has lower coinsurance in nursing homes and higher coinsurance in home care, with a constrained expansion of home care. Relative to the prevailing system, optimal provision increases home care use, triples public expenditure and delivers a large increase in consumer surplus.
papers.ident: Structural: optimal insurance model with demand estimated from a survey experiment.
papers.contribution: Estimates preferences for care settings with a survey experiment and calibrates health transitions and service supply to Quebec administrative data.
papers.dataDetail: Survey experiment on care preferences and Quebec administrative data on health transitions.

papers.title: Deep-Tech Innovation: A Multi-Method Study toward a Conceptual Framework and Research Agenda
papers.q: What defines deep-tech innovation as a distinct concept?
papers.summary: The term deep-tech innovation is applied inconsistently and lacks an agreed definition. At the invention level, six attributes are specified: three on the scientific and technological basis and three on its characteristic exposure.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework combining a systematic literature review and interviews with deep-tech founders, identifying twelve defining attributes across invention, venture and ecosystem levels.
papers.dataDetail: Systematic literature review and semi-structured interviews with deep-tech founders.

papers.title: What do news readers want?
papers.q: What kinds of news content are readers willing to pay for?
papers.summary: The model is used to construct optimal staff allocations under subscription-only and ad-supported counterfactual revenue models. Readers are willing to pay for local reporting, and demand measures based only on time use substantially understate it.
papers.contribution: Uses individual-level web traffic and subscription data from a major US metropolitan newspaper for 2020-2024, with quasi-random paywall arrival, to estimate demand by content category.
papers.ident: Quasi-random arrival of paywall events forcing subscription decisions.
papers.dataDetail: Individual-level web traffic and subscription data from a major US metropolitan newspaper, 2020-2024.

papers.title: How Much and How Fast Do Investors Respond to Equity Premium Changes? Evidence from Wealth Taxation

authors.inst: Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance

papers.q: How much and how fast do investors respond to equity premium changes caused by wealth taxation?
papers.summary: Allocation responses are strong but slow, with short-run responses resembling modest survey sensitivity and longer-run responses much larger and rationalized by moderate risk aversion. Shocks affect stock market entry but not exits, suggesting entry costs dominate participation costs.
papers.conclusion: Slow responses support adjustment-friction explanations of asset-pricing puzzles and bear on optimal capital taxation when rates differ across assets.
papers.ident: Wealth-tax-induced persistent shock to the after-tax equity premium across Norwegian investors.
papers.contribution: Uses Norwegian administrative panel data on investors' portfolios around a persistent wealth-tax-induced shock to the equity premium.
papers.dataDetail: Norwegian administrative panel data on investors' portfolios.

papers.title: The Risk-free Rate and the Risk-adjusted Growth Rate
papers.summary: Questions such as debt rollover without primary surpluses turn on whether the present value of the aggregate endowment is finite. A historical episode with French government bonds indexed to aggregate growth allows direct measurement, and the risk-adjusted growth rate is found to exceed the risk-free rate.
papers.ident: Theory with direct measurement from growth-indexed French government bonds.
papers.q: Is the risk-adjusted growth rate of the economy below the risk-free rate?
papers.contribution: Shows that the argument that the aggregate endowment must be finitely valued is incorrect, and measures the risk-adjusted growth rate from French growth-indexed bonds.
papers.dataDetail: Historical French government bonds indexed to aggregate growth.

papers.title: Factor Bias and Heterogeneous Output Quality in Multiproduct Production
papers.q: How do factor bias and heterogeneous output quality shape multiproduct production?
papers.summary: The model recovers plant-specific efficiencies, qualities, economies of scale and scope and substitution elasticities without imposing non-joint production or separability. It documents increasing returns to scale, labor-materials substitutability and cost complementarities from joint production.
papers.ident: Structural: translog multiproduct cost function with share and supply equations, estimated by GMM.
papers.contribution: Develops and estimates a structural multiproduct translog cost model with plant-product quality and factor-augmenting efficiency, using GMM on Taiwanese textile plants.
papers.dataDetail: Plant-level data from Taiwan's textile industry.

papers.title: Does the Import Invasion Explain the Mysterious Disappearance of Productivity Growth in U.S. Manufacturing?
papers.q: Did the import invasion cause the disappearance of productivity growth in US manufacturing?
papers.summary: Productivity growth fell from +3.3 percent a year in 1987-2010 to -0.3 percent in 2010-2023. The paper attributes the end of output growth in 2000 to imports that closed plants and squeezed profits, and identifies further handicaps including self-inflicted wounds by firms and reduced government-funded R&D.
papers.contribution: Traces a chain of causation from import competition after 2000 to falling capacity utilization, lower investment and R&D, and eroded innovation.
papers.ident: Descriptive: historical accounting of productivity, output and investment.
papers.dataDetail: US manufacturing productivity, output and R&D data, 1987-2023.

papers.title: Defining Innovatisation: The Case of NewSpace and the Changing Space Sector
papers.summary: In the technological achievements mode only technological performance matters, mainly for prestige, while in innovation customer preferences, commercial opportunities and costs become essential. The paper studies the economics of Apollo and the 1980s commercialization attempts, then provides quantitative evidence such as costs that innovation now shapes the sector.
papers.contribution: Introduces the concept of innovatisation, describing the transformation of a sector between a technological achievements mode and an innovation mode.
papers.q: How has the space sector changed from a logic of technological achievement to a logic of innovation?
papers.ident: Descriptive: historical case studies and quantitative evidence on costs.

papers.title: Right-sizing incentives
papers.summary: Effects of conditional payments are highly non-linear, with most of the incentive effect on the extensive margin and rapidly diminishing returns to incentive size. Incentives also increase healthcare use in childhood by index children and other children in the household, while the information signal has largely null effects.
papers.ident: Randomized conditional cash transfers of three sizes and a randomized information signal.
papers.q: How large should incentives for using formal medical care be for expectant mothers?
papers.contribution: Runs a field experiment in Nigeria offering conditional cash payments of N2500, N4000 or N10000, plus a secondary pregnancy risk information signal.
papers.dataDetail: Expectant mothers in a Nigerian field experiment.

papers.title: Monetary financing produces neither high inflation nor miraculous fiscal multipliers
papers.summary: Analytically, money-financed stimuli have zero impact on inflation and the real economy relative to debt-financed stimuli in several models. Relaxing the conditions behind this irrelevance result, money-financed stimuli barely increase inflation and output.
papers.ident: Theory: New Keynesian models with reserves and bonds as imperfect substitutes.
