papers.q: Does monetary financing of fiscal stimulus produce high inflation or large fiscal multipliers?
papers.contribution: Studies money-financed fiscal stimuli financed by interest-paying central bank reserves in New Keynesian models where bonds and reserves are imperfect substitutes.

papers.title: On the Benefits of Robo-Advice in Financial Markets
papers.q: Does robo-advice improve investors' portfolio choices and participation?
papers.summary: Robo-advice has no effect on initial market participation but positively affects continued participation, helps investors avoid mistakes, increases rebalancing and yields portfolios closer to the utility-maximising benchmark. Default implementation performs significantly better than advice alone.
papers.contribution: Runs a ten-week portfolio choice experiment with robo-advice, default implementation of recommendations, and self-directed investment.
papers.ident: Randomized assignment to robo-advice, default implementation or no advice.
papers.dataDetail: Ten-week portfolio choice experiment.

papers.title: Identifying Preference for Early Resolution from Asset Prices
papers.q: Can asset prices reveal investors' preference for early resolution of uncertainty?
papers.summary: Empirical evidence from the dynamics of implied volatility of S&P 500 index options before FOMC announcements supports preference for early resolution.
papers.ident: Theory-based test using implied volatility dynamics before FOMC announcements.
papers.contribution: Develops an asset market-based test of preference for the timing of resolution of uncertainty, characterized by the risk premium during the resolution of macroeconomic announcement informativeness.
papers.dataDetail: Implied volatility of S&P 500 index options around FOMC announcements.

papers.title: Friendship Networks and Political Opinions

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How do friendship networks shape political opinions?
papers.summary: Group assignment reduces political opinion gaps and fosters friendship. Friendship reduces opinion differences by 44 percent of the mean gap, through homophily: friendships form among politically similar students who then join political associations together.
papers.ident: Same-group membership from quasi-random integration group assignment as an instrument for friendship.
papers.contribution: Uses the quasi-random assignment of Sciences Po students to short-term integration groups as an instrument for friendship formation.
papers.dataDetail: Sciences Po students' integration groups, friendships and political opinions.

papers.title: Mergers, Foreign Competition, and Jobs: Evidence from the US Appliance Industry
papers.summary: Whirlpool's acquisition decreased consumer welfare by $271 million annually but preserved 797 domestic jobs. These jobs must be valued at more than $344,000 per year for employment benefits to offset the consumer harm.
papers.q: How does foreign competition alter the consumer welfare and employment effects of mergers?
papers.contribution: Builds a model of consumer demand, endogenous product portfolios and employment, and applies it to Whirlpool's acquisition of Maytag against a counterfactual foreign acquirer.
papers.ident: Structural: demand, product portfolio and employment model with a counterfactual foreign acquisition.
papers.dataDetail: US appliance industry data around the Whirlpool-Maytag merger.

papers.title: Long Wars

authors.inst: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.q: Does the Coase conjecture hold for bargaining during war?
papers.summary: A militarily strong player insists on a large share, which the other concedes only if the strong player credibly signals strength by fighting a sufficiently long war. The Coase conjecture therefore fails, and asymmetric information explains why long wars may be inevitable.
papers.ident: Theory: bargaining in war under asymmetric information.
papers.contribution: Models two players contesting a divisible resource under asymmetric information about military strength and derives a lower bound on the expected duration of war using mechanism design.

papers.title: The Impact of Unions on the Wage Distribution: Evidence from Higher Education
papers.q: How does unionization affect the wage distribution of university faculty?
papers.summary: Unionization compressed salaries: wages at the bottom of the unconditional distribution rose by roughly 10 percent while wages at the top were unaffected. The effects appear driven by contractual salary floors, with little impact on faculty employment, and the higher wage bill was financed by increased student enrollment.
papers.ident: Staggered rollout of unionization across Canadian universities.
papers.contribution: Uses longitudinal administrative salary data on Canadian faculty and the staggered rollout of unionization across institutions.
papers.dataDetail: Longitudinal administrative salary data for Canadian university faculty.

papers.title: Digital skills for better jobs: Experimental evidence from a bootcamp training program in Peru
papers.q: Does an online digital skills bootcamp improve youth employment in Peru?
papers.summary: The program significantly raises the probability of working in entry-level technology jobs two years after training. Some courses improve formal employment and income while others show no effects, giving null average impacts overall, with men gaining more in formal jobs and women moving into informal flexible jobs.
papers.ident: Randomized assignment to an online digital skills bootcamp.
papers.contribution: Evaluates a randomized online bootcamp, combining administrative formal employment records with survey data.
papers.conclusion: Differences may be driven by selection into tracks and limited local demand, and selected tracks yield positive net returns.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative formal employment records and survey data for Peruvian youth.

papers.title: Different Paths to College Success: The Impact of Massachusetts’s Charter Schools on College Trajectories
papers.q: How do different charter school models in Massachusetts affect college outcomes?
papers.summary: Urban charter schools, which mostly use No Excuses practices, boost college preparation, enrollment and graduation. Nonurban charters raise enrollment and graduation despite lowering state test scores and AP enrollment, and their graduation edge is more than twice as large.
papers.ident: Randomized admissions lotteries at charter schools.
papers.contribution: Uses randomized admissions lotteries to estimate effects of urban and nonurban charter schools on college preparation, enrollment and graduation.
papers.dataDetail: Massachusetts charter school lottery and college outcome records, 2010s.

papers.title: Governments’ home bias and efficiency losses: Evidence from national and subnational governments

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research
Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How much efficiency do national and subnational governments lose through home bias in procurement?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of governments' home bias and efficiency losses using evidence from national and subnational governments.

papers.title: The Architecture of Social Networks and the Diffusion of Innovations
papers.q: How does the architecture of social networks shape the diffusion of innovations?
papers.summary: Insularity of connections, the extent to which agents concentrate connections on a narrow set of others, determines contagion. Whether insularity helps or hinders depends on the technology being diffused.
papers.contribution: Extends a standard diffusion model with agents who can coordinate adoption decisions with friends or family.
papers.ident: Theory: network diffusion model with coordinated adoption.

papers.title: Quality upgrading and productivity gains from domestic market access changes in India
papers.q: Does greater access to higher-income domestic markets lead to quality upgrading and productivity gains?
papers.summary: When shocks were large, local firms produced higher-quality output using more skilled labor, capital and expensive materials, which raised productivity. For small shocks, firms also upgraded quality but only by using more input quantities, without productivity gains, suggesting substantial adjustment costs.
papers.contribution: Exploits a major highway project in India to study firms' responses to large and small increases in market access.
papers.ident: Variation in market access from a major highway project in India.
papers.dataDetail: Indian firm-level data and highway project market access measures.

papers.title: Firm-Worker Matches: Experience or Inspection Goods?
papers.q: Are firm-worker matches experience goods or inspection goods?
papers.summary: Using German administrative data, a firm and a worker receive a signal before the match that reduces the variance of their beliefs about match productivity by 67%. The informativeness of the signal varies with the worker's gender and education and has increased over time.
papers.contribution: Proposes an empirical strategy inferring the informativeness of pre-match signals from gaps in separation rates of workers hired from unemployment, low-tenure jobs and high-tenure jobs.
papers.ident: Structural: separation rate gaps by hiring origin used to infer match signal informativeness.
papers.dataDetail: German administrative employment data.

papers.title: Nonresponse Imputations and Related Measurement Issues in the CPI for Shelter
papers.q: How does nonresponse imputation bias CPI shelter inflation measurement?
papers.summary: Nonresponse has risen since 2000 to roughly 40 percent of observations, and the current class-mean imputation by rent tier may be biased because nonresponse correlates with factors beyond rent tier. A simple model shows alternative methods could yield sharply different index biases.
papers.contribution: Studies alternative simple imputation methods for missing rents in the BLS Housing Survey, based on variables such as structure type and tenure length.
papers.ident: Comparison of alternative imputation methods for missing rent data.
papers.dataDetail: BLS Housing Survey data underlying CPI shelter.

papers.title: The Heterogeneous Bank Lending Channel of Monetary Policy
papers.q: How does heterogeneity in banks' interest rate risk exposure affect monetary policy transmission?
papers.summary: Differences in interest rate risk exposure between banking systems with fixed and variable rate loans affect transmission only when bank solvency constraints become relevant. Idiosyncratic default risk pushes a substantial share of banks toward the solvency threshold, making heterogeneity quantitatively important.
papers.contribution: Develops a quantitative macroeconomic model with heterogeneous banks, calibrated to the euro area.
papers.ident: Quantitative: heterogeneous bank model calibrated to the euro area.
papers.dataDetail: Euro area bank data used for calibration.

papers.title: Scaling Point-in-Time Language Models
papers.summary: Models trained on unrestricted internet text embed future information and create lookahead bias in backtests and causal inference. Scaling narrows the gap, with the models approaching the performance of leading open-weight models on common-sense reasoning and language benchmarks.
papers.q: Can scaling up point-in-time language models close the performance gap with unrestricted models?
papers.contribution: Trains decoder-only transformers of up to 4 billion parameters on 1 trillion chronologically filtered FineWeb tokens, building monthly checkpoints spanning 2013-2024.
papers.ident: Machine learning: chronologically filtered pretraining to avoid lookahead bias.
papers.dataDetail: 1 trillion chronologically filtered tokens from FineWeb.

papers.title: The (Lack of) Efficacy of Social Belonging and Growth Mindset Interventions Among College Students
papers.q: Do social belonging and growth mindset interventions improve college students' outcomes?
papers.summary: There are no immediate or dynamic effects on grades and no effect on persistence through university, and no evidence of meaningful treatment effect variation across subgroups. Further research is needed to identify contexts where these light-touch interventions generalize.
papers.ident: Randomized experiments with machine learning analysis of heterogeneity.
papers.contribution: Evaluates the interventions in four large-scale experiments across two Canadian universities with nearly 12,000 students, and explores heterogeneity with machine learning.
papers.dataDetail: Nearly 12,000 students at two Canadian universities with survey and administrative data.

papers.title: Cheapflation Cycles
papers.q: Why do low-income households face more volatile inflation when upstream input costs rise?
papers.summary: Because low-income households buy lower-priced varieties, their inflation rates are disproportionately sensitive to upstream costs. Food-at-home purchase data show this mechanism generates cycles in inflation inequality and excess inflation volatility for low-income households, accounting for observed fluctuations over time.
papers.contribution: Documents a source of fluctuations in inflation inequality: absolute price increases that are similar across varieties are larger in percentage terms for low-price products.
papers.ident: Descriptive evidence from household purchase data, with a pricing mechanism.
papers.dataDetail: Food-at-home household purchase data.

papers.title: How Much Has Shale Gas Saved U.S. Consumers?
papers.summary: US consumers saved $3.1-$4.3 trillion between 2007 and 2025, or $164-$227 billion annually. Access to low-price US natural gas was especially valuable during major supply shocks such as the war in Ukraine.
papers.q: How much has shale gas saved US natural gas consumers?
papers.contribution: Calculates consumer savings from price differences between the United States, Europe and Japan.
papers.ident: Descriptive: counterfactual savings from price gaps between US, European and Japanese gas markets.
papers.dataDetail: Natural gas prices and consumption in the US, Europe and Japan, 2007-2025.

papers.title: Who bears the cost: Financial frictions and labor markdown

authors.inst: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.q: Who bears the cost of financial frictions through labor markdowns?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how financial frictions and labor markdown determine who bears the cost.

papers.title: Complex Modern Portfolio Theory
papers.summary: The finding holds with popular portfolio regularization methods, across several asset universes, and for large or small T. It runs against evidence that performance decreases rapidly with N.
papers.contribution: Presents new facts about MPT showing that its performance increases with the number of assets once N exceeds the number of training observations T.
papers.q: Does Modern Portfolio Theory perform better as the number of assets grows beyond the number of observations?
papers.ident: Theory and simulations of portfolio optimization in high dimensions.
papers.dataDetail: Several asset universes.

papers.title: The Sisyphean Pursuit of Evidence for Poverty Traps
papers.summary: Many papers assume asset thresholds with increasing returns to capital and incomplete financial markets, but far fewer demonstrate them empirically. The replication on seven other big push programs finds no evidence of such a threshold.
papers.ident: Replication of a nonlinear asset dynamics analysis across seven programs.
papers.q: Is there empirical evidence for asset-threshold poverty traps in other cash transfer programs?
papers.contribution: Applies the analysis of Balboni et al. (2022), which found a threshold in Bangladesh, to data from seven other similar programs in low-income countries.
papers.dataDetail: Data from seven big push transfer programs in low-income countries.

papers.title: Electoral Incentives and Government Transparency: Evidence from Freedom of Information Requests
papers.q: Do reelection incentives affect government transparency?
papers.summary: Because identical requests go to many agencies at once, the design holds constant timing, submitter and content while varying only proximity to an election. FOIA rejection rates are positively correlated with the electoral calendar.
papers.ident: Identical FOIA requests filed at the same time to agencies facing and not facing an upcoming election.
papers.contribution: Compares responses to identical freedom-of-information requests filed through MuckRock just before state and municipal elections with those filed elsewhere at the same time.
papers.dataDetail: FOIA requests filed through the MuckRock platform to US agencies.

papers.title: Management of Health Care Facilities and Patient Attendance during Major Disruptions: Evidence from Kenya
papers.q: How does management quality in Kenyan health facilities relate to patient attendance during major disruptions?
papers.summary: Management quality is low on average and its distribution is highly compressed. The paper tests the association between management quality and outpatient attendance during a period of disruption including the COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.contribution: Adapts the World Management Survey to measure management in 429 primary health care facilities and 73 hospitals and links it to administrative attendance data.
papers.ident: Association between measured management quality and attendance during disruptions.
papers.dataDetail: Nationally representative survey of 429 primary facilities and 73 hospitals linked to administrative data.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Distributional Preferences
papers.q: How inequality averse are people, according to structural estimates in the literature?
papers.summary: Mean sensitivity to disadvantageous and advantageous inequality is 0.533 and 0.326. Aversion to advantageous inequality is smaller and to disadvantageous larger in strategic environments, and the representative individual has Cobb-Douglas preferences with roughly 1/3 weight on others' earnings.
papers.contribution: Conducts a meta-analysis of 297 estimates of sensitivity to inequality from 41 articles estimating the Fehr and Schmidt model, and of 98 estimates of altruism from 17 articles estimating the Andreoni and Miller model.
papers.ident: Meta-analysis of structurally estimated preference parameters.
papers.dataDetail: 297 estimates from 41 articles and 98 estimates from 17 studies.

papers.title: Extreme Justifications Fuel Polarisation
papers.q: How do extreme justifications for discrimination fuel political polarisation?
papers.summary: Exposure to extreme justifications increases discrimination, particularly in a polarised environment where many others already discriminate, and leads participants to adopt more extreme justifications themselves.
papers.conclusion: The findings suggest a self-reinforcing dynamic in which extreme statements raise polarisation and the prevalence of extreme reasoning.
papers.ident: Randomized information on others' discrimination choices and justifications in an online experiment.
papers.contribution: Runs an online experiment where participants choose between splitting resources equally or discriminating against a supporter of the opposing party, varying information on others' choices and justifications.
papers.dataDetail: Online experiment participants.

papers.title: Addressing weak links in government implementation at scale: Experimental evidence from a school governance reform in Tanzania
papers.q: Can low-cost text messages to local monitors improve implementation of a national school governance reform in Tanzania?
papers.summary: Schools faced weak incentives to implement inspection recommendations, and local monitors reporting to a different ministry lacked access to the reports. Monitors in treated schools received texts encouraging them to follow up on compliance.
papers.contribution: Experimentally evaluates the nationwide roll-out of Whole School Visits, texting monitors the main recommendations in a randomly sampled subset of schools.
papers.ident: Randomized text messages to monitors in a subset of program schools.
papers.dataDetail: Tanzanian schools in the Whole School Visit program.

papers.title: Adjustment without accumulation: Evidence on capital formation from IMF programs
papers.q: Do IMF programs lead to adjustment without capital accumulation?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of capital formation under IMF programs, finding adjustment without accumulation.

papers.title: From housing gains to pension losses: Micro-macro integration to reveal wealth inequality dynamics in Chile
papers.q: How have housing gains and pension losses shaped wealth inequality in Chile?
papers.summary: The title indicates a micro-macro integration of data to reveal wealth inequality dynamics in Chile, from housing gains to pension losses.

papers.title: The employment effects of disability benefit reassessment
papers.q: What are the employment effects of disability benefit reassessment?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the employment effects of reassessing disability benefits.

papers.title: Temporary acceleration or long-term change? Experimental evidence on female empowerment and intimate partner violence in urban Liberia

authors.inst: KDI School of Public Policy and Management

papers.q: Does female empowerment in urban Liberia change intimate partner violence temporarily or durably?
papers.summary: The title indicates an experimental study of whether the effects of female empowerment on intimate partner violence in urban Liberia are temporary or long-lasting.

papers.title: From local to global: How foreign acquisitions reshape job mobility
papers.q: How do foreign acquisitions reshape workers' job mobility?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how foreign acquisitions reshape job mobility from local to global firms.

papers.title: Semi-nonparametric models of multidimensional matching: An optimal transport approach
papers.q: How can multidimensional matching models be estimated with semi-nonparametric methods using optimal transport?
papers.summary: The title indicates semi-nonparametric models of multidimensional matching built on an optimal transport approach.

papers.title: Monopsony Makes Firms Not Only Small but Also Unproductive: Why East Germany has Not Converged
papers.q: Does monopsony explain why East German firms are smaller and less productive than West German ones?
papers.summary: Employers facing a trade-off between size and low wages may forgo building large business networks and remain small. The model predicts 10% lower aggregate labour productivity in East Germany.
papers.contribution: Documents steeper size-wage curves, lower investment in business networks, smaller size and lower productivity in East German plants using administrative data, and builds a model with monopsony, product market power and network investments.
papers.ident: Structural: monopsony model with business network investment, matched to East-West plant differences.
papers.dataDetail: High-quality German administrative plant data.

papers.title: When neighbors stop knocking: The impact of Canada’s 2025 tourism decline on U.S. local labor markets
papers.summary: Exploiting heterogeneity in exposure, small establishments in the top 1% exposed local-industry markets saw employment declines of about 6% relative to less exposed ones. The estimates imply 13,900 to 42,100 lost jobs, concentrated in a few localities.
papers.contribution: Combines smartphone foot-traffic data on Canadian visitors at the ZIP code by industry level with real-time establishment employment records.
papers.q: How did the 2025 decline in Canadian visits to the United States affect local labor markets?
papers.ident: Heterogeneous local-industry exposure to the 25% decline in Canadian visits.
papers.dataDetail: Smartphone foot-traffic by ZIP code and industry and real-time establishment employment records.

papers.title: The effect of reminders for self-set goals on productivity
papers.q: Do reminders for self-set goals raise productivity?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effect of reminders for self-set goals on productivity.

papers.title: The Role of Firms and Job Mobility in the Assimilation of Immigrants: Former Soviet Union Jews in Israel 1990–2019
papers.q: What role do firms and job mobility play in immigrant wage assimilation?
papers.summary: Initial wage gaps relative to natives were 57% for men and 47% for women, and 12-20% of them are explained by sorting across firms and pay-setting within firms. The gap closes only after 27-29 years, with much of the convergence driven by climbing the firm ladder.
papers.ident: Worker-firm decomposition of wage gaps over time since arrival.
papers.contribution: Follows former Soviet Union Jewish immigrants to Israel for up to three decades using administrative data, in a setting without legal migration barriers.
papers.dataDetail: Israeli matched employer-employee administrative data, 1990-2019.

papers.title: Jackknife Standard Errors for Clustered Regression
papers.q: Should jackknife variance estimators replace conventional cluster-robust estimators in linear regression?
papers.summary: Conventional variance estimators have full downward worst-case bias, while the jackknife estimator is never downward biased. Confidence intervals from conventional standard errors have worst-case coverage equal to zero, while jackknife intervals have coverage bounded by the Cauchy distribution under normal errors.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: bias and coverage of jackknife variance estimators for clustered regression.
papers.contribution: Presents a theoretical case for jackknife variance estimators over heteroskedasticity-consistent and cluster-robust estimators, and extends the Bell and McCaffrey student t approximation.

papers.title: Global Policy Spillovers: How Environmental Policies Propagate through Product Attributes
papers.q: How do environmental policies propagate internationally through product attributes?
papers.summary: The Japanese subsidy led to substantial improvements in fuel economy in the United States. Most CO2 emissions reductions from the policy arise through effects in the United States.
papers.conclusion: Conventional economic analysis may understate the global impacts of many policies.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around Japan's fuel-economy subsidy, with structural estimation of firms' product design.
papers.contribution: Introduces attribute propagation and develops a framework with difference-in-differences and structural estimation, studying a Japanese fuel-economy subsidy.
papers.dataDetail: Vehicle models and fuel economy data for Japan and the United States.

papers.title: More Paths or More Contrast? A Theory of Experimentation Breadth
papers.q: How should an organisation choose the breadth of its experimentation portfolio?
papers.summary: Adding paths gives more chances to find a strong direction but dilutes learning and weakens the strongest feasible contrast. When ranking viable alternatives, broader portfolios become more attractive as the budget rises, but when paths share viability uncertainty, additional paths partly repeat the same test.
papers.contribution: Brings the number of paths and the contrast among them into a single framework under a fixed experimentation budget.
papers.ident: Theory: experimentation portfolio model with breadth and contrast margins.

papers.title: The Geography of Lifecycle Human Capital Accumulation
papers.q: Do places that best produce human capital in childhood also produce it in adulthood through local labor markets?
papers.summary: Wages across places reflect location wage premiums, adult human capital accumulation due to labor market exposure, and childhood human capital accumulation. The wage premium estimates are validated using out-migration from New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina, and the accumulation estimates using wage changes of multi-time movers.
papers.contribution: Constructs AKM-style estimates of location wage premiums from movers across US commuting zones and of adult human capital accumulation from local labor market exposure.
papers.ident: AKM-style mover design across commuting zones, validated with Hurricane Katrina out-migration.
papers.dataDetail: US administrative earnings data for movers across commuting zones.

papers.title: Intertemporal Arbitrage and Optimal Operation of Pumped Hydro Energy Storage
papers.q: How should a pumped hydro energy storage facility be operated optimally in liberalized electricity markets?
papers.summary: Pumped hydro is the most cost-effective long-duration storage and supports grids with growing variable renewable penetration. Understanding optimal operation and valuation is increasingly important for finance as electricity prices become more relevant.
papers.ident: Structural: optimal control model calibrated to plant parameters and observed prices.
papers.contribution: Develops a market-based optimal control framework modelling a pumped hydro facility as a profit-maximizing asset, calibrated to the La Muela plant and Spanish wholesale prices.
papers.dataDetail: La Muela pumped storage plant parameters and Spanish wholesale electricity prices.

papers.title: Sophisticated Borrowing Constraints and Macroeconomic Dynamics
papers.q: How do covenant-style borrowing constraints change macroeconomic dynamics relative to hard borrowing constraints?
papers.summary: Instead of indiscriminate cuts to borrowing and investment, creditors influence firms' decisions to maximize value after a violation. The model is quantitatively consistent with investment and earnings around covenant violations at the micro level.
papers.contribution: Models sophisticated borrowing constraints as debt thresholds that transfer control rights to creditors, matched to empirical patterns around covenant violations.
papers.ident: Structural: firm model with covenant-based constraints calibrated to covenant violation patterns.
papers.dataDetail: Large US nonfinancial firms' covenant violation data.

papers.title: Lands of Opportunity: Differences in the Geography of Wealth and Income Mobility in the United States
papers.q: How does intergenerational mobility in wealth differ geographically from mobility in income?
papers.summary: Relative mobility in wealth shows less spatial clustering and more spatial variation than in income, and many cities and suburbs have lower mobility in wealth. Local characteristics are associated with some mobility concepts but not others, for example the severity of the Great Recession is strongly negatively associated with child income.
papers.ident: Descriptive: small-area estimation of intergenerational persistence from linked survey and administrative data.
papers.contribution: Provides county-level estimates of intergenerational mobility in total income, labor income, homeownership, housing wealth and total wealth using small-area estimation and linked data on children born 1978-1986.
papers.dataDetail: Linked survey and administrative data on millions of US children born 1978-1986.

papers.title: The Psychology of Macroeconomic Expectations
papers.q: How do context and emotions shape macroeconomic expectations through recalled experiences?
papers.summary: The treatment causes instability in beliefs and reasoning tied to the similarity of primed experiences to different macro states, which also accounts for heterogeneity in beliefs across other personal experiences. The model microfounds narratives and yields a confidence multiplier in which some agents' spending cues optimism for others.
papers.ident: Randomized priming of recalled experiences in a survey experiment.
papers.contribution: Presents a model of animal spirits and tests it by priming Dutch National Bank Survey respondents to recall financial or health adversities before eliciting inflation and home price expectations.
papers.dataDetail: Dutch National Bank Survey respondents.

papers.title: Estimating the Present Value of R&D Tax Benefits in the United States

authors.inst: Government of the United States of America
Government of the United States of America
Government of the United States of America
Government of the United States of America
Government of the United States of America

papers.summary: Realized benefits deviate from statutory ones because firms in loss status carry forward credits and deductions. Present values vary substantially with loss status, age and size: old and large firms use benefits quickly, while young, small firms often operate in loss status and use them more slowly.
papers.q: What is the realized present value of R&D tax benefits for US firms?
papers.contribution: Develops a procedure tracking firms' intertemporal utilization of tax attributes from R&D spending in confidential corporate tax returns.
papers.ident: Descriptive: firm-level tracking of tax attribute utilization over time.
papers.dataDetail: Panel of confidential US corporate tax returns, covering 2012-2016.

papers.title: Forecasting long-run causal effects

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How can long-run causal effects be forecast?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of forecasting long-run causal effects.

papers.title: Does Unfairness Hurt Women? The Effects of Losing Unfair Competitions
papers.q: Are women more discouraged than men by losing unfair competitions?
papers.summary: Both genders reduce tournament entry after unequivocally meritocratic losses, but when the winner is not necessarily determined by merit, female losers are relatively more discouraged. Exploratory machine learning suggests risk preferences, age and adolescent sports participation are associated with a reduced impact of losing.
papers.ident: Randomized fairness of the tournament outcome in an online experiment.
papers.contribution: Runs an online experiment (N=2,086) comparing responses to losses in meritocratic and non-meritocratic tournaments.
papers.dataDetail: Online experiment with 2,086 participants.

papers.title: The Cost of Intermediary Market Power for Distressed Borrowers
papers.q: How much do distressed borrowers pay because of lender market power in debtor-in-possession lending?
papers.summary: Distressed borrowers pay exceptionally high spreads even after removing compensation for credit, liquidity and loan-making costs. Lender market power explains 533 basis points of risk-adjusted spreads in the DIP loan market and 300 in highly speculative loans.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic lending game estimated on facility-level DIP and speculative loan data.
papers.contribution: Develops and estimates a dynamic game of distressed lending with latent demand heterogeneity, endogenous participation, creditor blocking power and tacit collusion through repeated syndication.
papers.dataDetail: Granular facility-level data on debtor-in-possession and highly speculative loans.

papers.title: Domestic outsourcing and employment security
papers.q: How does domestic outsourcing affect employment security?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the relationship between domestic outsourcing and employment security.

papers.title: The Intergenerational Impact of Birth-Control Policies on Fertility: The Role of Norms

authors.inst: Central University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: Do birth-control policies lower fertility across generations through changed norms?
papers.summary: Birth-control policies reduce mothers' fertility and establish new norms that lower daughters' fertility even after the policies end. The staggered implementation starting in 1979 and phase-out from 2014 provide quasi-experimental variation.
papers.ident: Staggered implementation of China's One-Child Policy across regions, with a model of norm evolution.
papers.contribution: Develops a model with endogenously evolving fertility norms and tests it with China's One-Child Policy, using the 2020 census.
papers.dataDetail: China's 2020 population census.

papers.title: Supercompliers
papers.summary: Supercompliers are the only subpopulation to benefit from eligibility, and they require standard LATE assumptions plus outcome monotonicity. Estimation and inference use instrumental variable regression, and two job-training experiments illustrate incorporating social welfare weights into marginal-value-of-public-funds analysis.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: LATE framework with an outcome monotonicity assumption.
papers.contribution: Defines supercompliers as those whose take-up responds positively to eligibility and whose outcome responds positively to take-up, and gives tools to characterize them.
papers.q: Who are the subpopulation that benefits from treatment eligibility in an instrumental variable setting?
papers.dataDetail: Two job-training experiments.

papers.title: Burn now or never? Climate policy exposure and investment of fossil fuel firms
papers.q: How did expectations of future climate policy affect fossil fuel firms' investment after the Paris Agreement?
papers.summary: Firms with greater climate exposure significantly increased investment after the Paris Agreement relative to less exposed firms, directed towards traditional fossil fuel activities. There is no sign of investment in transitioning to renewables or in lowering carbon intensity.
papers.conclusion: The findings bear on the adverse effects of delaying climate regulation.
papers.contribution: Compares investment responses to the Paris Agreement by fossil fuel firms with high and low exposure to climate change.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences by firm exposure to climate policy around the Paris Agreement.
papers.dataDetail: Fossil fuel firm investment data around the 2015 Paris Agreement.

papers.title: International Trade Finance and Learning Dynamics
papers.q: How does relationship-specific learning shape exports and trade finance?
papers.summary: Transitions are faster in riskier destinations and for less experienced firms. The model is used to quantify how shocks to trade finance costs affect aggregate exports.
papers.conclusion: The response depends on destination riskiness and is amplified by disruption of long-term trading relationships.
papers.contribution: Documents with Chilean micro data that new exporters start with cash-in-advance and shift to trade credit as relationships mature, and builds a general equilibrium trade model with learning about demand and counterparty risk.
papers.ident: Structural: general equilibrium trade model with learning, calibrated to Chilean exporter data.
papers.dataDetail: Chilean firm-level export and payment terms data.

papers.title: Measurement Error and Counterfactuals in Quantitative Trade and Spatial Models
papers.q: How can uncertainty about counterfactuals be quantified when the current state of the world is measured with error?
papers.summary: Counterfactuals depend on the current state of the world and model parameters, and common practice treats the state as perfectly observed. The empirical Bayes approach is practical and theoretically justified.
papers.contribution: Provides tools for quantifying uncertainty about counterfactuals in quantitative trade and spatial models and recommends an empirical Bayes approach.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: empirical Bayes uncertainty quantification for counterfactuals.

papers.title: The Apple Does Not Fall Far From the Tree: Intergenerational Persistence of Dietary Habits
papers.q: How strongly are dietary habits transmitted across generations?
papers.summary: Persistence in dietary habits is strong and exceeds that of income. Socioeconomic status and geography account for only a small share, and there is no dietary response after a parent's unexpected lifestyle-related death.
papers.ident: Descriptive intergenerational persistence, with an event study of parents' unexpected deaths.
papers.contribution: Uses grocery transaction data linked with administrative records to document intergenerational persistence of dietary habits.
papers.conclusion: The results underscore early-life influences and habit formation.
papers.dataDetail: Grocery transaction data linked to administrative records.

papers.title: Globalization, Innovation, and Margins of Sourcing

authors.inst: University of International Business and Economics

papers.summary: Input liberalization lets firms substitute cheaper imported intermediates for self-made inputs, which lowers marginal production costs but discourages in-house varieties. The paper compares trade and innovation policies for boosting aggregate productivity growth.
papers.q: Why do input tariff reductions reduce domestic innovation?
papers.contribution: Documents that input tariff cuts lower innovation and develops a dynamic framework with task-specific labor-augmenting productivity and non-homothetic import demand.
papers.ident: Input tariff variation, with a structural model of sourcing and innovation.

papers.title: Growth-at-Risk Is Investment-at-Risk

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

papers.q: What drives US growth-at-risk: investment, consumption or other components?
papers.summary: Growth-at-risk is by a wide margin investment-at-risk, with consumption contributing only under extreme financial stress and government spending and net exports not mattering. Leverage plays a key role in both consumption- and investment-at-risk.
papers.contribution: Investigates the composition of growth-at-risk given financial conditions, in the lower tail of the conditional GDP growth distribution.
papers.conclusion: The results support the financial accelerator mechanism of Bernanke et al. (1999).
papers.ident: Quantile regressions of GDP components on financial conditions.
papers.dataDetail: US GDP components and financial conditions indices.

papers.title: Competition and Nonprofit’s Strategic Responses: Evidence from Fundraising in Donative Markets
papers.q: How do nonprofits respond strategically to rivals' fundraising?
papers.summary: The evidence points to strategic substitutes, with nontrivial responses to rivals' fundraising and important across-sector impacts. Counterfactuals show reducing competition decreases equilibrium fundraising levels.
papers.contribution: Develops and estimates a model of nonprofit fundraising effort in donative markets, where rival responses can be strategic complements or substitutes.
papers.ident: Structural: game of nonprofit fundraising effort estimated on nonprofit data.
papers.dataDetail: Nonprofit organization fundraising data.

papers.title: When is TSLS Actually LATE?
papers.q: When does two-stage least squares estimate a local average treatment effect?
papers.summary: With covariates, the LATE interpretation does not apply in general: TSLS reflects treatment effects for compliers and always/never-takers, and some effects for the latter are negatively weighted. Only saturated specifications controlling nonparametrically for covariates have a LATE interpretation.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: TSLS with covariates under LATE assumptions.
papers.contribution: Examines whether the LATE interpretation applies to TSLS specifications with covariates used in practice.

papers.title: Optimal Labour Income Taxation: A Flexible Moral Hazard Approach
papers.summary: Optimal tax rates on high earners and the optimal Pareto tail index are both endogenously determined by preferences. A society with less risk-averse agents optimally taxes the rich less, even though its choices produce a thinner Pareto tail.
papers.ident: Theory: flexible moral hazard model of optimal income taxation.
papers.q: How should very high earners be taxed when risk is endogenous and agents allocate time across tasks?
papers.contribution: Reconsiders optimal labour income taxation in a flexible moral hazard model where agents choose the probabilities of income outcomes by allocating time across tasks.

papers.title: Fundamentally Reforming the DI System: Evidence from Germany
papers.q: What happens to disability insurance inflows and private take-up after abolishing a public occupational DI tier?
papers.summary: In the long run, overall DI inflows fell by roughly one-third, while private ODI take-up responded only modestly. The model shows coverage denials and weak insurance demand driven by complementary social insurance explain the modest take-up, with substantial coverage gradients by income and health.
papers.conclusion: Counterfactuals highlight the limited scope of incremental reforms.
papers.ident: Cohort cutoff of the 2001 reform (born after 1960), with an equilibrium insurance model.
papers.contribution: Studies Germany's 2001 abolition of public occupational disability insurance for cohorts born after 1960 and builds an equilibrium model of public and private insurance interactions.
papers.dataDetail: German administrative DI data and representative survey data.

papers.title: Firm Responses to Hiring and Investment Subsidies: Regression Discontinuity Evidence from the California Competes Tax Credit
papers.q: Do hiring and investment subsidies make firms expand employment without shifting activity from other states?
papers.summary: Businesses expand employment in California in response to awards, with little evidence that expansions come at the expense of operations in other states.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity at the CCTC applicant score eligibility cutoff.
papers.contribution: Uses applicant score eligibility cutoffs in the California Competes Tax Credit in a regression discontinuity design with longitudinal establishment microdata.
papers.conclusion: Targeted and audited subsidies can promote local expansions without significant cross-state displacement.
papers.dataDetail: Longitudinal microdata on establishments and parent firms linked to CCTC awards.

papers.title: Cross-Country Heterogeneous Response to Competition: Theory and Evidence from Trade Data
papers.q: Why do poor countries cut export prices but not quantities when Chinese competition intensifies?
papers.summary: Poor countries reduce export prices relative to rich countries under Chinese competition in the US, but the opposite holds for export quantities. Rich countries have a comparative advantage in quality upgrading, which a nested model without quality cannot capture.
papers.ident: Structural: general equilibrium trade model with quality and Bertrand competition.
papers.contribution: Develops and estimates a general equilibrium trade model with cross-country heterogeneity in quality production ability and two-dimensional Bertrand competition on price and quality.
papers.dataDetail: US import data by exporting country.

papers.title: Sibling Spillovers and Free Schooling

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science
NOVA School of Business and Economics

papers.q: How did free secondary education change sibling spillovers on schooling in Tanzania?
papers.summary: Before FSE, students whose older siblings narrowly passed the secondary entrance exam were less likely to attend secondary school, and with FSE the effect became positive. Changes in parental investments were a more likely channel than direct sibling interactions.
papers.conclusion: By easing financial constraints, FSE allowed households to invest in more children.
papers.ident: Triple-differences using sibling exam-cutoff comparisons and geographic variation in FSE exposure.
papers.contribution: Uses administrative data and a triple-differences analysis with geographic variation in exposure to Tanzania's Free Secondary Education reform.
papers.dataDetail: Tanzanian administrative exam and enrollment data.

papers.title: How do bureaucrats respond to hybrid incentive contract? Evidence from China’s air pollution controls
papers.q: How do bureaucrats respond to hybrid incentive contracts in China's air pollution controls?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how bureaucrats respond to hybrid incentive contracts, using evidence from China's air pollution controls.

papers.title: Job Transitions and Employee Earnings after Acquisitions: Linking Corporate and Worker Outcomes
papers.summary: Earnings of workers at target firms fall after M&As relative to controls, mostly among those who move to other firms. Leavers move to larger and more profitable firms but still see wage declines, concentrated among longer-tenured workers.
papers.conclusion: Results are consistent with workers losing match-specific premia after M&A-induced job transitions.
papers.ident: Matched difference-in-differences comparing target-firm workers to control workers.
papers.q: How do job transitions explain workers' earnings losses after mergers and acquisitions?
papers.contribution: Links Canadian firm balance sheet data to individual earnings in a matched difference-in-differences design.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian firm balance sheet data linked to individual earnings.

papers.title: Monetary Policy and Endogenous Financial Crises

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.q: How does monetary policy affect financial stability through endogenous financial crises?
papers.summary: Monetary policy affects the probability of a crisis in the short run through aggregate demand and in the medium run through capital accumulation. The central bank can reduce medium-run crisis incidence by tolerating higher short-run inflation volatility, and prolonged loose policy followed by a sharp tightening can trigger crises.
papers.ident: Quantitative: New Keynesian model with endogenous financial crises.
papers.contribution: Builds a New Keynesian model with capital accumulation and endogenous crises arising from adverse selection and moral hazard in credit markets.

papers.title: Input Sourcing under Climate Risk: Evidence from U.S. Manufacturing Firms

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.q: How does shipping time risk from weather affect firms' input sourcing?
papers.summary: Unexpected shipping delays significantly reduce importers' sales, profits and employment. Firms diversify by using more routes and foreign suppliers, though import values decline, and the quantitative analysis predicts substantial costs for the US economy.
papers.ident: Unexpected component of shipping times induced by weather along maritime routes.
papers.contribution: Uses US import transaction data to build a measure of sourcing risk from unexpected, weather-induced shipping times across more than 331,000 maritime routes, and a general equilibrium model of importing.
papers.dataDetail: Transaction-level US manufacturing import data and ocean shipping times across 331,000 routes.

papers.title: A model of China’s economic vertical structure
papers.q: How can China's economic vertical structure be modeled?
papers.summary: The title indicates a model of China's economic vertical structure.

papers.title: Catastrophes, Delays, and Learning

authors.inst: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.q: How should experimentation be planned when reaching untried stock levels can trigger delayed catastrophes?
papers.summary: The optimal policy is characterized as a function of the legacy computed from prior beliefs and the chronicle of stock levels, giving a protocol for planning that applies to pandemics and climate change. Experimentation can stop but resume later.
papers.ident: Theory: experimentation with delayed catastrophes and learning.
papers.contribution: Proposes a model of experimentation in which untried stock levels may lead, after a stochastic delay, to a catastrophe, and shows how to measure the legacy of past experiments.

papers.title: The Power of Proximity to Coworkers

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.q: How does proximity to coworkers affect training and productivity?
papers.summary: Sitting near teammates raises coding feedback by 18.3% and improves code quality, with gains concentrated among less-tenured and younger employees, while experienced engineers write less code. National data show scarring effects of remote work on young college graduates in remotable jobs.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing co-located and distributed teams around office closures and return-to-office mandates.
papers.contribution: Uses two shocks to proximity for software engineers at a Fortune 500 firm from 2019 to 2024: the 2020 office closures and the 2022-2023 return-to-office mandates.
papers.dataDetail: Personnel and code repository data for software engineers at a Fortune 500 firm, 2019-2024, and national US labor data.

papers.title: Air access to foreign markets and export-biased growth: Evidence from business entries

authors.inst: Capital University of Economics and Business
Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.q: Does air access to foreign markets drive export-biased growth through business entry?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how air access to foreign markets drives export-biased growth, with evidence from business entries.

papers.title: Public Services Under Private Management

authors.inst: Escola de Administração de Empresas de São Paulo

papers.q: Does outsourcing the management of public hospitals to private operators improve efficiency without hurting quality?
papers.summary: The model enhances hospital production and operational efficiency without adverse effects on quality and equity. Increased inpatient production addresses unmet demand, expanding access and reducing population mortality, with gains from stronger management capacity that facilitates staffing adjustments.
papers.contribution: Assesses Brazil's Organizações Sociais de Saúde model, where the state remains residual claimant while management is outsourced.
papers.ident: Staggered adoption of the OSS management model across public hospitals.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian public hospital production, staffing and mortality data.

papers.title: The Price Effects of Prohibiting Price Parity Clauses: Evidence from Global Hotel Chains
papers.q: What happens to hotel prices when price parity clauses are prohibited?
papers.summary: Price effects are limited and not significant for consumer-visible channels such as hotel websites or online travel agencies, but there is a significant price reduction on channels not visible to consumers, such as direct offline bookings. Bookings shift from online travel agencies to hotels' direct offline channels.
papers.ident: Quasi-experimental removal of price parity clauses in France in 2015.
papers.contribution: Provides quasi-experimental evidence on the 2015 removal of price parity clauses in France for three major global hotel groups.
papers.dataDetail: Booking and price data by sales channel for three global hotel groups.

papers.title: International Reserve Management Under Rollover Crises
papers.q: How should a government manage international reserves when it faces rollover crisis risk?
papers.summary: Optimal policy first reduces debt and later increases both debt and reserves as the government nears a safe zone, and issuing debt to accumulate reserves can lower spreads. A panel of emerging economies shows reserves financed by external borrowing are associated with lower spreads and are not systematically drawn down in crises.
papers.ident: Theory of reserve and debt policy, with panel evidence on spreads.
papers.contribution: Characterizes optimal policy between accumulating reserves and reducing debt for a government exposed to rollover crises.
papers.dataDetail: Panel of emerging economies' reserves, external debt and sovereign spreads.

papers.title: The political consequences of vaccines: Quasi-experimental evidence from eligibility rules
papers.q: Do vaccination campaigns affect political participation and support for challengers?
papers.summary: Higher vaccination rates boost political participation and empower challengers regardless of party. Survey evidence suggests vaccines may have increased preferences for challengers by lowering decision-related anxiety.
papers.contribution: Studies Chile's election, with voluntary voting and vaccination halfway implemented by election day, using exogenous vaccine eligibility rules and a pre-analysis plan.
papers.ident: Exogenous age-based vaccine eligibility rules timed before an election, with a pre-analysis plan.
papers.dataDetail: Chilean vaccination and election data with survey evidence.

papers.title: Labor Market Effects of California’s $20 Fast-Food Minimum Wage
papers.summary: The policy raised fast-food wages by about 7 percent. Conventional DiD gives an employment own-wage elasticity of -0.19 and synthetic DiD shrinks it to -0.04, while across 32 specifications elasticities range from -0.29 to +0.26.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences and synthetic difference-in-differences around California's April 2024 fast-food minimum wage.
papers.q: How did California's $20 fast-food minimum wage affect employment?
papers.contribution: Uses QCEW and QWI data and difference-in-differences and synthetic difference-in-differences to estimate the effect of AB 1228.
papers.dataDetail: QCEW data through 2025Q3 and QWI data through 2024Q4.

papers.title: Mortality Rates by Race and Ethnicity Among People with Disabilities
papers.q: How do mortality rates differ by race and ethnicity among low-income adults with disabilities?
papers.summary: American Indian and Alaska Native and White recipients have the highest age-adjusted midlife mortality rates (2.85% and 2.48%), followed by Black and Hispanic (2.18% and 1.82%) and Asian recipients (1.53%). Controlling for diagnoses attenuates several gaps, but not the White-Black gap.
papers.contribution: Uses 2017-2021 Medicaid claims data on SSI recipients to measure racial and ethnic disparities in midlife mortality.
papers.ident: Descriptive: age-adjusted mortality and regressions controlling for diagnoses.
papers.dataDetail: Medicaid claims data on SSI recipients, 2017-2021.

papers.title: Crimes Against Campbell-Shiller
papers.summary: The formula is ill-defined for firms that pay no dividends, and for payers it records buybacks and new issuance as phantom cashflow shocks. Interpreting the forward-looking version as a dynamic Gordon model requires investors to think in present-value terms and know the cap rate with basis-point precision.
papers.ident: Theory and empirical illustrations of the approximation's failures.
papers.q: Does the Campbell-Shiller log-linear approximation hold as a model-free accounting identity?
papers.contribution: Argues that the identity does not hold in sample, in expectation or under arbitrary subjective beliefs.

papers.title: Interest Rate Caps, Competition, and Strategic Borrowing: Evidence from Kenya
papers.q: How did Kenya's interest rate caps reallocate borrowing between an exempt digital platform and capped lenders?
papers.summary: Lending on the exempt platform M-Shwari rose, but the safest borrowers substituted toward cheaper capped credit, riskier borrowers increased savings to build credit limits, and M-Shwari raised limits for safe borrowers to retain them. The carve-out preserves access for high-risk borrowers.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity around the implementation date of the 2016 interest rate cap.
papers.contribution: Uses borrower-level administrative data, survey data and an RD around the 2016 implementation date, plus a model of screening and credit limit-setting.
papers.dataDetail: Borrower-level data from M-Shwari and Kenyan survey data.

papers.title: Separations Revisited: Do Layoffs or Quits Drive Lower Separation Rates in High-Quality Firms?
papers.q: Do layoffs or quits drive the lower separation rates of high-productivity firms?
papers.summary: The productivity-separation gradient is driven mainly by layoffs rather than quits. Wage rigidity turns adverse shocks into layoffs, and high-productivity firms are less exposed because larger markdowns buffer productivity from wages.
papers.contribution: Uses matched employer-employee data from Brazil that distinguish the reason for each separation, and proposes a downward wage rigidity mechanism.
papers.ident: Firm markdowns and market-level wage rigidity in matched employer-employee separation data.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian matched employer-employee data with separation reasons.

papers.title: Health Inequalities Among Danish Retirees 2004-2022
papers.q: How have income gradients in health among Danish retirees evolved from 2004 to 2022?
papers.summary: Higher-income retirees are healthier across all dimensions. Functional and comprehensive health gaps narrow as lower-income retirees improve, while mental health gaps remain large and persistent, and diagnosed and cognitive gradients are smaller and less stable.
papers.ident: Descriptive: income gradients across health domains and survey waves.
papers.contribution: Uses Danish SHARE data to examine income gradients in functional, diagnosed, comprehensive, mental and cognitive health among retirees aged 60-79.
papers.dataDetail: Danish SHARE data, 2004-2022, retirees aged 60-79.

papers.title: Using price incentives to bound welfare from pay as you go solar electricity
papers.q: Can price incentives bound the welfare from pay-as-you-go solar electricity?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study using price incentives to bound welfare from pay-as-you-go solar electricity.

papers.title: On the Negative Consequences of Low-Wage Offshoring for Innovation
papers.q: Does offshoring to China reduce innovation by firms?
papers.summary: Offshoring lowers marginal costs and expands sales, raising returns to innovation, but offshoring low-quality intermediates also cheapens older-generation products and reduces returns to innovating into newer ones. Greater offshoring reduced R&D spending by 15% over 2002-2011.
papers.ident: Shift-share instrument from quality improvements in Chinese intermediate inputs.
papers.contribution: Uses 2002-2011 data on 6,024 Canadian firms and a model-consistent shift-share instrument based on improvements in the quality of HS6 Chinese intermediates.
papers.dataDetail: 6,024 Canadian firms, 2002-2011.

papers.title: Algorithmic Credentialism
papers.summary: The paper draws on research on workers skilled through alternative routes, disability theory's critique of the medical model and doctrine from Griggs v. Duke Power through the Civil Rights Act of 1991. It argues such screens misidentify the source of exclusion, locating it in the worker rather than the design of the selection system.
papers.q: How should credential-coded algorithmic hiring screens be evaluated under existing civil rights law?
papers.contribution: Develops a framework for evaluating algorithmic credentialism, where AI hiring tools encode bachelor's degree requirements as a proxy for skill, under disparate-impact doctrine.

papers.title: Building Opportunity: The Intergenerational Effects of Chilean School Construction
papers.summary: Exposure substantially improved adults' schooling and labor market outcomes and closed a persistent female disadvantage in attainment. Women's exposure had large intergenerational spillovers on children's on-time grade progression and completed schooling.
papers.conclusion: The marginal value of public funds is 13, including direct effects and intergenerational spillovers.
papers.ident: Variation in classroom construction across supply-constrained communities and birth cohorts.
papers.q: What were the intergenerational effects of Chile's 1965-66 school construction?
papers.contribution: Uses a quasi-experimental design and large census samples to study childhood exposure to the building and staffing of thousands of new primary classrooms.
papers.dataDetail: Large Chilean census samples.

papers.title: AlphaGlass: Interpretable Characteristic-Based Portfolio Choice
papers.q: Can an interpretable machine-learning framework build characteristic-based portfolios that directly optimize investment objectives?
papers.summary: End-to-end training optimizes objectives such as the Sharpe ratio while keeping weights traceable to characteristics. Theory shows in-sample maximization consistently estimates the population objective, and in US equities the model delivers strong out-of-sample performance.
papers.contribution: Proposes AlphaGlass, which maps stock characteristics into additive signals with sparse interactions and converts them into long-short portfolios through a differentiable rank-and-mask layer.
papers.ident: Machine learning: interpretable additive models with a differentiable portfolio layer.
papers.dataDetail: US equity returns and stock characteristics.

papers.title: Opt In? Opt Out?
papers.summary: Presumed-consent laws increase donation only when strictly enforced and family veto power is limited, while weak opt-out regimes show negligible or negative effects. The lab experiment shows opt-in generally produces equal or higher donation unless signaling is costly and family veto power is minimal.
papers.contribution: Combines cross-country panel data with an event-study design, a theoretical signaling model and a large laboratory experiment.
papers.q: Do opt-out donation laws raise organ donation more than opt-in systems?
papers.ident: Event study of presumed-consent laws across countries, with a signaling model and lab experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Newly assembled cross-country panel data on organ donation.

papers.title: Bounding treatment effects by pooling limited information across observations
papers.q: How can treatment effects be bounded robustly by pooling only limited information across observations under unconfoundedness?
papers.summary: The bounds are robust when conditioning variables take many values or when overlap fails. No pooling gives Manski bounds and unlimited pooling gives inverse propensity score weighting, and the paper explores the range between them.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: partial identification under unconfoundedness with limited pooling.
papers.contribution: Provides bounds on average treatment effects (on the treated) built from sample averages of functions where each outcome's contribution depends on the treatment status of a limited number of observations.

papers.title: How does Medicare Eligibility affect Choice and Utilization? Evidence from Veterans
papers.q: How does Medicare eligibility at 65 change health care choice and utilization for veterans enrolled in the VA?
papers.summary: Veterans' inpatient hospitalization rate increases by about 3.3 percent at 65, with large reallocations across payers: more use of Medicare and less of VA, commercial and other federal insurance. There are substantial reallocations among those who gain access to nearer hospitals and for more postponeable procedures.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity at the Medicare eligibility age of 65.
papers.contribution: Uses regression discontinuity at age 65 to study VA enrollees whose network is narrow, on the premise that Medicare expands it.
papers.dataDetail: Hospitalization data on veterans enrolled in the Veterans Health Administration.

papers.title: Winsorizing and trimming in RCTs
papers.summary: Pooled winsorizing can disproportionately affect treatment or control observations. A formal framework and Monte Carlo simulations show stratified winsorizing reduces treatment effect bias and Type II error, at the cost of more Type I errors, with applications to two published RCTs.
papers.ident: Econometric methodology: stratified outlier handling in randomized trials, with Monte Carlo simulations.
papers.q: Should winsorizing and trimming in randomized trials be done separately by treatment arm?
papers.contribution: Proposes Stratified Winsorizing/Trimming, which winsorizes each treatment group separately so equal proportions are winsorized per arm.
papers.dataDetail: Applications to Angelucci et al. (2023) and another published RCT.

papers.title: Restricting video games in China: Effects on time use, educational achievement, and health
papers.q: How did restrictions on video games in China affect time use, educational achievement and health?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effects of restricting video games in China on time use, educational achievement and health.

papers.title: What did we learn from the North American Income Maintenance Experiments? New data and evidence on two-parent families
papers.q: What did the North American Income Maintenance Experiments teach us about two-parent families?
papers.summary: The title indicates a reassessment of the North American Income Maintenance Experiments with new data and evidence on two-parent families.

papers.title: Open Rule Legislative Bargaining
papers.summary: In this class of equilibria, delays tend to be longer and allocations less egalitarian than originally predicted by Baron and Ferejohn. The results bear on efficiency and fairness of open versus closed rules and of bargaining more generally.
papers.q: How do open rule legislative bargaining outcomes differ from the Baron-Ferejohn predictions?
papers.contribution: Provides a fresh analysis of open rule bargaining based on a class of stationary equilibria.
papers.ident: Theory: stationary equilibria of open rule legislative bargaining.

papers.title: Counterfactual Analysis for Structural Dynamic Discrete Choice Models

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research
Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro

papers.q: How much can be learned about counterfactuals in dynamic discrete choice models under partial identification?
papers.summary: Discrete choice data recover utility differences but only a narrow set of counterfactuals are point-identified in dynamic models. Mild model restrictions can gradually shrink the identified set, and the paper develops tractable tools for high-dimensional problems.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: partial identification of counterfactuals in dynamic discrete choice models.
papers.contribution: Derives bounds for low-dimensional counterfactual objects such as average welfare, with a uniformly valid inference procedure and new computational algorithms.
papers.dataDetail: Monte Carlo illustrations.

papers.title: Weather or climate? A new perspective on temperature shocks
papers.q: Should temperature shocks be understood as weather or climate effects?
papers.summary: The title indicates a new perspective on temperature shocks, distinguishing weather from climate.

papers.title: Rate of return regulation revisited

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.summary: There is a significant premium for regulated returns, and firms strategically time rate cases so regulated returns respond faster to increases than decreases in capital costs. A one percentage point rise in return on equity corresponds to a 2%-4% increase in capital assets.
papers.q: Do regulated utilities earn excess returns and overinvest in capital under rate of return regulation?
papers.contribution: Uses a comprehensive database of utility rate cases to compare regulated returns on equity with capital cost benchmarks.
papers.conclusion: Excess costs to US consumers average $7 billion per year.
papers.ident: Panel regressions on rate case outcomes relative to capital cost benchmarks.
papers.dataDetail: Database of US utility rate cases.

papers.title: The Dynamics of Verification when Searching for Quality
papers.summary: With low verification cost and a long horizon, the optimal mechanism uses a deterministic rule that first discriminates on quality but chooses a project irrespective of quality at a deadline. Verification occurs with intermediate probability before the deadline, declining over time.
papers.contribution: Characterizes optimal mechanisms for a principal who can select one project and verify quality at a cost, without transfers.
papers.q: How should a principal verify project quality over time when an agent only wants a project chosen?
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic mechanism design with costly verification.

papers.title: Bayesian model averaging with non-conjugate priors
papers.q: How can Bayesian model averaging be done with non-conjugate priors?
papers.summary: The title indicates an econometric study of Bayesian model averaging with non-conjugate priors.

papers.title: Bank concentration, product market competition and productivity growth
papers.q: How does bank concentration affect product market competition and productivity growth?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how bank concentration, product market competition and productivity growth are related.

papers.title: Ignorance is Whose Bliss: The Repeal of Compulsory Premarital Health Examinations and Marital Outcomes in Rural China

authors.inst: École Supérieure des Sciences Économiques et Commerciales

papers.q: What happens to marital sorting and child health when compulsory premarital health examinations are repealed?
papers.summary: Removing health information shifts sorting toward socioeconomic status, with a larger shift in provinces with higher pre-policy exam rates. The decrease in health-based assortative matching worsens child health, followed by a decline in postmarital subjective well-being.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences across provinces by pre-policy premarital health exam rates.
papers.contribution: Builds a matching model with socioeconomic status and health and tests it with the repeal of premarital health exams in rural China using provincial exposure.
papers.dataDetail: Rural China survey and marriage data.

papers.title: Does irrigation reduce migration intentions after drought? Evidence from West Africa

authors.inst: United Nations University Institute on Comparative Regional Integration Studies
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
United Nations University Institute on Comparative Regional Integration Studies

papers.q: Does irrigation reduce migration intentions after drought in West Africa?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of whether irrigation reduces migration intentions after drought, using evidence from West Africa.

papers.title: Trafficking as choice? Evidence from Nigeria
papers.q: Is human trafficking from Nigeria sometimes a chosen, constrained migration strategy rather than deception?
papers.summary: A substantial share of respondents is willing to migrate via traffickers despite awareness of forced labor risks, and the list experiment suggests underreporting of approval, especially among women. Willingness is highest among those with strong aspirations but limited capabilities.
papers.contribution: Uses original survey data from two waves in 2021 and 2023 covering more than 2,700 respondents in Edo State, with a list experiment on trafficking approval.
papers.ident: List experiment and descriptive analysis in an aspirations-capabilities framework.
papers.dataDetail: Two survey waves (2021, 2023) of more than 2,700 respondents in Edo State, Nigeria.

papers.title: Concentrated MCMC estimation

authors.inst: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.q: How can MCMC estimation be done with concentrated likelihoods?
papers.summary: The title indicates an econometric study of concentrated MCMC estimation.

papers.title: Shaping Society's Character: The Role of Schools in Developing Social and Emotional Skills
papers.summary: Education fosters traits promoting cooperation, trust and long-term societal well-being beyond cognitive ability. School-based interventions can instill perseverance, enhance social learning, curb anti-social tendencies and promote prosocial behavior, shaping beliefs, attitudes and social capital across generations.
papers.q: How do schools shape social and emotional skills and society's character?
papers.contribution: Reviews how schools cultivate socio-emotional skills, drawing on neuroscience, psychology and economics and on experimental studies of school-based interventions.

papers.title: Understanding Medicaid Managed Care: The Procured Competition Model
papers.q: What does the economics of Medicaid managed care look like as a hybrid of public procurement and regulated competition?
papers.summary: Over three quarters of Medicaid's more than 75 million enrollees receive care through private managed care insurers. Evidence on privatization is mixed, since contracting out has not meaningfully reduced public costs or improved quality.
papers.contribution: Reviews the evidence on Medicaid privatization and proposes the procured competition framework, discussing policy levers across procurement, competition and consumer choice.

papers.title: Rental Prices and the Cost of Living in the United States, 1914–2006
papers.contribution: Constructs a new consistent shelter price series from the Historical Housing Prices Project rental index and revised shelter weights going back to 1914.
papers.summary: The BLS rent series implies nominal rents grew 2.6% a year versus 3.3% for overall prices, which is explained by the changing treatment of shelter in the CPI. The new series rises by a factor of 28.4 versus 10.7 for the official one, and an alternate CPI applying owners' equivalent rent consistently lifts average CPI growth from 3.3% to 3.6% a year.
papers.ident: Descriptive: reconstruction of consistent shelter price indices.
papers.q: Why do official rental price series show falling real rents from 1914 to 2006?
papers.dataDetail: Historical Housing Prices Project rental index and BLS CPI shelter data, 1914-2006.

papers.title: The Effects of School Phone Bans: National Evidence from Lockable Pouches
papers.q: What are the effects of lockable phone pouches in schools on phone use, behavior, wellbeing and achievement?
papers.summary: Pouch adoption substantially reduces phone use. Disciplinary incidents rise and student wellbeing appears to fall in the first year, consistent with short-term disruption, but disciplinary effects fade and wellbeing effects recover and become positive in later years.
papers.ident: Staggered difference-in-differences around school adoption of lockable phone pouches.
papers.contribution: Combines nationwide teacher survey data, GPS pings, test scores, school administrative records and pouch sales data in a staggered difference-in-differences design.
papers.dataDetail: Teacher survey, GPS pings, standardized test scores, school records and sales records from the largest pouch provider.

papers.title: Retrospective Versus Prospective Meritocracy
papers.q: What differs between retrospective and prospective conceptions of meritocracy?
papers.contribution: Proposes distinguishing retrospective meritocracy, based on past achievements, from prospective meritocracy, based on comparative contribution to social objectives, and analyzes them with formal models.
papers.summary: The two conceptions have very different implications for assigning students to schools or workers to jobs and need different information from a policymaker. Alternate versions may or may not be socially efficient.
papers.ident: Theory: formal models of meritocratic assignment.

papers.title: The Value of Reliable Statistics
papers.q: What is the economic value of public trust in official statistics?
papers.summary: Economic policy uncertainty rose sharply after the firing, consistent with reduced trust in official data raising uncertainty for investors, businesses and households. The baseline implies benefits of about $25 for every $1 of the agency's budget.
