papers.ident: Event study of the BLS commissioner's firing on policy uncertainty.
papers.contribution: Uses an event study of the August 2025 firing of the BLS head on policy uncertainty and maps it into implied macroeconomic outcomes.
papers.dataDetail: Economic policy uncertainty measures around August 1, 2025.

papers.title: Sticky Traditions: Origin, Persistence, and Evolution of Cultural Norms
papers.contribution: Reviews the literature on the origin, persistence and evolution of cultural norms, covering deep historical forces and vertical, horizontal and oblique transmission.
papers.summary: Cultural norms persist for remarkably long periods, though the speed of change varies across traits. Norms rooted in deep historical values are most resistant to change.
papers.q: Where do cultural norms come from, how do they persist, and when do they change?

papers.title: The State-Contingent Debt Premium: Evidence from French Public Bonds
papers.q: What premium do investors demand for state-contingent debt?
papers.contribution: Estimates the premium using a quasi-twin bond strategy with two similar French government bonds issued in 1956, one conventional and one with coupons linked to industrial production.
papers.summary: At issuance the expected yield on the state-contingent bond was 77 basis points higher than its twin, and the realized premium was roughly twice as large (146) given robust growth. Rising prices reduced both spreads to zero by 1964, and they rose again after the unexpected May 1968 general strike.
papers.ident: Quasi-twin bonds with similar terms but different coupon indexation.
papers.dataDetail: Prices of French government bonds issued in 1956.

papers.title: Adolescent Behavior, Learning, and Knowledge Diffusion: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
papers.q: Can shifting responsibility for classroom behavioral norms from teachers to students improve learning?
papers.summary: The program improves the classroom social climate, with stronger cooperation, behavioral norms and supportive peer networks, and high-performing students gain most in math and verbal tests. A follow-up 1.5 years later shows social climate gains fade while academic gains persist and extend more broadly.
papers.contribution: Evaluates a randomized program covering over 7,500 adolescents in 127 Bangladeshi middle schools.
papers.ident: Randomized school-level assignment of a student-led behavior management program.
papers.dataDetail: Over 7,500 students in 127 Bangladeshi middle schools.

papers.title: Beliefs, Attention, and Investments in Early Childhood
papers.q: How do distorted parental beliefs and limited attention trap parents in low investment in early childhood?
papers.contribution: Models bandwidth-constrained parents whose motivated reasoning distorts beliefs about the returns to responsive interaction, with four channels for escaping the trap.
papers.summary: Distorted beliefs suppress responsive parenting, which generates no calibration evidence and confirms the distortion. A randomized controlled trial confirms predictions on parental beliefs, responsive parenting and behavioral engagement, with no impact on materials or placebo outcomes.
papers.ident: Model predictions tested in a randomized controlled trial.

papers.title: Till the IRS Do Us Part: (Optimal) Taxation of Households

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.contribution: Builds a model with one- and two-earner households, human capital and extensive margin labor supply to compare tax systems.
papers.summary: A progressive system taxing individuals rather than couples jointly leads to higher labor force participation and human capital and more fiscal space. The peak of the Laffer curve is 18 percentage points higher than under the current system.
papers.ident: Quantitative: life-cycle model with one- and two-earner households comparing tax systems.
papers.q: Would individual progressive taxation of married couples raise more revenue than the US household-based system?

papers.title: Monetary Policy According to Households: Perceptions, Reactions and Channels
papers.q: How do households perceive the transmission of monetary policy and how do these perceptions affect their decisions?
papers.contribution: Combines a survey of over 25,000 US households with randomized information treatments to measure expectations of the effect of federal funds rate changes.
papers.summary: Households reduce spending, especially on durables, when rates rise, but through mechanisms that differ from standard models: they expect tightening to raise borrowing costs and inflation, and respond to higher expected inflation by reducing consumption. Inflation expectations emerge as a central driver.
papers.ident: Randomized information treatments in a large household survey.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of over 25,000 US households.

papers.title: The Annuity Puzzle Revisited: Barriers, Behavior, and Policy Paths to Lifetime Income
papers.q: Why do so few people buy annuities despite standard models predicting high demand?
papers.contribution: Introduces annuities, reviews the leading explanations for the annuity puzzle and outlines approaches to increase uptake and improve decision quality.
papers.summary: Wealth decumulation involves intertemporal tradeoffs, uncertainty, complexity and emotion, and many consumers receive little guidance. Few individuals purchase life annuities despite their insurance against outliving resources.

papers.title: How Artificial Intelligence Shapes Science: Evidence from AlphaFold
papers.q: How has AlphaFold changed structural biology and downstream science?
papers.summary: Researchers gained access to hundreds of thousands of predicted structures overnight, yet the rate of experimental structure determination has stayed almost unchanged. Researchers appear to use predicted structures to complement and facilitate experimental determination.
papers.contribution: Studies the 2021 release of AlphaFold2 and its impact on structural biology and related fields.
papers.ident: Event study around the July 2021 release of AlphaFold2 structures.
papers.dataDetail: Protein structure and publication data in structural biology.

papers.title: Power to the Personnel? The Impacts of Managerial Discretion vs. Worker Democracy in Employee Recognition
papers.contribution: Runs a firm-level RCT in India randomizing whether recognition and bonuses are allocated by worker vote, by manager discretion, or at random.
papers.summary: Workplace democracy increases worker attendance while managerial discretion improves productivity. The manager arm also reduces work-related discussions between workers, and winners differ in selection across arms.
papers.ident: Randomized allocation mechanism for employee recognition and bonuses.
papers.q: Does worker voting or managerial discretion work better for employee recognition?
papers.dataDetail: Firm-level data from an Indian firm.

papers.title: Industrial Policy with Development Characteristics: Fertilizer Policy in Times of Crisis
papers.q: How should governments time-consistently design fertilizer subsidies when farmers face financial frictions and price crises?
papers.summary: After fertilizer prices doubled with Russia's invasion of Ukraine, more fertilizer-intensive villages had 30% lower fertilizer spending, 21% lower harvests and 11% higher output prices than less intensive ones. These patterns discipline the model, where the optimal response balances reallocating production toward less fertilizer-dependent villages and dampening consumption losses in dependent ones.
papers.ident: Variation in village fertilizer intensity around the post-invasion price doubling, with a structural model.
papers.contribution: Builds a time-consistent optimal policy model with undiversified owner-operators and collects household data from 444 rural Rwandan villages for 2020-2024.
papers.dataDetail: Household data from 444 rural Rwandan villages, 2020-2024.

papers.title: Data Neutrality, Data Supply, and Market Competition
papers.q: How do data neutrality rules affect downstream competition, platform data production and consumer welfare?
papers.summary: Weak neutrality can be largely ineffective because the platform may restore exclusion through discriminatory pricing. Strong neutrality broadens access and intensifies downstream competition but reduces the platform's incentive to produce data, so it does not necessarily raise welfare.
papers.contribution: Analyzes weak data neutrality, equal data amounts to affiliated and unaffiliated sellers, and strong data neutrality, equal data and equal prices.
papers.ident: Theory: platform data supply with affiliated and unaffiliated sellers.

papers.title: The Labor Market as an Equilibrium Newsvendor Problem
papers.contribution: Models hiring under uncertainty with permanent labor as a buffer or spot hiring after demand is realized, and evaluates it with daily time sheet records for registered nurses.
papers.summary: One firm's reliance on spot labor thickens the market others use, which firms do not internalize, so equilibrium has too much buffering. Markets with thicker agency markets have less rationing and compressed upper tails of permanent staffing.
papers.ident: Structural: equilibrium newsvendor model estimated on facility-level time sheet data.
papers.q: Does the labor market involve too much permanent staffing buffer when spot hiring thickens a shared market?
papers.dataDetail: Universe of daily time sheet records from skilled nursing facilities.

papers.title: Filling the Gaps with MICE: Addressing Missing Data in Real Estate Price Indices
papers.q: How should missing characteristics be handled in hedonic real estate price indices?
papers.contribution: Proposes multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) to restore incomplete observations in index construction.
papers.summary: Missingness typically occurs in the characteristics used for quality adjustment, so complete-case analysis can skew measured price dynamics through selection and composition effects. The paper adapts the aggregation of multiple imputation results because Rubin's rules do not align with the multiplicative index structure.
papers.ident: Econometric methodology: multiple imputation for hedonic price indices.
papers.dataDetail: Micro-level real estate transaction data.

papers.title: Replacement and Reputation
papers.q: Does electoral replacement ensure officeholders eventually act in voters' interests?
papers.summary: Good long-run outcomes are always attainable, but the mechanism depends on economic conditions. Where incentive provision is feasible, some equilibria feature sustained effort while others have long-run shirking, and in the complementary case selection dominates and every equilibrium settles on a good politician.
papers.ident: Theory: reputational model of electoral accountability with good and opportunist types.
papers.contribution: Studies a reputational model of accountability in which voters observe incumbents' performance and decide on replacement.

papers.title: Moving to opportunity for polluting: Intra-city evidence from China’s land market

authors.inst: University of International Business and Economics

papers.q: Do polluting firms move to opportunity within cities through China's land market?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of intra-city pollution and land allocation in China's land market.

papers.title: Improved density forecasts using mixed frequency data:A Bayesian approach
papers.q: Can mixed frequency data improve density forecasts in a Bayesian framework?
papers.summary: The title indicates a Bayesian approach to improving density forecasts using mixed frequency data.

papers.title: Trade liberalization, wage rigidity, and labor market dynamics with heterogeneous firms
papers.q: How do trade liberalization and wage rigidity interact in labor market dynamics with heterogeneous firms?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of trade liberalization, wage rigidity and labor market dynamics with heterogeneous firms.

papers.title: Campaigning to a Polarised Electorate: Emotions and Information in Real Election Campaigns
papers.summary: In-person engagement providing policy information increases votes for the party even in polarised contexts. Both strategies increase learning and neither produces backlash among pro-incumbent voters, with some cross-cutting moderating effects.
papers.ident: Randomized canvassing treatments in a real election campaign.
papers.q: Do policy-focused and emotional campaign strategies move votes and polarisation in a polarised electorate?
papers.contribution: Runs a field experiment with a mainstream opposition party in the 2019 Philippine senatorial election, comparing policy canvassing with an added emotional engagement component.
papers.dataDetail: Field experiment in the 2019 Philippine senatorial election.

papers.title: Tariffs and Goods-Market Search Frictions
papers.q: How do goods-market search frictions change optimal tariffs?
papers.summary: Search frictions add two terms to the standard optimal tariff, one lowering tariffs when contact rates are low and one when private export costs exceed social opportunity costs, and create incentives to subsidize imports through market thickness. Calibrated to US and Chinese data, higher baseline search costs reduce optimal US unilateral and Nash tariffs.
papers.ident: Structural: calibrated search model of trade with optimal tariff analysis.
papers.contribution: Builds a general equilibrium dynamic model with search between heterogeneous exporters and importing retailers and characterizes welfare-maximizing unilateral tariffs.
papers.dataDetail: US and Chinese 2016 data.

papers.title: Raising the bar: An inclusive global poverty line

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: What is an appropriate global upper-bound poverty line to complement the dollar-a-day lower bound?
papers.summary: The upper bound is set at the consumption consistent with the achievement of adequate nutrition and other basic needs, using two conceptually distinct approaches. It complements the widely accepted lower bound of P$2.15 (2017 PPP) and gives an inclusive global poverty measure.
papers.contribution: Estimates a global upper-bound poverty line using two approaches grounded in the tension between the focus axiom and standard social welfare measures.
papers.ident: Descriptive: estimation of poverty line from consumption and welfare axioms.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country household consumption data in 2017 PPP.

papers.title: The Effect of Field Training Officers on Police Use of Force
papers.q: Do field training officers shape how much force new police recruits use?
papers.summary: A 1 standard deviation increase in the training officer's force propensity raises the recruit's use of force by 14 to 18 percent, persisting for at least two years. On-the-job training thus matters in policing, and field training is a promising avenue for reform.
papers.ident: Conditional as-good-as-random assignment of recruits to field training officers.
papers.contribution: Exploits conditional as-good-as-random assignment of recruits to field training officers to estimate the causal effect of the officer's force propensity.
papers.dataDetail: Police department records on recruits, field training officers and use of force.

papers.title: Identification and Estimation of Dynamic Random Coefficient Models
papers.contribution: Characterizes identified sets for the mean, variance and CDF of coefficients in linear panel models with predetermined regressors and individual-specific coefficients.
papers.summary: The model is partially rather than point identified in a short panel, and the characterization yields tractable estimation and inference. Applied to PSID lifecycle earnings dynamics, the results suggest unobserved heterogeneity in earnings persistence, so households face varying earnings risk.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: partial identification in dynamic random coefficient panel models.
papers.q: What can be identified about heterogeneous coefficients in dynamic panel models with short panels?
papers.dataDetail: Panel Study of Income Dynamics, US households.

papers.title: The Attention-Information Trade-Off
papers.q: How does information transmission change when senders must attract receivers' attention?
papers.summary: Attention incentives lead to significantly less information transmitted but not more inaccurate content. They raise knowledge among interested receivers but lower knowledge and increase biased beliefs among the majority who do not demand more information.
papers.ident: Randomized attention incentives for content creators and randomized exposure of receivers to content.
papers.contribution: Combines an experiment varying freelance professionals' attention incentives with online experiments exposing receivers to the content created.
papers.conclusion: Missing information is a channel through which misperceptions arise.
papers.dataDetail: Experiment with freelance professionals summarizing scientific findings and online receiver experiments.

papers.title: Local Projection-Based Inference under General Conditions
papers.q: How can local projection inference be made robust and efficient under general conditions?
papers.contribution: Develops uniform asymptotic theory for local projections with unknown, possibly infinite lag order, and proposes inference procedures for level and cumulated impulse responses.
papers.summary: Local projections can achieve semiparametric efficiency at a given horizon if the controlled lag order diverges, so the perceived efficiency loss can become negligible with many controls. The proposed inference procedures have robustness properties not shared by existing methods.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: uniform asymptotics for local projection impulse responses.

papers.title: Medical Technology and Life Expectancy: Evidence from the Antitoxin Treatment of Diphtheria
papers.q: How much did diphtheria antitoxin raise life expectancy in early twentieth-century Massachusetts?
papers.summary: Rapid availability of free antitoxin, the first effective treatment for an infectious disease, significantly increased life expectancy at young ages. Medicine combined with effective public health policy mattered more for the early twentieth century health transition than previously thought.
papers.contribution: Uses newly collected municipality-level antitoxin distribution data and over 1.5 million death certificates from 1880 to 1914.
papers.ident: Staggered municipal availability of free antitoxin compared with mortality changes.
papers.dataDetail: Municipality-level antitoxin distribution and over 1.5 million Massachusetts death certificates, 1880-1914.

papers.title: The Big Short (Interest): Closing the Loopholes in the Dividend-Withholding Tax
papers.q: What happens when enforcement of the dividend-withholding tax is tightened?
papers.summary: Shares on loan spike sharply around dividend dates across Nordic markets, consistent with abuse of the withholding tax system. After the reform the Danish spikes disappear and annual DWT revenue rises by 130 percent, with no harm to stock returns, investment or dividend yield.
papers.contribution: Compares a 2016 Danish enforcement reform with its Nordic neighbors using shares-on-loan data around dividend dates.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing Denmark with Nordic neighbors around the 2016 enforcement reform.
papers.dataDetail: Shares-on-loan data for Nordic stock markets and Danish tax revenue.

papers.title: Almost fare free: Impact of a cheap public transport ticket on mobility patterns and train delays
papers.q: How did a cheap public transport ticket change mobility patterns and train delays?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effects of a cheap public transport ticket on mobility patterns and train delays.

papers.title: Harnessing Deductions to Increase Tax Compliance and Formalization

authors.inst: European School of Management and Technology

papers.q: Can generous personal income tax deductions for receipts raise compliance among small self-employed businesses?
papers.summary: Reported profits increase significantly among self-employed businesses exposed to the reform, with spillover effects on VAT. Additional tax payments outweigh the foregone tax revenue in the net-revenue analysis.
papers.ident: Exposure to the reform varying across regions and professions with differing receipt demand.
papers.contribution: Evaluates an Ecuadorian reform introducing PIT deductions that encourage consumers to request receipts, using variation in receipt demand across regions and professions.
papers.dataDetail: Ecuadorian tax administration data on individuals and businesses.

papers.title: Cooking, Health, and Daily Exposure to Pollution Spikes
papers.q: Do improved cookstoves reduce daily pollution spikes and improve health?
papers.summary: Improved cookstoves cut PM2.5 spikes while cooking by 51.3 μg/m3 (41 percent) and reduce self-reported respiratory symptoms by 0.24 standard deviation. After more than three years of use there are no clinical health improvements, possibly because average exposure is unchanged.
papers.contribution: Combines experimental variation in cooking technology with high-frequency individual pollution exposure and time-use data in Kenya.
papers.ident: Randomized assignment of improved cookstoves.
papers.dataDetail: High-frequency personal PM2.5 monitoring, time-use and clinical measures in Kenya.

papers.title: Responses to Extreme Temperatures: Migrant Networks and International Migration from El Salvador
papers.summary: Income losses from extreme temperatures combine with established US migration networks to increase emigration from El Salvador. The pattern likely extends to roughly 30 million low-income farms globally with access to remittances.
papers.q: Do extreme temperatures increase international migration from El Salvador through migrant networks?
papers.contribution: Shows that extreme temperatures reduce corn yields, cutting postharvest input use and agricultural labor demand, and raise emigration where US networks are strong.
papers.ident: Panel variation in extreme temperature exposure across municipalities interacted with network strength.
papers.dataDetail: Salvadoran municipal temperature, agricultural and migration data.

papers.title: State Recreational Cannabis Laws and Racial Disparities in the Criminal Legal System

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.q: How does recreational cannabis legalization affect racial disparities in the criminal legal system?
papers.summary: Legalization reduces cannabis possession and sales arrests for both groups, narrowing but not eliminating disparities. Spillovers include increases in hospitalizations involving cannabis and other illegal drugs, while spillovers on arrests, incarceration and serious crime are insignificant or negative.
papers.contribution: Estimates direct and spillover effects of state legalization on arrests, incarceration, hospitalizations and crime for White and Black populations.
papers.ident: Staggered state legalization compared across states and time.
papers.dataDetail: State-level arrest, incarceration, crime and hospitalization data by race.

papers.title: Complements or substitutes? Labor market effects of foreign inputs in developing economies

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.q: Are foreign inputs complements or substitutes for labor in developing economies?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of labor market effects of foreign inputs in developing economies, asking whether they are complements or substitutes.

papers.title: China's Global Ownership
papers.q: How large is China's global corporate footprint and what are its real effects on target firms?
papers.contribution: Assembles a micro-level dataset of 161,773 firms in 159 countries (2012-2021) and reconstructs multi-layered ownership chains through offshore tax havens to the ultimate owner.
papers.summary: The footprint is substantially broader than official FDI statistics, with Chinese-controlled foreign assets growing 20% annually to $2.1 trillion, roughly 3% of global corporate assets, by 2021. Chinese investors, especially SOEs, target R&D-intensive and supply-chain-linked firms, whose capital and R&D rise after acquisition without higher patent output and with lower profitability.
papers.ident: Event-study comparison of acquired firms with controls, with ownership reconstructed from firm records.
papers.dataDetail: 161,773 firms in 159 countries, 2012-2021, with ownership chains.

papers.title: A Measure of Behavioral Heterogeneity

authors.inst: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.q: How can behavioral heterogeneity among stochastic individuals be measured from choices?
papers.contribution: Proposes a choice-based measure of heterogeneity equal to the probability that two sampled individuals' choices differ over a random menu.
papers.summary: The measure has axiomatic foundations and a decomposition that separates heterogeneity into intrapersonal and interpersonal components.
papers.ident: Theory: axiomatic characterization of a heterogeneity measure over stochastic choice.

papers.title: The Welfare Effects of Protecting Older Workers
papers.q: What are the welfare effects of banning mandatory retirement at age 65?
papers.summary: The bans sharply reduce retirements at 65, with sizable announcement effects, and raise post-65 employment and earnings by at least 14 percent. Older workers save more, spouses postpone retirement and public finances benefit, with no observable effects on mortality or younger workers, while exposed firms cut payroll costs through hiring adjustments and keep productivity and profitability.
papers.ident: Staggered provincial bans on mandatory retirement compared across provinces.
papers.contribution: Evaluates five Canadian provincial mandatory retirement bans from 2005 to 2009 with linked employer-employee tax data.
papers.conclusion: Protecting older workers was welfare-improving.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian linked employer-employee tax data, 2005-2009 bans.

papers.title: Trends in Health Inequalities among Spanish Retirees
papers.q: How have health inequalities among Spanish retirees evolved from 2004 to 2022?
papers.contribution: Analyzes eight SHARE waves, estimating income-related gradients, catch-up times and concentration indices across five health outcomes.
papers.summary: The outcomes are limitations in daily and instrumental activities, chronic conditions, a composite deficiency index, mental health (EURO-D) and cognitive performance. Linear regressions adjusted for age and sex assess income gradients, complemented by a catch-up time measure and concentration indices of bad health.
papers.ident: Descriptive: income gradients and concentration indices from repeated survey waves.
papers.dataDetail: Eight waves of SHARE for Spain, 2004-2022.

papers.title: Early Childcare Attendance and Cognitive skills in Adolescence
papers.q: Does starting childcare earlier improve cognitive skills in adolescence?
papers.summary: Starting childcare one year earlier raises grade 9 math scores by 9.7% of a standard deviation. Children of mothers without a high school diploma gain 28% of a standard deviation, reducing the gap with children of higher-educated mothers by about one third, with strong improvements for children of immigrants.
papers.contribution: Exploits a 2003 policy expansion creating quasi-random variation in childcare slots for ages 1-2 to estimate effects on grade 5 and grade 9 achievement.
papers.ident: Quasi-random childcare slot availability from the 2003 policy expansion.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative data on childcare attendance and grade 5 and 9 test scores.

papers.title: The Effect of Mergers on Innovation

authors.inst: National Research University Higher School of Economics
City St George's, University of London

papers.q: How does a merger affect innovation when the feasibility of innovation is uncertain?
papers.summary: A merger may reduce follow-up innovations, raise the probability of the first game-changer innovation and bring it forward in time. Mergers are more desirable when R&D outcomes are highly uncertain, and their benefit may be higher when first and subsequent innovations are closer substitutes.
papers.contribution: Builds a dynamic R&D model with uncertainty about feasibility and identifies three merger effects: cannibalization, appropriability and informational.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic R&D game with uncertain feasibility.

papers.title: On the Resilience of Payment Methods
papers.q: How resilient are payment methods to disruptions in digital infrastructure?
papers.summary: Natural disasters, especially hurricanes, generate persistent outages that sharply reduce expenditures. Disasters alone do not change payment choice; shifts toward cash arise through channels such as electronic methods becoming unavailable.
papers.ident: Event studies of natural disaster outages on spending and payment methods.
papers.contribution: Combines county-level electricity outage and weather data, transaction-level expenditure data, household scanner data and new surveys from the United States, Spain and Sweden.
papers.dataDetail: County-level electricity outages, weather records, transaction-level and scanner data and surveys in the US, Spain and Sweden.

papers.title: A Blended Data Approach to Measuring Monthly Housing Starts: Satellite Imagery, Survey Data and More!
papers.summary: Post-prediction steps exclude areas intersecting known buildings or roads, treat missing data from cloud cover and adjust the estimates. The work is part of the Census Bureau's Construction Re-engineering Initiative to supplement or replace field interviews.
papers.q: Can satellite imagery and machine learning measure monthly housing starts?
papers.contribution: Applies convolutional neural networks to monthly satellite images for a subset of Survey of Construction places to predict new single-family residential construction.
papers.ident: Machine learning: CNN prediction of construction from satellite images, blended with survey data.
papers.dataDetail: Monthly satellite images blended with US Census Bureau Survey of Construction data.

papers.title: Risky Insurance: Life-Cycle Insurance Portfolio Choice with Incomplete Markets
papers.q: Why do consumers hold so little life insurance, annuities and long-term care insurance?
papers.contribution: Studies demand for savings and insurance with novel survey data on beliefs about nonpayment risk and a structural life-cycle model with incomplete markets.
papers.summary: Individuals perceive substantial nonpayment risk and these beliefs predict ownership. Access to existing imperfect insurance reduces median wealth by 16% and gives a 0.6% welfare gain, while eliminating nonpayment risk would raise ownership, cut median savings a further 11% and add a 1.7% welfare gain.
papers.ident: Structural: life-cycle portfolio model with elicited beliefs about insurer nonpayment.
papers.dataDetail: Novel survey data on insurance ownership and nonpayment risk beliefs.

papers.title: Voter Information and Distributive Politics
papers.q: Does more information benefit voters in distributive politics?
papers.contribution: Models distributive politics with electoral accountability and informational heterogeneity, including voters' ability to communicate.
papers.summary: Homogeneously informed electorates can benefit from less information through better control or screening of politicians. With heterogeneous information, the distribution of resources and welfare depends on the nature of heterogeneity and communication, and less-informed voters can end up better off than more-informed ones.
papers.ident: Theory: electoral accountability model with heterogeneously informed voters.

papers.title: The Organization of Innovation: Incomplete Contracts and the Outsourcing Decision
papers.q: Why do firms outsource R&D for some products but conduct it in-house for similar ones?
papers.contribution: Introduces a theoretical model in which in-house development gives firms more control over a new product's location in product space to limit cannibalization.
papers.summary: The more profitable a firm's existing products, the more it wants to limit cannibalization and the more it favors in-house R&D. An empirical analysis of pharmaceutical patents, patent expiration and outsourcing at various R&D stages supports the predictions.
papers.ident: Theory: incomplete contracts model of R&D outsourcing, tested on pharmaceutical data.
papers.dataDetail: Pharmaceutical patents, patent expiration and R&D outsourcing data by stage.

papers.title: Forecasting with Feedback
papers.q: Can biased forecasts be optimal when forecasts feed back into policy and the target?
papers.summary: The result arises when actions taken in response to the forecast affect the realization of the target itself. The theory is motivated by stylized properties of Greenbook inflation forecasts, and implies that policy feedback challenges traditional tests of forecast rationality.
papers.ident: Theory: forecasting model with policy feedback, motivated by Greenbook forecasts.
papers.contribution: Proposes that forecasts informing policy decisions can be optimally biased even under quadratic loss when the forecaster is uncertain about the policymaker's reaction.
papers.dataDetail: Federal Reserve Greenbook inflation forecasts.

papers.title: Strategic Evidence Disclosure in Networks and Equilibrium Discrimination
papers.summary: In one equilibrium, adversarial disclosure leads the principal to statistically discriminate between agents by their number of neighbors. All equilibria satisfying robustness criteria lie between this one and a less informative equilibrium with no snitching and no discrimination.
papers.q: How does strategic disclosure of evidence in networks lead to equilibrium discrimination?
papers.contribution: Models agents with ex ante identical uncertain quality who may hold evidence about their network neighbors and themselves, competing for a prize.
papers.ident: Theory: evidence disclosure game on a network.

papers.title: Concentration in Product Markets
papers.q: How concentrated are narrowly defined consumer product markets in the United States, and how has concentration changed?
papers.contribution: Measures concentration in narrowly defined markets for a broad range of consumer goods and services from 1994 to 2019.
papers.summary: Concentration levels are high, with 44.4 percent of markets highly concentrated by US regulators' definition, yet concentration has been falling since 1994, with the median HHI declining from 2,362 to 2,045. This contrasts with prior literature using overly broad market definitions.
papers.ident: Descriptive: HHI measured in narrowly defined product markets.
papers.dataDetail: US consumer goods and services market data, 1994-2019.

papers.title: On Taking a Skewed Risk More than Once
papers.summary: Classical behavioral theories such as prospect theory therefore explain penny-picking straightforwardly. The dynamics of skewness also reconcile apparent preference reversals concerning avoidance and acceptance of skewed and non-skewed risks.
papers.q: Why do people repeatedly take negatively skewed risks despite seeking skewness?
papers.contribution: Shows that penny-picking can occur because of skewness-seeking, since risks with arbitrary negative skewness can be gambled over time so overall skewness is positive.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic gambling strategies and skewness under prospect theory.

papers.title: Identification of first-price auctions with endogenous entry and possibly biased beliefs
papers.q: How are first-price auctions identified with endogenous entry and possibly biased beliefs?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the identification of first-price auctions with endogenous entry and possibly biased beliefs.

papers.title: Have global value chains shifted?
papers.q: Have global value chains shifted?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of whether global value chains have shifted.

papers.title: Transfer estimates for causal effects across heterogeneous sites
papers.q: How can causal effects be transferred across heterogeneous sites?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of estimating transfers of causal effects across heterogeneous sites.

papers.title: The Effects of Mandatory Profit-Sharing on Workers and Firms: Evidence from France
papers.summary: Firms with excess profits distribute on average 10.5% of pretax income to workers, and the cost to firms shows up as bunching at 100 employees that disappears after the reform. Mandated profit-sharing raises the labor share by 1.8 percentage points, lowers the profit share by 1.4 points and has small to nonexistent effects on investment.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences and bunching around the 1990 employment threshold change from 100 to 50 employees.
papers.q: What are the effects of mandatory profit-sharing on workers and firms in France?
papers.contribution: Exploits the 1990 reduction of the eligibility threshold from 100 to 50 employees for mandatory profit-sharing in bunching and difference-in-differences analyses.
papers.dataDetail: French firm and employee administrative data around the 1990 reform.

authors.inst: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics
Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How can multivariate spatial autoregressive models be estimated for large-scale networks with reduced rank?
papers.summary: The title indicates a reduced rank multivariate spatial autoregressive model for large-scale networks.

papers.title: Better late than never? Quantifying funding and liquidity effects of the PPP on pandemic-era employment recovery
papers.q: How did funding and liquidity effects of the PPP shape pandemic-era employment recovery?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study quantifying funding and liquidity effects of the Paycheck Protection Program on pandemic-era employment recovery.

papers.title: Wealth Heterogeneity and the Marginal Propensity to Consume Out of Wealth

authors.inst: Centre de Recherche en Économie et Statistique
Institut National de la Statistique et des Etudes Economiques

papers.q: How does the marginal propensity to consume out of wealth vary across the wealth distribution and euro area countries?
papers.summary: MPCs are lower for high-wealth households, and housing wealth plays a significant role in all countries, which is indicative of a collateral channel. Cross-country differences are mostly explained by country-specific institutional and socio-economic characteristics, as in Germany compared with Spain.
papers.ident: Instrumented household-level panel regressions of consumption on wealth.
papers.contribution: Builds a household-level panel combining wealth and consumption surveys for five European countries and estimates MPCs with instrumented panel regressions.
papers.dataDetail: Household panel built from wealth and consumption surveys for five European countries.

papers.title: Landmine clearance and economic development: Evidence from multispectral satellite imagery, nighttime lights, and conflict events in Afghanistan
papers.q: Does landmine clearance raise economic development in Afghanistan?
papers.summary: Landmines block transport corridors and prevent productive use of contaminated land. Multispectral imagery allows effects to be detected in rural areas, where nighttime lights have been poor proxies of activity in earlier work, and the event studies avoid forbidden comparisons.
papers.ident: Staggered-adoption event study of landmine clearance, avoiding forbidden comparisons.
papers.contribution: Maps more than 15,000 cleared hazardous areas and builds land use and crop productivity measures from Landsat multispectral imagery, then estimates staggered event studies.
papers.dataDetail: Landsat imagery, nighttime lights and conflict events for over 15,000 hazardous areas in Afghanistan.

papers.title: Ancestral irrigation and collective climate action
papers.q: Does ancestral irrigation shape societies' collective climate action today?
papers.contribution: Uses geographic suitability for irrigated agriculture as an exogenous source of variation in historical irrigation adoption to study contemporary climate policies.
papers.summary: Societies whose ancestors jointly practiced irrigated agriculture tend to adopt less effective climate policies today, and pro-climate political responses to severe natural disasters are weaker. Ancestral irrigation fostered tight kinship networks that likely constrained impersonal cooperation.
papers.ident: Geographic suitability for irrigated agriculture as an instrument for historical irrigation.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country and subnational data on ancestral irrigation, climate policies and disasters.

papers.title: Credit Conditions when Lenders are Commonly Owned
papers.q: How does common ownership between lenders affect the terms of syndicated loans?
papers.contribution: Examines common ownership among lenders and uses deposit multimarket contact as an exclusion restriction to identify the effect on loan pricing.
papers.summary: Higher common ownership lowers loan spreads, decreases the share of loans retained by the lead bank and relaxes liquidity constraints at issuance. Common ownership mitigates information asymmetries about borrower quality and contractual distortions.
papers.ident: Deposit multimarket contact as an exclusion restriction for common ownership.
papers.dataDetail: Syndicated loan data with lender ownership.

papers.title: “Immigration, Search and Redistribution: A Quantitative Assessment of Native Welfare” A Reply

authors.inst: Vienna University of Economics and Business

papers.q: How do corrections to the capital income calculation and the bargaining solution affect estimated native welfare gains from immigration?
papers.summary: Correcting the coding mistake has only a minor effect on the original results under Kalai proportional bargaining. Switching to Nash bargaining makes the estimated gains from immigration smaller, so welfare effects depend on the nature of bargaining.
papers.ident: Quantitative: re-calibration of a search model under Kalai versus Nash bargaining.
papers.contribution: Acknowledges a coding mistake and a mismatch with Nash bargaining, and re-calibrates the model to wage tax rates under Kalai and Nash bargaining.

papers.title: Emotions, Beliefs, and Policy Views
papers.q: How do emotions affect policy views and the processing of factual information about immigration?
papers.summary: Highly emotional news stories significantly raise demand for anti-immigration policies, an effect that persists when statistical information holds posterior beliefs constant, consistent with a causal role of emotions. Information generally corrects factual beliefs, though learning is slightly disrupted when participants are emotionally triggered.
papers.ident: Randomized exposure to emotional news, statistical information or both in a survey experiment.
papers.contribution: Runs a survey experiment in Italy randomly exposing 12,000 participants to sensational news about immigrant crimes, statistical information or both.
papers.dataDetail: Survey experiment with 12,000 participants in Italy.

papers.title: Unrest, Layoffs, and Productivity at a Bangladeshi Sweater Factory

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How do workers respond when management lays off a quarter of the workforce after unrest?
papers.summary: Productivity dropped substantially after the unrest. Surviving workers with likely friends among the fired co-workers suffered larger declines in productivity, and additional evidence points to deliberate shading of effort to punish management.
papers.contribution: Combines ethnographic, survey and administrative records from a Bangladeshi sweater factory to study the response to layoffs after labor unrest.
papers.ident: Comparison of surviving workers with and without friends among fired co-workers.
papers.dataDetail: Ethnographic, survey and administrative records from a Bangladeshi sweater factory.

papers.title: Mixture matrix-valued autoregressive model
papers.q: How can regime shifts be modeled in matrix-valued time series?
papers.summary: The standard matrix autoregressive model is linear with parametric constraints and cannot capture nonlinear patterns such as regime shifts, for instance recession versus expansion or stable versus pandemic periods. The mixture model analyzes shifts in the dynamics between two sets of attributes such as countries and economic indices.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: mixture matrix autoregression with EM estimation.
papers.contribution: Proposes a mixture matrix autoregressive (MMAR) model estimated by an EM algorithm, and derives its theoretical properties.
papers.dataDetail: Matrix-valued time series such as countries and economic indices.

papers.title: The unintended consequences of accountability: Quasi-experimental evidence from policing in Pakistan
papers.q: What unintended consequences does accountability have in policing in Pakistan?
papers.summary: The title indicates a quasi-experimental study of unintended consequences of accountability in policing in Pakistan.

papers.title: Nudging Parents out the Door: The Impacts of Parental Encouragement on School Choice and Test Scores
papers.q: Does SMS outreach to caregivers improve test scores and affect school choice in Kenya?
papers.summary: Outreach improved test scores by 0.07 standard deviations, with stronger gains among initially lower-performing students, yielding 12 learning-adjusted years of schooling per US$100. It also increased student exit rates by 4.7-5.0 percentage points, concentrated among higher-achieving students, consistent with a model of vertically differentiated schools.
papers.ident: Two-stage randomization of weekly SMS message types to caregivers.
papers.contribution: Tests growth-mindset encouragement and personalized performance information SMS messages in a two-stage randomization of caregivers in Kenyan private primary schools.
papers.dataDetail: Test scores and school exit data for private primary school students in Kenya.

papers.title: Changes in Health Inequalities among Older Individuals in Japan
papers.q: How have income-related health inequalities among older people in Japan changed from 2001 to 2022?
papers.summary: The pro-rich concentration of good health became less clear for self-rated health and ADLs among older men, but income-related inequality in stress and anxiety rose in men, with no clear trend for health deficiencies or conditions. Women show more mixed results, with widening inequalities in health deficiencies and conditions.
papers.contribution: Examines trends in income-related health inequality among older adults over two decades marked by pension reforms and higher old-age labor force participation.
papers.ident: Descriptive: income-related concentration of health outcomes over time.
papers.dataDetail: Japanese survey data on older adults, 2001-2022.

papers.title: Declining Occupations and Career Outcomes in Norway
papers.q: What are the career consequences of starting in an occupation that later declines in Norway?
papers.summary: Workers in later-declining occupations show 0.4 fewer future years of work, though this is mostly explained by other individual traits. Conditional on controls, they lose 4.7% of future cumulative earnings relative to starting earnings, akin to one year of earnings over 2007-2024.
papers.contribution: Compares workers initially employed in occupations that decline by at least 25% during 2007-2024 with other workers, conditional on controls.
papers.ident: Conditional comparison of workers by the later decline of their initial occupation.
papers.dataDetail: Norwegian administrative worker records, 2007-2024.

papers.title: The Unseen Costs of Blue Skies: Pollutant Substitution and Biodiversity Loss
papers.q: Did China's air monitoring network replace one pollutant with another and harm biodiversity?
papers.summary: Facing binding PM2.5 targets, local governments prioritized particulate precursors and neglected ozone precursors. The policy reduced PM2.5-attributed deaths but its ozone surge raised ozone-attributed mortality and reduced bird abundance, cutting the policy's net benefits by about 23.8%.
papers.ident: Staggered roll-out of China's national air monitoring network across cities.
papers.contribution: Exploits the staggered roll-out of the national air monitoring network to document PM2.5 reductions alongside an ozone surge, and traces it to local governments' strategic abatement.
papers.dataDetail: Air pollution monitoring data, mortality and bird abundance data for China.

papers.title: The Effect of Annuities on Longevity
papers.q: Do annuities reduce retiree mortality?
papers.summary: Annuity sales vary with recent market returns, consistent with extrapolative beliefs, and the decision to annuitize substantially reduces mortality at five- and ten-year horizons. Annuities shield retirees from income volatility and investment stress, and survey evidence suggests annuitants invest more in health and report less disability.
papers.contribution: Uses administrative payout data on about 600,000 Chilean retirees from 2004 to 2022 and instruments annuitization with recent market returns.
papers.ident: Instrument: recent market returns shifting annuity take-up.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative payout data on about 600,000 Chilean retirees, 2004-2022, plus survey evidence.

papers.title: Measuring the Impact of Data Centers in the United States Economy: Monetary Damage from Air Pollution and Greenhouse Gas Emissions
papers.q: What are the environmental damages from US data centers' electricity consumption?
papers.summary: Data centers consume roughly 250 TWh, about 5-6% of US generation, and generate approximately $25 billion in gross external damages, with a range of $10-33 billion. Damages are geographically concentrated, with Texas and Virginia accounting for 30% of the total, and equal about 5% of industry GDP.
papers.contribution: Combines facility-level data on about 2,800 data centers in 2025 with grid and emissions data, the AP4 integrated assessment model and the social cost of carbon.
papers.ident: Descriptive: integrated assessment valuation of pollution and GHG damages.
papers.dataDetail: Facility-level data on about 2,800 US data centers in 2025, grid characteristics and emissions.

papers.title: The Medical Expansion, Life Expectancy, and Endogenous Directed Technical Change
papers.summary: As income growth fuels demand for basic health goods, life expectancy rises in the early nineteenth century, and a century later directed technological progress produces a modern health sector. The model implies the quality-adjusted relative price of modern health goods fell about 2.5% per year from 1940 to 2020.
papers.q: What explains rising adult life expectancy and the emergence of a modern health sector over two centuries?
papers.contribution: Builds a unified quantitative theory of life expectancy and income growth with endogenous directed technical change and three phases of a dynamic equilibrium.
papers.ident: Quantitative: dynamic equilibrium model with directed technical change matched to long-run data.
papers.dataDetail: Long-run data on life expectancy, income and health prices (BEA health price index).

papers.title: Gender Mix and Team Performance: Evidence from Obstetrics
papers.q: How does the gender mix of expert teams affect performance in childbirth?
papers.contribution: Uses data on 2.5 million births and quasi-exogenous assignment of patients to two-member obstetrician teams to compare team compositions.
papers.summary: Female-only teams achieve the best maternal outcomes and male-only teams the worst, with severe complications 15.8% higher in male-only and 7.1-10.8% higher in mixed teams. Female-led mixed teams perform worse than male-led ones, and the patterns are not explained by patient risk, team formation or C-section preferences, pointing to gender norms.
papers.ident: Quasi-exogenous assignment of patients to lead and assisting obstetrician teams.
papers.dataDetail: Data on 2.5 million births with obstetrician team assignments.

papers.title: If You Build It, They May Not Come: Willingness to Participate in Managed EV Charging
papers.q: Do households willingly enroll in managed EV charging when the program is offered to all EVs of a utility?
papers.summary: Enrollment is low even with high incentives, and even modest intent-to-treat effects on electricity consumption can be rejected. Managed charging is less effective than found in RCTs among volunteers, underscoring the value of population-wide experiments.
papers.ident: Population-wide randomized experiment offering managed charging with varying incentives.
papers.contribution: Tests managed EV charging in an experiment covering all EVs within a California utility rather than a self-selected volunteer sample.
papers.dataDetail: All EVs within a California utility, with electricity consumption data.

papers.title: Belief Dispersion and Entrepreneurial Entry
papers.q: How does belief dispersion among rivals affect entrepreneurial entry?
papers.summary: A founder enters only when conviction exceeds a threshold set by anticipated rival optimism, so entry can be unsupported at any dispersion, supported at all levels or only at a middle range. With delay, high dispersion that deters immediate entry need not prevent entry altogether.
papers.contribution: Models entry when entrepreneurs hold heterogeneous beliefs about an opportunity and each knows only the range of views rivals might hold.
papers.ident: Theory: entry game with heterogeneous beliefs and strategic uncertainty about rivals.

papers.title: Aging at the Very Top

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: Why has the age at which CEOs are appointed risen sharply?
papers.summary: The increase is concentrated outside the largest listed firms and driven by longer and more diverse external career paths, not demographics, schooling or tenure. A rising value of experience reallocates older workers toward top positions, with a rising return to experience and older CEOs in larger firms.
papers.contribution: Documents the rise in CEO appointment age with newly assembled data and develops a matching model with hierarchies in which workers differ in ability and experience.
papers.ident: Theory: assignment model with hierarchies, tested against newly assembled CEO data.
papers.dataDetail: Newly assembled data on CEO appointments across a wide set of firms.

papers.title: Testing Mechanisms
papers.q: How can one test whether a treatment affects an outcome only through a particular mechanism?
papers.contribution: Develops tests for the sharp null of full mediation by connecting mediation analysis to tests of instrument validity, with sharp bounds for always-takers when the null is rejected.
papers.summary: The tools quantify the magnitude of alternative mechanisms by bounding the fraction of individuals affected despite having the same mediator value under both treatments, and the average effect for them. The approach avoids stringent assumptions required by existing mediation tools.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: testing full mediation using instrument validity tests.

papers.title: Can early public childcare reduce child penalties? Evidence from Germany
papers.q: Can early public childcare reduce mothers' child penalties in Germany?
papers.summary: A 20-percentage-point rise in childcare coverage lowers earnings penalties by 4.5 percentage points, about 56% of the 8-point decline over the reform period. Childcare raises employment, days worked, daily wages and the likelihood of working in higher-paying firms and occupations, with effects persisting, and effects are larger where initial penalties and reliance on informal care are high.
papers.contribution: Exploits county-level variation in the expansion of public childcare for children under three.
papers.ident: County-level variation in the expansion of public childcare for under-threes.
papers.dataDetail: German administrative employment records linked to county childcare coverage.

papers.title: Political Pressure on the Fed

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.contribution: Builds a dataset of personal interactions between US Presidents and Fed officials from 1933 to 2016 and identifies pressure with a narrative based on Nixon and Burns in a structural VAR.
papers.summary: Political pressure to ease raises the price level strongly and persistently, brings no positive effects on real activity and contributed to inflationary episodes outside the Nixon era. It transmits differently from a typical monetary policy easing.
papers.ident: Narrative restrictions on a structural VAR using President-Fed interaction data.
papers.q: How does political pressure on the Fed affect inflation and real activity?
papers.dataDetail: Archival records of President-Fed interactions, 1933-2016.

papers.title: Estimating how much children work: Questionnaires versus time use diaries
papers.contribution: Compares questionnaire and time diary work hours using data from nine low- and middle-income countries, including China and India.
papers.summary: Time diaries report considerably more work hours, with diary-to-questionnaire ratios above five at ages 5-11 and above two even at ages 15-17. Current estimates may substantially understate child labour, and activities such as collecting water or firewood appear to contribute to the gap.

papers.ident: Descriptive: comparison of questionnaire and time diary hours for the same children.
papers.dataDetail: Survey data with time diaries and questionnaires from nine LMICs including China and India.

papers.q: How did Poland's self-employment flat tax affect business entry?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of taxation and business entry using the Polish self-employment flat tax.

papers.summary: The title indicates a study of contract enforcement in a stateless economy.

papers.summary: The title indicates a study of intertemporal substitution in response to non-linear health insurance contracts.

papers.title: High Schools and the Uneven Rise in American Opportunity
papers.contribution: Builds new data on every US high school and compares attendance and adult outcomes of children in towns that opened a high school with those in nearby towns without one.
papers.summary: The share of young Americans in towns with high schools rose from 17% to 46%. High schools raised attendance, women's labor force participation and job quality while reducing early marriage and childbearing, accounting for a third of the 1870-1930 rise in women's participation, but widened class and racial inequalities.
papers.q: How did the expansion of US high schools between 1850 and 1910 change opportunity?
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing towns that opened a high school with nearby towns without one.
papers.dataDetail: Data on every US high school, 1850-1910, linked to census records.

papers.title: A Model of Leveraged Bubbles
papers.q: Why are recessions after leveraged asset price booms deeper and longer-lasting, and how should policy respond?
papers.summary: The bubble raises collateral values and relaxes borrowing limits in upswings but tightens them when it bursts, reproducing the empirical regularities. Borrowing-tax rules approximating the optimal policy substantially reduce the frequency and severity of recessions triggered by bursting leveraged bubbles.
papers.ident: Quantitative: general equilibrium model with a rational bubble and occasionally binding constraint.
papers.contribution: Develops a dynamic general equilibrium model with a rational bubble and an occasionally binding borrowing constraint, and derives time-consistent optimal policy and simple borrowing-tax rules.

papers.title: Credit Crunches and the Great Stagflation
papers.q: Did credit crunches from Regulation Q contribute to the Great Stagflation of the 1970s?
papers.contribution: Adds Regulation Q to a standard working-capital model and tests three predictions on the supply effects of credit crunches.
papers.summary: Under Reg Q, Fed tightening triggered deposit outflows that led banks to contract lending, making working capital costlier so firms raised prices and cut output. The model implies an augmented Phillips curve in which tightening reduces aggregate supply in addition to demand, increasingly with crunch severity, external finance dependence and working capital intensity.
papers.ident: Quantitative: working-capital model with Reg Q, tested with industry variation in finance dependence and working capital intensity.
papers.dataDetail: US banking, deposit and industry data from the 1970s.

papers.title: Forecasting the Economic Effects of AI

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.summary: The median respondent in each group expects substantial AI advances by 2030, small declines in labor force participation consistent with demographics and 2.5% annual GDP growth, above agency and private baselines. Under a rapid-progress scenario, experts forecast substantial but not historically unprecedented shifts, with GDP growth rising to around 4%.
papers.ident: Descriptive: elicited forecasts compared across respondent groups and scenarios.
papers.q: How do different groups forecast the economic effects of AI?
papers.contribution: Elicits forecasts from academic economists, AI company employees, AI policy researchers, highly accurate forecasters and the general public.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of five groups: economists, AI company employees, AI policy researchers, superforecasters and the public.

papers.title: The Empathy Channel in Fertility
papers.summary: Exposure to infants activates neurobiological mechanisms that increase the desire for parenthood, and as children become scarcer this stimulus weakens. Each birth raises others' desire, a positive externality that makes the equilibrium inefficient; the first-order Pigouvian rate overshoots the general-equilibrium optimum, and subsidies should target the group with the most externality per fiscal dollar.
papers.ident: Theory: overlapping-generations quantity-quality model with an empathy externality.
papers.q: Does exposure to infants raise the desire for children, and how should fertility be subsidized?
papers.contribution: Formalizes an empathy channel in a two-group overlapping-generations quantity-quality model and characterizes the optimal per-child subsidy.

papers.title: Beyond Demo Day: Sorting and Value Added in Startup Accelerators

papers.summary: Better ventures are more likely to enter accelerators and sort into higher-value-added programs. Most accelerators have negative value added relative to no accelerator while a small right tail generates large gains, and high-value-added accelerators predict better long-term outcomes and faster shutdown of weaker ventures.

papers.ident: Value-added estimation accounting for selection and sorting across accelerators, validated with applicant data.
