papers.title: Wellbeing, Youth and Survey Mode: Comparisons across 23 Countries Using Three International Datasets
papers.q: Does survey mode explain inconsistent evidence on youth wellbeing across international surveys?
papers.summary: The clearest evidence that wellbeing rises with age and illbeing falls with age comes from the web-based surveys. The age profiles look very different in telephone surveys, where the higher illbeing among the young is far less apparent, and survey mode is not randomly assigned.
papers.ident: Descriptive: age profiles across three surveys with different modes in the same 23 countries.
papers.contribution: Compares age profiles of wellbeing and illbeing across the Gallup World Poll, Global Minds and the Global Flourishing Survey for 23 countries.
papers.dataDetail: Gallup World Poll, Global Minds and Global Flourishing Survey for 23 countries.

papers.title: Understanding Support for Cost-Ineffective Environmental Policy Instruments
papers.q: Why do voters support cost-ineffective environmental standards over market-based instruments?
papers.summary: Respondents prefer the weakest targets for consumer taxes and the strongest for standards, a tradeoff between stringency and cost-effectiveness. Unlike experts, they believe market-based instruments raise consumer energy bills more than standards do.
papers.ident: Randomized educational videos in a survey experiment, benchmarked against expert beliefs.
papers.contribution: Compares a probability-based US sample with expert environmental economists and tests educational videos designed to induce economic expertise.
papers.dataDetail: Probability-based US sample and a survey of expert environmental economists.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Countries – The Real Estate Crises in 1990s Japan and Contemporary China
papers.q: How does China's real estate downturn compare with Japan's 1990s crisis, and what are the risks of prolonged stagnation?
papers.contribution: Documents the macroeconomic propagation of China's real estate downturn and compares it with Japan's experience.
papers.summary: Real estate, with its linkages and infrastructure, accounts for nearly one third of aggregate demand, and housing is nearly 70 percent of household wealth, so the price correction generates negative wealth effects that depress consumption, investment and sentiment. The paper assesses the risks of prolonged stagnation if the sector continues to deteriorate.
papers.ident: Descriptive: macro propagation analysis with a comparison to Japan in the 1990s.
papers.dataDetail: Aggregate Chinese and Japanese real estate, wealth and demand data.

papers.title: When Does Acquisition Integration Succeed? Evidence from Inside the Integration Black Box
papers.summary: Business unit leaders' target-industry experience raises integration success and lowers failure through better realization of transaction synergies. Other leader attributes are unrelated to integration outcomes, and the experience improves integration planning, acquisition performance and post-acquisition careers.
papers.q: Do business unit leaders' characteristics shape whether post-acquisition integration succeeds?
papers.contribution: Uses natural language processing measures of realized integration outcomes and financial metrics to study executives responsible for integrating acquired targets.
papers.ident: Regression of NLP-measured integration outcomes on leader experience.
papers.dataDetail: Text-based measures of integration outcomes and financial metrics for acquisitions.

papers.title: Consumer Tobacco Product Choices in China: The Impact of a Ban on Flavored E-cigarettes
papers.q: How did China's ban on flavored e-cigarettes change smokers' product choices?
papers.summary: Subjects made hypothetical choices between cigarettes, e-cigarettes and quitting with experimentally varied prices and e-cigarette attributes, identifying the impact of flavor availability on stated preferences. The ban was part of a comprehensive 2022 regulatory package.
papers.contribution: Runs two discrete choice experiments in 2021 and 2023 with about 600 adult smokers each and estimates conditional logit models of cigarettes, e-cigarettes and quitting.
papers.ident: Discrete choice experiments with randomized prices and flavor availability.
papers.dataDetail: Two discrete choice experiments in 2021 and 2023 with about 600 adult current smokers each.

papers.title: The Economic Value of Eliminating Cancer
papers.q: What is the economic value of eliminating cancer mortality in the United States?
papers.summary: Eliminating cancer mortality would avert 30.7 million deaths and 380 million life-years, generating $197 trillion in benefits, about $16,282 per American per year. Viewed as R&D investment, it yields an internal rate of return of 570% to 1,024%.
papers.contribution: Estimates the value of eliminating cancer mortality over 35 years from 2030, monetizing longevity gains with valuations used in US federal cost-benefit analysis.
papers.ident: Descriptive: monetized life-year valuation of eliminating cancer deaths.
papers.dataDetail: US cancer mortality projections and federal value-of-statistical-life valuations.

papers.title: Trade in AI-Related Products
papers.q: What do trade flows in AI-related products look like?
papers.summary: AI-related products account for 23 percent of US imports in 2025 and have grown 73 percent since 2023, against 3 percent for other imports. Mexico and Taiwan together account for about half of US trade in these products, which tariff exemptions largely shield.
papers.contribution: Develops a large language model classification tool mapping HS10 codes in US trade data to products used in building and operating AI infrastructure.
papers.ident: Descriptive: LLM-based product classification of customs data.
papers.dataDetail: US HS10 trade data through 2025.

papers.title: Identification and Estimation of Labor Supply Elasticities from Kinked Budget Sets
papers.q: What can be identified about labor supply elasticities from kinked budget sets with income effects and heterogeneity?
papers.summary: Clear bunching around the kink indicates the self-employed respond to the change in incentives, and the bounds are often tight even under weak assumptions. Uncompensated elasticities are near zero and compensated elasticities small enough to conclude that the excess burden of taxation is low.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: partial identification from kinked budget sets, applied with bunching at the Norwegian kink.
papers.contribution: Provides point and partial identification results for compensated and uncompensated elasticities and income effects, applied to the Norwegian tax kink for the self-employed.
papers.dataDetail: Norwegian administrative tax data on the self-employed.

papers.title: Tariffs in 2025: Short-Run Impacts on the U.S. Economy
papers.q: What were the short-run impacts of the 2025 US tariffs?
papers.contribution: Explores the structure of the 2025 tariffs, estimates pass-through and combines price and trade responses in a static trade framework to assess welfare.
papers.summary: The US raised average tariff duties from 2.4% to 9.6%, the highest in eighty years, with tariffs correlated with trade deficits but not strategic goals other than targeting China. In the baseline, 90% pass through to importers' prices, and overall welfare ranges from a loss of 0.13% to a gain of 0.10% of GDP, with sizable consumption losses offset by income and revenue gains.
papers.ident: Pass-through estimates from tariff changes, fed into a static trade framework.
papers.dataDetail: US customs data on tariffs, prices and trade flows in 2025.

papers.title: Macro-prudential policy under asymmetric risks: A Bayesian structural quantile VAR approach
papers.q: How should macro-prudential policy be assessed when downside risks and upside potential are asymmetric?
papers.contribution: Defines measures of downside risk and upside potential with an explicit policy loss function, and develops a Bayesian structural quantile VAR to evaluate policy.
papers.summary: The model delivers flexible and potentially asymmetric predictive distributions of macroeconomic outcomes, and quantile impulse responses assess the trade-off between limiting downside risk and preserving upside growth.
papers.ident: Bayesian structural quantile VAR with quantile impulse responses.
papers.dataDetail: Macroeconomic and financial condition time series.

papers.title: Exploring Trends in Severe Maternal Morbidity in the U.S.
papers.q: What explains the rise in severe maternal morbidity and the Black-White gap in the US?
papers.contribution: Evaluates a large set of maternal, hospital and county characteristics with decomposition methods, using inpatient data from 1998 to 2019.
papers.summary: Observed characteristics explain very little of the overall variation in severe maternal morbidity but account for a substantial share of the Black-White gap. The broader approach lets the data indicate which factors matter most, rather than focusing on select variables.
papers.ident: Descriptive: decomposition of trends and racial gaps in morbidity.
papers.dataDetail: US inpatient data 1998-2019 with maternal, hospital and county characteristics.

papers.title: Reason for Treason
papers.q: Why did high-ranking Nationalist officers defect to Japanese puppet regimes in the Second Sino-Japanese War?
papers.contribution: Builds a dataset of career paths for over 2,800 KMT colonels and generals and examines defection cases.
papers.summary: Officers who advanced more slowly were more likely to defect, as were those underpromoted relative to schoolmates and townsmen. Defection was also more likely when defected peers had better career prospects in the enemy's camp, pointing to internal recognition, peer comparison and external recognition.
papers.ident: Regression of defection on relative promotion speed against peers.
papers.dataDetail: Career records of over 2,800 high-ranking Nationalist officers during the Second Sino-Japanese War.

papers.title: Disagreement of Disagreement
papers.q: Why do major investor disagreement proxies fail to correlate, and how should disagreement be measured?
papers.summary: Major proxies have near zero correlation, complicating inference. DIS predicts cross-sectional returns better and more consistently across macroeconomic regimes than the proxies, separates the Miller (1977) friction channel from a frictionless mechanism, and absorbs the IVOL puzzle's predictability.
papers.contribution: Develops a frictionless model generating overpricing from latent disagreement and derives a new disagreement measure, DIS.
papers.ident: Theory: frictionless disagreement model, with cross-sectional return predictability tests.
papers.dataDetail: US stock returns and investor disagreement proxies.

papers.title: Winning hearts after tying hands: The political impact of land titling reform in China

authors.inst: Central University of Finance and Economics
University of International Business and Economics

papers.q: What was the political impact of China's land titling reform?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the political impact of a land titling reform in China.

papers.title: The stalled quiet revolution: Population control, skewed sex ratios, and the widening gender gap in labor force participation
papers.q: How did population control and skewed sex ratios widen the gender gap in labor force participation?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of population control, skewed sex ratios and the widening gender gap in labor force participation.

papers.title: The Confederate Diaspora
papers.q: When and how do migrants shape culture, as in the Confederate diaspora?
papers.contribution: Develops a framework for migrant cultural influence and applies it to Southern Whites who migrated after the Civil War.
papers.summary: Their influence spread Confederate symbols and racial norms across the US by the early twentieth century, stemming from ideological intensity rooted in slavery, secession and defeat and access to malleable power structures during westward expansion. They transmitted culture to kin and neighbours and through civil society organisations and positions of authority.
papers.ident: Descriptive: diffusion of Confederate culture by migrant Southern Whites using historical records.
papers.dataDetail: Census and historical records on Southern migrants and Confederate symbols.

papers.title: Product quality, the scope of export destinations and skill demand for sustainable development: An investigation for China
papers.q: How do product quality and export destination scope shape skill demand in Chinese firms?
papers.summary: The model predicts an inverted U-shaped relationship between export scope and quality upgrading, with a substitution between export scope and relative skill demand below a quality threshold. Above the threshold, higher export quality raises skilled-labor demand by narrowing export market ranges.
papers.contribution: Incorporates export-destination breadth into a skill-selection framework and tests it with a segmented mediating-effect model on Guangdong firm data for 2013-2015.
papers.ident: Theory: skill-selection model with export scope, tested with a segmented mediation model.
papers.dataDetail: Firm-level data from Guangdong Province, 2013-2015.

papers.title: The information matrix test for Gaussian mixtures

authors.inst: Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros
Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros

papers.summary: Monte Carlo simulations for finite Gaussian mixtures indicate that a parametric bootstrap gives reliable sizes and good power against various misspecification alternatives. The test confirms that three-component Gaussian mixtures describe cross-sectional per capita income distributions in the 1960-2000 Penn World Tables.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: information matrix test with EM-based moments.
papers.q: How can the information matrix test be implemented for Gaussian mixtures?
papers.contribution: Uses the EM principle to express the tested moments as conditional expectations of the complete-data moments and derives interpretable asymptotic covariance matrices.
papers.dataDetail: Penn World Tables per capita income, 1960-2000.

papers.title: Self-affirmation and productivity: Backfiring among those who could benefit the most
papers.q: Does self-affirmation raise labour productivity among extremely poor and stigmatised people?
papers.contribution: Runs a field experiment in Namibia asking participants to recall proud experiences or daily routines before working on a real piece-rate job, plus an online follow-up with US participants.
papers.summary: The self-affirmation intervention backfires, leaving participants substantially less productive than controls. The backfiring is explained by difficulty in recalling positive experiences, which a well-powered online experiment provides causal evidence for.
papers.ident: Randomized self-affirmation versus daily-routine recall before a piece-rate job.
papers.dataDetail: Field experiment in Namibia and an online experiment with US participants.

papers.title: Life Expectancy, Age and Patience
papers.q: Is higher life expectancy associated with greater patience, conditional on age?
papers.summary: Higher life expectancy is associated with greater patience conditional on age, and the association is unique to patience, not other preferences. The paper also documents a hump-shaped age profile and an association of patience with institutions.
papers.contribution: Uses data on 80,000 individuals in 76 countries and expected remaining years of life from period life tables.
papers.ident: Cross-country individual regressions of patience on life expectancy, conditional on age.
papers.dataDetail: Global preference survey data for 80,000 individuals in 76 countries and period life tables.

papers.title: Access to credit reduces the value of insurance
papers.q: Does access to credit reduce the value of insurance?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how access to credit reduces the value of insurance.

papers.title: Measuring Organizational Capital
papers.q: How can organizational capital be measured at the firm-year level?
papers.contribution: Constructs an organizational capital measure from over a million Glassdoor employee reviews using a word embedding model and ChatGPT-generated synthetic reviews.
papers.summary: The measure varies over time with macro trends and differs across and within firms, reflecting heterogeneity and major internal changes. Validation tests indicate it captures a slowly evolving intangible asset significantly associated with firm performance.
papers.ident: Machine learning: embedding-based construction of a firm-level text measure, validated against known properties.
papers.dataDetail: Over a million Glassdoor employee reviews with synthetic reviews generated by ChatGPT.

papers.title: Liquidity-Driven Growth Cycles in Small Open Economies
papers.summary: Foreign credit with perfectly elastic supply fuels investment that validates the initial optimism, a feedback loop generating multiple balanced growth paths and self-fulfilling cycles. In closed economies or with only FDI inflows, funding is limited by consumption smoothing and the growth path is unique.
papers.q: Why does growth stagnate after credit-driven capital account liberalization in emerging markets?
papers.contribution: Builds a small open economy model with endogenous growth and borrowing constraints in which optimistic growth expectations raise asset prices and relax liquidity constraints.
papers.ident: Quantitative: small open economy model with endogenous growth and self-fulfilling expectations.

papers.title: Investment-based Costs of Equity
papers.summary: The q5 cost of equity beats the accounting implied cost of equity in predicting cross-sectional returns, is precise at the industry level and aligned with factor premiums. The accounting measure outperforms in the time series, factor models do poorly out of sample and gradient-boosted trees improve on regressions but not reliably.
papers.ident: Out-of-sample cross-sectional return forecasts evaluated against implied cost of equity.
papers.q: How well does the q5-characteristics model estimate costs of equity?
papers.contribution: Estimates costs of equity as out-of-sample forecasts from cross-sectional regressions on q5 characteristics, following Lewellen (2015).
papers.dataDetail: US firm accounting data and stock returns.

papers.title: Capital in the Capitol: Congressional Trades Resemble Uninformed Retail Trading
papers.q: Do members of Congress exploit informational advantages in their personal stock trading?
papers.contribution: Constructs a novel dataset of the stock trading of all US members of Congress and their immediate families from 2012 to 2023.
papers.summary: After the STOCK Act, legislators' portfolios underperform or at best match market benchmarks. Their positions track financial professionals' recommendations and their timing largely reflects that of uninformed retail traders.
papers.ident: Portfolio performance relative to benchmarks and comparison with analyst recommendations and retail trading.
papers.dataDetail: Stock trades of all US members of Congress and immediate families, 2012-2023.

papers.title: Which U.S. States Suffered a Greater Great Depression and Why?

authors.inst: United States Department of the Treasury

papers.contribution: Digitizes Slaughter's (1937) state-by-sector production income panel for 48 states, constructs sector- and state-specific deflators and disciplines a dynamic spatial stochastic general equilibrium model.
papers.summary: Per capita income fell by 15 percent in Maryland and 48 percent in South Dakota. Separating physical quantities from relative price changes with correct deflation is central, and the model recovers sector-state productivity shocks that reproduce observed quantity paths.
papers.ident: Quantitative: three-sector, 48-region spatial model inverted to recover productivity shocks.
papers.q: Which US states suffered a greater Great Depression, and why?
papers.dataDetail: Digitized Slaughter (1937) panel of state-by-sector production income, 1929-1932, with new deflators.

papers.title: Amortized Inference for Correlated Discrete Choice Models via Equivariant Neural Networks
papers.q: Can neural networks provide amortized inference for discrete choice models with correlated errors?
papers.summary: Logit-based models dominate applied work but impose restrictive assumptions on the stochastic utility component that limit realistic substitution patterns. The paper provides group-theoretic foundations for the architecture, including a universal approximation proof given a minimal set of invariant features.
papers.ident: Machine learning: equivariant neural network emulator of choice probabilities.
papers.contribution: Proposes a neural network emulator approximating choice probabilities for general error distributions, with a specialized architecture respecting invariance properties of discrete choice models.

papers.title: AI Patents in the United States and China: Measurement, Organization, and Knowledge Flows
papers.q: How do AI patenting in the United States and China compare in scale, organization and knowledge flows?
papers.summary: The classifier reaches 97.0% precision, 91.3% recall and 94.0% F1 and generalizes to Chinese patents. AI patenting grew rapidly in both countries with convergence in intensity and subfield composition, even as China passes the US in annual counts, but US patenting is concentrated among large incumbents and hubs, while Chinese patenting is more geographically dispersed.
papers.contribution: Develops a high-precision classifier by fine-tuning PatentSBERTa on labeled USPTO AI Patent Dataset data and applies it to US (1976-2023) and Chinese (2010-2023) patents.
papers.ident: Machine learning: fine-tuned language model classifier for AI patents.
papers.dataDetail: Granted US patents 1976-2023 and Chinese patents 2010-2023.

papers.title: Adversarial Selection

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How should adversarial parties select items that represent a population?
papers.summary: The procedure is optimally representative among all feasible mechanisms. It is illustrated for jury selection, multi-district litigation and committee formation.
papers.contribution: Proposes the Quantile Mechanism, where one party partitions the population into k subsets and the other selects one item from each.
papers.ident: Theory: mechanism design for representative selection by adversarial parties.

papers.title: Pharmaceutical Advertising in Dynamic Equilibrium
papers.q: What would a ban on direct-to-consumer drug advertising do to firm profits?
papers.summary: DTCA may expand treatment access but risks overuse and business stealing without welfare gains. The framework incorporates constraints on decision-makers' cognitive abilities and eases computation, and is validated by replicating observed advertising patterns.
papers.contribution: Adapts the Experience-Based Equilibrium of Fershtman and Pakes (2012) for empirical analysis and simulates a counterfactual DTCA ban using data from four therapeutic markets.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic experience-based equilibrium model with a counterfactual advertising ban.
papers.dataDetail: Advertising, sales and pricing data for four therapeutic markets.

papers.title: Tariffs, Global Value Chains, and the Incidence of Protection: Evidence from US Automobiles
papers.q: Who bears the incidence of tariffs on vehicles and parts in the US automobile market?
papers.contribution: Develops a structural model combining random-coefficients demand, multiproduct pricing and imperfect pass-through of imported parts costs, using model-level imported-parts exposure and exchange rate variation.
papers.summary: Tariffs operate through consumer substitution, firm pricing, and firms' cost structures and sourcing decisions in a market reliant on global value chains. Counterfactuals quantify effects of alternative tariff policies on prices, profits and welfare.
papers.ident: Structural: random-coefficients demand with exchange-rate variation identifying cost pass-through.
papers.dataDetail: US automobile market data with model-level imported-parts exposure.

papers.title: Can Personal Access to Medical Expertise Overcome Vaccine Hesitancy?
papers.q: Does having a physician in the family reduce vaccine hesitancy?
papers.summary: A physician in the family raises the likelihood that relatives comply with the recommended second COVID-19 booster for those over 59. The effects are strongest for having a female physician in the family, pointing to gender differences in how medical expertise is communicated.
papers.ident: Lottery admission to Dutch medical school among applicants.
papers.contribution: Uses lottery outcomes determining admission to Dutch medical schools and data on applicants' older relatives aged 60 and over.
papers.dataDetail: Dutch medical school applicants linked to older relatives' vaccination records.

papers.title: Immigrants at the Margin: Labor Market Effects of the Minimum Wage
papers.q: How do minimum wages affect immigrant and native workers differently?
papers.summary: Minimum wage increases reduce hours of work among immigrants with no effect on employment, concentrated among recently arrived, likely undocumented workers in high-turnover industries. Natives show no response, even similar subgroups, suggesting low-surplus, flexible-hours employment relationships in labor markets where replacement is unusually costly.
papers.contribution: Compares labor market effects of minimum wage increases on immigrants and natives in the United States.
papers.ident: State minimum wage variation, comparing immigrant and native workers.
papers.dataDetail: US survey data on immigrant and native workers' hours and employment.

papers.title: LASSO inference for high dimensional predictive regressions
papers.q: How can inference be conducted for high dimensional predictive regressions using LASSO?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of LASSO inference for high dimensional predictive regressions.

papers.title: From Gridlock to Polarisation?
papers.q: Does legislative gridlock increase voters' support for extreme co-partisan candidates?
papers.contribution: Proposes a mechanism where voters rationally discount proposals on gridlocked issues and tests it in an online experiment randomly varying perceived gridlock.
papers.summary: Greater perceived gridlock on a specific issue raises moderate partisans' propensity to vote for extreme co-partisan candidates on that issue. The evidence is consistent with the mechanism and alternative explanations.
papers.ident: Randomized perceptions of gridlock in candidate-choice tasks in an online experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Large-scale online experiment with candidate-choice tasks.

papers.title: Scalable Demand and Markups
papers.q: How have markups changed across 72 product markets from 2006 to 2018 under a demand-based approach?
papers.contribution: Estimates nested logit demand with household panel data automating product nest assignment, and inverts firms' first-order pricing conditions to infer markups.
papers.summary: Markups trend upward overall between 2006 and 2018 with considerable heterogeneity across and within markets. Changes in marginal costs and household price sensitivity are the primary drivers, with firm ownership changes playing a much smaller role.
papers.ident: Structural: demand estimation with nested logit and inversion of pricing first-order conditions.
papers.dataDetail: Household panel scanner data across 72 product markets, 2006-2018.

papers.title: Testing for differences in high-frequency network connectedness from variance decompositions
papers.q: How can differences in high-frequency network connectedness be tested from variance decompositions?
papers.summary: The statistic is asymptotically chi-squared under the null and performs well in Monte Carlo simulations. In high-frequency options data on sectoral ETFs from 2013 to 2023, connectedness among implied volatilities increases significantly after FOMC announcements and persists for about an hour on days with monetary policy surprises.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: Wald-type test of connectedness, applied around FOMC announcements.
papers.contribution: Develops a Bayesian Wald-type test for temporal differences in connectedness and derives asymptotic normality of impulse responses and variance decompositions at fixed local time points.
papers.dataDetail: High-frequency options data on sectoral ETFs, January 2013 to June 2023.

papers.title: Elections that inspire: Effects of Black mayors on educational attainment

authors.inst: Escola Superior de Propaganda e Marketing

papers.q: Does electing a Black mayor raise educational attainment of Black students in Brazil?
papers.summary: In municipalities where Black candidates won, Black students are more likely to register for the national high school exam, attend university and graduate. The evidence points to changed aspirations, as mayors have no primary education responsibility and do not perform better on relevant policies, and effects are weaker for White students in public schools.
papers.ident: Close-election regression discontinuity between Black and non-Black mayoral candidates.
papers.contribution: Uses a regression discontinuity design in close mayoral elections in Brazil.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian municipal election results and National High School Examination records.

papers.title: The global transmission of U.S. monetary policy
papers.q: How is US monetary policy transmitted globally?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the global transmission of US monetary policy.

papers.title: Robust Estimation and Inference in Panels with Interactive Fixed Effects
papers.q: How can regression coefficients be estimated reliably in panels with interactive fixed effects when some factors are weak?
papers.summary: Previously developed estimators and confidence intervals are heavily biased and size distorted when some factors are weak. The proposed method substantially outperforms conventional approaches with weak factors, at little cost to estimation error when factors are strong.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: minimax linear estimation with nuclear norm bound for interactive fixed effects.
papers.contribution: Combines minimax linear estimation theory with a nuclear norm bound on the initial estimate's error to propose estimators with improved rates and uniformly valid confidence intervals.

papers.title: Extreme temperatures, physical activity, and adaptation
papers.q: How do extreme temperatures affect physical activity, and can people adapt?
papers.summary: Physical activity falls significantly on hot and cold days, mitigated by intraday and interday substitution. Hotter regions are less sensitive to extreme heat, evincing adaptation, and projections that allow adaptation imply large welfare gains, unlike those that ignore it.
papers.contribution: Uses 24 billion person-minute observations from US Fitbit users to estimate behavioral and performance responses to extreme temperatures.
papers.ident: Panel variation in daily temperature within individuals.
papers.dataDetail: 24 billion person-minute Fitbit observations in the US.

papers.title: The global network of liquidity lines
papers.summary: The lines form a network through which banks can indirectly obtain USD even without an agreement between their central bank and the Federal Reserve, giving the People's Bank of China a central role. Indirect connections reduce CIP deviations at the tails and liquidity lines are causal substitutes for FX reserves.
papers.q: How does the global network of central bank liquidity lines shape access to US dollars?
papers.contribution: Maps the evolution of 177 cross-border central bank liquidity lines from 2000 to 2025 in a new comprehensive dataset.
papers.ident: Descriptive: network mapping of liquidity lines, with causal evidence on reserve substitution.
papers.dataDetail: New dataset of central bank cross-border liquidity lines, 2000-2025.

papers.title: Ruling the roost: the vicious circle and the emergence of pecking order
papers.summary: Under patronage the powerful accumulate more power and wealth, leading to substantial inequality, attenuated by the powerless opposing the powerful. No vicious circle arises without patronage and inequality is markedly lower, and gender differences are small without patronage but large with it.
papers.q: Does patronage generate a vicious circle of power and wealth accumulation in the lab?
papers.contribution: Constructs the rule-the-roost game where players compete repeatedly for power and wealth, with a patronage treatment that allows buying support and a no-patronage treatment.
papers.ident: Randomized assignment to patronage versus no-patronage treatments in a laboratory game.
papers.dataDetail: Laboratory experiment with a repeated power and wealth game.

papers.title: The local-area incidence of exporting

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin
The University of Texas at Austin

papers.q: Who bears the local-area incidence of exporting?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the local-area incidence of exporting.

papers.title: The modified conditional sum-of-squares estimator for fractionally integrated models

authors.inst: WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management
WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management

papers.q: How can the bias of the conditional sum-of-squares estimator for fractionally integrated models be removed when a constant is estimated?
papers.contribution: Derives expressions for the CSS estimator's bias in type-II ARFIMA models and proposes a modified CSS (MCSS) estimator that removes the leading term.

papers.title: It is not Just about the price: Matching subsidies fail when the ask can be avoided
papers.q: Do matching subsidies raise charitable giving when donors can avoid the ask?
papers.contribution: Runs experiments varying whether the ask can be avoided under a donation match.
papers.summary: The match increases donations only when avoiding the ask is not possible. The data fit a norm-signalling mechanism in which the match raises the psychological cost of deviating from the norm of giving, and giving zero, but not avoiding the ask, is seen as less socially desirable under a match.
papers.conclusion: Matching subsidies have limits and can cause welfare losses.

papers.title: Monetary policy trade-offs amid global supply chain disruptions
papers.q: What monetary policy trade-offs arise amid global supply chain disruptions?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of monetary policy trade-offs amid global supply chain disruptions.

papers.title: Chat over coffee? Diffusion of agronomic practices and market spillovers in Rwanda
papers.q: Do agronomy training programs diffuse through social networks and spill over to untrained coffee farmers in Rwanda?
papers.summary: The program raised knowledge and self-reported adoption and created new social ties mainly among co-trainees, while treated farmers' higher yields are not statistically significant. Knowledge did not diffuse, and control farmers with more treated friends at baseline reduced audited adoption.

papers.title: Customer accumulation, returns to scale, and secular trends
papers.q: How did rising returns to scale contribute to declining dynamism, higher markups and higher customer acquisition spending?
papers.contribution: Introduces a firm dynamics model with heterogeneous markups and customer accumulation through directed search in which larger firms gain from higher returns to scale.
papers.summary: Rising returns to scale make markets less contestable for new firms and lead to superstar firms. The model quantitatively accounts for a substantial share of the secular trends, and the micro-level mechanisms align with empirical evidence.
papers.ident: Quantitative: firm dynamics model with customer accumulation calibrated to US trends.
papers.dataDetail: US firm-level and aggregate data on dynamism, markups and customer acquisition expenditure.

papers.title: Clustered network connectedness: A new measurement framework with application to global equity markets
papers.q: How can network connectedness be measured when shocks are orthogonal across clusters but correlated within them?
papers.contribution: Develops a clustered connectedness framework that nests full orthogonalization and generalized identification, applied to global equity markets.

The framework generalizes the Diebold-Yilmaz variance decomposition approach, whose standard identifications are special extreme cases.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: clustered identification of VAR variance decompositions.

papers.title: “Compensate the Losers?” Economic Policy and the Origins of U.S. Partisan Realignment
papers.q: Does the Democratic Party's retreat from predistribution explain the education-based partisan realignment in the US?
papers.contribution: Documents educational gradients in support for predistribution and redistribution since the 1940s and the Democratic Party's shift using bills and PAC donations.
papers.summary: Educated Americans differentially oppose predistribution such as job guarantees, minimum wages, protectionism and unions, while the educational gradient for redistribution is close to zero, unchanged since the 1940s. The number of predistribution bills introduced by Democratic House Speakers fell by half since the 1970s, and unions' share of Democratic PAC donations dropped from 90% to 40% between 1968 and 1980.
papers.ident: Descriptive: opinion data by education over time, with legislative bill and donation records.
papers.dataDetail: Public opinion surveys since the 1940s, congressional bills and PAC donation records.

papers.title: Cross-border trade competition and international stock return comovement
papers.q: How does cross-border trade competition affect international stock return comovement?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of cross-border trade competition and international stock return comovement.

papers.title: Comment on “Telementoring and Homeschooling during School Closures: A Randomized Experiment in Rural Bangladesh” By Hassan et al.

authors.inst: Ragnar Frisch Centre for Economic Research

papers.q: Do the original findings of the Bangladesh telementoring and homeschooling experiment hold up?
papers.summary: The title indicates a comment on the Hassan et al. randomized experiment on telementoring and homeschooling during school closures in rural Bangladesh.

papers.title: Globalization and the gender gap in mental well-being
papers.summary: A decline in business hour overlap between a Danish firm and its foreign partners increases antidepressant use among women relative to men. The effect is economically meaningful and largest for college-educated workers under 45.
papers.q: Does working with distant trading partners harm women's mental well-being more than men's?
papers.contribution: Uses Danish matched employer-employee data linked to antidepressant prescriptions and firm import and export transactions, with variation within job spells.
papers.ident: Within-job-spell variation in business hour overlap with foreign trading partners, controlling for firm-year effects.
papers.dataDetail: Danish matched employer-employee data, prescription antidepressant records and firm trade transactions.

papers.title: Real Credit Cycles
papers.summary: A realistic degree of overreaction generates realistic credit cycles in which good times produce fragility and predict later disappointment, low bond returns and investment declines. The model needs only moderate negative shocks to produce the spread increases observed during 2007-2009.
papers.ident: Quantitative: heterogeneous firm model with diagnostic expectations calibrated to earnings forecasts.
papers.q: Can diagnostic expectations generate realistic credit cycles in a neoclassical model?
papers.contribution: Embeds diagnostic expectations in a neoclassical model with heterogeneous firms and risky debt, with overreaction estimated from US firms' earnings forecasts.
papers.dataDetail: US firms' earnings forecasts and credit spread data.

papers.title: Robust Misspecified Models
papers.q: Which misspecified models persist when decision-makers compare them with competing models?
papers.summary: Misspecified models can persist against any competing model, including the true model, despite infinite data. Simple misspecified models with entrenched priors can be more robust than complex correctly specified ones.
papers.ident: Theory: model persistence under Bayesian learning with misspecification.
papers.contribution: Characterizes robust misspecified models by their asymptotic accuracy in predicting equilibrium outcome distributions and the tightness of the prior around such equilibria.

papers.title: A Long and a Short Leg Make for a Wobbly Equilibrium
papers.q: Why do short sellers abruptly abandon the market even as mispricing widens?
papers.summary: Rational short sellers may exit even as mispricing widens, producing abrupt changes in short selling activity. Short selling dynamics are fat tailed and subject to abrupt changes, especially for stocks the model identifies as susceptible.
papers.contribution: Models the interaction between the spot and lending markets for stocks, and documents empirical short selling dynamics.
papers.ident: Theory: stock lending and spot market model, tested on short selling data.
papers.dataDetail: Stock short selling and lending market data.

papers.title: Winters of discontent
papers.q: Does snowfall affect migration in the Great Lakes region?
papers.summary: Higher-than-average snowfall in lake-effect counties leads to net population loss the next year, driven by fewer in-migrants, dissipating after one or two years and strongest among young and middle-aged populations. Snow has virtually no effect in non-lake-effect regions, suggesting baseline exposure interacts with anomalous weather.
papers.contribution: Compares the effect of snow on county net migration across lake-effect snow regions and other regions since 1970.
papers.ident: Comparison of snowfall effects on net migration across lake-effect and non-lake-effect counties.
papers.dataDetail: County-level migration and snowfall data for the Great Lakes region since 1970.

papers.title: Spillovers in State Capacity Building: Evidence from the Digitization of Land Records in Pakistan

authors.inst: City St George's, University of London

papers.summary: Digitization had a negative effect on tax collection that was not due to a decrease in the tax base. It affected bureaucrats' capacity to collect taxes, an unintended consequence of reshaping the organization of bureaucracies.
papers.ident: Staggered rollout of land record digitization across Punjab.
papers.q: Did digitizing land records strengthen or weaken state capacity in Punjab, Pakistan?
papers.contribution: Exploits the staggered rollout of land record digitization with administrative agricultural tax data and surveys of local bureaucrats.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative agricultural tax data and surveys of bureaucrats in Punjab, Pakistan.

papers.title: Should we augment large covariance matrix estimation with auxiliary network information?
papers.q: Should large covariance matrix estimation be augmented with auxiliary network information?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of whether auxiliary network information improves large covariance matrix estimation.

papers.title: Making Bricks from Straw: Resources and Productivity in Health Care
papers.q: Do financial constraints explain poor productivity in health facilities in developing countries?
papers.contribution: Runs an experiment surprising health workers in randomly selected public clinics in Nigeria with a N600,000 grant paid in installments over one year and administered entirely by workers.
papers.summary: The award led to large productivity gains. Expenditure data and novel textual data show it increased investments in physical and human capital, lowered prices for patients and inspired health workers to do better.
papers.ident: Randomized unconditional grants to public health clinics.
papers.dataDetail: Expenditure records and textual data from public health clinics in Nigeria.

papers.title: Market Power and Capital Constraints

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How do traders' capital constraints affect asset prices and liquidity under market power?
papers.summary: Looser capital constraints raise both asset prices and price impact, with the latter reducing market liquidity. The constraints are only infrequently binding, but their relative impact when activated can be sizable.
papers.contribution: Builds a model of capital-constrained traders in an imperfectly competitive market and estimates shadow costs of constraints using Canadian Treasury auction data and a temporary policy exemption in 2020-2021.
papers.ident: Structural: auction model with capital constraints, using a temporary policy exemption in 2020-2021.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian Treasury auction data.

papers.title: Networked Information and Industrial Output: Evidence from Chile’s 1972 Truckers’ Strike
papers.q: Did Chile's Cybersyn coordination system help industrial sectors weather the 1972 truckers' strike?
papers.summary: The strike cut aggregate industrial output by roughly 9 percent. The four priority sectors outperform structural predictions by an average of 17 index points, with the differential at the 90th percentile of a permutation null (p = 0.100), concentrated in sectors with state ownership, simple supply chains and military distribution support. Food and beverages, where coordination needs were greatest, got no measurable protection.
papers.ident: Quantitative: calibrated CES-Leontief counterfactuals with a permutation test of priority sectors.
papers.contribution: Builds sector-specific counterfactuals for the trucking shock with monthly data for twenty sectors and a calibrated CES-Leontief model, and compares priority and non-priority sectors.
papers.dataDetail: Monthly industrial output data for twenty Chilean sectors, 1972.

papers.title: The Hidden Cost of Stock Market Concentration: When Funds Hit Regulatory Limits
papers.summary: Funds perform worse when constrained, and the ownership measure predicts stock returns, especially among the largest firms. Constraints on long positions can generate underpricing by suppressing optimists' views, just as short-sale constraints produce overpricing.
papers.q: How do regulatory limits on fund concentration distort stock prices as market concentration rises?
papers.contribution: Shows that funds approaching regulatory concentration limits trim their largest holdings and reduce equity exposure, and builds a constraint-based ownership measure.
papers.ident: Variation in funds' proximity to regulatory concentration limits.
papers.dataDetail: Mutual fund holdings and returns with regulatory diversification limits.

papers.title: Real Effects of Academic Research Revisited
papers.contribution: Surveys social science evidence on the causal effects of universities through knowledge creation, education and training, and technology transfer.
papers.summary: The literature has examined each mechanism and its variation across disciplines and sectors, helped by new microdata linking inventions, scientists and institutions and by network science methods. Research has established the importance of these effects on average, but says less about the determinants of success.
papers.q: What does research show about universities' contributions to innovation and economic growth?

papers.title: The Economics of Postdoctoral Researcher Positions
papers.summary: The expansion reflects fragmented science funding, especially the NIH budget doubling in the early 2000s, which raised supply of and demand for postdocs but worsened employment conditions. Economic returns outside academia are limited and transitions to faculty declining, and the US may have reached peak postdoc.
papers.q: Why did the number of postdoctoral researchers grow so much in the US scientific workforce?
papers.contribution: Examines the growth and role of postdocs from 1979 to 2023, highlighting a fourfold increase outpacing graduate students and faculty.
papers.dataDetail: US data on the scientific workforce, 1979-2023.

papers.title: Decoupling Dollar and Treasury Privilege
papers.q: Why have the convenience yields on the US dollar and on US Treasuries decoupled?
papers.summary: The dollar retains strong convenience after the Global Financial Crisis, while Treasury convenience has declined substantially and turned negative, most strongly at medium and long maturities. The relative supply of government bonds in the US versus other developed markets is argued to be a key driver.
papers.contribution: Measures dollar convenience with CIP deviations between risk-free bank rates and Treasury convenience with CIP deviations between government bond yields.
papers.ident: Descriptive: covered interest parity deviations for bank rates and government bond yields.
papers.dataDetail: CIP deviations from secured overnight rates and government bond yields in developed markets.

papers.title: Supporting Student Engagement During Remote Learning: Three Randomized Controlled Trials in Chicago Public Schools
papers.q: Can interventions raise student engagement during remote learning in Chicago Public Schools?
papers.summary: Personalized phone calls increased families' likelihood of registering for virtual summer school, the pre-specified primary outcome. Weekly text messages had no effect on summer absences or Khan Academy usage.
papers.ident: Three randomized field experiments in Chicago Public Schools.
papers.contribution: Reports three field experiments testing personalized phone calls, weekly text messages and further engagement supports for virtual summer schooling.
papers.dataDetail: Chicago Public Schools administrative records and Khan Academy usage data.

papers.title: Special Education Substantially Improves Learning: Evidence from Three States
papers.q: How much does special education improve student learning?
papers.summary: Scores decline before placement and rise sharply afterward in a V-shaped pattern. Within three years achievement is 0.2-0.4 standard deviations above counterfactual trends, with similar gains across disability categories and subgroups that are not driven by testing accommodations.
papers.ident: Event study of achievement around initial special education classification.
papers.contribution: Uses longitudinal data from Massachusetts, Indiana and Connecticut and an event-study design around initial classification.
papers.conclusion: Individualized supports substantially raise learning productivity.
papers.dataDetail: Student longitudinal administrative data from Massachusetts, Indiana and Connecticut.

papers.title: Optimism about Graduation and College Financial Aid
papers.q: Does optimism about graduation make federal student loans welfare-reducing for some students?
papers.summary: College can be financed by loans, grants, family transfers or earnings. Access to federal student loans can reduce welfare for low-skilled, poor and optimistic young adults because of their mistaken beliefs.
papers.ident: Quantitative: overlapping generations model with a belief distribution measured from survey data.
papers.contribution: Documents that beliefs about earning a bachelor's degree predict enrollment and are widely optimistic, and builds an overlapping generations model of college as a risky investment.
papers.dataDetail: US survey data on beliefs about earning a bachelor's degree and college enrollment.

papers.title: Using Global Shocks to Understand the Level and Structure of Executive Compensation
papers.summary: Trade shocks increase firm size and value and CEO compensation, the CEO's share of firm value rises with size and with global-shock volatility, and higher-ability CEOs generate firm value gains more than 100 times their compensation.
papers.ident: Exogenous global trade shocks to firms, with a model of scale, volatility and ability magnification.
papers.q: How do trade shocks shape the level and structure of executive compensation?
papers.contribution: Builds a CEO compensation model uniting principal-agent and assignment models and tests it with Danish matched worker-firm data and exogenous trade shocks.
papers.dataDetail: Danish matched worker-firm data with trade exposure.

papers.title: Misallocation in Indian Agriculture
papers.q: How much do land-market distortions explain agricultural productivity differences across Indian states?
papers.contribution: Develops a model of heterogeneous farms with state-level barriers to land-market participation and farm-level size distortions, estimated with household panel data.
papers.summary: The two sources of distortions are separately identified in each state. States differ substantially in rental barriers with large negative effects on productivity, and participation distortions contribute substantially to productivity differences across states.
papers.ident: Structural: heterogeneous farm model with land-market barriers, using state institutional variation.
papers.dataDetail: Household-level panel data on Indian farms and state land-market institutions.

papers.title: Not a Typical Firm: Capital–Labor Substitution and Firms' Labor Shares
papers.summary: Large firms automate and reduce the aggregate labor share while the median firm keeps a labor-intensive technology. Calibrated to match adoption heterogeneity, the model reproduces the aggregate and firm-level facts quantitatively, especially in manufacturing.
papers.ident: Quantitative: heterogeneous firm model with fixed automation costs calibrated to adoption patterns.
papers.q: Why has the aggregate labor share declined while the typical firm's labor share has risen?
papers.contribution: Introduces a model where firms pay fixed costs to automate tasks, so a decline in capital goods prices leads large firms to automate.
papers.dataDetail: US firm-level data in manufacturing and retail.

papers.title: Housing Constraints and Spatial Misallocation: Comment
papers.summary: The original counterfactual would lower output, a discrepancy explained by code errors, and the results depend on the arbitrary choice of population unit. In the modified model the experiment raises output, but by two orders of magnitude less than originally reported.
papers.q: Do Hsieh and Moretti's estimates of GDP gains from relaxing land use regulation hold up?
papers.contribution: Attempts to replicate their counterfactual, documents errors in their code and proposes a modification that eliminates dependence on the population unit.
papers.ident: Replication and revision of a spatial equilibrium model of housing constraints.

papers.title: Paid Caregiving Leave Policies and an Update on Paid Parental Leave
papers.contribution: Reviews the evidence on paid family leave and paid sick leave for non-childbirth caregiving and updates the evidence on paid parental leave.
papers.summary: The chapter outlines informal caregiving prevalence and the policy landscape, then reviews impacts on leave take-up, labor market outcomes, caregiver health, employer outcomes and formal care use. Paid leave policies have increased leave take-up, and paid family leave improves labor market outcomes for workers.
papers.q: What does the evidence show on the effects of paid caregiving leave policies?

papers.title: Mind the Gap: AI Adoption in Europe and the U.S.
papers.summary: Worker demographics and firm composition account for an important share of the gaps, and adoption is closely linked to personnel management practices and firms encouraging AI use. Industries with higher adoption have had faster productivity growth in Europe and the US, a statistically significant relationship in which causality is not established.
papers.q: How large are AI adoption gaps between Europe and the US, and are they linked to productivity?
papers.contribution: Combines international worker and firm surveys from 2025 and 2026 to document gaps in AI adoption between the US and Europe and across European countries.
papers.ident: Descriptive: cross-country worker and firm survey comparison, with industry-level productivity regressions.
papers.dataDetail: Worker and firm surveys from 2025 and 2026 in Europe and the US with industry productivity data.

papers.title: Dynamic Adjustment to Trade Shocks
papers.q: How do sourcing frictions and anticipation shape the dynamic adjustment of trade to shocks?
papers.summary: Short-run trade elasticities are a fraction of long-run ones, indicating dynamic frictions. Sourcing frictions and anticipation effects alter the time pattern of specialization and can produce short-term welfare losses but long-term gains.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic sourcing model with time-varying trade elasticity, calibrated to two trade events.
papers.contribution: Develops a tractable model with forward-looking firms and sticky sourcing choices that nests an Eaton-Kortum model as the long-run limit, and calibrates it to the 2004 EU enlargement and the 2018 US-China trade war.
papers.dataDetail: Trade flow data around the 2004 EU enlargement and the 2018 US-China trade war.

papers.title: Banking Networks and Economic Growth: From Idiosyncratic Shocks to Aggregate Fluctuations
papers.q: How do banking networks transmit shocks and shape business cycle comovement?
papers.contribution: Combines US banking deregulation with state-level idiosyncratic demand shocks to show how geographically diversified banks reallocate funds.
papers.summary: Diversified banks move funds from economies experiencing negative shocks to unaffected regions, so financial integration reduces business cycle comovement and synchronizes consumption. The findings help explain the Great Moderation and support theories that banking integration insures region-specific risk.
papers.ident: Staggered US banking deregulation interacted with state-level idiosyncratic demand shocks.
papers.dataDetail: US state-level bank, output and consumption data around banking deregulation.

papers.title: The Cold War and the U.S. Labor Market
papers.contribution: Isolates exogenous shifts in military procurement across states and firms, and studies the effect of the Cold War draft on young men's labor supply.
papers.summary: Military procurement increases manufacturing employment and reduces inequality, and the decline in defense production since the 1950s explains about one quarter of manufacturing employment decline and nearly one tenth of the rise of the top-ten income share. The draft removed millions of young men from the labor force and reduced young male civilian unemployment, and procurement raised voter support for hawkish foreign policy.
papers.q: Did the Cold War contribute to inclusive growth in the US post-war decades?
papers.ident: Exogenous shifts in military procurement across states and firms.
papers.dataDetail: US state and firm data on defense procurement, employment and income, 1950s-1990s.

papers.title: Steering Technological Progress
papers.q: How can technological progress be steered to raise labor demand and create better-paying jobs?
papers.summary: Applications include robot taxation, factor-augmenting progress and task automation. The welfare benefits of steering are greater the less efficient social safety nets are, and as technology devalues labor they first rise and then change beyond a point.
papers.ident: Theory: planner problem with directed technological change and labor market impacts.
papers.contribution: Develops a theoretical framework identifying properties that make an innovation desirable for workers, including complementarity to labor, affected workers' relative income and labor's factor share.

papers.title: Time for Growth
papers.q: What was the long-run impact of public mechanical clocks on European economic growth?
papers.summary: Solar eclipses triggered a medieval cultural movement to understand the motion of stars and clocks, producing astronomical instruments and prestige symbols. Early-adopter cities show a significant increase in population, especially between 1500 and 1700.
papers.ident: Instrument: repeated solar eclipse appearances shifting adoption of public clocks.
papers.contribution: Studies the adoption and diffusion of the public mechanical clock using an instrument based on the appearance of repeated solar eclipses.
papers.dataDetail: Historical data on European city adoption of public mechanical clocks and populations.

papers.title: Knowledge Spillovers and Local Outcomes: An Existence Proof from the Establishment of the National Labs
papers.q: Did the establishment of US National Laboratories generate local knowledge spillovers?
papers.summary: Lab counties see large persistent increases in patenting by non-lab inventors, whose patents shift toward the labs' fields and cite lab patents more often. Newly digitized county data for 1936-1970 show sustained rises in retail sales and household income, and linked census records show wage gains for pre-existing residents.
papers.contribution: Studies the 1940s-1950s siting of National Laboratories, with sites chosen largely for security and political reasons and runner-up locations identified from archives.
papers.ident: Comparison of lab counties with archival runner-up sites.
papers.dataDetail: Patents, newly digitized county data 1936-1970 and linked 1940-1950 census records.

papers.title: The Effects of Fiscal News on Household Expectations and Spending: New Causal Evidence

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.summary: Exogenous increases in expected future public debt raise expected inflation and consumer spending. Exogenous increases in expected fiscal balance raise expected output growth with no significant effect on spending.
papers.q: How does fiscal news shape household expectations and spending?
papers.contribution: Runs a survey experiment with about 11,000 Korean individuals linked to high-frequency spending data, randomly providing one of five pieces of fiscal information.
papers.ident: Randomized information about debt, deficits and deficit reduction plans in a survey experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of about 11,000 Korean individuals linked to automatically collected spending data.

papers.title: Bank Fees and Household Financial Well-Being
papers.q: Did eliminating NSF fees and relaxing overdraft policies improve household financial well-being?
papers.summary: Eliminating NSF fees immediately reduced NSF charges across the income distribution, while relaxing overdraft policies reduced overdraft fees only for wealthier households, who also saw fewer late fees, interest payments, maintenance fees and payday loan use. The changes were not substantial enough to reduce financial stress among more vulnerable households.
papers.ident: Staggered bank policy changes with multiple treatments in a difference-in-differences design.
papers.contribution: Examines policy changes by large US banks from 2017 to 2022 using individual transaction-level data.
papers.dataDetail: Individual transaction-level data from US bank accounts, 2017-2022.

papers.title: Cash Transfers and Productive Inclusion: Evidence from Bolsa Familia

authors.inst: Escola Brasileira de Economia e Finanças

papers.q: Do cash transfers to the extremely poor raise work and improve health?
papers.summary: The reform raised employment by 5 percent while hospitalization fell 8 percent and mortality 14 percent, saving about 1,000 lives. Transfers can relax subsistence and health constraints, raise productivity and expand labor supply, challenging the view that transfers reduce work.
papers.contribution: Exploits an increase in the generosity of Bolsa Familia and formalizes a model of productive inclusion to evaluate welfare.
papers.ident: Increase in program generosity across eligible households and regions, with a productive inclusion model.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian administrative data on employment, hospitalization and mortality.

papers.title: Planning under Diagnostic Uncertainty: Question-Driven Learning in the Age of AI
papers.q: How do agents choose which questions to ask under diagnostic uncertainty?
papers.summary: The organization of inquiry is largely absent from formal economic analysis, although it determines whether decisive distinctions are identified or missed. Agents may incur cognitive cost to refine their understanding of the diagnostic structure before each inquiry step.
papers.ident: Theory: sequential question selection with uncertainty over diagnostic structure.
papers.contribution: Develops a model in which agents choose questions sequentially before commitment while facing uncertainty over a latent diagnostic structure governing how questions generate answers.

papers.title: Impact or Responsibility? Giving Behaviour in a Televised Natural Experiment
papers.contribution: Compares impact and responsibility considerations using a television show in which an audience of one hundred divides ten thousand euros among three candidates, plus independent rater evaluations.
papers.summary: The well-being benefit of donations outweighs the candidate's control over their situation. Giving rises more with impact than it falls with responsibility, and impact's contribution to the explanatory power of the regressions is about twice that of responsibility.
papers.q: Does giving respond more to impact or to responsibility?
papers.ident: Regressions of audience allocations on rater-evaluated impact and responsibility attributes.
papers.dataDetail: Allocations by a television audience and independent rater evaluations of candidates.

papers.title: FraNK: Fragmentation in the NK Model
papers.q: How does fragmentation in the New Keynesian model change macroeconomic dynamics?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of fragmentation in the New Keynesian model.

papers.title: The effects of workers’ compensation experience rating on workers’ absences and employment

authors.inst: IRDES Institut de Recherche et Documentation en Économie de la Santé

papers.q: Does experience rating of workers' compensation insurance reduce absences and employment?
papers.summary: Higher experience rating significantly reduced work-related injury and illness absences, with an elasticity of annual absence days to the share of benefit costs borne by firms of -1.20 and an extensive-margin elasticity of -0.43. The reduction is not offset by more nonwork-related absences.
papers.contribution: Exploits a French reform that increased the degree of experience rating for medium-size firms.
papers.ident: French reform increasing experience rating for medium-size firms compared with other firms.
papers.dataDetail: French administrative data on workers' compensation, absences and employment.

papers.title: Does restricting access to credit affect learning outcomes? Evidence from a regulatory shock to microfinance in India
papers.q: Does restricting access to credit affect learning outcomes in India?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of how a regulatory shock to microfinance in India affected learning outcomes through restricted credit access.

papers.title: The impact of working conditions on productivity: Evidence from the U.S. public defense system
papers.q: How do working conditions affect productivity in the US public defense system?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the impact of working conditions on productivity in the US public defense system.

papers.title: Estimation and inference of the forecast error variance decomposition for set-identified SVARs
papers.q: How can the forecast error variance decomposition be estimated and tested in set-identified SVARs?
papers.summary: The paper establishes differentiability of the FEVD bounds in reduced-form parameters using perturbation theory. Monte-Carlo exercises at macroeconomic sample sizes show the confidence interval balances validity and tightness.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: set-identified SVARs with internal and external proxy restrictions.
papers.contribution: Characterizes FEVD endpoints as extreme eigenvalues of a symmetric reduced-form matrix and proposes a consistent plug-in estimator and a set-length-adjusted delta-method confidence interval.
papers.dataDetail: Macroeconomic time series used for Monte Carlo calibration.

papers.title: The Impact of Dating Apps on Young Adults: Evidence from Tinder

authors.inst: Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance
Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: How did Tinder affect sexual activity, relationships and mental health among college students?
papers.summary: The launch led to a sharp, persistent increase in sexual activity with little impact on long-term relationships or their quality. Dating outcome inequality rose, especially among men, along with sexual assault and STDs, yet mental health did not worsen on average and may have improved for women.
papers.contribution: Uses Tinder's initial marketing focus on Greek organizations for identification of its full-scale launch effects.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing Greek-affiliated students with others around Tinder's launch.
papers.dataDetail: College student survey data around Tinder's launch.

papers.title: Cassatts in the Attic: Is There a Gender Gap in the Commercialization of Science
papers.q: Is there a gender gap in the commercialization of science?
papers.summary: The gap of 14 percent is not explained by the quality of the science or its commercial potential. It is widest for papers with female last authors, vanishes when authors self-commercialize through new ventures and is reduced when partnering with smaller firms or firms with more female inventors.
papers.contribution: Analyzes nearly 70 million scientific articles to estimate gender differences in commercialization.
papers.ident: Regression of commercialization on author gender controlling for paper quality and commercial potential.
papers.dataDetail: Nearly 70 million scientific articles linked to patents.

papers.title: Wealth, Marriage, and Sex Selection

authors.inst: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.summary: The implications are tested on a representative sample of rural households. Simulations suggest existing policies targeting daughter aversion might exacerbate the problem, while other policies could be effective.
papers.q: How do wealth, marriage markets and dowries shape sex selection in India?
papers.contribution: Builds a model with son preference and daughter aversion, with microfoundations from the marriage institution, in which marital matching, sex selection and dowries are jointly determined.
papers.ident: Structural: joint model of marital matching, dowries and sex selection tested on household data.
papers.dataDetail: Representative sample of rural Indian households.

papers.title: How Equality Created Poverty in Preindustrial Japan, 1600–1870
papers.summary: Many Japanese peasants owned land, unlike mostly landless English counterparts. Evidence from Japanese village censuses supports the mechanism, and the unusual equality may have shaped Japan's failure to industrialize first if high wages in Western Europe spurred industrialization.
papers.q: Why were real wages in preindustrial Japan around half of those in England?
papers.contribution: Uses a Malthusian model to show that Japan's greater landownership equality, from land inheritance institutions, paradoxically led to lower wages and GDP per capita.
papers.ident: Theory: Malthusian model of land inheritance and wages, supported by village census evidence.
papers.dataDetail: Japanese village censuses, 1600-1870.

papers.title: Real-World Effectiveness of the Influenza Vaccine in Young Children
papers.q: How effective is the influenza vaccine in young children in real-world settings?
papers.summary: Children whose visits occur when the vaccine is available are 23.4 percentage points more likely to be vaccinated. The vaccine significantly reduces outpatient and ED visits, implying that more convenient pediatric vaccination could raise vaccination and cut health care expenditures.
papers.ident: Timing of well-child visits relative to seasonal vaccine availability as an instrument for vaccination.
papers.contribution: Exploits variation in whether well-child visits occur when the seasonal vaccine is broadly available, using large administrative health care datasets.
papers.dataDetail: Large administrative health care datasets on children's visits and vaccinations.

papers.title: Age at School Entry and Human Capital Development: Evidence from Lesotho
papers.q: How does age at school entry affect human capital development in Lesotho?
papers.summary: Children who start at older ages overcome initial skill deficits, are more likely to remain in school, work less and obtain substantially more total years of schooling. In adulthood they are more likely to hold professional occupations and less likely to marry or have children as teenagers, to become HIV infected (men) or to experience a child's death (women).
papers.contribution: Exploits an enrollment age threshold to assess school starting age impacts.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity at the enrollment age threshold.
papers.dataDetail: Household survey data on schooling and adult outcomes in Lesotho.

papers.title: Information Frictions and Employee Sorting between Start-ups

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: Do informed workers sort to better start-ups?
papers.summary: Making ratings visible strongly reallocates applications toward higher-rated firms, including among high-quality workers, partly by shifting beliefs about right-tail outcomes. Workers still make post-treatment bets that show highly overoptimistic beliefs about start-up success.
papers.contribution: Creates a custom job board with 26 science-based start-ups, randomizing the display of coarse expert ratings of start-up science and business model quality to business school alumni.
papers.ident: Randomized visibility of expert ratings on a job board.
papers.dataDetail: Job board applications by business school alumni to 26 science-based start-ups.

papers.title: The Effects of Gender Integration on Men: Evidence from the U.S. Military
papers.q: Do men respond negatively when women enter previously all-male occupations, as in US military combat units?
papers.contribution: Exploits the staggered integration of women into combat units after 2016 and monthly administrative personnel records with survey responses.
papers.summary: Integrating women into all-male units does not negatively affect men's performance or behavior, including retention, promotions, demotions, misconduct separations, criminal investigations and medical conditions. Most results are precise enough to rule out meaningful negative effects.
papers.ident: Staggered integration of women into combat units across the US military after 2016.
papers.dataDetail: Monthly administrative US military personnel records and survey responses.

papers.title: Monitoring joint tail risks: An application to growth and inflation
papers.q: How can joint tail risks to growth and inflation be monitored?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of monitoring joint tail risks to growth and inflation.

papers.title: Spread too thin: The impact of lean inventories
papers.q: What is the impact of lean inventories on the economy?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the impact of lean inventories.

papers.title: Curbing pretextual stops: Police efficiency and racial disparities
papers.q: Does curbing pretextual police stops improve police efficiency and reduce racial disparities?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of curbing pretextual stops, police efficiency and racial disparities.

papers.title: Robust econometrics for growth-at-risk
