papers.summary: The measure compares distributions of extreme multi-exposure across groups and time. It is applied using public data on air toxics, PM2.5 and land surface temperature.
papers.contribution: Adapts the Alkire-Foster multi-dimensional poverty measure to rank extreme simultaneous exposure to environmental harm by frequency, breadth and severity.
papers.ident: Descriptive: multi-dimensional index of extreme simultaneous exposure.
papers.dataDetail: Public data on air toxics, PM2.5 and land surface temperature.

papers.title: AI and the Quantity and Usage of Creative Products: Have LLMs Boosted Creation of Valuable Books?
papers.summary: Monthly book releases tripled as LLMs diffused, and average usage and quality fell while the number of modestly used books rose. AI books are less used and topped half of 2025 releases, raising consumer surplus only modestly, with author selection explaining most of the usage differential.
papers.ident: Structural: nested logit calibration of consumer surplus.
papers.q: Have large language models boosted the creation of valuable books?
papers.contribution: Documents book releases from 2022 to late 2025 and uses a nested logit calibration to assess consumer surplus from AI-containing books.
papers.dataDetail: Book release, rating and sales rank data, 2022-2025.

papers.title: Why Does Height Pay? Evidence from the Kenya Life Panel Survey
papers.q: Why do taller people earn more in Kenya?
papers.contribution: Uses longitudinal microdata on a cohort of middle-aged Kenyan adults with a rich battery of 27 cognition modules.
papers.summary: Monthly earnings increase by 1.07% per centimeter of height. Nearly half the effect is explained by cognition, with further shares attributable to physical strength and non-cognitive ability and little role for occupational sorting.
papers.ident: Decomposition of the height premium into cognition, strength and non-cognitive channels, with repeated height measures.
papers.dataDetail: Kenya Life Panel Survey with cognitive test battery.

papers.title: Audit Centralization and Audit Quality: Evidence from Chinese Cities
papers.q: Does centralizing city audits improve audit quality in China?
papers.summary: Centralization raises detection of suspicious expenditures by over 50%, including in cities with auditors appointed before 2016, and financial but not human resources devoted to audits increase. The improvements reflect stronger incentives and resources rather than auditor selection.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing pilot and non-pilot provinces in 2016.
papers.contribution: Uses a difference-in-differences design around a 2016 pilot in six provinces giving provincial governments control over city audit budgets and personnel.
papers.dataDetail: Chinese city audit data around the 2016 pilot.

papers.title: Changing Culture and Norms in Developing Countries
papers.q: How can culture and social norms be changed in developing countries?
papers.summary: The chapter reviews interventions targeting each component and their interactions: schooling, curricula, information campaigns, mass media and empowerment programs for gender norms, intimate partner violence and harmful practices, and social determinants such as misperceptions and coordination failures.
papers.contribution: Surveys recent research and proposes a framework where individual utility from an action combines intrinsic valuations, material payoffs and social interactions.

papers.title: Mapping Technological Trajectories: Evidence from Two Centuries of Patent Data

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How have countries' technological trajectories evolved over two centuries?
papers.summary: The data show the relative decline of the UK, the rise of the US and Germany and later of Japan and China. Trajectories are strongly positively correlated with TFP growth and less strongly with labour productivity growth and capital intensity.
papers.contribution: Introduces a methodology to measure technological trajectories from sustained patenting across multiple patent offices and implements it on patents between 1836 and 2016.
papers.ident: Econometric estimation of country trajectories from patenting across offices.
papers.dataDetail: Patents across multiple countries and offices, 1836-2016.

papers.title: How do Foundations Help Charities (Beyond Giving them Money)?
papers.q: How do foundations help charities beyond giving money?
papers.contribution: Studies applicants to a $100 million funding competition whose sponsor offered publicity, networking and advice to a subset of unsuccessful entrants.
papers.summary: This support substantially improved later fundraising for smaller charities, generating over $40 million in income in the years after the competition. Large donors can influence nonprofit success without awarding funds.
papers.ident: Support offered to a subset of unsuccessful entrants in a funding competition.
papers.dataDetail: Applicants to a $100 million foundation funding competition and later charity income.

papers.title: A.I. and Our Economic Future
papers.q: How will AI affect long-run economic growth?
papers.summary: Despite access to 100 million times more transistors than in the 1970s, people are not 100 million times more productive because humans must still decide what to compute and test. Accelerating growth requires automating the vast majority of tasks.
papers.contribution: Argues that automating intelligence could accelerate growth beyond the roughly 2 percent per year stable for 150 years, but that weak links slow it.
papers.ident: Theory: growth with automation and weak links.

papers.title: The Effect of Charter Schools on Identification, Service Provision, and Achievement of Students with Disabilities
papers.q: How do charter schools affect identification, services and achievement of students with disabilities?
papers.summary: Charters are slightly more likely to identify students as having disabilities after entry, and assignments to special education programs increase comparably. The paper estimates impacts on services and achievement.
papers.ident: Heterogeneous difference-in-differences comparing students entering charters with not-yet-treated future entrants.
papers.contribution: Uses Michigan data and a heterogeneous difference-in-differences model comparing students who enter charters with those who eventually will.
papers.dataDetail: Michigan student-level administrative data.

papers.title: The Life-cycle of Concentrated Industries
papers.q: Should competition policy differ for innovative industries over their life cycle?
papers.summary: The equilibrium features intense entry, then a shakeout and concentration as some firms scale through innovation while most exit. Innovation and dynamic competition do not necessarily justify intervention, and optimal policy depends on whether firms compete mainly for the market.
papers.ident: Theory: industry life-cycle model with optimal subsidies.
papers.contribution: Develops a life-cycle model of an oligopolistic industry, a finite-firm version of Jovanovic and MacDonald (1994), and analyzes the second-best problem of subsidizing small firms.

papers.title: The Future of Monetarism after Milton Friedman

authors.inst: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.summary: Friedman's 1956 quantity of money challenged the Keynesian view that money did not matter, and his research attributed much of twentieth-century macro instability, including the Great Depression and Great Inflation, to money supply changes. His ideas underlie modern macroeconomics and rules-based central banking, though monetary aggregates as the key tool have been superseded.
papers.q: What is the future of monetarism after Milton Friedman?
papers.contribution: Reflects on the legacy of monetarism on the fiftieth anniversary of Friedman's Nobel Prize.

papers.title: Creating High-Opportunity Neighborhoods: Evidence from the HOPE VI Program
papers.q: Can revitalizing distressed public housing create high-opportunity neighborhoods?
papers.summary: HOPE VI reduced neighborhood poverty by attracting higher-income families but had no causal effect on the earnings of adults in public housing. Children raised in revitalized units earned more, were more likely to attend college and less likely to be incarcerated, due to changes in neighborhoods' causal effects.
papers.ident: Matched difference-in-differences with a movers exposure design and sibling comparisons.
papers.contribution: Estimates the impacts of the $17 billion HOPE VI program, covering 262 developments, with a matched difference-in-differences design on anonymized tax records.
papers.dataDetail: Anonymized tax records for residents of 262 public housing developments.

papers.title: Clientelism: How It Works, Why It Persists and How to Break It
papers.q: How does clientelism work, why does it persist and how can it be broken?
papers.contribution: Surveys the economics and political science literature on clientelism, defined as the exchange of votes or participation for targeted material benefits.
papers.summary: Clientelism undermines electoral accountability, fostering rent-seeking and underprovision of public goods, and is facilitated and perpetuated by underdevelopment. The chapter analyzes broker-voter and politician-broker agency problems and the roles of monitoring, selection and networks, and assesses interventions.

papers.title: Dynamic Selection and the Puzzle of Slow Climate Change Adaptation in U.S. Agriculture
papers.q: Why does climate adaptation in US agriculture appear slow once dynamic selection is accounted for?
papers.summary: Counties that exit farming change the composition of balanced panels, higher-skilled workers leave rural areas as weather worsens, and smaller farms consolidate into larger ones. The slope of the yield damage function depends on county education and farm size.
papers.ident: Structural selection model of heterogeneous farmers' exit and adaptation.
papers.contribution: Uses a selection model incorporating heterogeneous farmers' optimizing behavior and data from 1980 to 2020 to document three dynamic selection effects.
papers.conclusion: Causal estimates of weather impacts must account for selection along several adaptation margins.
papers.dataDetail: US county-level agricultural data, 1980-2020.

papers.title: The factor structure of jump risk
papers.q: What is the factor structure of jump risk?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the factor structure of jump risk.

papers.title: The comovement of voter preferences: Insights from U.S. presidential election prediction markets beyond polls

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: What do presidential election prediction markets reveal about the comovement of voter preferences beyond polls?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the comovement of voter preferences using US presidential election prediction markets beyond polls.

papers.title: Gender Differences in Economics Seminars
papers.q: Are women treated differently from men when presenting in economics seminars?
papers.summary: Within a seminar series, women are interrupted more than men, controlling for presenter, paper and audience characteristics. Negative or mid-sentence interruptions increase for women presenters, and female audience members engage more with female presenters, suggesting a role model effect.
papers.contribution: Collects data across thousands of seminars, job market talks and conference presentations and uses human judgment and audio-processing algorithms to measure interruptions.
papers.ident: Within-seminar-series comparison of interruptions by presenter gender.
papers.dataDetail: Audio of thousands of seminars, job market talks and conference presentations.

papers.title: Raising the Stakes: Physician Facility Investments and Provider Agency
papers.q: Do physicians' investments in ambulatory surgery centers reduce medical spending?
papers.contribution: Uses novel data on physician ownership of ambulatory surgery centers to show equity holdings cause substitution away from higher cost rival settings.
papers.summary: Ownership lowers Medicare spending by 10 to 40 percent per physician, with no clear evidence of perverse behavior. Entrepreneurial activity can indirectly limit principal-agent problems and improve efficiency.
papers.ident: Physician equity investments in ambulatory surgery centers and subsequent referral patterns.
papers.dataDetail: Novel data on physician ownership of ambulatory surgery centers and Medicare claims.

papers.title: Reprint of: Nonparametric estimation for high-frequency data incorporating trading information
papers.q: How can nonparametric estimation for high-frequency data incorporate trading information?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of nonparametric estimation for high-frequency data incorporating trading information.

papers.title: Financial Frictions: Micro versus Macro Volatility
papers.q: How do consumer credit spreads affect household choices and aggregate volatility?
papers.summary: Consumer credit spreads have heterogeneous effects on asset dynamics and consumption across the wealth distribution, and time-varying spreads induce a countercyclical marginal propensity to consume. Frictional finance amplifies aggregate shocks, and less leveraged banks reduce aggregate volatility but may raise household-level volatility and lower welfare.
papers.ident: Quantitative: HANK model with bank-provided credit, with Danish micro evidence.
papers.contribution: Studies Danish household data and builds a HANK model where banks provide consumer credit and corporate loans.
papers.dataDetail: Danish household data on assets, credit and consumption.

papers.title: Competition under Incomplete Contracts and the Design of Procurement Policies
papers.q: How does intensifying competition for contracts affect procurement outcomes under incomplete contracts?
papers.summary: Expanding the set of bidders reduces award prices but worsens post-award performance through cost overruns and delays. Estimates show substantial performance heterogeneity across contractors, and simple adjustments to the regulation could give significant savings.
papers.contribution: Uses a discontinuous regulation mandating publicity of certain US Defense contract opportunities, and estimates an auction model with endogenous entry and stochastic execution performance.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity at the regulatory threshold mandating publicity of contract opportunities.
papers.dataDetail: US Defense procurement contract data.

papers.title: Dynamic Regulation with Firm Linkages: Evidence from Texas
papers.q: How efficient is linked environmental regulation across plants with a common owner?
papers.summary: Linked regulation performs substantially better than both unlinked and untargeted regulation, by letting regulators target enforcement toward bad actors without inspecting everyone. The paper tests a firm-wide moral hazard mechanism and a correlated compliance cost mechanism.
papers.contribution: Develops an empirical framework of dynamic moral hazard under linked regulation with large portfolios of plants and evaluates a Texas scheme.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic moral hazard model of linked inspections.
papers.dataDetail: Texas environmental inspection and plant ownership data.

papers.title: Hacked to Pieces? The Effects of Ransomware Attacks on Hospitals and Patients
papers.q: How do ransomware attacks affect hospitals and patients?
papers.summary: Attacks decrease hospital volume by 17-24 percent in the initial attack week, with recovery within three weeks. In-hospital mortality increases by 34-38 percent among patients already admitted when an attack begins.
papers.contribution: Creates and links a database of hospital ransomware attacks to Medicare claims data.
papers.ident: Timing of ransomware attacks across hospitals.
papers.dataDetail: Database of hospital ransomware attacks linked to Medicare claims.

papers.title: Distorted prices and targeted taxes in the New Keynesian Network model
papers.q: What is the optimal tax response to sectoral shocks in a New Keynesian network economy?
papers.summary: The optimal response uses twice as many instruments as sectors, is budget-neutral and is not confined to the sector where the shock originates. A simple rule responds to inflation in the shocked sector and adjusts other sectors' taxes according to input-output linkages, and is evaluated in a calibrated model.
papers.ident: Theory: optimal sector-specific taxes in a New Keynesian network model.
papers.contribution: Characterizes the optimal tax response in the New Keynesian Network model and shows it can be approximated by a simple rule.

papers.title: Weather and U.S. railways: risk, adaptation, and congestion
papers.q: How do weather, adaptation and congestion affect US railways?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of weather risk, adaptation and congestion on US railways.

papers.title: Foreign technology and informal employment: Evidence from Mexico

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.q: How does foreign technology affect informal employment in Mexico?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of foreign technology and informal employment in Mexico.

papers.title: Rethinking fiscal rules in resource-rich economies
papers.q: How should fiscal rules be rethought in resource-rich economies?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of fiscal rules in resource-rich economies.

papers.title: Beyond lost earnings: Job displacement and the cost of commuting
papers.q: How much does job displacement raise workers' commuting costs beyond lost earnings?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of job displacement and the cost of commuting beyond lost earnings.

papers.title: Sweeping up Gangs: The Effects of Tough-on-Crime Policies from a Network Approach
papers.q: Do gang sweeps reduce crime for those arrested and their peers?
papers.summary: Crime falls by 85 percent among those arrested and 31 percent among their peers, from incapacitation and a less criminal environment respectively. Broader targeting of key network players could have reduced crime by 43 percentage points more.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around a policy shift toward gang sweeps in Barcelona.
papers.contribution: Uses a difference-in-differences strategy and network analysis on a policy shift in the Barcelona metropolitan area.
papers.dataDetail: Police data on arrests and criminal networks in the Barcelona metropolitan area.

papers.title: A Theory of How Workers Keep up with Inflation
papers.q: How do workers keep up with inflation when nominal wages are sticky?
papers.summary: Nominal wage stickiness induces job-to-job transitions after an unexpected rise in the price level, raising vacancies and associating a seemingly tight labor market with lower real wages. Historical data show earlier high-inflation periods also saw rising vacancies and outward shifts in the Beveridge curve.
papers.ident: Quantitative: search model with nominal wage rigidity calibrated to worker flows.
papers.contribution: Develops a model integrating labor market flows with nominal wage rigidities and calibrates it to 2021-2024 worker flows and wages.
papers.dataDetail: US aggregate and cross-sectional worker flow and wage data, 2021-2024, and historical series.

papers.title: Wage growth and labor market tightness

authors.inst: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Federal Reserve Bank of New York

papers.q: How do wage growth and labor market tightness relate?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the relationship between wage growth and labor market tightness.

papers.title: Attitudes toward Success and Failure

authors.inst: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.summary: The definitions give a unified view of several models of reference-dependent preferences and suggest new comparative statics exercises.
papers.ident: Theory: preference characterizations with a reference point.
papers.q: How can attitudes toward success and failure be defined as features of preferences over lotteries?
papers.contribution: Defines attitudes toward success and failure in an expected utility setting with an exogenous reference point, as a local reversal of risk attitude across the reference point.

papers.title: Cardinality and Utilitarianism through Social Interactions
papers.summary: The weights are group independent when one additional axiom and a mild linear independence assumption hold.
papers.q: Can cardinal utility and utilitarian group preferences be derived from group preference axioms?
papers.contribution: Provides axioms relating each group's preferences to those of its subgroups, yielding cardinal utility indices and a representation of group preferences as a group-dependent weighted sum.
papers.ident: Theory: axiomatic representation of group preferences.

papers.title: Backward Induction Reasoning beyond Backward Induction

authors.inst: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.summary: Backward induction is defined only for perfect information games, yet its logic is invoked in imperfect and incomplete information concepts. The paper shows several properties and applications, including a new version of Lipnowski and Sadler's peer-confirming equilibrium.
papers.q: What does backward induction reasoning mean beyond perfect information games?
papers.contribution: Introduces backward rationalizability, a nonequilibrium solution concept for incomplete information games that distills the logic of backward induction.
papers.ident: Theory: nonequilibrium solution concept for incomplete information games.

papers.title: Financial Crises: History, Theory and New Insights
papers.contribution: Reviews the history, causes and consequences of financial crises and revisits the chronology of US crises since 1870 using bank failure rates and large-bank equity losses.
papers.summary: Some panics were not full-blown financial crises, and some episodes with no panic could be considered crises. The essay highlights new insights from new data sources and empirical designs and covers theoretical models.
papers.q: What do new data and designs teach us about financial crises?

papers.title: A Macroeconomic Perspective on Stock Market Valuation Ratios
papers.q: Can macroeconomic trends explain high US stock market valuation ratios?
papers.summary: Traditional valuation metrics have been above historical norms for 25-30 years. The decline occurs even without changes in expected returns or growth rates.
papers.contribution: Uses macroeconomic data to argue that falling labor share of corporate output with weak corporate investment mechanically lowers the ratio of earnings to valuation.
papers.ident: Descriptive: accounting relation between labor share, investment and valuation ratios.
papers.dataDetail: US aggregate corporate output, labor share, investment and market value data.

papers.title: Modeling the Labor Implications of the Energy Transition
papers.contribution: Outlines a conceptual framework for labor-market risks in the energy transition, reviews empirical research on barriers to adjustment and surveys ex-ante modeling literature.
papers.summary: The transition will disrupt labor markets, concentrating risks on workers in carbon-intensive sectors and regions reliant on fossil fuels. The review focuses on obstacles to labor-market adjustment that can inform modeling.
papers.q: How should the labor implications of the energy transition be modeled?

papers.title: Rational Disagreement

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: Can agents be rational yet disagree about which individuals perform better?
papers.contribution: Proposes rational disagreement as a formal framework for persistent seemingly irrational behavior, with agents correctly anticipating the distribution of aggregate outcomes.
papers.summary: A simple entry game illustrates the concepts, and unordered individual outcome distributions are identified solely from aggregate statistics. The paper characterizes the resulting game and its Nash equilibria and develops a statistical test of the null hypothesis of agreement.
papers.ident: Theory: identification of individual outcome distributions from aggregate statistics.

papers.title: Consumer Demand and Market Competition with Time-Intensive Goods
papers.q: How does time allocation theory shape demand and competition for time-intensive goods like social media?
papers.summary: The model predicts higher diversion ratios for goods with large time shares and high time costs relative to prices. Users show low elasticity to ad load, and time shares and costs significantly influence diversion, with implications for an FTC-proposed de-merger of Facebook and Instagram.
papers.ident: Field experiments varying platform use, with a Beckerian demand model.
papers.contribution: Applies Becker's time allocation theory to demand for Facebook and Instagram using data from two field experiments.
papers.dataDetail: Two field experiments on Facebook and Instagram use.

papers.title: Speculative Growth and the AI "Bubble"
papers.q: Can a temporary AI valuation bubble leave a permanent real legacy?
papers.summary: Temporary optimism supplies the valuation needed for transition, raises investment demand and pushes up the real interest rate. An earlier correction returns the economy to the low state, whereas a later one lowers valuation, depending on the size and duration of optimism.
papers.contribution: Develops a model where AI investment expands capacity and shifts income to capital owners whose saving rises with wealth, supporting a rational high-capital steady state.
papers.ident: Theory: multiple steady states with wealth-dependent saving and temporary optimism.

papers.title: Missing Black Men? The Impact of Non-Reporting on Estimates of Labor Market Outcomes for Black Men
papers.q: How does non-reporting by Black men bias estimates of labor market outcomes?
papers.summary: Non-reporting rates are up to 5.5 percentage points larger than prior estimates, driven by Black men at risk of incarceration, with 35-83% of the incarcerated population estimated to be non-reporting otherwise. Adjusted Black-white gaps are 20-39% larger for high-school completion, 8-18% for college attendance and 10-20% for earnings, but 4-8% smaller for employment.
papers.contribution: Derives a method to account for incomplete data on non-reporting in household surveys, using state-year variation in incarceration rates.
papers.ident: Method accounting for non-reporting, with state-year variation in incarceration rates.
papers.dataDetail: Household-based surveys from 1970-2020 with demographic estimates of non-reporting.

papers.title: The Twenty-four Hour Economy or Rolled-up Sidewalks: Trends in Work Timing and Their Causes
papers.q: Has the timing of paid work shifted toward daytime hours and why?
papers.summary: Work has shifted away from evenings and nights toward usual daytime hours, mostly related to rising real incomes, educational attainment, manufacturing's changing composition and a higher wage premium for undesirable times. The trend exists in all major industries except retail, accelerated with telework after COVID, and appears in France but not in the UK.
papers.contribution: Documents trends in the timing of work in the US from 1973 to 2023 and compares France and the UK.
papers.ident: Descriptive: decomposition of trends in work timing.
papers.dataDetail: Time-use data for the US (1973-2023), France (1966-2010) and the UK (1974-2015).

papers.title: The Dynamics of Retail Deposit Balances
papers.q: What drives the dynamics of retail deposit balances?
papers.summary: With 10% of depositors holding 70% of deposits, large-balance accounts drive aggregate flows, usually becoming large after one-time inflows and being likelier to see large idiosyncratic drawdowns. High-balance depositors are not sensitive to interest rate shocks, and deposit stickiness seems driven by accounts used as medium-run liquidity stores.
papers.contribution: Uses account-level data on 12 million accounts across 154 US credit unions.
papers.dataDetail: Account-level data on 12 million accounts in 154 US credit unions.

papers.title: Scaling Sustainable Investing in Emerging and Developing Economies: Frictions and Opportunities
papers.q: What frictions limit private investment in sustainable development in emerging and developing economies?
papers.contribution: Conducts a global survey of senior investment decision-makers, including asset managers, pension and sovereign wealth funds and development finance institutions.
papers.summary: Conditional on investor type, return expectations in emerging and developing economies are comparable to those in developed markets, suggesting categorical exclusions might be inefficient. Investors' dominant risk perceptions concern currency and political risk.
papers.dataDetail: Global survey of senior investment decision-makers.

papers.title: Structural Change and Jobless Development
papers.q: Why does early development reduce total employment rates?
papers.summary: Early development is associated with a substantial decline in total employment, contrary to benchmark models that hold employment constant. The calibrated model accounts for the patterns qualitatively and quantitatively.
papers.ident: Quantitative: structural change model with endogenous labor supply calibrated to panel facts.
papers.contribution: Documents a positive relationship between the share employed in agriculture and the overall employment rate in a panel of 48 mostly developing economies for 1990-2018, and extends a structural change model with Stone-Geary preferences to endogenous labor supply.
papers.dataDetail: Panel of 48 mostly developing economies, 1990-2018.

papers.title: No Taxation Without Administration: Bringing The State Back Into The Public Finance Of Developing Countries
papers.q: How can tax administration reforms raise tax capacity in developing countries?
papers.contribution: Reviews the emerging literature on strengthening tax administration through reforms to organizational structure, personnel management and task management, and on state legitimacy.
papers.summary: Leveraging third-party information is out of reach in many developing countries because of informal economies and low state capacity. Efforts to raise the state's legitimacy, meaning popular acceptance of its right to tax, can increase capacity and complement administrative investments.

papers.title: Technology and Economic Development
papers.summary: Lower absorptive capacity, institutional distortions, inappropriate technology and credit market frictions slow adoption, leaving the economy farther from the frontier and with lower income per capita, although its long-run growth rate equals the frontier's.
papers.q: How do technology adoption and diffusion shape differences in income across countries?
papers.contribution: Presents a tractable framework for technology adoption and diffusion in countries behind the frontier and extends it to the choice between innovation and imitation.
papers.ident: Theory: technology adoption model with distance to frontier.

papers.title: Global Imbalances and Power Imbalances
papers.q: Can global imbalances generate power imbalances between creditor and debtor nations?
papers.contribution: Discusses conditions under which global imbalances, such as China as a large creditor and the United States as a large debtor, might generate power imbalances.
papers.summary: The paper highlights possible theoretical channels and empirical measures for future research to investigate.

papers.title: Historical military conflict, current trade tensions, and global supply chains
papers.q: How do historical military conflicts affect current trade tensions and global supply chains?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of historical military conflict, current trade tensions and global supply chains.

papers.title: Choosing Career and Family: The Multidimensional Returns to College Majors
papers.q: How do college majors shape earnings and family formation?
papers.summary: Earnings payoffs show substantial preference-based heterogeneity but limited gender heterogeneity, while fertility effects show limited idiosyncratic but substantial gender heterogeneity. This points to majors as gender-specific career-family bundles, supported by associations with career-family compatibility.
papers.ident: Admissions-based variation in major assignment using preference and admission data.
papers.contribution: Uses administrative data linking students' preferences, admissions, graduation, earnings and births to characterize heterogeneity in the multidimensional returns to majors.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative data linking college preferences, admissions, graduation, earnings and births.

papers.title: Psychology and Development: Applications from Cognitive and Social Psychology
papers.q: How can psychology inform behavioral development economics?
papers.summary: Tools and services that help overcome biases will be under-supplied by markets, so biases can matter in steady state even among experienced agents. Biases matter especially in development because proximity to subsistence, volatility, market failures, weak institutions and reliance on social ties amplify psychological constraints.
papers.contribution: Outlines a research agenda on psychological channels that impede escape from poverty and shape production, markets and informal institutions, applying a missing markets lens.

papers.title: Migration and the Making of the English Middle Class

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: Did migration shape class identity in early twentieth century Britain?
papers.summary: Migration that raised the local share of culturally distant workers reduced working-class identification, making workers less likely to join unions, voters less likely to support Labour and candidates less likely to target working-class voters.
papers.ident: Within-household variation in exposure to migration patterns increasing cultural distance.
papers.contribution: Develops and validates a measure of class identity from naming decisions and exploits within-household variation in migration patterns.
papers.dataDetail: Early twentieth-century British data with naming decisions as a measure of class identity.

papers.title: Gender Norms and the Labor Market
papers.q: How do gender norms shape labor market outcomes?
papers.contribution: Provides a unified framework distinguishing internalized norms from external norms arising from peer pressure and coordination, and reviews the evidence on their origins, persistence and effects.
papers.summary: Gender gaps persist despite convergence in economic roles. The review covers variation in gender attitudes and effects on human capital, labor supply, wages and policy take-up, and mechanisms through which policies, institutions and media can induce norm change.

papers.title: You Only Live Twice: Financial Inflows and Growth in a Westward-Facing Ukraine

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.summary: Investment in physical capital relaxes borrowing constraints, allowing more capital inflows, and raises wages, encouraging refugees to return. The earlier EU and NATO accession of Eastern European countries serves as a template.
papers.q: How can financial inflows support growth and refugee return in postwar Ukraine?
papers.contribution: Shows theoretically that the government can refine an FDI and structural funds strategy by internalizing positive externalities from a higher capital stock.
papers.ident: Theory: growth model with capital externalities, borrowing constraints and refugee return.

papers.title: Measuring the Growth of Skills
papers.q: Can skills be measured without imposing arbitrary scales?
papers.contribution: Measures skills with a novel measurement scheme and estimates a stochastic learning process, testing the common scale assumption across levels for language and cognitive skills.
papers.summary: New skills emerge that are not just more of previously acquired skills, and psychometric convention forces them onto arbitrarily constructed scales that can distort measurement. The common scale assumption is rejected, and dynamic complementarity is estimated without arbitrary scales.
papers.ident: Structural: stochastic learning process estimated with scale-free skill measures.

papers.title: Senior Migration, Local Economic Development and Spatial Concentration
papers.q: Can attracting retired migrants promote development in lagging regions?
papers.summary: Senior inflows raise the working-age population, total employment, GDP, incomes, fiscal revenues and housing construction over a decade, especially in initially poorer regions, along with a larger share of services. Retirement migration flows from richer, urban regions to poorer, rural ones.
papers.contribution: Combines French microdata with a new empirical strategy to estimate the effects of senior in-migration on local economies.
papers.dataDetail: Unique collection of French microdata on migration flows at retirement and local economic outcomes.

papers.title: Understanding Latin America’s Fertility Decline: Age, Education, and Cohort Dynamics
papers.q: What explains the fertility decline in Latin America?
papers.contribution: Combines Vital Statistics, Census microdata and UN population data to decompose fertility changes by age, education and joint groups using period and cohort measures.
papers.summary: The 2000-2022 decline in period fertility is driven primarily by falling within-group birth rates rather than composition, mostly among younger and less-educated women. Between cohorts born in the mid-1950s and mid-1970s, completed fertility fell through delayed childbearing and fewer children per mother rather than rising childlessness.
papers.ident: Descriptive: decomposition of fertility changes by age and education.
papers.dataDetail: Vital Statistics, Census microdata and UN population data for Latin America.

papers.title: Protection for sale without aggregation bias
papers.contribution: Estimates the Grossman-Helpman model with a new production dataset at the tariff-line level rather than the industry level.
papers.summary: Earlier estimates of the weight on social welfare are often close to 1, unrealistically high. With tariff-level data, the average weight in a sample of 142 countries declines by 77 percent.
papers.q: Is the weight governments put on welfare in Protection for Sale overstated by aggregation bias?
papers.ident: Structural estimation of Protection for Sale at the tariff-line level.
papers.dataDetail: New production dataset at the tariff-line level for 142 countries.

papers.title: Minimax rates of convergence for nonparametric location-Scale models

authors.inst: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

papers.q: What are the minimax rates of convergence for nonparametric location-scale models?
papers.summary: The models include mean, quantile and expectile regression, and examples cover asymmetric Laplace, connected normal-Laplace, Cauchy and asymmetric normal errors. Applications cover low order interaction models and multiple index models.
papers.contribution: Shows the minimax rate for estimating the regression function under squared L2 loss is determined by the metric entropy of the function class, under Hellinger differentiability of the error distribution.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: minimax rates for nonparametric location-scale regression.

papers.title: Strategic emissions in the rain
papers.q: Do firms strategically emit pollution when it rains?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of strategic emissions in the rain.

papers.title: Motivating banks to lend? Credit spillover effects of the Main Street Lending Program
papers.q: Did the Main Street Lending Program create credit spillovers by motivating banks to lend?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of credit spillover effects of the Main Street Lending Program.

papers.title: Precautionary liquidity and worker decisions: Evidence from French employee saving plans
papers.q: How does precautionary liquidity affect worker decisions in French employee saving plans?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of precautionary liquidity and worker decisions in French employee saving plans.

papers.title: Strategic Trading and Blockholder Dynamics

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.q: How does a privately informed blockholder trade strategically, and what does asymmetric information do to welfare?
papers.summary: Private information results in larger blocks in good states but, by increasing selling speed, can lower block sizes in bad states. Asymmetric information leads to Pareto improvements, raising stock prices and benefiting small shareholders and the block owner despite reducing liquidity.
papers.contribution: Studies a model of strategic trading by a privately informed blockholder who monitors a company.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic trading model with a privately informed blockholder.

papers.title: GMM inference in the matrix exponential spatial specification

authors.inst: Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.q: How can GMM inference be done in the matrix exponential spatial specification?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of GMM inference in the matrix exponential spatial specification.

papers.title: Inference Based on Time-Varying SVARs Identified with Sign Restrictions
papers.q: How can Bayesian inference be done in time-varying SVARs identified with sign restrictions?
papers.contribution: Proposes a class of rotation-invariant time-varying SVARs and the first algorithm drawing from a uniform distribution over sequences of orthogonal matrices given the reduced-form parameters.
papers.summary: The approach is illustrated by analyzing the role of monetary policy during the latest inflation surge.
papers.ident: Sign restrictions in time-varying SVARs.

papers.title: Destabilizing Capital Flows amid Global Inflation
papers.summary: Inflows raise demand for domestic non-tradables and put upward pressure on firms' costs in the hardest-hit countries. A reverse pattern of flows would improve the output-inflation trade-off globally, requiring less aggressive tightening and delivering welfare gains.
papers.q: Do capital flows toward high-inflation countries destabilize the global inflation-output trade-off?
papers.contribution: Uses an open-economy model with nominal rigidities and cost-push shocks to explain capital flows from low- to high-inflation countries over the latest tightening cycle.
papers.ident: Open-economy New Keynesian model with cost-push shocks.

papers.title: Likelihood specification in simultaneous equation models for discrete data
papers.q: What is the correct likelihood for simultaneous equation models with discrete data?
papers.contribution: Derives the likelihood as the invariant distribution of a suitably specified Markov process, with a well-defined reduced form and no recursivity or ad hoc indeterminacy rules.
papers.summary: The likelihood is unique, proper, coherent, complete and grounded in conditional distribution modeling, resolving puzzling paradoxes from earlier work. The method is implemented in three empirical applications, including female labor force participation.
papers.dataDetail: Three empirical applications, including female labor force participation.

papers.title: (Not) Thinking About the Future: Financial Information and Maternal Labor Supply
papers.q: Does information about the long-run costs of reduced labor supply increase mothers' working hours?
papers.summary: Long-term financial factors are not top of mind and many women hold overly optimistic expectations about pensions and wage growth. The treatment raises demand for information and planned labor supply, and mothers who underestimate the costs increase working hours by 7% a year later.
papers.ident: Randomized information treatment in a field experiment, with administrative follow-up.
papers.contribution: Runs a large-scale field experiment in Switzerland randomizing information on long-run financial costs of part-time work among part-time teachers, linked to administrative employer data.
papers.dataDetail: Part-time teachers in Switzerland, with linked employer administrative data.

papers.title: Never Enough: Dynamic Status Incentives in Organizations
papers.q: Can a rat race of hierarchical status incentives elicit repeated effort from workers?
papers.summary: Fighter pilot performance rises as pilots approach medal eligibility and falls after receipt, and the pattern repeats for the next medal. Medals substitute for other status forms, and their cachet declines as lower-ability pilots receive them, making new medals desirable.
papers.contribution: Uses data on more than 5,000 German air force pilots in World War II to study status-based incentives from medals.
papers.ident: Effort around medal eligibility thresholds and the introduction of new medals.
papers.dataDetail: Over 5,000 German air force pilots in World War II.

papers.title: FinTech and Customer Capital
papers.summary: FinTech firms invest significantly more in customer capital, which builds valuable customer capital, and the gap is not explained by sector focus or firm age. Candidate reasons include trust building, downstream focus, platform business models and reliance on customer data.
papers.q: Do FinTech firms invest more in customer capital than traditional financial firms?
papers.contribution: Compares customer capital investment of FinTech and traditional financial firms and explores reasons for the gap.

papers.title: Why is the Mental Health of the Youngest American Workers in Decline?
papers.summary: Mental health has worsened most quickly among young workers, steepening the age gradient of ill-being for workers, while non-workers show a hump-shaped pattern. Age differences in reported working conditions mirror improvements in worker wellbeing with age.
papers.q: Why is the mental health of the youngest American workers in decline?
papers.contribution: Documents the disappearance of the U-shape in wellbeing and hump-shape in illbeing using two large US datasets and a job quality survey.
papers.dataDetail: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System 1993-2025, National Health Interview Survey 1997-2024 and American Job Quality Survey 2025.

papers.title: The Distributional Effects of Cost-Sharing in a Universal Healthcare System
papers.q: What are the distributional effects of cost-sharing in a universal healthcare system?
papers.summary: Cost-sharing increased substantially for adolescents. The paper finds that females and native-born Norwegians have higher baseline demand, with consequences for how cost-sharing shapes out-of-pocket costs across groups.
papers.contribution: Distinguishes consumers' demand elasticity from their baseline demand level and studies a 2010 Norwegian reform raising the age threshold for cost-sharing exemption, using administrative data.
papers.ident: Policy change in 2010 raising the age threshold for the cost-sharing exemption.
papers.dataDetail: Norwegian national health insurance administrative data.

papers.title: Pricing Residential Mortgage Credit Risk in the Post-GFC Era
papers.q: How are residential mortgage credit risk transfer bonds priced, and who cross-subsidizes whom?
papers.summary: GSEs compensate investors about fairly on average but overpay for low-risk tranches and underpay for high-risk ones. Guarantee fee increases broadly align with credit risk, high-risk borrowers subsidize low-risk ones, and the 2023 reform partially corrected this.
papers.contribution: Develops an asset pricing framework for CRT bonds consistent with Treasury, corporate bond and housing markets.
papers.ident: Structural asset pricing model of CRT bonds.
papers.dataDetail: Credit risk transfer bond data.

papers.title: Stable Price Dispersion under Heterogeneous Buyer Consideration

authors.inst: European School of Management and Technology

papers.q: What stable price dispersion arises when buyers consider different sets of suppliers?
papers.summary: Stable and dispersed prices are derived across several consideration specifications and contrasted with conventional approaches.
papers.contribution: Identifies prices at which no firm wishes to undercut a rival or raise its price when rivals can respond with special deals.
papers.ident: Theory: pricing with heterogeneous consumer consideration sets.

papers.title: Topography of the FX Derivatives Market: A View from London
papers.contribution: Uses 100 million transactions to map participants' roles in the world's largest FX derivatives market.
papers.summary: Pension and investment funds, insurers and nonfinancials mainly hedge, with dealer banks providing liquidity and offsetting speculative demand. Hedge fund flows help transmit monetary policy shocks to exchange rates, and investment funds' unwinding of hedges contributes to dollar appreciations.
papers.q: How do speculators, hedgers and market makers interact in the London FX derivatives market?
papers.dataDetail: 100 million FX derivative transactions in London.

papers.title: How Restrictive is U.S. Trade Policy?
papers.summary: As of October 2025 the index is 23 percent against an 11 percent average tariff rate, so policy is twice as restrictive as headline tariffs suggest. Restrictiveness toward Canada and Mexico is two to three times average tariff rates and concentrated in vehicles, machinery and electrical equipment.
papers.q: How restrictive is current US trade policy?
papers.contribution: Computes Trade Restrictiveness Index measures following Anderson and Neary for current US trade policy.
papers.dataDetail: US tariff data as of October 2025.

papers.title: Business Concentration around the World: 1900-2020

authors.inst: Kiel Institute for the World Economy

papers.q: How has business concentration evolved around the world from 1900 to 2020?
papers.contribution: Collects new data on the firm size distribution in ten market-based economies across Asia, Europe, North America and Oceania.
papers.summary: Concentration of sales, net income and equity capital has risen over the past century in aggregate and within industries, while employment concentration has been stable in most cases. Large firms often achieve greater scale without proportionally more workers.
papers.dataDetail: New data on firm size distributions in ten economies, 1900-2020.

papers.title: Community College Bachelor’s Degrees: How CCB Graduates’ Earnings Compare to AAs and BAs
papers.q: How do earnings of community college bachelor's graduates compare with AA and BA holders?
papers.summary: CCB graduates earn $4,000 to $9,000 more annually than AA holders one year after graduation but about $2,000 less than traditional BA recipients. Penalties are largest in IT and engineering technology and minimal in nursing, other healthcare, business and criminal justice.
papers.contribution: Provides the first descriptive analysis of the economic value of CCB degrees, covering early-career earnings, program costs and field alignment, with administrative data.
papers.ident: Descriptive comparison controlling for institution and field.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative data on community college baccalaureate graduates.

papers.title: The Geography of Science
papers.q: How has the global geography of science shifted, in who produces it, what it studies and where it diffuses?
papers.summary: The US share of publications fell from 40% in 1980 to 15% in 2022 while China's rose from near zero to 32%, including over 35% of top-journal publications. The shift reflects both a larger researcher base and, to a large extent, higher individual productivity, and varies by field.
papers.contribution: Documents the geography of science using data on 44 million publications from 1980 to 2022.
papers.ident: Descriptive: shares of publications by country, field and outlet.
papers.dataDetail: 44 million publications, 1980-2022.

papers.title: Tenure-Dependent Severance Costs and Labor Market Dynamics over the Life Cycle

authors.inst: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.q: How do tenure-dependent severance costs affect labor market dynamics over the life cycle?
papers.summary: Tenure-dependent severance pay induces labor hoarding among low-productivity, long-tenured workers, with distortions strongest late in the life cycle as firms delay separation and impose higher hiring thresholds on older unemployed workers.
papers.contribution: Develops an overlapping-generations search-and-matching model with rising separation costs and estimates it on Brazilian employer-employee data.
papers.ident: Structural: OLG search-and-matching model estimated on Brazilian employer-employee data.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian administrative employer-employee data.

papers.title: Research to Improve the Quality, Impact, and Value of Home and Community-Based Services
papers.q: What does research say about the quality, impact and value of Medicaid home and community-based services?
papers.contribution: Characterizes the goals and financing of HCBS and, from a literature review and expert panel input, summarizes the evidence and knowledge gaps.
papers.summary: Nearly eight million Americans use Medicaid HCBS for long-term services and supports. Based on gaps in the evidence, the paper sets out research priorities at the federal, state and direct service provision levels.

papers.title: Customer Overlap and Diversion Ratios
papers.summary: Unlike diversion ratios, which are hard to estimate, customer overlaps are straightforwardly observed in many datasets, and the paper illustrates their use where estimating diversion ratios would be prohibitive.
papers.q: Can customer overlap proxy for diversion ratios in measuring competition between substitutes?
papers.contribution: Defines customer overlap as the share of one product's customers who buy another and shows theoretically and empirically its close link to diversion ratios.
papers.ident: Theory linking customer overlap to diversion ratios, validated empirically.

papers.title: Hitting Rock Bottom: Economic Hardship and Cheating
papers.q: Does economic hardship undermine preferences for honesty?
papers.summary: Cheating responds strongly to financial incentives. Covid-19 hardship, marked by a 51% drop in monthly earnings, sharply increases cheating, and the effect grows with prolonged hardship.
papers.contribution: Uses controlled, high-stakes measures of cheating in a large sample of 5,664 Kenyans, combining manipulated incentives, randomized salience of finances and the Covid-19 income shock.
papers.ident: Experimentally manipulated incentives, randomized salience, and randomized survey timing before versus during Covid-19.
papers.dataDetail: 5,664 Kenyans.

papers.title: Party Pressure and Representation
papers.summary: Accounting for party pressure, member and constituent ideologies are much more closely aligned than in a model without it, implying that parties drive a wedge between members and those they represent. Evidence suggests parties do so strategically.
papers.q: How do political parties affect representation in the US House?
papers.contribution: Adds party pressure to a spatial model of roll call voting and jointly estimates member and voter ideologies from votes and survey responses.
papers.ident: Structural: spatial voting model with party pressure estimated on roll calls and survey responses.
papers.dataDetail: US House roll call votes and voter survey responses on issues before Congress.

papers.title: Financial Globalization: Risk Sharing or Risk Exposure?
papers.q: Does financial globalization bring risk sharing or risk exposure?
papers.summary: Cross-country ownership improved risk sharing and reduced volatility from financial crises but raised exposure to foreign crises and international co-movement. Financial globalization reduced volatility worldwide, significantly more in emerging economies.
papers.contribution: Studies the effect of cross-country ownership of financial assets between advanced and emerging economies on volatility, using a two-region quantitative model.
papers.ident: Quantitative: two-region model of advanced and emerging economies.

papers.title: Subcontracting in Federal Spending: Micro and Macro Implications
papers.q: How does subcontracting shape the spatial and firm-level effects of federal government spending?
papers.summary: A substantial share of spending is reallocated across regions via subcontracts, and firm-to-firm flows redirect spending toward large, goods-producing firms. Accounting for subcontracting modestly raises prime-contract multipliers.
papers.contribution: Merges new defense subcontract data with firm-level data and develops a strategy separately identifying local effects of prime and subcontract spending.
papers.ident: Empirical strategy separating local effects of prime and subcontract spending using merged contract and firm data.
papers.dataDetail: Newly available US defense subcontract data merged with firm-level data.

papers.title: SNAP Work Requirements, Administrative Burden and Procedural Denials
papers.q: Do SNAP work requirements reduce participation through administrative burden and procedural denials?
papers.contribution: Studies ABAWD work requirements using age-based exemptions at 50 and older and waiver periods, with administrative data.
papers.summary: Work requirements significantly increase procedural and overall denials, indicating that these policies deter participation through administrative burdens.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences leveraging waiver periods and age-based exemptions for those aged 50 and older.
papers.dataDetail: SNAP administrative data.

papers.title: AI-Enhanced Handheld ECGs to Screen for Prior Myocardial Infarction in Rural India

authors.inst: Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab

papers.q: Can AI-enhanced handheld ECGs screen for prior myocardial infarction in rural India?
papers.contribution: Addresses the diagnostic bottleneck in low- and middle-income countries by applying AI to low-cost handheld ECG signals, noting that most medical AI is trained in high-income settings and deteriorates elsewhere.
papers.summary: The abstract describes the problem of moving diagnosis out of formal health facilities and the promise of AI to interpret raw signals from low-cost devices at scale.

papers.title: Ricardian Non-Equivalence
papers.q: Do households incorporate future tax liabilities into their spending plans in response to fiscal transfers?
papers.summary: The planned propensity to spend out of transfers equals the MPC, so households do not incorporate future tax liabilities. The canonical HANK model cannot account for this, whereas inattention dampens forward-looking intertemporal MPCs and brings the model in line with the survey evidence.
papers.ident: Quantitative: HANK model with inattention calibrated to survey evidence on planned spending.
papers.contribution: Provides new survey evidence on planned spending out of transfers and develops an extended HANK model with households partially inattentive to future taxes and general-equilibrium consequences.

papers.title: How Adaptable Are American Workers to AI-Induced Job Displacement?

authors.inst: Centre for the Governance of AI
Centre for the Governance of AI

papers.q: How adaptable are American workers to AI-induced job displacement?
papers.summary: AI exposure and adaptive capacity are positively correlated: of 37.1 million workers in the top exposure quartile, 26.5 million are in occupations with above-median adaptive capacity. However, 6.1 million workers (4.2% of the sample) are in occupations that are both highly exposed and low in adaptive capacity.
papers.contribution: Constructs an occupation-level adaptive capacity index covering 356 occupations that represent 95.9% of the US workforce.
papers.ident: Descriptive: occupation-level adaptive capacity index compared with AI exposure.
papers.dataDetail: 356 occupations covering 95.9% of the US workforce.

papers.title: The housing wealth effect: Quasi-experimental evidence
papers.q: How much do households cut consumption when housing wealth falls?
papers.summary: The short-run elasticity of new car purchases is 0.28, corresponding to a one-year car MPX of 0.09 cents per dollar of housing wealth lost. Households with high loan-to-value ratios and small deposits respond most, and a quantitative model aligns with the evidence.
papers.ident: Quasi-experiment: unexpected continuation of airport operations lowering nearby house prices.
papers.contribution: Uses a quasi-experiment, the unexpected continued operation of a Stockholm airport after political bargaining, which lowered nearby single-family house prices by 19.4 percent.
papers.dataDetail: Swedish household data with residence locations relative to the Stockholm airport.

papers.title: Cooperation between national armies: Evidence from the Sahel borders

authors.inst: NOVA School of Business and Economics
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.q: Did the G5-Sahel Joint Force reduce conflict by enabling cooperation between national armies?
papers.summary: The G5 mission lowered conflict intensity locally in its zone of operation, and propagation patterns indicate it facilitated security operations in border areas.
papers.ident: RDD at the boundary of the G5-Sahel Joint Force zone of operation.
papers.contribution: Applies a regression discontinuity design to the creation of an international force that can operate across borders.
papers.dataDetail: Geolocated conflict event data for the Sahel.

papers.title: The Future in Mind: Aspirations and Long-Term Outcomes in Rural Ethiopia

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.summary: Five years after screening, treated households had higher future-oriented investments in agriculture, children's education and assets.
papers.ident: Randomized video documentary screenings to rural households.
papers.q: Do aspirations affect long-term investment decisions and poverty in rural Ethiopia?
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized controlled trial in which treated households watched documentaries featuring role models who escaped poverty.
papers.dataDetail: Rural Ethiopian households surveyed five years after the screening.

papers.title: Heatwaves and delivery practices: The effects of extreme temperature in Brazilian maternity wards

authors.inst: Escola de Economia de São Paulo
Escola de Economia de São Paulo

papers.q: How do heatwaves affect delivery practices in Brazilian maternity wards?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of the effects of extreme temperature on delivery practices in Brazilian maternity wards.

papers.title: The effects of cash and group therapy in the context of conflict: Evidence from a randomized evaluation in Ethiopia
papers.summary: The therapy was delivered by non-specialist health staff and followed by a large one-time cash transfer. Sixteen months after baseline, the abstract reports no persistent positive effects.
papers.ident: Randomized trial with therapy, cash and combined arms against a control.
papers.q: What are the effects of group therapy and cash transfers on depression in conflict-affected rural Ethiopia?
papers.contribution: Reports a randomized trial with three arms (group therapy, cash, both) against a status quo control among people with depressive symptoms or functional impairment, run in 2022-2024 during active armed conflict.
papers.dataDetail: Rural Ethiopia, 2022-2024, sixteen months of follow-up.

papers.title: Higher education expansion and the rural–urban gap in secondary schooling and labor outcomes: Evidence from China’s 1999 reform
papers.q: How did China's 1999 higher education expansion affect the rural-urban gap in secondary schooling and labor outcomes?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of China's 1999 higher education expansion and its effect on the rural-urban gap in secondary schooling and labor outcomes.

papers.title: Leveraging Virtual Contact and Social Networks to Foster Interethnic Harmony
papers.q: Can virtual contact through a documentary film promote interethnic harmony?
papers.contribution: Runs a cluster-randomized field experiment with over 3,300 households in 121 multiethnic villages in Bangladesh and uses emotion-detecting software on viewers' facial expressions.
papers.summary: A film humanizing the Santal minority increased the Bengali majority's prosociality toward minorities, though the strength of evidence varies by treatment arm and outcome. Facial expressions are consistent with empathy.
papers.ident: Cluster-randomized documentary screenings across villages in Bangladesh.
papers.dataDetail: Over 3,300 households in 121 multiethnic villages in Bangladesh.

papers.title: A few good masks: Mask manufacturing and supply networks in Rwanda during the COVID-19 pandemic
papers.q: How did mask manufacturing and supply networks operate in Rwanda during COVID-19?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of mask manufacturing and supply networks in Rwanda during the COVID-19 pandemic.

papers.title: The timing of shocks matters in optimal monetary policy
papers.q: How does the timing of shocks within the year change optimal monetary policy?
papers.summary: The slope of the Phillips curve and the welfare loss weights differ systematically by quarter, so optimal responses depend on when shocks hit. History-dependent policy rules can mitigate much of the welfare loss from not following quarter-specific responses.
papers.ident: Theory: New Keynesian model with seasonal wage staggering.
papers.contribution: Studies optimal monetary policy in an economy with seasonal wage staggering.

papers.title: The Illiquidity of Water Markets
papers.q: Is an auction or a quota the more efficient way to allocate water when poor farmers are liquidity constrained?
papers.summary: Poor farmers were liquidity constrained while wealthy elite farmers were not. Because water demand is set by the crop production technology, the approach separates liquidity constraints from other demand features.
papers.contribution: Estimates a structural dynamic demand model using a change in the institution for allocating water in southeastern Spain.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic demand model estimated on water market data around an institutional change from quota to auction.
papers.dataDetail: Water market data from southeastern Spain.

papers.title: Growth Experiences and Trust in Government

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: Does experiencing higher GDP growth over a lifetime increase trust in government?
papers.summary: People who experienced higher GDP growth trust their governments more, with larger effects in democracies, and have better perceptions of government performance and living standards. No similar channel appears for interpersonal trust, and more recent growth experiences matter most.
papers.contribution: Assembles a harmonized global dataset across 11 opinion surveys with 3.3 million respondents in 166 countries since 1990 and exploits cohort-level variation in growth experiences.
papers.ident: Cohort-level variation in GDP growth experienced since birth across countries.
papers.dataDetail: 11 harmonized opinion surveys, 3.3 million respondents in 166 countries since 1990.

papers.title: State and Time-Dependent Pricing
papers.q: How do firms set prices, and how do state-dependent and time-dependent pricing affect inflation dynamics?
papers.contribution: Uses direct questions from a large economy-wide survey of UK firms and a randomised survey experiment.
papers.summary: Since 2023, 54% of firms report state-dependent pricing versus 44% in 2019, more likely for smaller firms, those with higher non-labour cost shares and those with higher uncertainty. State-dependent firms had a sharper rise in price growth in 2022-2023 and a faster subsequent decline.
papers.ident: Descriptive: survey responses on pricing behaviour, with a randomised survey experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Large economy-wide survey of UK firms, 2019 and since 2023.

papers.title: How In-School Supervised Ed-Tech Support Produces Massive Learning Gains: A Khan Academy Field Experiment in India
papers.q: Does in-school supervised support raise the usage and learning gains of ed-tech in Indian schools?
papers.summary: All schools had access to Khan Academy; the study tests whether strengthening implementation structure raises the quantity and quality of computer-assisted learning usage and, in turn, learning gains. The title reports massive learning gains.
papers.contribution: Randomly assigns implementation support for Khan Academy across 83 residential government middle schools in Uttar Pradesh.
papers.ident: Randomized school-level implementation support for Khan Academy across 83 schools.
papers.dataDetail: 83 residential government middle schools in Uttar Pradesh, India.

papers.title: Dementia and Long-run Trajectories in Household Finances
papers.summary: The wealth divergence is not explained by reduced earnings, higher healthcare spending, Medicaid spend-down, state-dependent utility or reverse causation. The results point to impaired financial decision-making beginning about six years before clinically recognizable dementia.
papers.q: Why does household wealth decline before dementia onset?
papers.contribution: Compares household finance trajectories of those who later develop dementia and those who do not using the Health and Retirement Study.
papers.ident: Event-study-style comparison of wealth trajectories before dementia onset against matched non-dementia individuals.
papers.dataDetail: Health and Retirement Study longitudinal data.

papers.title: Aging and Housing Returns
papers.summary: Older sellers renovate less, upkeep their homes worse, and are more likely to sell off-MLS and to investors, leading to lower prices. Reforms reducing pocket listings reduced both their prevalence and the age gap in returns.
papers.q: Why do older home sellers receive lower returns than younger sellers?
papers.contribution: Documents the age gap in housing returns and uses reforms increasing the transparency of pocket listings for causal evidence.
papers.ident: Reforms making pocket listings more transparent, compared across seller ages.
papers.dataDetail: Home sales and listing data.

papers.title: The Impacts of Parole Supervision
papers.q: What are the impacts of shorter parole supervision?
papers.summary: The reform reduced prison re-entry rates through sharp drops in technical revocations, while re-admissions for new crimes were unchanged, and Cook County court records confirm this. It reduced parole costs without measurable harm to public safety.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around the Illinois reform shortening supervision terms.
papers.contribution: Studies an Illinois reform that cut supervision terms for some parolees from 12 to 6 months, with a conceptual framework for how shorter terms affect criminal activity.
papers.dataDetail: Illinois parole and prison records, and Cook County court records.

papers.title: Does Advertising Expand the Market for Hospital Services? Evidence from Medicare
papers.contribution: Provides what it describes as the first causal evidence on market expansion effects of hospital advertising, using Medicare data.
papers.summary: Hospital advertising may steal existing patients, expand the market, or both, with public finance implications given taxpayer subsidies. The identification leverages spikes in advertising exposure, and the abstract is cut off before the results.
papers.q: Does advertising expand the market for hospital services?
papers.dataDetail: Medicare data.

papers.title: Do GLP-1 Medications Pay for Themselves?
papers.q: Do GLP-1 medications pay for themselves through lower downstream health spending?
papers.summary: Over five years, GLP-1 drugs do not reduce downstream medical spending and lead to a small increase, mostly in outpatient care, with similar offsets across baseline health groups. Cost increases for semaglutide are smaller and statistically indistinguishable from zero.
papers.ident: Staggered adoption design on insurance claims over a five-year follow-up.
papers.contribution: Estimates GLP-1 cost offsets from insurance claims with a staggered adoption design.
papers.dataDetail: Insurance claims data.

papers.title: Firm Emissions and Credit Allocation
papers.q: Do banks help or hamper the green transition through the allocation of credit by firm emissions?
papers.summary: For US borrowers, bank lending was likely hampering the green transition, in contrast to the other settings the paper examines. The abstract is cut off before the remaining results.
papers.contribution: Analyzes bank lending dynamics in relation to borrowers' CO2 emissions across and within industries in the US, EU and Denmark, using syndicated loan data.
papers.dataDetail: Syndicated loan data matched to borrower CO2 emissions for the US, EU and Denmark.

papers.title: Re-Examining Geographic Variation in Health and Health Care
papers.q: Do places that raise health care spending also raise health?
papers.contribution: Re-examines geographic variation in health and health care using mover designs that estimate the causal impact of place on spending and mortality.
papers.summary: Places that increase health care spending do not tend to be places that increase health, and the paper discusses the implications.
papers.ident: Mover design estimating place effects on health care spending and mortality.

papers.title: Does LLM Assistance Improve Healthcare Delivery? An Evaluation Using On-site Physicians and Laboratory Tests
papers.summary: Health workers changed their prescribing for more than half of patients in response to LLM feedback and reported high satisfaction, and retrospective academic physician reviews were also conducted. The abstract is cut off before the full quality results.
papers.q: Does LLM decision support improve healthcare delivery in outpatient clinics in Nigeria?
papers.contribution: Deploys LLM decision support for health workers at two Nigerian clinics and evaluates plans with blinded randomized assessments by on-site physicians and laboratory tests.
papers.ident: Comparison of unassisted and LLM-assisted care plans with blinded randomized physician assessments and lab tests.
papers.dataDetail: Two outpatient clinics in Nigeria, with on-site physician assessments and laboratory tests.

papers.title: Experiences, Expectations, and Asset Prices
papers.summary: The experience-based model resembles Bayesian updating but predicts heterogeneity between age groups that evolves over time as individuals of different ages learn from different histories.
papers.q: How do experience-based beliefs shape asset prices?
papers.contribution: Reviews research on experience-based belief formation, where individuals overweight data observed during their own lifetimes when learning about the data-generating process.

papers.title: Automation Experiments and Inequality
papers.q: What can automation experiments tell us about inequality?
papers.summary: The theoretical content of the test of whether technology raises output more for high- or low-skill workers had been unclear. The model describes how improved automation shifts the inequality effect.
papers.contribution: Formalizes a theory of the experimental effect of automation technologies on worker-level output, with a task-level production function, heterogeneous skills and delegation of tasks to the technology.
papers.ident: Theory: task-based model of worker output with delegation to automation.

papers.title: The Effects of Pension Reforms on Health Inequality in Italy
papers.q: Did Italy's pension reforms affect health inequality?
papers.summary: The health-income gradient differs somewhat by gender, but there is no evidence that the pension reforms increased health inequality.
papers.contribution: Builds health indexes from SHARE waves, 2004-2022, and analyzes their relationship with household income over time.
papers.ident: Evolution of the health-income gradient across SHARE waves around the Italian pension reforms.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe, 2004-2022.

papers.title: Global Stratification Economics (GSE): A Primer - Definitions and Research Implications
papers.q: How can stratification economics be extended to international contexts?
papers.summary: Building on the insight that groups compete over scarce resources and dominant groups shape rules to preserve advantage, GSE foregrounds historical genesis such as settler colonialism, slavery, caste, extractive governance and military intervention, and local institutions.
papers.contribution: Coins Global Stratification Economics, extending stratification economics to settings with universal mechanisms matched to development paths or context-specific, historically dependent mechanisms.

papers.title: World Trading System For Whom? Evidence from Global Tariffs
papers.summary: Countries internalize the impact of their policies on others to a substantial extent but not fully, valuing transfers to foreigners 25% less than transfers to their own residents on average. Countries that place higher weight on foreigners also receive higher weights from them, consistent with reciprocity.
papers.q: What weights do nations implicitly place on the welfare of trading partners, as revealed by global tariffs?
papers.contribution: Estimates welfare weights from global tariffs.
papers.ident: Structural: welfare weights revealed by tariffs in a trade policy model.
papers.dataDetail: Global tariff data.

papers.title: Nuclear Operations with a High Penetration of Renewables: The Case of France
papers.summary: Nuclear units are operated quite flexibly and the foregone production from load following is currently limited, though the abstract notes that additional load following events carry further consequences.
papers.q: Can French nuclear units operate flexibly alongside high shares of wind and solar?
papers.contribution: Uses hourly data from the French power system to study nuclear load following.
papers.dataDetail: Hourly French power system data.

papers.title: Macroeconomic Impacts of Microeconomic Damages in General Equilibrium: Productivity and Capital Losses
papers.q: What are the macroeconomic effects of microeconomic damages from pollution and climate shocks?
papers.summary: Market distortions, supply chains and changes in capital and labor costs can magnify or diminish the costs of these shocks.
papers.ident: Quantitative: analytical and numerical general equilibrium models with productivity and capital damages.
papers.contribution: Uses analytical and numerical general equilibrium models to study channels through which micro shocks affect the macroeconomy, including anticipation and welfare costs relative to the value of direct damages.

papers.title: Knowledge diffusion through FDI: Worldwide firm-level evidence
papers.q: Does FDI diffuse knowledge, as shown in worldwide firm-level data?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of knowledge diffusion through foreign direct investment using worldwide firm-level evidence.

papers.title: Income Taxation Across Countries
