papers.q: How do income tax systems and their progressivity compare across countries and over time?
papers.summary: Higher average tax rates go with higher progressivity, richer countries have more progressive systems, and progressivity varies by family structure, with marriage and children linked to higher progressivity. Transfers play an important role in redistribution.
papers.contribution: Estimates a two-parameter log-linear effective tax function for over thirty countries over forty years using Luxembourg Income Study microdata.
papers.ident: Descriptive: country-year estimates of effective tax functions.
papers.dataDetail: Luxembourg Income Study microdata, over thirty countries over forty years.

papers.title: Air pollution as comparative disadvantage

authors.inst: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics
Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.q: Does air pollution act as a comparative disadvantage for trade?
papers.summary: The title indicates a study of air pollution as a source of comparative disadvantage.

papers.title: When protection becomes exploitation: The impact of firing costs on Naïve Employees
papers.summary: Naive employees accept such contracts expecting to complete the high-reward track, but drop out or sort into other paths mid-career when costs loom large and rewards remain distant.
papers.q: Can firing costs enable employers to exploit naive present-biased employees?
papers.contribution: Identifies a new channel through which employment protection laws harm workers, built on a career structure with an unattractive entry phase, a worse mid-career stage and high rewards at the end.
papers.ident: Theory: contracting with naive present-biased workers under firing costs.

papers.title: The Unequal Costs of Carbon Pricing: Economic and Political Effects Across European Regions
papers.q: What are the economic and political effects of carbon pricing across European regions?
papers.contribution: Identifies the effects of carbon price increases on emissions, output, employment and voting across regions, complemented by opinion surveys.
papers.summary: Higher carbon prices reduce emissions but significantly reduce output and employment and increase vote shares of extremist and populist parties, contributing to political fragmentation. Surveys show a more pessimistic outlook and lower environmental concern, and carbon-intensive regions bear larger output declines.
papers.ident: Well-identified increase in carbon prices, tracked across European regions.
papers.dataDetail: European regional output, employment and vote shares, plus opinion surveys.

papers.title: Kinship ties in politics and response to extreme weather shocks
papers.q: Do kinship ties between local politicians influence disaster response to typhoons?
papers.summary: Kin-connected governors respond better than other governors to typhoon shocks. The abstract is cut off before the remaining results.
papers.ident: Close-election RDD on kinship ties between governors and congresspersons in the Philippines.
papers.contribution: Uses a close-election regression discontinuity design on provincial governors and congresspersons in the Philippines.
papers.dataDetail: Philippine local election results and typhoon exposure.

papers.title: Services trade and the choice of online versus in-person delivery
papers.summary: Studies how firms choose between online and in-person delivery of services in trade.

papers.title: Firms under fire! How insecurity affects formal firms’ existence

authors.inst: Centre d'Etudes Prospectives et d'Informations Internationales

papers.q: How does insecurity from conflict affect the existence of formal firms in Afghanistan?
papers.summary: Exposure to military events has on average a positive effect on formal firms' existence in post-2003 Afghanistan, with strong heterogeneity by actor, location, timing and firm type. A 1% increase in instrumented exposure raises the probability of formal activity by 4.17%.
papers.ident: IV exploiting foreign countries' involvement in the Afghan conflict as exogenous source of variation in military events.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework where insecurity affects firm entry, exit and formality, and uses foreign involvement in the Afghan conflict as exogenous variation with an original firm dataset.
papers.dataDetail: Original dataset on Afghan firms, georeferenced military events data, post-2003.

papers.title: The Gas Trap: Outcompeting Coal versus Renewables
papers.q: Can a climate coalition producing natural gas reduce emissions by exporting more gas to outcompete coal?
papers.summary: Without commitment, a climate coalition is tempted to export more gas to outcompete coal. When this is anticipated, investment in renewables falls and emissions ultimately increase. If the coalition can invest directly in renewables, the commitment outcome can be implemented under certain conditions.
papers.contribution: Identifies a time-inconsistency problem in which anticipated gas exports to outcompete coal reduce renewables investment, and discusses commitment solutions.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic game of a gas-exporting climate coalition with renewables investment and time-inconsistency.

papers.title: The Macroeconomic Consequences of Early Childhood Development Policies
papers.summary: In a calibrated model, a randomized evaluation of a short-run small program predicts effects on education and income similar to the empirical evidence. A long-run large-scale program yields over twice as large welfare gains, even after general equilibrium and taxation effects.
papers.ident: Quantitative: heterogeneous agent overlapping generations general equilibrium model calibrated on US data.
papers.q: What are the long-run macroeconomic and welfare effects of large-scale early childhood development policies?
papers.contribution: Incorporates early childhood investment into a general equilibrium heterogeneous agent overlapping generations model, validated against a randomized trial of a small program.
papers.dataDetail: US data used for calibration.

papers.title: Financial Aid and Upward Mobility: Evidence from Colombia’s Ser Pilo Paga
papers.summary: Studies the effect of financial aid on upward mobility, using Colombia's Ser Pilo Paga program.

papers.title: Labor market consequences of homicides: A gender perspective from Mexico
papers.summary: Studies labour market consequences of homicides in Mexico, with a gender perspective.

papers.title: A Method to Estimate Discrete Choice Models That Is Robust to Consumer Search

authors.inst: NOVA School of Business and Economics

papers.summary: The method forecasts the average response to new information in a lab experiment with costly search. In Expedia data it identifies which attribute was not immediately visible in search results and computes the value of additional information.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: identification of preferences in discrete choice models robust to consumer search, tested in a lab experiment and Expedia data.
papers.q: Can preferences be identified from choice data when consumers are not fully informed about attributes because of search?
papers.contribution: States conditions under which choice data identify preferences under imperfect information, giving tests for full information and tools to forecast responses to information and compute its value.
papers.dataDetail: Lab experiment and Expedia search data.

papers.title: Sovereign Default Risk and Firm Heterogeneity
papers.q: How much of the output decline during the Italian debt crisis was due to sovereign default risk operating through banks and firms?
papers.summary: Higher sovereign risk lowers the price of government debt and hurts bank balance sheets, reducing credit supply to firms that need financing or borrow from banks holding more government debt. Calibrated to measured firm-level elasticities, heightened sovereign risk explains one-third of the observed output decline in the Italian debt crisis.
papers.ident: Quantitative: sovereign debt model with heterogeneous firms and banks, calibrated to firm-level regression elasticities.
papers.contribution: Combines a sovereign debt model with firm- and bank-level data and shows direct and indirect effects can be recovered with a firm-level regression.
papers.dataDetail: Italian firm- and bank-level data during the debt crisis.

papers.title: One Instrument, Many Treatments: Instrumental Variables Identification of Multiple Causal Effects
papers.q: How can a single instrument identify causal effects of multiple treatments or varying treatment intensity?
papers.contribution: Generalizes the always-taker/never-taker/complier partition to multinomial and ordered treatments, yielding estimators from a single randomly assigned instrument.
papers.summary: The framework identifies causal effects averaged over complier types and a causal conditional expectation function over response types. Applications cover the Head Start Impact Study with multiple fallbacks, two channels of post-secondary financial aid on degree completion, and the effect of additional births on mothers' earnings.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: IV identification with multinomial and ordered treatments and heterogeneous potential outcomes.

papers.title: The Effects of Regulating Greenwashing: Evidence from Europe’s Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR)
papers.q: Did the EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation reduce greenwashing by affecting fund flows and portfolio sustainability?
papers.summary: The regulation had little effect on fund flows or portfolio sustainability, partly because disclosures offered little information beyond fund names and mandates. In an experiment, current disclosures have minimal impact on investor decisions, but more intuitive information could improve effectiveness.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences on SFDR fund classification, plus an experiment on investor decisions.
papers.contribution: Estimates the effect of the SFDR fund classification on flows and sustainability and adds an experiment on investor responses to disclosures.
papers.conclusion: Making disclosure information more intuitive could improve the regulation's effectiveness.
papers.dataDetail: Mutual fund flows and portfolio holdings in Europe, investor experiment.

papers.title: Why Care About Debt-to-GDP?
papers.q: Does the debt-to-GDP ratio give an accurate picture of government indebtedness compared with other measures?
papers.contribution: Constructs an international panel with debt-to-GDP, interest-to-GDP and debt-to-equity ratios to compare conclusions about debt trends.
papers.summary: Debt-to-GDP has reached historically high levels, but interest-to-GDP and debt-to-equity show no clear trend or a decline over recent decades. The measures give differing conclusions about recent trends in government indebtedness.
papers.ident: Descriptive: three measures of government indebtedness in an international panel.
papers.conclusion: Stronger theoretical foundations are needed for the measures used, and assertions about debt unsustainability may otherwise be premature.
papers.dataDetail: International panel of government debt, interest and equity measures.

papers.title: What Are the Benefits of Metro Rail in Mumbai, India?
papers.q: How did the first Mumbai metro line affect property values?
papers.summary: Property prices rose significantly and persistently by 6-8% for residential and commercial categories in areas within 1 km of the metro relative to areas 1-3 km away. Commute time savings and better employment accessibility are plausible mechanisms.
papers.contribution: Estimates metro effects on assessed property prices for commercial, industrial and residential land uses across 723 subzones.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing areas within 1 km of Metro Line 1 to those 1-3 km away, before and after opening.
papers.dataDetail: Assessed property prices for 723 subzones in Mumbai, 2011-18.

papers.title: Employment Impacts of the CHIPS Act

authors.inst: Center for Economic and Policy Research

papers.q: What were the short-term employment effects of the CHIPS Act in affected US counties?
papers.summary: Both designs show positive employment impacts, beginning at the Senate passage of a precursor bill in anticipation of the Act, of about 110 and 180 jobs per affected county. Local construction employment also rises.
papers.ident: Two county-level difference-in-differences designs around the CHIPS Act using semiconductor facility exposure.
papers.contribution: Implements two county-level difference-in-differences designs using QCEW data comparing semiconductor counties with other high-tech or non-fabrication counties.
papers.dataDetail: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, industry-by-county, United States.

papers.title: Broadband Internet Access and Adolescent Mental Health in the U.S.
papers.q: Does broadband internet access raise suicide ideation among US adolescents?
papers.summary: A one-standard-deviation increase in state broadband access is associated with a 9.3-16.5% increase in adolescent suicide ideation, most pronounced for girls. Broadband raised cyberbullying and body dissatisfaction among girls and reduced adequate sleep among boys.
papers.contribution: Uses the nationwide broadband rollout and state-level Youth Risk Behavior Survey data to link internet access to adolescent mental health, with mechanisms for girls and boys.
papers.ident: Panel analysis using the nationwide rollout of broadband across states, 2009-2019.
papers.dataDetail: National and State Youth Risk Behavior Survey, 2009-2019, United States.

papers.title: Ruling for the Rich: the Supreme Court over Time
papers.q: How has a pro-wealthy bias emerged in US Supreme Court rulings on economic cases since 1953?
papers.summary: In the 1950s justices appointed by the two parties had similar propensity for pro-rich votes. Polarization rose steadily over the sample, reaching an implied party gap of 47 percentage points by 2022.
papers.contribution: Builds a dataset of all economic cases since 1953, classifies parties as rich or poor, and estimates justice ideal points and party time trends with Bayesian Martin-Quinn methods.
papers.conclusion: The size of the gap suggests an economic metric is useful for prediction relative to ideologies such as originalism or textualism.
papers.ident: Descriptive: Bayesian estimation of case intercepts, justice ideal points and party-level time trends on classified Supreme Court votes.
papers.dataDetail: All US Supreme Court economic cases, 1953 to present, with parties classified as rich or poor.

papers.title: The Labor Market Return to Permanent Residency
papers.q: What is the labour market return to temporary foreign workers gaining permanent residency in Canada?
papers.summary: Gaining permanent residency raises the job switching rate by 21.7 percentage points and earnings by 3.2% after three years. Gains come mainly from moves to higher-paying firms, with no within-firm effects.
papers.ident: Event study around gaining permanent residency, plus a calibrated search-and-matching model with segmented labour markets.
papers.contribution: Links employer-employee data to visa records and combines an event study with a search-and-matching model with a segmented market for temporary foreign workers.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian matched employer-employee data linked to temporary and permanent visa records, 2004-2014.

papers.title: Market Power and Capital Constraints
papers.q: How does traders' equity capitalization shape asset prices and liquidity under market power?
papers.summary: Looser capital constraints raise asset prices and price impact, which reduces market liquidity. Constraints bind only infrequently, but their relative impact when active can be sizable.
papers.contribution: Develops a model of capital-constrained traders in an imperfectly competitive market and applies it to Canadian Treasury auctions, using a temporary policy exemption to estimate shadow costs.
papers.ident: Structural: model of market power with capital constraints, estimated on Treasury auction bids using a temporary 2020-2021 policy exemption.
papers.dataDetail: Canadian Treasury auction data, 2020-2021 exemption.

papers.title: Global Ripple Effects of Corporate Tax Reforms
papers.q: How do corporate tax reforms such as the 2017 US Tax Cuts and Jobs Act spill over across countries through multinational firms?
papers.summary: The TCJA raised US multinationals' intangible investment and output at foreign subsidiaries, and raised tangible investment by US subsidiaries of foreign multinationals, inducing parents to expand intangible investment at home. A Global Minimum Tax with top-up taxes generates negative inward ripple effects on US GDP and tax revenue.
papers.contribution: Combines firm-level evidence on the TCJA with a quantitative general-equilibrium model where intangible capital is nonrival and has mobile ownership.
papers.conclusion: No corporate tax policy is purely domestic.
papers.ident: Quantitative: general-equilibrium model with multinationals and intangible capital, matched to firm-level evidence on the 2017 TCJA.
papers.dataDetail: Firm-level data on US multinationals and foreign subsidiaries around the 2017 TCJA.

papers.title: The Ins & Outs of Chinese Monetary Policy Transmission
papers.q: How is Chinese monetary policy transmitted domestically and internationally?
papers.contribution: Builds a novel indicator of the People's Bank of China policy stance and estimates a policy rule that reflects its dual price stability mandate and changing operational framework.
papers.summary: Domestic transmission follows textbook patterns, with exceptions due to active management of the renminbi and the financial account. International spillovers are powerful, affecting commodity markets, global production and trade, with substantial pass-through to US prices. Financial spillovers are second-order and mostly derive from trade spillovers.
papers.ident: Time series: policy rule and shock identification using a new indicator of the People's Bank of China stance.
papers.dataDetail: Novel indicator of People's Bank of China policy stance with macro and international series.

papers.title: Making Entrepreneurs: Long Term Returns to Training Youth in Business Skills
papers.q: What are the medium and long-term effects of business skills training for secondary school students in Uganda?
papers.summary: After four years, training improved hard and soft skills, raised firm starts and survival, and led to higher-quality ventures. After nine years business ownership converged as control ownership doubled, but graduates kept an edge in business quality.
papers.ident: Randomized field experiment of a 3-week entrepreneurship training program with long-run follow-up.
papers.contribution: Follows a randomized entrepreneurship training program (SEED) with a nationally representative sample of 4,402 youth for nine years.
papers.dataDetail: Nationally representative sample of 4,402 secondary school youth in Uganda, followed four and nine years.

papers.title: Household Finance in Retrospect and Prospect
papers.summary: Household finance has matured through computational advances, large administrative datasets, microeconometrics for causal inference and behavioral economics. Reviews the distinctive concerns of the field relative to other areas of financial economics.
papers.contribution: Reviews household finance research and outlines directions for its future growth.
papers.conclusion: Outlines directions for the future growth of the field.

papers.title: From Treatment to Safety: The Role of Substance Use Treatment in Preventing Intimate Partner Violence
papers.q: Does expanding substance use treatment access reduce intimate partner violence in the United States?
papers.summary: Adding three treatment facilities, the average annual increase per county, reduces drug-involved intimate partner violence by about 1.5-1.7%. Treatment admissions data show new centers raise treatment entry, particularly among men, consistent with reduced perpetration.
papers.ident: Continuous difference-in-differences exploiting county-level openings and closings of substance use treatment facilities.
papers.contribution: Uses county-level treatment facility openings and closings with agency-level incident data in a continuous difference-in-differences design.
papers.dataDetail: NIBRS agency-level IPV incidents 1998-2019, county treatment facility records, Treatment Episode Data Set.

papers.title: A Unified Theory of Delegated Capital Management
papers.summary: With liquid transparent assets the mutual fund contract is optimal and investors earn zero alpha. With illiquid opaque assets costly due diligence is efficient with institutions as information producers, and the standard alternative contract implements the first best. Delegation is necessary because bilateral contracting is inefficient.
papers.q: Why do alternative funds differ from mutual funds in investor base, fees and access?
papers.contribution: Shows in a unified model that features of alternative funds arise endogenously in competitive markets when managerial skill is uncertain and assets are illiquid and opaque.
papers.ident: Theory: competitive model of delegated capital management with uncertain manager skill and costly due diligence.

papers.title: Green Waste
papers.q: How much of a Norwegian carbon-reduction subsidy program is misallocated, and why?
papers.summary: The decision-maker could have achieved the same emission reductions at less than half the cost. It identifies ex-ante the projects with the highest ex-post reductions but is unwilling to select them.
papers.contribution: Develops a framework to test for and measure green waste using project-level emissions and subsidy data for marginal and inframarginal projects, with ex-ante and ex-post reductions.
papers.ident: Framework testing for misallocation using marginal and inframarginal projects' emissions and subsidy amounts.
papers.dataDetail: Project-level carbon emissions and subsidy data for a Norwegian subsidy program.

papers.title: Expanding the Landscape of Cross-Border Flow Restrictions: Modern Tools and Historical Perspectives
papers.q: How have restrictions on cross-border financial flows evolved worldwide since the 1950s?
papers.contribution: Uses large language models on official documents to build daily de jure measures of restrictions across eight categories, validated against established capital account indicators.
papers.summary: The measures document the wide array of instruments and their prevalence over seven decades, with variation by flow, direction, instrument type and stance. They replicate and substantially extend existing benchmarks and are used to study crises, political economy determinants and policymakers' stated motivations.
papers.ident: Descriptive: LLM classification of official documents into daily changes in capital flow restrictions.
papers.dataDetail: Official documents on cross-border flow restrictions worldwide since the 1950s.

papers.title: GIFfluence: A Visual Approach to Investor Sentiment and the Stock Market

authors.inst: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.q: Can GIFs posted on an investment social media platform proxy for investor sentiment and predict stock returns?
papers.summary: GIFsentiment correlates with seasonal mood and COVID lockdown severity, rises with contemporaneous returns and negatively predicts returns for up to four weeks, more for portfolios prone to mispricing. It also predicts trading volume, volatility and flows toward equity funds.
papers.contribution: Builds a sentiment index from millions of GIF posts on an investment social media platform.
papers.conclusion: GIFsentiment appears to proxy for misperceptions that are later corrected.
papers.ident: Return predictability regressions using a GIF-based sentiment index, controlling for other sentiment and attention measures.
papers.dataDetail: Millions of GIF posts on an investment social media platform, market returns and flows.

papers.title: The Incredible Shrinking Instruments: Using Empirical Bayes to Increase Efficiency in IV Designs with Many Instruments
papers.q: How can empirical Bayes shrinkage improve the efficiency of IV designs with many instruments such as judge designs?
papers.summary: SJIVE has weakly lower asymptotic variance than JIVE and identifies a weighted average of individual treatment effects under exclusion and monotonicity. In an application on patent approval and startup follow-on innovation it gives substantially smaller standard errors than UJIVE.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: shrunken jackknife IV estimator for many-instrument designs such as judge fixed effects.
papers.contribution: Proposes a Shrunken JIVE estimator that shrinks leave-one-out first-stage predictions by their precision, with a variance-minimizing shrinkage rule.
papers.dataDetail: Patent approval and startup follow-on innovation application.

papers.title: How Monetary Policy Is Made: Lessons from Historical FOMC Discussions

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.q: How do individual preferences and the Chair shape monetary policy decisions at FOMC meetings?
papers.contribution: Constructs a new dataset from FOMC transcripts, 1966-1990, manually coding each participant's preferred policy and reasoning.
papers.summary: Participants' beliefs about the Phillips Curve slope play a central role: those seeing stronger real effects cite output for easing, those seeing stronger price effects cite inflation for tightening. The Chair reconciles views and minimizes dissent because dissenters' influence on later meetings is curtailed.
papers.ident: Descriptive: manual coding of FOMC participants' preferred policies and justifications from meeting transcripts.
papers.dataDetail: FOMC meeting transcripts, 1966-1990.

papers.title: What Drives Corporate Savings
papers.q: What drives corporate cash holdings?
papers.summary: Realistic cash holdings arise only when costly external financing, persistent productivity shocks and contemporaneous productivity shocks are combined. Persistent shocks alone make cash flows align with investment needs and give little reason to save, while contemporaneous shocks make cash flows random and induce cash holdings.
papers.contribution: Extends q theory of investment with financing frictions and productivity shocks to show which ingredients are needed to generate realistic cash holdings.
papers.ident: Theory: q theory model of investment with financing frictions and productivity shocks.

papers.title: Renewable Energy Expansion: Key Challenges and Emerging Opportunities
papers.q: What challenges and opportunities does the global expansion of renewable energy face?
papers.summary: Renewables have approached cost parity with fossil generation after a decade of cost reductions, yet solar and wind provide only about 15% of global generation as of 2023. The review points to regulatory design and market integration as ways to scale up.
papers.contribution: Reviews recent economic studies and identifies three central challenges: regulatory and market design, intertemporal market integration, and spatial market integration.
papers.conclusion: Effective ways to accelerate the global transition include improving market design and integration across time and space.

papers.title: Entry and Exit in Treasury Auctions
papers.q: How does the shift from dealers to hedge funds in Treasury auctions affect the costs and benefits of debt issuance?
papers.summary: Dealers exit and hedge funds enter Canadian Treasury auctions. The expected gains from greater hedge fund competition are smaller than the costs from hedge funds not participating regularly. Dealer participation remains strong enough that policies stabilizing participation have little effect on funding costs.
papers.contribution: Documents dealer exit and hedge fund entry over 20 years of Canadian auctions and develops an auction framework with endogenous participation.
papers.ident: Structural: auction model with endogenous participation estimated on Canadian Treasury auction bids.
papers.dataDetail: Over 20 years of Canadian Treasury auction data.

papers.title: Valuing Sticky Deposits
papers.q: How should sticky bank deposits be valued, and what are their interest-rate and runoff risks?
papers.summary: Deposit duration can be positive or negative, which matters for hedging bank balance sheets. Banks following optimal deposit beta strategies may significantly increase interest-rate and runoff risks. Deposit premia in bank mergers and acquisitions strongly support the model's predictions.
papers.contribution: Develops a fixed-income valuation framework with closed-form deposit values and tests it on deposit premia in bank mergers.
papers.ident: Theory: fixed-income valuation model of sticky deposits, tested on deposit premia observed in bank merger transactions.
papers.dataDetail: Deposit premia in bank merger and acquisition transactions.

papers.title: Quality Upgrading in Global Supply Chains: Evidence from Colombian Coffee
papers.q: Do returns to quality upgrading pass through supply chains to primary coffee producers in Colombia?
papers.summary: Quality premia are not passed through to farmers under normal circumstances, but an international buyer imposing a vertical restraint on the exporter can solve the hold-up problem. The findings come from the staggered rollout of a buyer-driven quality-upgrading program, and model calibration quantifies the gains.
papers.ident: Staggered rollout of a buyer-driven quality-upgrading program, with a model of hold-up and vertical restraints calibrated to the data.
papers.contribution: Formalizes a hold-up problem in quality upgrading and uses a buyer-driven program rollout, exporter records and administrative data to test it.
papers.dataDetail: Internal records from two Colombian coffee exporters and comprehensive administrative data.

papers.title: Digital Incentives in Surveys: Response Rates and Sociodemographic Effects in a Large-Scale Parental Nudge Intervention
papers.q: How do digital incentives affect survey participation among parents across language backgrounds?
papers.summary: Incentivized parents were more likely to engage, from starting the survey to choosing a gift card. Spanish-speaking parents had higher survey participation but lower gift redemption. Higher incentive value and advance information both improved engagement.
papers.ident: Randomized controlled trial varying incentive amount and vendor option information across parents.
papers.contribution: Tests incentive amount and vendor information in a large randomized trial of parents in six school districts and compares outcomes by language.
papers.conclusion: Findings inform the design of equitable and effective digital incentive strategies for diverse populations.
papers.dataDetail: Parents in six school districts in a large nudge intervention.

papers.title: Principled Identification of Structural Dynamic Models

authors.inst: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.summary: OASIS closes roughly twice as much of the gap to perfect correlation as recursive orderings. Revisiting 22 published SVARs, reduced-form innovations are typically only weakly correlated, which explains the robustness of recursive schemes, while proxy applications reveal economically important leakage across shocks.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: correlation-maximizing rotation for SVAR and Proxy VAR identification.
papers.q: How can structural identification in dynamic models be done by optimizing an objective rather than imposing restrictions alone?
papers.contribution: Proposes OASIS, an order- and scale-invariant rotation selecting the orthogonal rotation most aligned with target variables, and an estimation strategy for Proxy VARs.
papers.dataDetail: 22 published SVAR applications and seminal proxy VAR applications.

papers.title: The Incidence of Tariffs: Rates and Reality
papers.q: Who bears the incidence of the 2018-2019 and 2025 US tariffs?
papers.summary: Actual implemented rates are only half the statutory rates because of shipping lags, exemptions and enforcement gaps. Pass-through to US import prices is almost 100%, so the United States bears a large share of the costs.
papers.contribution: Compares statutory and implemented tariff rates and studies pass-through to US import prices and implications for sourcing, manufacturing costs and the dollar.
papers.ident: Descriptive: statutory versus implemented tariff rates and pass-through to US import prices.
papers.dataDetail: US import price and tariff data for 2018-2019 and 2025.

papers.title: Aging in Haze
papers.summary: Studies the effect of air pollution (haze) on ageing, as the title says.

papers.title: Robots and Workers
papers.summary: Studies how robots affect workers.

papers.title: Keeping up with the Joneses to Impress the Smiths: Conspicuous Consumption in a Society with Income Segregation
papers.summary: Conformists have a greater incentive for conspicuous consumption with many well-off neighbours, snobs with few. Despite these opposite incentives, conspicuous consumption is always higher in a more segregated society.
papers.q: How does income segregation affect conspicuous consumption when neighbours are the reference group and an outside observer is the audience?
papers.contribution: Develops a signalling model with conformists and snobs where neighbourhood income distributions set the reference point for social comparison.
papers.ident: Theory: signalling model of conspicuous consumption with neighbourhood income distributions.

papers.title: Professional survey forecasts and expectations in DSGE models

authors.inst: Center for Economic Research and Graduate Education – Economics Institute

papers.summary: Survey data improve identification of fundamental shocks and predictive power by separating low and high frequency volatility. Models with adaptive learning better capture macroeconomic trend shifts and achieve superior long-term predictions than rational expectations.
papers.ident: Quantitative: Bayesian DSGE estimation with Survey of Professional Forecasters expectations and adaptive learning.
papers.q: Does adding professional survey forecasts to DSGE estimation improve identification and forecasting, and does adaptive learning outperform rational expectations?
papers.contribution: Adds Survey of Professional Forecasters data on consumption, investment, output and inflation expectations and re-specifies shocks into persistent and transitory components.
papers.dataDetail: US macro series and Survey of Professional Forecasters expectations.

papers.title: Changing Opportunity: Sociological Mechanisms Underlying Growing Class Gaps and Shrinking Race Gaps in Economic Mobility
papers.summary: Earnings gaps by parental income grew by 30% for white children, while white-Black earnings gaps for low-income children fell by 30%. Outcomes improve for children in communities with rising parental employment rates, with larger effects for those moving at younger ages.
papers.ident: Quasi-experimental design using childhood moves between communities defined by race, class and county, with parental employment rates as the environment.
papers.q: What explains growing class gaps and shrinking race gaps in intergenerational mobility in the United States?
papers.contribution: Documents mobility trends across 1978-1992 birth cohorts by race and class and uses a quasi-experimental design to identify childhood community environments as the cause.
papers.dataDetail: US administrative and census data on children from 1978-1992 birth cohorts.

papers.title: Nickell bias in panel local projection: Financial crises are worse than you think
papers.q: Does Nickell bias in panel local projections lead to underestimating the economic losses of financial crises?
papers.summary: The bias invalidates standard t-statistic inference. Revisiting four influential studies, the fixed-effects method underestimates the economic losses of financial crises relative to split-panel jackknife estimates.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: Nickell bias in panel local projections corrected with a split-panel jackknife.
papers.contribution: Shows panel fixed-effects local projections suffer from Nickell bias and proposes a split-panel jackknife estimator that restores valid inference.
papers.dataDetail: Four published cross-country studies of financial crises.

papers.title: Genetic Prediction and Adverse Selection
papers.q: How much adverse selection arises in critical illness insurance when consumers have genetic information that insurers cannot use?
papers.summary: Current genetic prediction technology produces noticeable selection in the critical illness insurance market, and expected future technology could produce potentially crippling selection.
papers.contribution: Combines quantitative genetics, economic selection measures, and genetic and health record data on nearly 500,000 people in the UK Biobank.
papers.ident: Structural: selection measures from economic theory applied to polygenic predictions under scenarios of current and future technology.
papers.dataDetail: UK Biobank genetic and electronic health record data on nearly 500,000 individuals.

papers.title: The Role of Trade in Premature Deindustrialization and Industry Polarization
papers.q: What role does trade play in premature deindustrialization and rising industry polarization?
papers.summary: Trade alone does not cause premature deindustrialization, but its interaction with sector-biased technological change deepens it over time. Industry polarization emerges only through trade-driven specialization along comparative advantage.
papers.contribution: Documents two patterns of structural change and uses a dynamic open-economy model with sector-biased technological change to evaluate trade's role.
papers.ident: Quantitative: dynamic open-economy model with sector-biased technological change, matched to cross-country structural change patterns.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country sectoral data on manufacturing and structural change.

papers.title: Curtailing False News, Amplifying Truth
papers.q: Which policy interventions best curb false news sharing on social media while preserving true news?
papers.summary: Priming for misinformation awareness is most effective in reducing false-news sharing while preserving true news. Policies work through veracity updating, reputation salience and engagement costs, with differences explained by the salience and cost channels.
papers.ident: Randomized experiment on Twitter and X in 2022 and 2024 elections, with a structural model of sharing.
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized experiment on Twitter and X during US elections and structurally estimates a model of sharing driven by persuasion, partisan signaling and reputation.
papers.conclusion: Content-neutral priming enhances reputation salience at minimal cost and is almost as effective as fact-checking in updating veracity.
papers.dataDetail: Randomized experiment on Twitter and X during the 2022 and 2024 US elections.

papers.title: Security Design Under Common‐Value Competition
papers.q: What securities do bidders with dispersed information offer for a common-value investment opportunity?
papers.summary: Bidders offer debt, the flattest securities, because debt mitigates winner's curse exposure with two bidders and because the entrepreneur is more likely to select debt when optimistic. Signaling is dominated and does not affect the equilibrium. Committing to an ordered set of securities does not raise revenue.
papers.contribution: Characterizes security design under common-value competition and contrasts it with monopolistic investors and private-value competition.
papers.ident: Theory: security design game among bidders with dispersed information.

papers.title: Locally Robust Semiparametrically Efficient Bayesian Inference
papers.q: How can Bayesian parametric models be made robust to local misspecification while staying semiparametrically efficient?
papers.summary: The marginal posterior of the parameter of interest is asymptotically normal, centered at the semiparametrically efficient estimator with variance equal to the efficiency bound. An MCMC algorithm is developed and illustrated in applications.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: local misspecification robustness for Bayesian inference using efficient scores.
papers.contribution: Augments the baseline likelihood with a multiplicative factor involving baseline scores, efficient semiparametric scores and an auxiliary parameter.

papers.title: Dynamic Screening of Buyers With Heterogeneous Purchase Frequency

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.summary: With commitment, full surplus extraction is possible via limited-time offers. Without commitment, ratcheting is mitigated because not buying is not necessarily a sign of strength. The seller starts with a pooling offer and then switches permanently to screening if alternative sellers are easy to find, or occasionally experiments with separating offers if they take time.
papers.q: How should a seller dynamically screen buyers whose private information is how often they need to trade?
papers.contribution: Studies dynamic screening where purchase frequency, not valuation, is private information, with and without commitment.
papers.ident: Theory: dynamic mechanism design with private purchase frequency.

papers.title: Information Design in Common Value Auction With Moral Hazard: Application to OCS Leasing Auctions
papers.q: How does the disclosure of losing bids affect revenue in US offshore oil and gas lease auctions with post-auction exploration moral hazard?
papers.summary: The exploration rate correlates positively with publicly observed losing bids, suggesting winners infer rivals' private information. Counterfactual bid disclosure policies significantly improve auctioneer revenue.
papers.contribution: Characterizes equilibrium bidding when an auctioneer commits to how losing bids are revealed to the winner, and documents the link between exploration and observed losing bids.
papers.ident: Structural: common-value auction model with moral hazard and information design, estimated on OCS lease auctions.
papers.dataDetail: US offshore oil and gas (OCS) lease auction data.

papers.title: The Equilibrium Effects of Campaign Finance Deregulation on U.S. Elections
papers.summary: Super PAC spending by both sides prompts offsetting responses, producing limited net equilibrium effects. By amplifying the role of donors, Super PACs may still reshape the electoral landscape.
papers.q: What are the equilibrium effects of Super PACs after Citizens United on US congressional elections?
papers.contribution: Estimates a multistage model of political competition using Congressional election data to evaluate Super PAC spending.
papers.ident: Structural: multistage model of political competition estimated on US Congressional elections, 2010-2020.
papers.dataDetail: US Congressional elections and campaign finance data, 2010-2020.

papers.title: Identification in Instrumental Variables Models: The Central Role of Abadie's Kappa
papers.q: When are causal parameters identified in instrumental variables models, and what role does Abadie's kappa play?
papers.summary: Under unobserved heterogeneity of potential outcomes and response types, conditional independence of the instrument and convex restrictions, identification is equivalent to existence of a kappa. Asymptotically normal doubly robust estimators are developed for a leading special case.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: identification in IV models with convex restrictions on unobserved heterogeneity.
papers.contribution: Shows causal parameters are identified if and only if a version of Abadie's kappa exists, giving constructive moment conditions and doubly robust estimators.

papers.title: Walras–Bowley Lecture: Climate Policy in the Wide World
papers.q: What are the effects of alternative climate policies in an integrated assessment model with very high geographic resolution?
papers.summary: The model implies very large geographic dispersion in damages. A modest uniform carbon tax substantially limits warming and damages worldwide. Exempting the poorest countries from carbon taxes brings large efficiency losses, and fast green technology growth is a poor substitute for carbon taxes.
papers.contribution: Builds a dynamic integrated assessment model of climate and economy with fine geography and no migration across countries.
papers.ident: Quantitative: dynamic integrated assessment model with high geographic resolution, parameterized with data on output, population, energy and local damages.
papers.dataDetail: Geographic distributions of output, population, energy use and local climate damages.

papers.title: Economic Growth and the Rise of Large Firms

authors.inst: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.summary: The model has an asymptotic balanced growth path along which Gibrat's law holds and the tail thickens toward Zipf's law. Policies favoring large firms can improve welfare by better using diffusion externalities from idea search.
papers.ident: Theory: idea search growth model with endogenous firm size distribution.
papers.q: Why does the right tail of the firm size distribution thicken with economic development?
papers.contribution: Documents the thickening tail and develops an idea search model where growth and the firm size distribution are jointly determined.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country firm size distributions across levels of development.

papers.title: Comment on ‘Fisher–Schultz Lecture: Contracting Over Pharmaceutical Formularies and Rebates’ by Kate Ho and Robin Lee
papers.summary: Comments on the role of pharmacy benefit managers in managing medicine access and spending, and on formulary models by Ho and Lee and others. Points to future research on PBM entry, vertical integration, pharmacy steering and innovation.
papers.conclusion: Future research should focus on PBM market entry, vertical integration, pharmacy steering and effects on innovation.

papers.title: Training Specificity and Occupational Mobility: Evidence From German Apprenticeships
papers.summary: 40% of individuals work in occupations different from their training. Lacking training in one's occupation brings an average wage penalty of 14%, equivalent to two years of experience, rising with task distance between training and occupation.
papers.q: What is the wage cost of working outside one's apprenticeship training occupation in Germany?
papers.contribution: Estimates the cost of mismatch using vacancy instruments and extends methods for high-dimensional selection settings.
papers.conclusion: Retraining is crucial to mitigate the consequences of imperfect information in specialized training settings.
papers.ident: IV using vacancy instruments in a high-dimensional occupational selection model.
papers.dataDetail: German administrative data on apprentices and occupations.

papers.title: Comment on ‘Fisher–Schultz Lecture: Contracting Over Pharmaceutical Formularies and Rebates’ by Kate Ho and Robin S. Lee
papers.summary: Comment on the Fisher-Schultz Lecture on contracting over pharmaceutical formularies and rebates by Kate Ho and Robin Lee.

papers.title: Holding up Green Energy: Counterparty Risk in the Indian Solar Power Market
papers.q: How does counterparty risk of hold-up affect procurement prices and investment in Indian solar power?
papers.summary: The counterparty risk of an average state raises solar prices by 10%. This premium sharply reduces investment because demand for green energy is elastic, and central government intermediation eliminates it.
papers.contribution: Uses the universe of Indian solar auctions, where plants in the same states built by the same firms are procured by risky states or the trusted central government.
papers.ident: Comparison of solar auctions intermediated by risky states versus the central government, for plants in the same states built by the same firms.
papers.dataDetail: Universe of Indian solar power auctions.

papers.title: Assortative Matching on Income
papers.q: How do couples match on income in marriage?
papers.contribution: Develops a flexible matching methodology and applies it to Dutch tax files using pre-marriage incomes.
papers.summary: A majority of couples match assortatively, but a small significant minority display negative assortative matching. Standard approaches using current incomes of all married couples may produce misleading conclusions.
papers.ident: Structural: flexible matching model estimated on pre-marriage incomes of couples married 2013-2019.
papers.dataDetail: Dutch tax files over seven years, marriages 2013-2019.

papers.title: Why Do Workers Dislike Inflation? Wage Erosion and Conflict Costs
papers.q: Why do workers dislike inflation when real wages need not fall?
papers.summary: Wage catch-up from more frequent conflict does not raise welfare, so inflation's cost is set by wage erosion, and observed wage growth understates it. A survey shows workers would give up around 1.75% of wages to avoid conflict, and calibration shows conflict significantly raises the costs of inflation.
papers.ident: Quantitative: menu-cost model of wage conflict calibrated to survey evidence on willingness to sacrifice wages.
papers.contribution: Develops a menu-cost style model where workers engage in costly conflict to catch up wages and introduces the notion of wage erosion.
papers.dataDetail: Survey of workers on willingness to give up wages to avoid conflict.

papers.title: Screening Property Rights for Innovation

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How effective is US patent screening and what are the social costs of the examination process?
papers.summary: Patent screening is moderately effective given existing patentability standards, and examiners show substantial intrinsic motivation that improves quality. Annual social costs are $15.38bn, equal to 5% of US private sector R&D, and limiting negotiation rounds significantly reduces them.
papers.ident: Structural: dynamic model of applicant and examiner decisions estimated on examiner decisions and NLP-based patent distance.
papers.contribution: Builds a dynamic structural model of patent screening with incentives, intrinsic motivation and multiround negotiation, and uses NLP to measure patent distance.
papers.dataDetail: US Patent Office examiner decisions and patent text.

papers.title: The Emergence of the Poverty–Mental Health Gradient and the Great Pakistan Earthquake of 2005
papers.summary: Studies how the poverty-mental health gradient emerged around the 2005 Pakistan earthquake.

papers.title: Firm Accommodation After Workplace Disability: Labor Market Impacts and Implications for Subsidy Design
papers.q: How does firm accommodation after workplace disability affect worker outcomes, and how should subsidies be designed?
papers.summary: Accommodation rates respond to the subsidy rate, and receiving accommodation significantly raises employment and earnings a year later. Worker turnover and imperfect experience rating lead to underaccommodation, and subsidizing accommodation improves long-run outcomes and yields welfare gains for most workers.
papers.ident: Policy change in the Oregon workers' compensation wage subsidy, with an estimated frictional labor market model.
papers.contribution: Uses an Oregon workers' compensation wage subsidy and a policy change, plus a frictional labor market model of accommodation as human capital investment.
papers.dataDetail: Oregon workers' compensation administrative data.

papers.title: Empirical Bayes When Estimation Precision Predicts Parameters
papers.q: How can Gaussian empirical Bayes methods handle cases where estimation precision predicts the parameters?
papers.summary: The framework unifies proposals under precision dependence, and its most flexible member is a computationally efficient default competitive in regret. Using it brings sizable gains for selecting high-mobility Census tracts.
papers.contribution: Proposes a family of methods (CLOSE) modeling the parameter conditional on standard errors as a flexible location-scale family.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: empirical Bayes under dependence between parameters and standard errors.
papers.dataDetail: Census tract mobility estimates.

papers.title: The Complexity of Multidimensional Learning in Agriculture

authors.inst: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.q: How do farmers learn and adopt when agricultural decisions involve many inputs and practices at once?
papers.summary: Adoption rises steadily after the trials even without positive profits for several seasons. Know-how increases rapidly, faster for high-skill farmers who experiment most, at the cost of new mistakes. A model with multidimensionality and complementarities explains higher adoption costs.
papers.contribution: Randomly invites Kenyan farmers to agronomic research trials with different input combinations and tracks learning and adoption over six seasons.
papers.ident: Randomized invitation to agronomic research trials with different input combinations, six seasons, plus a theoretical model.
papers.dataDetail: Kenyan farmers followed over six seasons.

papers.title: An Experimental Evaluation of Deferred Acceptance: Evidence From Over 100 Army Officer Labor Markets
papers.summary: Deferred acceptance reduces administrative burden and improves match quality by reducing justified envy and raising truthful preference reporting. Impacts on retention and performance are limited by strategic preference coordination, but retention and promotions improve in markets with inexperienced managers.
papers.ident: Randomized trial assigning officer labor markets to deferred acceptance or manager-directed matching.
papers.q: Does deferred acceptance improve matching of officers to jobs in the US Army relative to manager-directed matching?
papers.contribution: Runs a randomized trial across over 100 Army officer labor markets comparing deferred acceptance with the traditional process.
papers.conclusion: Cross-market communication between agents can attenuate the benefits of strategyproof matching algorithms.
papers.dataDetail: US Army internal labor market, over 14,000 officers per year, over 100 markets.

papers.title: Optimal Shrinkage Estimation of Fixed Effects in Linear Panel Data Models
papers.summary: The estimator is intuitive, easy to implement, allows fixed effects that vary over time and are serially correlated, and incorporates the correlation structure. A method to forecast fixed effects one period ahead is also provided.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: optimal shrinkage estimation of fixed effects in linear panel models.
papers.q: How can fixed effects in linear panel models be estimated with optimal shrinkage without distributional assumptions?
papers.contribution: Develops an estimator attaining the best mean squared error within a class of shrinkage estimators without distributional assumptions.

papers.title: Trade and Domestic Distortions: The Case of Informality
papers.q: How does trade affect welfare and inequality in the presence of informality as a domestic distortion?
papers.summary: With a large informal sector, gains from trade are significantly amplified as resources reallocate from less to more distorted firms. The informal sector mitigates negative labor demand shocks on unemployment but can exacerbate real income losses in downturns, and the research sheds light on trade and cross-firm wage inequality.
papers.ident: Quantitative: general equilibrium model of trade with informal firms and imperfect enforcement.
papers.contribution: Builds a quantitative model where informality arises from burdensome taxes and regulation imperfectly enforced, so smaller firms face fewer distortions.

papers.title: Optimally‐Transported Generalized Method of Moments
papers.q: How can GMM results be interpreted sensibly when overidentification tests reject the null?
papers.contribution: Proposes an optimal transport GMM that allows errors in variables of least mean-square magnitude to satisfy all moment conditions, instead of reweighting data as in generalized empirical likelihood.
papers.summary: Revisiting Duranton, Morrow and Turner's study of city exports and transportation infrastructure, the method corroborates their results under weaker assumptions and gives insight into the error structure of the variables.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: optimal transport and Wasserstein metric approach to overidentified GMM.
papers.dataDetail: Application revisits Duranton, Morrow and Turner (2014) on city exports and transportation infrastructure.

papers.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Markup Estimation: Assessing Estimates From Financial Data
papers.q: Can markup trends and dispersion be measured from financial statement data that lack price information?
papers.summary: Measuring the average markup level does require pricing data, but trends and dispersion do not. Results are validated with simulations of a quantitative macro model and supported by firm-level administrative production and pricing data.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: markup estimation from financial data, validated by simulation and firm-level production and pricing data.
papers.contribution: Provides an analytical framework showing trends and dispersion of markups are well measured from financial data, and a consistent estimator for the markup level when pricing data are available.
papers.conclusion: The analysis supports using financial data to measure trends in aggregate markups.
papers.dataDetail: Firm financial statements and firm-level administrative production and pricing data.

papers.title: Equilibrium Existence in First‐Price Auctions With Private Values
papers.summary: Existence often depends on the minimum value in the support of the high-value distribution. Modifying the tie-breaking rule only at that value guarantees existence without the conditions. Results also apply to Bertrand competition with private marginal costs.
papers.q: When does an equilibrium exist in first-price auctions with private values?
papers.contribution: Gives sufficient conditions allowing non quasi-linear utilities and atoms or correlation in value distributions, showing existence turns on a single statistic of the joint distribution.
papers.ident: Theory: equilibrium existence in first-price auctions with private values.

papers.title: A Framework for Geoeconomics
papers.summary: The hegemon demands costly actions such as mark-ups, import restrictions, tariffs and political concessions, and shifts the global equilibrium in its favor to increase its power. A sector is strategic if it helps form threats or manipulates the equilibrium through input-output amplification. The hegemon adds value as a global enforcer but destroys value by distorting the equilibrium.
papers.q: What are the sources and uses of geoeconomic power for a hegemonic country?
papers.contribution: Provides a model in which a hegemon coordinates threats across disparate economic relationships to enforce demands on foreign entities.
papers.ident: Theory: model of hegemonic coordination of threats across economic relationships.

papers.title: Subgroup Decomposition of the Gini Coefficient: A New Solution to an Old Problem

authors.inst: Organisation de Coopération et de Développement Economiques

papers.contribution: Derives a decomposition from a set of axioms that is unique, easy to compute and has a geometric interpretation.
papers.summary: The within- and between-group terms sum to the aggregate Gini coefficient and satisfy desirable axiomatic properties.
papers.q: How can the Gini coefficient be decomposed into within-group and between-group inequality terms that sum to the total?
papers.ident: Econometric theory: axiomatic decomposition of the Gini coefficient.

papers.title: Choosing Who Chooses: Selection‐Driven Targeting in Energy Rebate Programs

authors.inst: Center for Infectious Disease Education and Research, The University of Osaka

papers.q: How can policymakers optimally combine targeting by observables with targeting through self-selection in rebate programs?
papers.summary: Targeting that optimally exploits both observables and self-selection outperforms conventional targeting. Estimates of several LATEs show whose self-selection is valuable or harmful to social welfare.
papers.ident: Randomized controlled trial of an energy rebate program with an optimal assignment rule and LATE estimates.
papers.contribution: Develops an optimal policy assignment rule integrating both approaches, usable with experimental or quasi-experimental data, and applies it to a randomized energy rebate trial.
papers.dataDetail: Randomized controlled trial of a residential energy rebate program.

papers.title: Multidimensional Screening With Precise Seller Information
papers.summary: Pure bundling achieves the same convergence rate to first-best revenue as optimal mechanisms, while separate sales converge at a suboptimal rate.
papers.ident: Theory: multidimensional screening with a multi-product monopolist and precise seller information.
papers.q: How do pure bundling and separate sales compare for a multiproduct monopolist when seller information about buyer valuations is precise?
papers.contribution: Shows that with sufficiently precise seller information, pure bundling always outperforms separate sales and matches the optimal mechanism's convergence rate to first-best revenue.

papers.title: A simple, robust identification approach for first-price auctions
papers.summary: Proposes a simple and robust approach to identification in first-price auctions.

papers.title: Inference for two-stage experiments under covariate-adaptive randomization
papers.q: How should inference be done in two-stage randomized experiments under covariate-adaptive randomization?
papers.summary: Ignoring covariate information in the design stage can cause efficiency loss, and common inference methods can be conservative or invalid. The results are applied to optimal use of covariate information under covariate-adaptive randomization.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: inference in two-stage experiments with stratified cluster and individual randomization under partial interference.
papers.contribution: Establishes consistency and asymptotic normality of difference-in-average-of-averages estimators for primary and spillover effects and derives variance estimators and optimal covariate use.

papers.title: Dynamic panel data quantile regression with network-linked fixed effects

authors.inst: University of Science and Technology of China
University of Science and Technology of China
University of Science and Technology of China

papers.summary: Studies dynamic panel data quantile regression with network-linked fixed effects.

papers.title: GLS estimation of local projections: Trading robustness for efficiency
papers.summary: Studies GLS estimation of local projections, trading robustness for efficiency.

papers.title: Efficient estimation of structural models via sieves
papers.q: How can structural models be estimated efficiently without repeatedly solving them?
papers.summary: The estimators avoid repeated solution of the model, apply to a broad class of models, are consistent, asymptotically normal and efficient, solve unconstrained problems with fewer unknowns and give convenient standard errors. They are illustrated with an entry game between Walmart and Kmart.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: sieve-based efficient estimation of structural models, applied to an entry game.
papers.contribution: Proposes sieve-based efficient estimators (SEES) that approximate the solution with basis functions and impose equilibrium conditions as a penalty.
papers.dataDetail: Entry game between Walmart and Kmart.

papers.title: Identification in nonlinear dynamic panel models under partial stationarity
papers.contribution: Provides a general identification approach for binary choice, ordered response and other limited dependent variable models with any number of lags and endogenous covariates.
papers.summary: The approach allows unknown error distributions and temporal dependence, yields partial identification and establishes sharpness of the identified set in the binary choice case. Monte Carlo simulations show robust finite-sample performance, and it is applied to income categories with ordered choice models.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: partial identification of nonlinear dynamic panel models under partial stationarity.
papers.q: How can nonlinear dynamic panel models be identified under partial stationarity?
papers.dataDetail: Application to income categories with ordered choice models.

papers.title: Doubly-robust inference for conditional average treatment effects with high-dimensional controls
papers.q: How can doubly-robust inference for conditional average treatment effects be obtained with high-dimensional controls?
papers.summary: Inference remains valid even if either the logistic propensity score or the linear outcome regression model is misspecified.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: doubly robust inference for CATE with Lasso in high-dimensional settings.
papers.contribution: Proposes a CATE estimator based on the augmented inverse propensity weighting signal with Lasso-estimated logistic propensity and linear outcome models, whose Wald-type confidence intervals are doubly robust.

papers.title: On generalized CCE estimation
papers.summary: Studies generalized common correlated effects (CCE) estimation.

papers.title: Promoting Women to Managerial Roles in the Bangladeshi Garment Sector

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: Are women inefficiently under-represented among line supervisors in Bangladeshi garment factories?
papers.summary: Female candidates had skills similar to males despite negative beliefs, but performed worse during the trial, related to bias against them. After the trial, many were retained and performed similarly, and factories permanently increased the share of women among new supervisors.
papers.ident: Field experiment randomly assigning marginal female and male supervisor candidates to production lines.
papers.contribution: Runs a field experiment with 24 large factories identifying marginal female and male supervisor candidates and randomly assigning them to lines, with a framework of experimentation over discrimination.
papers.conclusion: Equal or even worse performance of marginal candidates of a discriminated group is not evidence against discrimination when performance is uncertain.
papers.dataDetail: 24 large garment factories in Bangladesh.

papers.title: Estimation and inference for causal functions with multi-way clustered data
papers.q: How can estimation and uniform inference for causal functions be done under multi-way clustering?
papers.contribution: Proposes a two-step ML and sieve projection procedure with full-sample and multi-way cross-fitting, and a multi-way cluster-robust sieve score bootstrap.
papers.summary: The paper derives a functional limit theory and shows favorable finite-sample performance in simulations. It applies the approach to the relationship between mistrust in Africa and historical exposure to the slave trade, with clustering by ethnicity and region.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: Neyman-orthogonal signals with sieve projection and multi-way clustered bootstrap.
papers.dataDetail: Application on mistrust levels in Africa and historical slave trade exposure.

papers.title: Estimation and inference for large-dimensional generalized matrix factor models
papers.summary: Studies estimation and inference for large-dimensional generalized matrix factor models.

papers.title: The long run effects of a teacher-focused school reform on student outcomes
papers.q: What are the long-run effects of a teacher-focused reform combining performance pay with observation and feedback on student outcomes?
papers.summary: The reform improved educational attainment, reduced felony activity before age 19 and lowered dependence on government assistance at ages 18-22. Student sorting and teacher composition changes explain little, while school climate and teacher efficiency improved. Benefits far exceeded costs.
papers.contribution: Uses linked administrative data and the quasi-random timing of program adoption across schools to measure educational, criminal justice and self-sufficiency outcomes.
papers.conclusion: The individual incentive component is necessary but not sufficient to improve student outcomes.
papers.ident: Staggered timing of program adoption across high-need schools.
papers.dataDetail: Linked administrative data from a Southern US state.

papers.title: Coordination and Sophistication

authors.inst: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.summary: Coordination in canonical games is more likely when players perceive heterogeneity rather than homogeneity in cognitive ability, and higher sophistication is not necessarily beneficial. Laboratory behavior is consistent with the model and against alternative mechanisms.
papers.ident: Theory: cost-benefit model of reasoning in games, tested in a laboratory experiment.
papers.q: How can players coordinate in one-shot games without communication or focal points, and how does cognitive sophistication matter?
papers.contribution: Develops a cost-benefit model of strategic reasoning that predicts coordination depends on perceived heterogeneity of cognitive abilities.
papers.dataDetail: Laboratory experiment on coordination games.

papers.title: Comment on ‘Asset Bubbles and Overlapping Generations’ by Jean Tirole
papers.summary: An example economy satisfying all assumptions of Proposition 1(c) has a unique equilibrium that is bubbleless. The result is restored when initial capital is sufficiently large and dividends sufficiently small, and examples show these conditions are essential.
papers.ident: Theory: counterexample and corrected proposition in an overlapping generations model with asset bubbles.
papers.q: Is Tirole's Proposition 1(c) on the necessity of asset bubbles in overlapping generations economies correct?
papers.contribution: Shows by counterexample that the proposition as stated is incorrect and restores it under additional assumptions.

papers.title: Continuity of the Distribution Function of the argmax of a Gaussian Process
papers.summary: The continuity result supports several recently proposed inference procedures whose validity needs a result of this kind. The key assumption is demonstrably weak and close to minimal in a leading special case.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: asymptotic distributions of extremum estimators as argmax of Gaussian processes.
papers.q: When does the argmax of a Gaussian process have a continuous distribution function?
papers.contribution: Gives high-level sufficient conditions for continuity, verified for maximum score, empirical risk minimization and threshold regression, using the Cameron-Martin theorem.

papers.title: Double Robustness of Local Projections and Some Unpleasant VARithmetic
papers.summary: LP confidence intervals have correct coverage under local misspecification of the VAR. VAR intervals with short-to-moderate lags can severely undercover for small, hard-to-detect misspecification, and are robust only if the lag length makes them as wide as LP intervals.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: impulse response inference under local misspecification of VARs.
papers.q: How robust are local projection and VAR confidence intervals for impulse responses under local misspecification?
papers.contribution: Shows conventional local projection intervals have a double robustness property that holds even for large detectable misspecification, unlike VAR intervals.

papers.title: Existence of Myopic‐Farsighted Stable Sets in Matching Markets
papers.q: Do myopic-farsighted stable sets exist in matching markets?
papers.summary: The existence result holds for coalitions of arbitrary size and when not all coalition members need strictly gain. It gives a foundation for the efficiency-adjusted deferred acceptance algorithm, whose outcome is a singleton stable set when one side is farsighted and the other myopic.
papers.contribution: Proves existence of myopic-farsighted stable sets in one-to-one matching markets, with extensions to coalitions, weak stability and many-to-one markets.
papers.ident: Theory: myopic-farsighted stable sets in matching markets, constructive existence proof.

papers.title: Nonparametric treatment effect identification in school choice
papers.q: Which causal effects are nonparametrically identified in centralized school assignment with lottery and regression discontinuity variation?
papers.summary: Many aggregations of atomic treatment effects and their estimators place vanishing weight on RD-driven effects and mask heterogeneity. A diagnostic, new aggregation schemes and inference results are provided.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: identification of school-pair effects from lottery and RD variation in centralized assignment.
papers.contribution: Characterizes the full set of identified atomic treatment effects between school pairs and shows common aggregations put zero weight on RD-driven effects.
